title: What is the right sql syntax of one local table join with one cluster table?
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

With a small local table small_local_tb with several thousands data, and a large cluster table big_cluster_tb with billion-level data.
How to select data from these 2 tables with join relation?
I have try with sql
```
select from big_cluster_tb A join small_local_tb B on A.FILE_ID=B.FILE WHERE A.FILE_ID=100 AND B.FILE_ID=100
```
Usually join with big table on the left, and small table on the right, Is that right?

But raise with error
```
zk3:9000. DB::Exception: Table xxx_db.small_local_tb doesn't exist. (UNKNOWN_TABLE)
```
It seems like right table must be also cluster table when left table is cluster table, then can be joined.

So I did in reverse order with small_local_tb on left and big_cluster_tb on the right, as sql showed below
```
select from small_local_tb B  join big_cluster_tb A on B.FILE_ID=A.FILE WHERE B.FILE_ID=100 AND A.FILE_ID=100
```

But raise with another error
```
DB::Exception: Memory limit (for query) exceeded: would use 27.94 GiB (attempt to allocate chunk of 4249488 bytes), maximum: 27.94 GiB
```
It seems like right table data will all be put in memory first, but table big_cluster_tb is so big, then failed.

So how to solve this problem?

clickhouse version is 21.12.3.32, a little old, maybe not support table join function very well in this version.
And with newer clickhouse version, for example clickhouse23 or clickhouse24, 
what is the right sql syntax of one local table join with one cluster table?
author: flyly0755

comments.body: It is `global join`.

title: How to configure to stop insert data into local table in specific machine with cluster table scenario?
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

In such situation, a clickhouse cluster with 4 machines: ck0, ck1, ck2, ck3,
and local table test_tb in all 4 machines, and corresponding cluster table test_tb_cluster in ck0.
Select test_tb_cluster table data in ck0 will query every test_tb table data from all 4 machines.
What I want is store table test_tb data in just ck1, ck2, ck3 these 3 machines, not store in ck0(reduct insert stress and select stress in this machine, just use for insert&select task distribution), 
Must create table test_tb in ck0, right? Otherwise operate test_tb_cluster will raise error: 
There is no table `dbxxx`.`test_tb ` on server: ck0:9000

So how can I config table test_tb in ck0 to make it just as a empty local table? 
Insert data into test_tb_cluster will never choice test_tb in ck0 to store.
author: flyly0755

comments.body:
I come up with 3 ways, hope one of them can be helpful:

1. Configure the ingestion behavior on client side (for example only let the client know about the addresses of ck1 ~ ck3).

2. Another cluster and another Distributed table

    Create another logical cluster in `<remote_servers>` without ck0, say `cluster_no_ck0`

    Create another Distributed table on cluster `cluster_no_ck0`


3. With `insert_distributed_one_random_shard`
 
    Recreate the distributed table with NO sharding key.

    Configure the weight of shard 0 to zero in `<remote_servers>`.

    And insert with settings `insert_distributed_one_random_shard=1`
I have tried the second ways, which is perfect for solving this problem, thx!

title: MySQL engine tables do not survive reboot
body:
### Question

I have few MySQL connected tables that works well, however they do not survive reboot.
I was looking in the file system to see where they are persist, and could not find it anywhere.

Is there a way to persist MySQL tables that are created with the MySQL engine?
author: ronenb75

comments.body:
All tables created with the CREATE statement are persisted in the database,
unless you DROP this table, DETACH it, or DROP the entire database.

There is also a chance that you RENAME'd this table,
and there is a chance that you've used a table function rather than a table.

Thanks @alexey-milovidov 
This is what I'm expecting, but I can't find where. Can you point me to where the definition is kept?

I was looking at the metadata directory and it was not there, so I guess it's saved to the system database.

Sorry, I will close this issue as I just found out we did something wrong (I'm still not sure what exactly), but our database was created with a MySQL definition rather than Atomic engine.
That means our tables exists, but will not survive reboot.

Our database definition (in the metadata directory):
```
ATTACH DATABASE test1
ENGINE = MySQL(tools)
```
That will not have a storage link nor tables metadata definition.

When creating the database with the usual "create database" definition:
```
ATTACH DATABASE _ UUID '85db78c5-8088-40cd-9005-29b8d23462f4'
ENGINE = Atomic
```

This will work as expected. It will have a storage link location and tables will have .SQL definitions.

title: Sampling After Where Filtering
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

Hey, we have a table using sampling on userId. We want to use a "sample N" on the table but I want this sampling N size to be applied after the where conditions. 

For example, if I have a table with 1M rows and want to sample 100K of it but the where condition hits only the 1K of the whole 1M row there is a big possibility that the sampled data wont contain any of the filtered data.

Is there a way for us to define sample row count after the filtering?
author: ataberkgrl-dr

comments.body:
> Is there a way for us to define sample row count after the filtering?

No, there isn't a special syntax for this. You can always generate random numbers for each row after `WHERE` and drop however many you want, but it's not going to be efficient.

title: Performance Factors Influencing argMax vs. FINAL Usage
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

I'm observing varying performance between queries using argMax and FINAL in ClickHouse (version 23.3) and would like to understand the factors affecting their performance. In some cases, queries with FINAL perform better, while in others, argMax is faster. This inconsistency seems to depend on various aspects of the data or query structure.

Here are some key points for context:

    Cardinality of Columns:
        Columns with lower cardinality sometimes perform better with FINAL.
        Conversely, higher cardinality columns seem to favor argMax.

    Data Characteristics:
        The volume of data, the number of rows involved, and the distribution of unique values might play a role.
        Deduplication processes and how efficiently FINAL can be applied may impact query speed.

    Table Engine:
        The table in use is based on the ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree engine.
        Considering how FINAL operates on this engine, could its behavior differ from using argMax?

    Query and Indexing Impact:
        Queries using argMax may involve more explicit column operations.
        FINAL automatically deduplicates rows but might result in additional overhead depending on the dataset.

Questions:

    What are the primary factors influencing performance differences between argMax and FINAL?
    Are there specific scenarios where one approach is consistently recommended over the other?
    How do data distribution and cardinality interact with the performance of these methods?
    Are there optimizations or configurations (e.g., max_final_threads) that can help balance performance?

Any insights into these factors or best practices for selecting between argMax and FINAL would be greatly appreciated.
author: furkankahvecinsider

comments.body:
>version 23.3

FINAL was drastically improved since then with multiple optimizations.


The biggest difference is in reading orderby key. In general if most of optimizations are not applicable then FINAL reads all columns of a table's ORDERBY to evaluate the final row for each key. So if your table has `ORDER BY (a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h)` then FINAL needs to read and process in the memory all (a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h) columns in the contrary argMax/group by(a,e) needs to read only (a,e) and will outperform FINAL. But if optimizations are applicable then FINAL can have zero overhead and can be infinite times faster than argMax/group.

Thank you for your response, much appreciated! @den-crane 

I’ve gone through the changelogs related to these optimizations, but they weren’t as detailed as I’d hoped. From my testing, I’ve observed that in most cases, FINAL is indeed more performant compared to argMax. However, I’ve also seen scenarios where the opposite is true—where argMax outperforms FINAL.

I’m particularly interested in understanding these scenarios in more detail so that I can make informed decisions on when to use FINAL versus argMax. Could you provide insights or guidelines on the specific conditions or table structures where each method excels? That would be incredibly helpful for optimizing performance in my use cases. Thank you again!

>I’m particularly interested in understanding these scenarios in more detail so that I can make informed decisions

I can explain them in a 16-hour lecture. 
You need to consistently study each example, each optimization, how FINAL works, how GROUPBY works, it took 3 years for me (I am an ordinary DBA).

Parts are renamed to ‘cloned’ if ClickHouse have had some parts on local disk while repairing lost replica so already existed parts being renamed and put in detached directory. Controlled by setting `merge_tree/detach_old_local_parts_when_cloning_replica`.

**Logs**
Have dropped 4002 ranges
Checking drop range d97395418e2b6cdafcd7b0cefff6a7dd_0_32_999999999

title: Efficiently Handling Null or Empty Checks for Nullable and Array Columns in ClickHouse
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

Hello,

I have encountered a scenario where I need to determine whether a column is either:
* Nullable and check if it's NULL.
* Array and check if it's empty.

To handle this, I wrote the following SQL condition:
`if(startsWith(toTypeName(vtlVar), 'Array'), empty(vtlVar), isNull(vtlVar))`

This works functionally as expected, but I have a few concerns and questions about its performance and potential optimization:

1. Performance Impact:
Does repeatedly calling toTypeName() and startsWith() introduce any significant overhead, especially on large datasets?
Are there any internal optimizations in ClickHouse that mitigate the cost of type detection at runtime?

2. Recommended Best Practices:
Is there a better approach to achieve the same result without relying on toTypeName()?

3. Future Improvements:
Are there any plans to introduce functions like isNullOrEmpty() to simplify this type of check?

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated. If additional context or a sample dataset is needed, I’d be happy to provide it.

Thank you for your help!
author: minQZ

comments.body:
> 1. Performance Impact

`toTypeName()` and `startsWith()` are both quite lightweight operations, but, of course, they are executed in the runtime. When dealing with large datasets and billions of rows, even these small operations could contribute some overhead.

> 2. Recommended Best Practices

The best thing you can do is to change the schema so that there are no nullable arrays. From my knowledge, there are no ways to do it more efficiently, but you can try to do it like this:

``` SQL
CASE 
    WHEN empty(vtlVar) THEN 1
    ELSE (CASE WHEN isNull(vtlVar) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
END
```

I'm not sure if it will help, but worth trying.

> 3. Future Improvements

Yes, it's a good idea to add something like `isNullOrEmpty()`, I've created an issue about it.

title: 24.11 toJSONString function is not full json string
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

If toJSONString(tuple(node_id, data)) previously output something like:

{"node_id": 1, "data": ["tuple": 2]}
In version 2424.11, it now outputs:
[1, ["tuple", 2]]
This change indicates that the JSON serialization format for tuple in ClickHouse has been modified, resulting in a different structure when converting tuple to JSON.
author: huuns

comments.body: This is the traditional output of tuples vs named tuples. For a few minor releases `tuple` starting generating named tuples instead of unnamed tuples and it changed how they are output. If you want a named tuple you can either create it or enable `enable_named_columns_in_function_tuple`

body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

ClickHouse 24.10.3.21 running on x64 Debian

I'm trying to extract, ideally as a ClickHouse array, values of a nested array from JSON. I can do it in quite a convoluted way:

```
SELECT JSONExtractArrayRaw(JSONExtract(JSONExtract('{"user": {"details": {"hobbies": [{"key":1},{"key":2},{"key":3}]}}}', 'user', 'String'), 'details', 'String'), 'hobbies')

Query id: 2628ff82-8ad1-4669-98df-183700e03779

   ┌─JSONExtractArrayRaw(JSONExtract(JSONExtract('{"user": {"details": {"hobbies": [{"key":1},{"key":2},{"key":3}]}}}', 'user', 'String'), 'details', 'String'), 'hobbies')─┐
1. │ ['{"key":1}','{"key":2}','{"key":3}']                                                                                                                                  │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

That's verbose. 

Is it possible to pass nested path to JSONExtractArrayRaw - something like _user.details.hobbies_?

I know that the new JSON data type / functions are on their way, but I'd like to stick to stable functionality.

Thank you!
author: pakud

comments.body:
`JSONExtract*` all support multiple keys:

```
SELECT JSONExtractArrayRaw('{"user": {"details": {"hobbies": [{"key":1},{"key":2},{"key":3}]}}}', 'user', 'details', 'hobbies')
```

You can also use `JSON_VALUE` if you prefer:

```
SELECT JSON_VALUE('{"user": {"details": {"hobbies": [{"key":1},{"key":2},{"key":3}]}}}', '$.user.details.hobbies') settings function_json_value_return_type_allow_complex=true
```
that's it - thanks a lot @tiagoskaneta !

Hi guys, I got an issue with replacing mergetree table. My table has more than 5 billions records and data is comming to that tables almost 1k records per second (using kafka connect to insert). The reason is when I use final syntax, Clickhouse took too long to return the data, comparing without using final synctax
```
select count() from event
1.8 seconds to respond 
```
```
select count() from event final
30 mins to respond
```
Can you guy suggest me a solution for this?
author: phongbui81062

comments.body:
Yes, but check the results. With `FINAL` you probably get a lower, actual correct number. It has to filter out duplicates. This means it has to scan all of your rows to compare primary keys. Without `FINAL` you just get how many rows do you have without filtering out duplicates. This doesn't require any scanning.

None of the tables meant for full table scans in large volume. You should write queries that are restricted on the primary key, or at least partially, so ClickHouse can efficiently skip records.
what CH version you're running?

title: Does a JOIN in ClickHouse preserve the order from an ORDER BY in a subquery?
body:
### Question

When I use an ORDER BY in a left table subquery and then perform a JOIN in ClickHouse, does the final result maintain the order of the rows as specified in the subquery, or does the JOIN operation affect the order?
author: AmalDarKhalil

comments.body:
Operations over a subquery are never guaranteed to keep the order. The only guarantees are ORDER BY on the final result.

It's entirely possible that order might be kept now in some cases and it might be broken in the future when improvements are included.

title: Appropriate disk size when using s3.
body:
### Company or project name

jaeger

### Question

We separate hot and cold data, put hot data (one day) on disk, and cold data (more than one day) on S3, and configure the data to be moved from disk to S3 when the disk usage is greater than 90%.

So what is the appropriate disk size? We hope to minimize it to reduce costs.

Is one day's data enough?
author: zdyj3170101136

comments.body:
It's impossible for someone to give you any good answer to this as it depends in many factors that only you can know, such as how data is ingested and updated, what's your infrastructure and how much you pay for each element of it, what are the performance and reliability requirements.

If you want to minimize cost you shouldn't use s3 and just buy physical, cheap and reliable sata disks, but it's likely that performance will be worse and you'll have to maintain them.

> So what is the appropriate disk size? We hope to minimize it to reduce costs.
> Is one day's data enough?

Basically you'll need to test things out in your requirement, see if it's enough and iterate.

My recommendation, set it to a day (or any other value), see how the system performs for a while, and then decide if you need to increase or decrease it.

**example_B** with columns: city, additional_info_names(array), additional_info_values(array)
with order by key(city, additional_info_names, additional_info_values)

Considering that city is ALWAYS populated with a string value, a is 50% of the times, and b, c, d, e, f are frequently empty. Is it better to keep them as columns like example_A, or include them in a variable array "additional_info_names/values" like in example_B (e.g. when they have a non-empty value, it would be like additional_info_names = ["a", "b", "c"] and additional_info_values = ["aaa", "foo", "bog"])

I need the table to be fast for subsequent select queries including filtering/grouping on those columns, so I included in both cases all the columns in the ORDER BY.

Thanks in advance!
author: enzorevo

comments.body:
I think I can skip the boring detailed explanations and will just point out the benefits in short (in my opinion):

example_A (separate columns) is the better choice for your use case in ClickHouse:

1. in terms of performance, provides faster SELECT queries for filtering and grouping
2. of storage: efficiently handles sparse data with columnar compression
3. of simplicity: easier to write and maintain queries

Additional Recommendations:

1. Include only the most commonly filtered or grouped columns to improve performance in `ORDER BY` clause
2. Use secondary indexes like Bloom filters for columns with high cardinality if necessary
3. Always benchmark your queries and monitor performance to ensure the chosen design meets your requirements

Thanks.

What is the drawback of adding all the columns into the ORDERBY, if it can happen that I groupby / do WHEREs on most of them most of the times?

Also, how would you order the columns in the ORDER BY? I.e. criteria priority between: how frequently u query the column, its sparsity, if its high cardinality or not

1. Yes, it's better not to add all columns to `ORDER BY`, it leads to performance and storage drawbacks with minimal query benefits. It can enlarge the primary key index and will require more detailed sorting, so it's better to filter on leading columns.

2. Firstly, there should be columns frequently used in WHERE or GROUP BY clauses - you should prefer the most used columns as the first, then you prioritize columns with low cardinality, and then sparsity (prioritize if they are often populated)

Thanks, but regarding 1, in theory I may have to filter on all the columns or use some of the "non-frequently used" columns as single GROUPBY, and in those cases having them in the ORDER BY would speed everything up, right?

Clear for the 2, thanks!

It should be okay, but keep in mind that if you have a lot of columns in your `ORDER BY` statement, the more columns you have, the less effective sorting you will have (If you have `ORDER BY (city, a, b, c, d, e, f)`, filtering on f alone won’t benefit much from the index) and it won't increase the performance a lot
In that case, is there any other better indexes that can help me increase the filtering performance in most cases? Like for example: filtering on f alone, filtering on f,b,c, filtering on a, c.

You can use projections; it's similar to materialized views but stored within the table and optimized for specific query patterns. You can create projections that reorganize data with a different `ORDER BY` suitable for your queries.

for example,
``` SQL
ALTER TABLE example_A ADD PROJECTION proj_fbc
(
  SELECT city, a, b, c, d, e, f
  ORDER BY (f, b, c)
);
```

it accelerates queries filtering on `f, b, c` without affecting the main table’s `ORDER BY`. ClickHouse automatically uses projections when beneficial.

You can use materialized views as well, but they are not as transparent as projections.
Thanks! And there is no automated way to create all the possible projections for all the n-column combinations, right?
Also, do projections slow down INSERTs?

> And there is no automated way to create all the possible projections for all the n-column combinations, right?

As far as I know, no. We didn't consider this use-case as it is not really usual, you have to specify conditions for projections explicitly.

> do projections slow down INSERTs?

Yes, because they need to apply those conditions, but not much AFAIK. It's always better to optimize projections and keep only those you really need.
Thanks a lot!

title: How to force ClickHouse to return column names prefixed with table names when INNER JOIN?
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

For example:

CREATE TABLE ta
(
    `a` UInt32,
    `id` UInt32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id

CREATE TABLE tb
(
    `b` UInt32,
    `id` UInt32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id

insert into ta(*) VALUES (0,1)
insert into tb(*) VALUES (1,1)

WITH
    a AS
    (
        SELECT
            a,
            id
        FROM ta
    ),
    b AS
    (
        SELECT
            b,
            id
        FROM tb
    )
SELECT *
FROM a
INNER JOIN b ON a.id = b.id

This returns
┌─a─┬─id─┬─b─┬─b.id─┐
│ 0     │  1    │ 1     │    1 │
└───┴────┴───┴──────┘

How to force the returned qualified column names, i.e. a.a, a.id, b.b and b.id?
author: wlzywang

comments.body:
In `ClickHouse`, column names are not automatically prefixed with their respective table names when performing a `join`. 

However, you can achieve this by explicitly specifying the column names in your `SELECT` statement. Here's an example that forces the returned qualified column names as a.a, a.id, b.b, and b.id:

```
CREATE TABLE ta
(
    a UInt32,
    id UInt32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id;

CREATE TABLE tb
(
    b UInt32,
    id UInt32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id;

INSERT INTO ta VALUES (0, 1);
INSERT INTO tb VALUES (1, 1);

WITH
    a AS
    (
        SELECT
            a,
            id
        FROM ta
    ),
    b AS
    (
        SELECT
            b,
            id
        FROM tb
    )
SELECT
    a.a AS `a.a`,
    a.id AS `a.id`,
    b.b AS `b.b`,
    b.id AS `b.id`
FROM a
INNER JOIN b ON a.id = b.id;
```
This will return:
```
┌─a.a─┬─a.id─┬─b.b─┬─b.id─┐
│  0  │   1  │  1  │   1  │
└─────┴──────┴─────┴──────┘
```
Yeah, actually the alias is what I am doing now but it is kinda tedious if I have many columns to select and several tables to join together. Thank you for confirming, Amabilee.

Even though I am using high-speed SSDs for local S3 cache storage, enabling `direct_io` could still lead to significant performance degradation under heavy random access patterns. In this case, would the OS filesystem cache still be necessary, even with high-speed SSDs and the S3 cache in use?

> Does the current S3 cache behavior in ClickHouse involve a significant amount of random access?

we could say that reading from cache will have exactly the same pattern as reading from data parts itself. because there is 1-1 correspondence. thus it is 100% determined by the given query itself.

> under heavy random access patterns

i'd say it is not about random access specifically. rather about temporal locality, i.e. if the data is going to be accessed again until it will be evicted from the cache. and given that os cache might be 100-s of GBs in size (or even more) eviction might never happen. so, if you will be able to reuse cached byte range you're probably willing to pay the overhead of writing to os cache. if it surely never happen - only then it makes sense to disable os cache.

in what sense access pattern might play a role - direct io should disable io prefetching. so even if you're not certain that data will ever be needed again i'd still consider leaving os cache working in case access pattern is sequential (or well-predictable).
Got it, thanks for your response!

title: Are Memory tables dropped right away without using SYNC?

title: s3 table function fetch the whole parquet instead of metadata for count when it's a small file
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

i observed an issue with select count(*) from s3() reading parquet files that are small (900-1000KB)
when i check how much byte it read
it shows ReadBufferFromS3Bytes = sum of size of all files
but if i merge 2 files together and size is about 1.8MB
```
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(gcs_login, filename = 'clickhouse/test_merged.parquet') SELECT *
FROM s3(gcs_login, filename = 'clickhouse/account_id=..../dataset_name=..../group_id=..../device_id=..../time_cadence=..../time=..../{0,1}.parquet', format = 'Parquet')
```
and try again, it only fech 64KB which i think it's the metadata


```
SELECT
    query,
    formatReadableSize(ProfileEvents['ReadBufferFromS3Bytes']) AS bytes
FROM system.query_log
WHERE (event_date = today()) AND (query_id IN ('85c68382-d77f-4f23-929b-27752199a873', '209b6fd3-7dd8-432b-9c91-d7adbb9efd6d')) AND (type = 'QueryFinish')
ORDER BY event_time DESC;

Query id: 6f912e2d-ded3-4a29-ba2f-004bff20ff47

   ┌─query──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─bytes─────┐
1. │ select count(*) from s3(gcs_login,filename='clickhouse/test_merged.parquet', format='Parquet');                                                                                        │ 64.00 KiB │
2. │ select count(*) from s3(gcs_login,filename='clickhouse/account_id=..../dataset_name=..../group_id=..../device_id=..../time_cadence=..../time=..../*', format='Parquet'); │ 66.17 MiB │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘

2 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.005 sec.
```

is there any threshold that decide to fetch the whole file or just the metadata? can i force clickhouse to only read the metadata? we need to run qa validation script on few TB data to monitor the count and most of them are small files (<1.5MB) so it only make sense if we can just fetch the metadata.

Thanks

title: clean up all the Replicated*MergeTree table information for a node in ZooKeeper
body:
### Question

Is there a way to clean up all the Replicated*MergeTree table information for a node in ZooKeeper?
I have used SYSTEM DROP REPLICA, but it didn't work. I also tried SYSTEM DROP REPLICA FROM ZKPATH, which was effective, but it only allows me to delete the replica information for a single table at a time.
author: honobi

comments.body:
`SYSTEM DROP REPLICA` should drop the replica along with all the Keeper info related to it.
Can you tell me why you think the nodes are not being cleaned after `DROP REPLICA` was called?
Each replicated table will create a single Keeper node which will act as a root table node. Under it (as a child of `replicas` node), all replicas will create their nodes. And those nodes are deleted when the replica is dropped.

title: Window View not working
body:
### Company or project name

IOT Engine Analytics

### Question

I have a table tbltrackerlagdata where data will be inserted once every day. When i creating window views on this table i was not getting any results, but while running insert query for window view it was working fine. I have 3 use cases with this table tbltrackerlagdata , where i need to use window views at two cases. I tried checking logs but didn't get any error logs. Please help.

create table tbltrackerlagdata(deviceid String, uniqueid Int32,   ignitionstatus Int8, speed Int32, tenantgroupname String, devicetypename String, parsername String,     latitude Float32,    longitude Float32,  devicedatetime DateTime, insertdatetime DateTime, vehicleid String,  lagignition Int8, laglatitude Float32, laglongitude Float32, lagspeed Int32) Engine = MergeTree()PRIMARY KEY (insertdatetime) TTL insertdatetime + INTERVAL 2 DAY

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW viewtrackerlagdata REFRESH EVERY 1 DAY TO tbltrackerlagdata  as select deviceid, uniqueid,   ignitionstatus, speed, tenantgroupname, devicetypename, parsername,     latitude,    longitude,  devicedatetime, insertdatetime, vehicleid, lagInFrame (ignitionstatus) over win as  lagignition, lagInFrame(latitude) over win as laglatitude, lagInFrame (longitude) over win as laglongitude, lagInFrame(speed) over win as lagspeed from tbltrackerdata WHERE recordstatus = 1 AND devicetypename != '' AND insertdatetime >= toDateTime(toStartOfDay(now() - interval 1 day)) AND insertdatetime < toDateTime(toStartOfDay(now())) AND devicedatetime < insertdatetime + INTERVAL 1 MINUTE  window win as (partition by deviceid order by devicedatetime)


CREATE TABLE tblignitionstatetransitions ( deviceid String, tenantgroupname String, devicetypename String, parsername String, windowstart DateTime, windowend DateTime, transitions Int32) Engine = MergeTree() PRIMARY KEY (deviceid, windowstart)
CREATE WINDOW VIEW viewignitionstatetransitions to tblignitionstatetransitions select deviceid, any(E.tenantgroupname) as tenantgroupname, any(E.devicetypename) as devicetypename, any(E.parsername) as parsername, tumbleStart(windowid) AS windowstart, tumbleEnd(windowid) AS windowend, countIf(ignitionstatus , ignitionstatus != lagignition) as transitions FROM tbltrackerlagdata  E GROUP BY tumble(insertdatetime, toIntervalDay('1')) AS windowid, deviceid

comments.body: It's expected behaviour. Refreshable materialized views don't do insertion. They insert into temporary invisible tables and swap tables in the end. WINDOW VIEWs don't not track the insertion into temporary invisible tables.

> Why i was using the refreshable materialized view instead of normal materialized view is because of the fact that materialized views can't read from the source table. So for achieving the lag i used the refreshable materialized views.

OK.

> So is there any alternative other than create an refreshable view upon the table created after the refreshable view.

Sorry, why do you need the alternative? You created a refreshable materialized view and ... ? Why do you need something else?

What i mean is, after creating the refreshable table which insert(shifts) data to a table x. i need to do queries on  table x as it updates the data and saves it in a table Y for the analytical purpose.
create one more refreshable materialized view which reads `x` and saves to `y`

title: Why sorting order affects `OSReadChars` significantly
body:
Sorting order affects query duration and `OSReadChars` significantly, this is a minimal reproducible example.
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE test(ts UInt64, uuid UUID)
Engine=MergeTree
ORDER BY ts;

-- Enough data to see difference for queries below.
INSERT INTO test SELECT * FROM generateRandom('ts UInt64,uuid UUID') LIMIT 50000000;

-- Here the read data amount differs significantly
SELECT uuid FROM test ORDER BY ts DESC FORMAT Null;
SELECT uuid FROM test ORDER BY ts ASC FORMAT Null;

SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS;

SELECT
    initial_query_id,query_start_time,query_duration_ms,
    ProfileEvents['OSReadChars'] AS os_read_chars_including_cache,read_rows,read_bytes,query
FROM system.query_log
WHERE is_initial_query AND (type != 'QueryStart') AND event_time>now()-toIntervalMinute(5)
    AND query LIKE 'SELECT uuid FROM test ORDER BY ts %'

┌─query_duration_ms─┬─os_read_chars_including_cache─┬─read_rows─┬─read_bytes─┐
│              6409 │                    2038859527 │  50000000 │ 1200000000 │
│              2386 │                    1210128941 │  50000000 │ 1200000000 │
└───────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────┘
```
But `read_rows` and `read_bytes` are exactly same for the two queries. I'm confused, can some one explain a bit for me, thks!
author: cangyin

comments.body: In both cases, the "read in order" algorithm is used, while the DESC case is a bit more complex than the ASC case. The difference in OSReadChars (the number of bytes read from the Linux's filesystem including the page cache) can be explained if it reads and discards some extra bytes.

title: When the clickhouse distributed table query, why only read very little data from the node，How did this do？
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

After testing, I found that when the distributed table query data of Clickhouse is not simply, it is not simply to gather all data from other nodes to nodes that initiate requests.

In fact, there are very few data read from other nodes，But I did not find related articles to explain its principle or algorithm.

Do you have related articles or blogs?
author: ChaoHsupin

comments.body:
Explanation from chatgpt, it's close to the reality):

-----

In ClickHouse, distributed tables are used to handle data that is spread across multiple servers (shards). The system allows for efficient querying and processing by distributing the workload across these shards and then combining the results. Here's a breakdown of how this works, especially concerning aggregate functions:

### 1. **Distributed Table Structure**
   - A **distributed table** is a virtual table that does not store data itself. Instead, it references physical tables (often replicated tables) on multiple shards.
   - When a query is executed against a distributed table, ClickHouse automatically distributes the query to the underlying shards, which contain the actual data.

### 2. **Aggregate Function States**
   - Aggregate functions in ClickHouse can operate in multiple stages: **state calculation** and **finalization**.
   - **State Calculation:** When an aggregate function is applied, it calculates an intermediate state (e.g., sum, average, count) rather than the final result. This intermediate state can be merged with other states later.
   - **Finalization:** The final result is obtained by finalizing the merged states (e.g., computing the average from the sum and count).

### 3. **Pre-calculation on Shards**
   - When a query involves an aggregation, each shard independently calculates the **aggregate function states** for its portion of the data.
   - This distributed pre-calculation reduces the amount of data that needs to be transferred across the network, as only the intermediate states (instead of raw data) need to be sent to the initiator node.

### 4. **Finalization at the Initiator**
   - The initiator node is the server that initially receives the query.
   - After receiving the pre-calculated aggregate states from all shards, the initiator node **merges** these states.
   - The initiator then **finalizes** the aggregate function by computing the final result from the merged states (e.g., summing counts and computing the final average).

### 5. **Example Workflow**
   1. A query requesting an aggregate, like `SELECT AVG(value) FROM distributed_table`, is issued.
   2. The query is distributed to all shards.
   3. Each shard calculates the **sum** and **count** for `value` and returns these states to the initiator.
   4. The initiator merges the sums and counts from all shards.
   5. The initiator finalizes the `AVG` by dividing the merged sum by the merged count.

### 6. **Benefits**
   - **Efficiency:** By performing most of the heavy lifting on the shards and only sending essential data back to the initiator, ClickHouse minimizes network overhead and speeds up query processing.
   - **Scalability:** This approach allows ClickHouse to scale horizontally, effectively handling large datasets spread across multiple nodes.

This distributed approach is particularly powerful for large-scale data processing, making ClickHouse a strong choice for analytics on massive datasets.

title: Best Method to Delete Data from ReplicatedMergeTree Tables in a Cluster
body:
My cluster has 12 nodes: 6 primary and 6 replicas. Each node’s size exceeds 80%, and the total data size is 8 petabytes. There are 3 tables from which I want to delete the first 6 months of data. The table engine is ReplicatedMergeTree. Should I use ALTER TABLE and add a TTL clause to delete only the first 6 months, or should I use the DELETE clause?
Version:23.8.1.2992
author: aol-59

comments.body:
Preferably "alter table drop partition" or properly configured TTL (aligned with partition expression or with ttl_only_drop_parts) -- very light process, just removes files, without reading/writing.

`alter table delete` -- less preferable, processes rows (can read and write your petabytes)
`delete from ....` -- least preferable (it does not remove data, just marks rows as deleted using tombstones.

>Version:23.8.1.2992

You should upgrade, there is: 23.8.16.40.

error message:

author: 12frame

comments.body:
Hey @12frame, it seems there is a bug when creating a table using named collections. When I try to create the table with `on_duplicate_clause=1`, clickhouse raises an error.

```
CREATE TABLE test_mysql3 (
    id Int32,
    name String
) ENGINE = MySQL('localhost:3306', 'test', 'test', 'root', '', 0, 1);

Received exception:
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Argument 'on_duplicate_clause' must be a literal with type String, got UInt64. (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
 ```

But indeed, if I do the same thing with named collections, no errors are raised.
 
The docs are not clear IMHO, but you need to define it as `on_duplicate_clause=UPDATE source_app_name = source_app_name`. And then, not pass anything when doing the insert: `insert into ... values ...;`

BTW, your duplicate syntax didn't work as expected for me. You might need to look into MySQL correct syntax to update with the new value. It worked with a fixed string though: `on_duplicate_clause = 'UPDATE name=\'duplicate\''`.

Thank you very much. You can now work normally
The description in the document is indeed very vague, and there are no relevant cases to describe it. I hope you can supplement and explain it to him. Thank you

Clickhouse version : 23.12.4.15
author: GandiYaswanthSai

comments.body: Found the root cause. I am not using ON CLUSTER xxxxxx in my query. Thank you.

BTW you can store users in ZK, then all servers in the cluster will be in sync. And you don't need to use on_cluster.


```
    <user_directories replace="replace">
        <users_xml>
            <path>/etc/clickhouse-server/users.xml</path>
        </users_xml>
        <replicated>
            <zookeeper_path>clickhouse/mycluster/access/</zookeeper_path>
        </replicated>
    </user_directories>
```

### Question


What is the Synchronous insert behavior when Zookeeper error? 


1 Asynchronously Insert the data(replicated merge tree)

author: kazhou2024

comments.body:
It's normal behaviour. 

Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to remove a part inserted with an error. While this time "failed" data is available for selects.

```
14:25:36  960f5f93-e440-4459-9a1d-6b7c69a6b50a   Renaming temporary part tmp_insert_88709600-202312_3309680_3309680_0 to 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0
14:25:36  960f5f93-e440-4459-9a1d-6b7c69a6b50a   Session expired, path: XID overflow


14:25:38 Part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 in zookeeper: false, locally: true
14:25:38 Young part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 with age 2 seconds hasn't been added to ZooKeeper yet. It's ok.


14:34:50 There is no part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 in ZooKeeper, it was only in filesystem
14:34:50 Removing 8 parts from filesystem (serially): Parts: [..., 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 ...]
```

> It's normal behaviour.
> 
> Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to remove a part inserted with an error. While this time "failed" data is available for selects.
> 
> ```
> 14:25:36  960f5f93-e440-4459-9a1d-6b7c69a6b50a   Renaming temporary part tmp_insert_88709600-202312_3309680_3309680_0 to 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0
> 14:25:36  960f5f93-e440-4459-9a1d-6b7c69a6b50a   Session expired, path: XID overflow
> 
> 
> 14:25:38 Part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 in zookeeper: false, locally: true
> 14:25:38 Young part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 with age 2 seconds hasn't been added to ZooKeeper yet. It's ok.
> 
> 
> 14:34:50 There is no part 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 in ZooKeeper, it was only in filesystem
> 14:34:50 Removing 8 parts from filesystem (serially): Parts: [..., 88709600-202312_37300_37300_0 ...]
> ```

Thanks Den, 
  So currently our insert logic is like 1. check exsiting , 2 insert. And we have loop retry logic to handle failure. But based on this behaviour, seems out insert logic is not correct. So any suggestion to turning our insert logic?

> So any suggestion to turning our insert logic?

2 recommendations:
* Upgrade to a more recent version for 2 reasons: 1) It will be supported and 2) It has retries when there are issues with keeper so it recovers seamlessly when it goes down (settings `insert_keeper_max_retries`, `insert_keeper_retry_initial_backoff_ms`...). This way you'll have less errors.
* Use deduplication so you can retry immediately, without needing to check if the data exists. If you insert the same block (exactly the same) twice, the second one will be deduplicated (not inserted) if the one succeed. See `insert_deduplicate` or `insert_deduplication_token`.

>Upgrade to a more recent version for 2 reasons:

My log is from pretty recent version 24... something.

>Use deduplication so you can retry immediately, without needing to check if the data exists. If you insert the same block (exactly the same) twice, the second one will be deduplicated (not inserted) if the one succeed.

Not like that. Data will be doubled for a period of time. Deduplication won't work because no information in ZK about this block. 
And it's even worse if deduplication will work. Because eventually this part will be detached and you will lost data the same way as of topic-starter.

>So any suggestion to turning our insert logic?

I have no suggestions. I have the same problem, I also check that data is inserted using select and I don't do re-tries on errors if data exists.
I just have a mechanism to check consistency for the last two days, and that's why I know that data is lost.
Probably re-tries on error and a temporary data duplication is a better solution.

> My log is from pretty recent version 24... something.

Sorry, I was replying to the original poster. You should probably tweak the retries to see why `960f5f93-e440-4459-9a1d-6b7c69a6b50a` did not recover from the ZK "failure".

> And it's even worse if deduplication will work. Because eventually this part will be detached and you will lost data the same way as of topic-starter.

This should not possible (with the current RMT code). The part will be detached only when we confirm that the data is not in keeper. If the data is not in keeper, neither should be the deduplication token, so deduplication will not happen.

title: Why is it that when the HTTP client disconnects, only the "readonly" queries are canceled.
labels: close in a month if not active
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

Only cancel queries that have "readonly"\"cancel_http_readonly_queries_on_client_close" set. Why can't we cancel all types of queries?
author: luffyhwl

comments.body:
INSERT queries are being canceled automatically if connection closed. Server will try to connect to the client to fetch new portion of data, and if it fails to do so, the query will be cancelled. 

DDL queries are either cheap and executed immediately or run and wait for asynchronous operations (mutations, queries in DDL queue and similar). Cancelling the query itself doesn't make sense because it almost doesn't consume any resources, but this feature was implemented mostly to avoid wasting resources uselessly. Cancelling asynchronous operations is not easy and may be dangerous, there are other mechanisms to cancel some of them (e.g. `KILL MUTATION` query).

title: How to handle delays in replication of data to be joined in Materialized Views?
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

I have a Materialized View that joins with tables replicated from PostgreSQL:

(database with replicated tables)
```
CREATE DATABASE postgres_tables
ENGINE = MaterializedPostgreSQL('DB_HOST:DB_PORT', 'DB_NAME', 'DB_USER', 'DB_PASS')
SETTINGS materialized_postgresql_tables_list = 'note_time_logs,notes'
```

(materialized view)
```
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW my_db.note_time_logs__mv
TO my_db.time_logs
AS SELECT
  ntl.person_id as person_id,
  toDate(ntl.created_at) as date,
  n.tag as tag,
  ntl.service_id as service_id,
  sum(CAST(CEIL(COALESCE(ntl.duration, 0)), 'UInt16')) as total_minutes
FROM postgres_tables.note_time_logs ntl
LEFT JOIN postgres_tables.notes n ON n.id  = ntl.note_id
GROUP BY person_id, date, service_id, tag
```

The records generated by the MV are missing values from the joined table (`tag`, in this case). It looks like the data of that table is taking a bit longer to be replicated and, when the MV does the JOIN, the data is not there yet.

Is there a way to handle this case?
author: rjmAmaro

>  (tag, in this case)

Replication in MateriailzedPostgreSQL is done by rows, so you cannot miss one column, but have another column. Is it the case you have you mean?

title: Clickhouse Server data is deleted when Kubernetes Cluster is restarted
body:
I am creating a Clickhouse DB setup in Kubernetes cluster on Azure AKS.

**Describe the unexpected behaviour**
When the AKS cluster is restarted, all the data in the DB is wiped out. It is always refreshing the DB.

**How to reproduce**
* Use the latest Clickhouse Docker image
* Create a default Helm Chart and deploy it into the cluster using Helm install command
* Insert some data in the DB
* Stop the AKS cluster and start again
* Connect to the DB to retrieve the data.

**Expected behavior**
The data should remain in the persistant volume of the Kubernetes Statefulset

**Error message and/or stacktrace**
There is no error message, the data is getting wiped off.

title: Temporary stopping automatic dictionary updates
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Question

When a dictionary is based on a clickhouse table with a lifetime, what should be done when updating the source table (truncate table source_table; insert into source_table...) to prevent clickhouse from updating the dictionary with partial or no data?
author: bjne

comments.body:
As far as I know, there is no way to stop a dictionary reload.

Maybe you could avoid having partial data in the source table. For example, instead of truncating + insert, you could create a temporal table with the same schema, insert into that table, then EXCHANGE it with the old one and drop the temporal table (that now has the old data). Would that help in your situation?

> what should be done

Awful hack, but you can add WHERE throwIf((SELECT * FROM status FINAL) = 'Updating' ) in dictionary source definition

So, you will have additional status table, which you can use as lock for your dictionary updates. (to explicitly trigger exception which prevent reload of dictionary)

But, it's not better than doing EXCHANGE TABLES and staging tables
Thanks to the both of you. I think I will go for the table exchange, but I like your style, @UnamedRus :laughing:

title: Questions about the difference between the DELETE statement and TTL?
body:
After reading docs about TTL and lightweight DELETE, There are some questions about their performance diff。

In my occasaion,the following is the create statement
```sql
CREATE TABLE my_table
(
    id UInt32,
    timestamp Int64
    ORDER BY (`timestamp`, `id`) 
) 
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toStartOfWeek(toDateTime(`timestamp` / 1000))
ORDER BY (timestamp, id)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;
```
Q1:
Insteading of adding TTL for the `timestamp` column, If the statement "DELETE FROM my_table where timestamp < now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY“ is execed periodically, would performance be significantly worse?

Q2:
As the above statements, timestamp is the partitioning key. If there are multi partitions, could I assume that based on the timestamp in the where condition the clickhouse can quickly determine which partitions will not be hit, so that the delete statement will have no effect on those partitions?
author: Maplestory1998

comments.body:
TTL can drop whole partitions if a partitioning expression is aligned with a TTL expression or if ttl_only_drop_parts is set.

A1: with LWD your data may never be removed at all. Because Clickhouse does not force the real deletion of rows marked as deleted by LWD. It deletes data during the usual merges which may never happen for the old parts.

A2: LWD mutates all parts (recreates parts using hardlinks), but it reads (and writes is_deleted=1 column) only parts which match a condition and it uses a minmax index derived from a partition expression. A mutation of all parts is mandatory by the other reasons.

I would use TTL and I would align a TTL expression with a PartitionBy expression and adjust PartitionBy if possible.

Check replication status in all replicas and check what nodes are being created / maintained to investigate your specific circumstances.

title: Does ClickHouse support local node execution switching?
body: Does ClickHouse support local node execution switching  on distributed query execution? This would prevent a slow query on one node from slowing down the entire query, just like `use_hedged_requests`
author: 0xfei

comments.body: No. ClickHouse can't change the number of nodes dynamically during query execution. It is either fully local of fully distributed with the number of nodes based on the statically defined cluster topology.

author: taotaizhu-pw

comments.body:
The recommended Keeper setup is 3 nodes.
Note that 4 or any other even number of nodes doesn't make much sense because Keeper implements consensus protocol where it needs confirmation from more than half of nodes. For 3 nodes the quorum is 2, for 4 nodes the quorum is 3 and for 5 nodes the quorum is also 3.

How to implement a dual-center deployment for ClickHouse? There are two geographically separated database centers, A and B, each consisting of 3 ClickHouse servers. Center A serves as the primary center, and Center B acts as the backup, forming a primary-backup dual-center system. All tables use the replicated engine. Given that a certain degree of latency is acceptable for Center B, how can data synchronization between Center A and Center B be achieved?

Any suggestion about it? Thanks!

title: "Data Synchronization Issue and Query Management When a Read-Only Replica Exists in a Shard"
body:
Hello,

I encountered a situation while using ClickHouse where a replica within a shard is in read-only mode. In this case, I can write data to another node through a local table as usual. However, it seems that the read-only replica is not receiving any data leading to a failure in synchronizing.

What's more troubling is when querying a distributed table, it randomly queries these two replicas, one of which is in a read-only state. This could lead to inconsistent query results which is not expected.

Additionally, even though I can promptly eliminate the faulty nodes, there's inevitably a delay between the time the nodes become unserviceable and my response to it. My key concern is how to prevent queries from being directed to nodes that hold incomplete data during this interim period.

Ideally, there should be a mechanism to detect a node failure or changes to read-only state, and instantly exclude it from the pool of queryable nodes until it's fully back in sync with other replicas within the same shard. This could help to ensure data integrity and consistency for all queries.

Steps to reproduce:

Set a replica in a shard to read-only.
Write data to another node in the shard.
Attempt to query the distributed table while the problematic node still exists.
Expected Result:

The query to the distributed tables should not include the read-only replica, or there should be some fail-safe mechanism to uphold the consistency of the results.

Actual Result:

Data is not synchronized to the read-only replica, and during the query, it considers the not-yet-synchronized read-only replica, leading to inconsistent results.

I would greatly appreciate your advice and any guidance on mitigating this issue. Many thanks in advance for your help!
author: huoarter

comments.body: @huoarter - I have forwarded your question on to our Core team.

@tavplubix Helped me to answer your question.
> I encountered a situation while using ClickHouse where a replica within a shard is in read-only mode. In this case, I can write data to another node through a local table as usual. However, it seems that the read-only replica is not receiving any data leading to a failure in synchronizing.

Isn't it expected that readonly replica doesn't get new data?

> Set a replica in a shard to read-only.

How do you switch it to readonly mode? There's no way to do it without breaking something (like removing some metadata from ZooKeeper, or disconnecting the replica from ZooKeeper)

> The query to the distributed tables should not include the read-only replica

This is questionable. The replica is not unavailable, it's readonly, so why not to read from it? We only guarantee eventual consistency anyway.

Yes, you might be right, ClickHouse guarantees eventual consistency. For instance, if a disk on a node becomes read-only at a certain moment, during this time one replica of the shard is writable while the other is not, and there might be differences in data during the fault period. Is there any method that can make the distributed table aware that one of the replicas in this shard has incomplete data, so that when querying through the distributed table, the faulty replica is not accessed? I know that if writing through the distributed table, when one replica fails to write data, an error_count is automatically inserted into the system.replication_queue, and the distributed table will choose the replica with the lower error_count for queries. But what if writing occurs through a local table, is there a way to avoid querying the bad replica in this case?

# 2. Manually create /var/lib/clickhouse/data/default/file_engine_table/data.CSVWithNames containing:

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.008 sec.
```

But with `Native` I don't know if it's ok to just touch the file ( 0 bytes ).
author: mirusky

comments.body:
Yes, an empty `Native` file is a valid representation of an empty dataset of any structure.

Example:
```
$ touch test.native
$ clickhouse-local --query "SELECT * FROM file('test.native', Native, 'x String')"
$ clickhouse-local --query "SELECT * FROM file('test.native', Native, 'x String, y Array(UInt64)')"
```

However an empty file does not contain the structure, so it has to be specified manually:

title: Port is not opened on keepers only using composable protocols
body:
**Description**
When using the composable protocols configuration for serving prometheus metrics with tls, clickhouse server with only keeper configuration does not open specified port.

**How to reproduce**
* Clickhouse version 23.3.19.32

To reproduce the issue two nodes should be deployed, one as "data" node and the other one as a keeper.
Example config:
```xml
<remote_servers>
<example>
  <shard>
    <internal_replication>true</internal_replication>
    <replica>
      <host>data-node.example.com</host>
      <port>9000</port>
      <secure>true</secure>
    </replica>
  </shard>
</example>
</remote_servers>

<keeper_server>
  <server_id>1</server_id>
  <tcp_port_secure>2181</tcp_port_secure>
  <raft_configuration>
      <secure>true</secure>

      <server>
          <id>1</id>
          <hostname>keeper-node.example.com</hostname>
          <port>2182</port>
      </server>
  </raft_configuration>
</keeper_server>


```

In both configs I do specify prometheus metrics endpoint using composable protocols following explanation given in this issue #49003:
```xml
<prometheus>
  <endpoint>/metrics</endpoint>
  <metrics>true</metrics>
  <events>true</events>
  <asynchronous_metrics>true</asynchronous_metrics>
</prometheus>

<protocols>
  <prometheus_protocol>
      <type>prometheus</type>
      <description>prometheus protocol</description>
  </prometheus_protocol>

  <prometheus_secure>
      <type>tls</type>
      <impl>prometheus_protocol</impl>
      <port>9999</port>
      <description>prometheus over tls</description>
  </prometheus_secure>
</protocols>

```


**Expected behavior**
Port 9999 is opened on both "data" node and keeper node and is under TLS.

**Actual behavior**
Port 9999 is only opened on the "data" and not the keeper node.

**Logs**
There were no messages in log with a mention of this prometheus configuration, checked it on trace level.
author: ilyatrefilov

comments.body: Keeper currently doesn't support composable protocols so the "old" way should be used of specifying `<port>` under `<prometheus>`.

@ilyatrefilov I can't promise you anything specific but I think it should be done in the near future along with some small changes to Keeper prometheus metrics (send only Keeper specific data).

I'll close this issue for now and ping you when there is update for it.

title: HTTP chunked transfer encoding semantics
body:
Does Clickhouse support chunked transfer encoding for inserts with the HTTP interface?

Documentation doesn't give a clear answer.

To implement batching on the client side, Clickhouse should collect all chunks from one HTTP session and insert them as one part, but only if the client acknowledges the transfer correctly by sending a zero-size chunk.

(Unfinished transfer sessions should be ignored and not inserted.)

Can you confirm that this works as expected?
author: ivan-tkatchev

comments.body:
> Does Clickhouse support chunked transfer encoding for inserts with the HTTP interface?

Yes.

> To implement batching on the client side, Clickhouse should collect all chunks from one HTTP session and insert them as one part, but only if the client acknowledges the transfer correctly by sending a zero-size chunk.

ClickHouse server will parse and accumulate the data up to `max_insert_block_size` rows and do the insertion of every batch in an atomic way. If the amount of data is less than the `max_insert_block_size` it will be a single atomic insertion after the stream of data is consumed.

title: OPTIMIZE ... DEDUPLICATE does not work?
body:
The command

```
OPTIMIZE TABLE data_slim FINAL DEDUPLICATE SETTINGS optimize_throw_if_noop = 1
```

raises an exception:

```
Code: 388. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot select parts for optimization: Part all_81574178_82904081_154_82864826 has already been assigned a merge into all_81574178_82931927_155_82864826 (in partition all). (CANNOT_ASSIGN_OPTIMIZE)
```

Which I interpret as that deduplication is impossible, because the table is currently merging. (And since the table is always merging, deduplication is thus never possible.)

I would expect that deduplication work like any other mutation. Am I wrong in my assumptions?
author: ivan-tkatchev

comments.body:
`DEDUPLICATION FINAL` works by merging and removing rows with the same values on all columns. 

You can monitor ongoing merge using the `system.merges` table
I understand the mechanism. Problem is that the merges for deduplication never start, because replication queue is always full with regular replicated table merges.

You can stop insertion. Wait while merges are finished, then run optimize. I understand that is ridicule workaround, but the problem is that  `OPTIMIZE TABLE` is a special admin command, which cannot be used on a daily bases and it requires. special admin actions

title: Metadata Loading Issue on ClickHouse Cluster Restart
body:
We rely on the ClickHouse Altinity operator deployed on Kubernetes to manage our ClickHouse infrastructure. Our current ClickHouse setup comprises three shards with a single replica, housing various databases such as default, olap, olap_local, staging, and staging_local. The primary database is named olap.

Our typical approach to table creation involves first establishing a simple MergeTree table on local databases and subsequently creating a distributed table on another database. To illustrate, when creating a table like users, we execute the following commands:

```sql
CREATE TABLE olap_local.users ON CLUSTER 'cluster' (id Int32) ENGINE MergeTree;
CREATE TABLE olap.users ON CLUSTER 'cluster' AS olap_local.users ENGINE Distributed('cluster', 'olap_local', 'users');
```

However, upon cluster restarts, we encounter issues during the loading metadata phase. It's important to note that our ClickHouse cluster houses approximately 200 GB of data on each shard.

I initially suspected was related to ClickHouse's inability to load dependencies on the OLAP database. However, when attempting to reproduce the bug in the staging cluster, I observed successful dependency loading.

Now, my hypothesis is leaning towards the size of the database potentially causing the problem.

I'm reaching out to the community for insights, experiences, or solutions related to this issue.

Thank you for your time and support.

title: Issue with Thread Safety during Multiple DELETE mutations
body:
I may have encountered a potential thread safety problem related to multiple DELETE mutations in ClickHouse.

```sql
-- Thread 1
ALTER TABLE test_table DELETE WHERE id = 1 AND toYYYYMM(timestamp) BETWEEN 202309 AND 202310;

-- Thread 2
ALTER TABLE test_table DELETE WHERE id = 2 AND toYYYYMM(timestamp) BETWEEN 202309 AND 202310;

I know that ClickHouse already has a lightweight deletion feature, but we haven't upgraded to the new version of ClickHouse yet. I would like to know if there are any thread safety issues associated with using lightweight deletion.

title: [Query Performance]Performance Discrepancy in CK Queries with Different Field Selections
body:
Hello ClickHouse Community,

I'm currently experiencing a performance discrepancy in two similar ClickHouse queries, where the only difference is the number of selected fields. The first query with fewer fields executes significantly faster than the second query with all fields selected. 

The table is structured with PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(toDate(timestamp)) and ORDER BY timestamp:

version 23.2.4.10

Surprisingly, the first query scans 2.93 million rows, while the second query scans 5.79 million rows. I expected the number of scanned rows to be the same, given that the WHERE clause is identical, and only the selected fields differ.

Can anyone in the community shed light on why the number of scanned rows would differ between these two queries

Query 1:

```
SELECT timestamp AS timestamp, uuId AS uuId
FROM `business`.`log`
WHERE `ip` LIKE '10.11.%'
  AND (`timestamp` >= 1698940799)
  AND (`timestamp` <= 1699405199)
ORDER BY `timestamp` DESC
LIMIT 20;
--20 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.113 sec. Processed 2.93 million rows, 180.15 MB (25.99 million rows/s., 1.60 GB/s.)
```

Query 2:
```
SELECT *
FROM `business`.`log`
WHERE `ip` LIKE '10.11.%'
  AND (`timestamp` >= 1698940799)
  AND (`timestamp` <= 1699405199)
ORDER BY `timestamp` DESC
LIMIT 20;
--20 rows in set. Elapsed: 3.957 sec. Processed 5.79 million rows, 1.55 GB (1.46 million rows/s., 391.84 MB/s.)
```
author: Ronniexie

comments.body:
Additional Information:

Effect of Time Range on Query Performance:

> Query 1 only takes effect when the time range is greater than 7 days; for time ranges less than or equal to 7 days, it scans the same data as Query 2.

Impact of Query Method on Scanned Data:

> The performance difference occurs only when using a LIKE condition in the query. For other conditions (e.g., '=', etc.), the data scanned is essentially the same.

>version 23.2.4.10 

This version is out support. Also multistage prewhere was implemented later, it might help you. You should upgrade to 23.8.16 or 23.10.2.


This is expected behaviour. 
By many reasons:
* `*` need to read / uncompress more data
* Clickhouse reads all columns for all rows even though need to read them for only 20 rows (LIMIT 20)
* PREWERE seems does not hit with LIKE in your case.

Try 

```
SELECT *
FROM `business`.`log`
PREWHERE 

  `ip` LIKE '10.11.%'
  AND (`timestamp` >= 1698940799)
  AND (`timestamp` <= 1699405199)
ORDER BY `timestamp` DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

```
SELECT *
FROM `business`.`log`
PREWHERE `ip` LIKE '10.11.%'
  AND (`timestamp` >= 1698940799)
  AND (`timestamp` <= 1699405199)
  and (timestamp , uuId) in (
      SELECT timestamp AS timestamp, uuId AS uuId
      FROM `business`.`log`
      WHERE `ip` LIKE '10.11.%'
        AND (`timestamp` >= 1698940799)
        AND (`timestamp` <= 1699405199)
      ORDER BY `timestamp` DESC
      LIMIT 20)
ORDER BY `timestamp` DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

> So what exactly does concurrently mean? Does it refer to queries within the same second or the same millisecond?

body:

Even if i run SYSTEM FLUSH DISTRIBUTED ON CLUSTER cluster default.table, i get the same error.

Inserts on local node work ok. It also works ok with insert_distributed_sync=1. But as i would prefer to use async, i would like to go back to background inserts.

Memory limits are the same on all nodes:
```
┌─name─────────────────────────────┬─default─┬─value─┐
│ max_memory_usage                 │ 0       │ 0     │
│ max_memory_usage_for_user        │ 0       │ 0     │
│ max_memory_usage_for_all_queries │ 0       │ 0     │
└──────────────────────────────────┴─────────┴───────┘
```

system.distribution_queue has 2 entries(1 for each node it is trying to insert to). 
data_compressed_bytes: 9692170902

Each shard has a queue of around 13k files, ~10G in size. Even if i leave just 1 file in the queue, it still throws memory exceeded.
If i remove the first file, i get file not found exception.

How do i tell clickhouse to not use 10G memory limit?
author: Nikoslav

comments.body:
It's because `.bin` file stores settings which were applied during the initial insertion and the distributed table applies them during propagation of data into *MergeTree.

Here is an example

```
create table T ( A Int64 ) Engine MergeTree partition by A order by A;

create table TD as T Engine Distributed (default, currentDatabase(), T);

set prefer_localhost_replica = 0;
set max_partitions_per_insert_block = 1;

insert into TD select * from numbers(100);

select substr(last_exception,1, 150) from system.distribution_queue format Vertical;
Code: 252. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Too many partitions for single INSERT block (more than 1).
```

Now TD is unable to re-insert `1.bin` and it's impossible to change `1.bin` to redefine `max_partitions_per_insert_block`. 

you can:

* recreate table TD (drop/create and lost all not inserted data, all .bin files)
* detach table, move bin files to user_files and try to read them

```
:) detach table TD;

# cd /var/lib/clickhouse/data/default/TD/shard1_replica1/

# mv *.bin /var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/

:) attach table TD;

-- data is accessible using `Distributed` format
:) select * from file('*.bin', Distributed) limit 3
┌─A─┐
│ 0 │
│ 1 │
│ 2 │
└───┘

:) select count() from file('*.bin', Distributed);
┌─count()─┐
│     100 │
└─────────┘

:) insert into T select * from file('*.bin', Distributed);

:) select count() from T;
┌─count()─┐
│     100 │
└─────────┘

# rm /var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/*.bin
```
Thanks a lot! Detach, move files, attach and insert worked perfectly.

title: `arrayElement` function in clickhouse: What is the run-time complexity?
body:
We use `arrayElement(<array>, index)` function to pick an item at a specific index from within the array in clickhouse. We were curious about whats the run-time complexity of this function? Is it a constant time operation (i.e O(1) ) or a linear one (i.e. O(n))? 

Let's say, I want to pick the last element in the array, with array length being 100. If I do `arrayElement(<array>, 100)` , will it first scan the 99 ones before returning the 100th element?
author: saifamp

comments.body:
It will do a lookup in constant time, and then create a new column in memory that requires walking through the contents of the original column in memory, which takes linear time.

TLDR: Linear time.

title: Some questions about parallel  read replicas， How to ensure correctness In the following scenarios？
body:
1、How to ensure correctness if one replica has merged parts and the other has not?
     For example： replica1  parts：1-1-0    2-2-0
     replica2 parts：1-2-1

2、How to ensure correctness if one replica has new parts and the other no time to synchronize?
     For example： replica1  parts：1-1-0    2-2-0   3-3-0
     replica2 parts：1-1-0    2-2-0
author: Sallery-X

comments.body:
> How to ensure correctness if one replica has merged parts and the other has not?

There is a step during query announcement where each replica replies with the list of parts available, then the coordinator decides what's going to be read (preferring sets with higher number of replicas owning them IIRC) and assigns the work to the replicas that have those parts.

> > How to ensure correctness if one replica has new parts and the other no time to synchronize?

Same as above, the work of reading those parts will go to the replicas that have those parts only.

comments.body:

title: Replica connections health check
body:
We have two replicas for a shard and using `in_order` as load balancing. However, very often we see a secondary query goes to 2nd replica instead of the first one.

I did some investigate and this is what's I observe:  sometimes, establishing connection to first replica fails with `Broken pipe`, the first replica will be marked as error for 60s, during that time, some secondary queries will go to 2nd replica. For more context, we're using hedged request and w/o parallel replicas. I tried to look at hedge request and connection establisher logic but it's quite hard to understand.

My questions:
1. Does replica connections fail with `Broken pipe` indicates a bug in connection establisher, or it indeed relates to network?
2. If it's indeed a network issue, how can we reduce the network rate from CH side?

On the other hand, I think we should have a column `last_error_message` in `system.clusters`

Thanks.
cc @den-crane @Algunenano
author: canhld94

comments.body:
Check network by ping 1500k packets `ping -c 20 -s 1500 shard`

>Broken pipe

Can you provide more logs? How fast it fails?

How big is the network latency between initator and in_order shard?
Does it reproduce if you disable  hedged request?
What clickhouse version do you use?

> Check network by ping 1500k packets ping -c 20 -s 1500 shard

Thanks, I will try this

> Can you provide more logs? How fast it fails?

It's something like this:

```
<Warning> HedgedConnectionsFactory: Connection failed at try №1, reason: Code: 210. DB::NetException: I/O error: Broken pipe, while writing to socket
```

Doesn't happens too frequent, but the problem is once if happens, in 60s the first replica will be marked as error and secondary queries will go to 2nd replica, which is bad for us.
We've consider to reduce the 60s error period, but we want to know exactly why the connection fails first. It can be a network issue, but can also be a bug in connection establishing code.

> How big is the network latency between initator and in_order shard?

Should be very fast. The initial is always 1st replica, and the ping from 1st replica to 2nd replica is sub-milliseconds

> Does it reproduce if you disable hedged request?

I haven't tested yet because we enable hedged request by default.

> What clickhouse version do you use?

Latest stable as always, with our own modification, but pretty sure we didn't touch any logic related to network connection.

It looks like a correct behaviour. Clickhouse was unable to connect to another server. You can increase timeout if the latency is big.

>first replica will be marked as error for 60s,

This is controllable BTW, 

  --distributed_replica_error_half_life arg                                            Time period reduces replica error counter by 2 times.
  --distributed_replica_error_cap arg                                                  Max number of errors per replica, prevents piling up an incredible amount of errors if replica was offline for some time and allows it to be

> It looks like a correct behaviour. Clickhouse was unable to connect to another server.

@den-crane This is what I'm trying to make it clear here. If the network error is something like connection timeout, or refuse, etc.. then it's no doubt that network has problem. But here it's  `Broken pipe`...

> Does replica connections fail with Broken pipe indicates a bug in connection establisher, or it indeed relates to network?

Yes, it is a network problem. Nothing special about it.
