ALTER TABLE  TEST MODIFY COLUMN type LowCardinality(String)
ALTER TABLE  TEST MODIFY COLUMN version LowCardinality(String)
```
and the history data in clickhouse  will be rebuid three times, 
 How to make those three modify in one sql and only rebuild once?
author: kaynewu

comments.body:
You should be able to execute multiple `MODIFY COLUMN` expressions in a single `ALTER TABLE` statement separated by commas:

```
ALTER TABLE TEST MODIFY COLUMN type LowCardinality(String), MODIFY COLUMN version LowCardinality(String)
```
 
Note that in your example you cannot modify the id column because it's a primary key.  Modify column types for primary keys is not permitted because it would require a rewrite/resort of the entire table.

author: rkozlo

comments.body:
Sorry, I misunderstood your question :)
When circular replication is used each host is responsible for two replicas (db1.numbers and db2.numbers), so each host should execute query twice with different databases. It's not implemented, currently each host can execute only one query per one distributed DDL task. And when database name is not specified, then it's not clear which one to choose, so it just fails with the error like this.
Thanks for explanation!

comments.body: does the size of temporary table also counted for the query memory usage?

Yes.  Memory tracking operates by having a MemoryTracker object associated with the current query and all allocations and deallocations (C++ `new` and `delete`) are proxied through that MemoryTracker object.  That includes allocations for temporary tables which are of course entirely in memory.  Note that many aggregate functions also generate temporary tables to calculate results, which are similarly tracked.

It looks like you are putting 299 million rows of data in your temporary table (which are normally uncompressed).

You should consider just a regular MergeTree table for something like this.  In several ways MergeTree tables are superior to Memory tables for many operations (compression being one of them).
Thanks!

```
There is no documentation about those columns. Can someone please care to explain what they are for?

comments.body:
Some tables may depend on others, for example:
```
:) create table test.dict_src (n int, m int, s String) engine=MergeTree order by n;
:) create dictionary test.dict1 (n int default 0, m int default 1, s String default 'qqq')
            PRIMARY KEY n
            SOURCE(CLICKHOUSE(HOST 'localhost' PORT tcpPort() USER 'default' TABLE 'dict_src' PASSWORD '' DB 'test'))
            LIFETIME(MIN 1 MAX 10) LAYOUT(FLAT());
:) create table test.mt (n int, m int default dictGet('test.dict1', 'm', 42::UInt64)) engine=MergeTree order by n

:) select database, table, loading_dependencies_database, loading_dependencies_table, loading_dependent_database, loading_dependent_table from system.tables where database='test'

┌─database─┬─table────┬─loading_dependencies_database─┬─loading_dependencies_table─┬─loading_dependent_database─┬─loading_dependent_table─┐
│ test     │ dict1    │ ['test']                      │ ['dict_src']               │ ['test']                   │ ['mt']                  │
│ test     │ dict_src │ []                            │ []                         │ ['test']                   │ ['dict1']               │
│ test     │ mt       │ ['test']                      │ ['dict1']                  │ []                         │ []                      │
└──────────┴──────────┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘
```

Table `test.mt` depends on dictionary `test.dict1` that depends on table `test.dict_src`. It means that you cannot just drop `test.dict1`, because `test.mt` may stop working:
```
:) drop dictionary test.dict1
Received exception from server (version 22.5.1):
Code: 630. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot drop or rename test.dict1, because some tables depend on it: test.mt. (HAVE_DEPENDENT_OBJECTS)

:) drop table test.dict_src
Received exception from server (version 22.5.1):
Code: 630. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot drop or rename test.dict_src, because some tables depend on it: test.dict1. (HAVE_DEPENDENT_OBJECTS)

:) drop table test.mt
Ok.
:) drop dictionary test.dict1
Ok.
:) drop table test.dict_src
Ok.

```

See also #15170

title: Effective range of MergeTree settings
body: What is the effective range of MergeTree settings? Is it effective for one MergeTree table or all MergeTree tables? For example, parts_to_throw_insert = 1200. Will it be triggered when the parts of one MergeTree table reach 1200, or when the parts of all MergeTree tables reach 1200? Thanks.
author: LGDHuaOPER

comments.body:
It depends on the setting.  That particular setting applies **_per partition_**, as listed in the description, not even per table.  Other settings such as `max_parts_in_total` apply per table, and others a per server, like `max_replicated_sends_network_bandwidth` apply for all Replicated tables.

As a general rule, the default setting values have been carefully selected, and we strongly advise against changing `parts_to_throw_insert` above its default value of 300.  If you have more than 300 parts in a single partition this very often indicates a server issue that should be addressed, and otherwise is a sign that your inserts are probably too small (at least a 1000 rows is recommended).

title: Including a Data Skipping Index for a Materialized View
body: Hello! Is it possible to include the creation of a Data Skipping Index while creating a materialized view in a single command? I understand that I can create a target table for the materialized view and create the index there but I would like to know if it's possible to have the index create with the `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW...` construct. Thanks!
author: a-dot

comments.body: This is not supported.  In general the TO form of Materialized Views is to be preferred in almost any use case except for the simplest test tables, so the functionality for "automatic" MVs is limited and unlikely to be enhanced.   The TO form allows all the features of a table in a transparent and maintainable way.

title: Is it possible to have different index granularity per wide column
body: I use ClickHouse for log analysis. The `message` column is used to store the original log lines, and the `level` column is used to store the log level. Generally, the length of the `message` column is much larger than the length of the `level` column. I set the index_granularity_bytes to 320 kb, which improves the query efficiency of the message, but the query performance of the level decreases. So is it possible to have different index granularity per wide column, the `message` colmun use low index_granularity_bytes and the `level` column use index_granularity = 8192.
author: yandd

comments.body:
`index_granularity`, like the names suggests, applies **only** to the granularity of the index on the column -- the ORDER BY parameter of the MergeTree engine.  It does not make sense to discuss the index_granularity of different columns.  Index granularity determines how many rows are stored in each "granule" for **all columns**.

`index_granular_bytes` limits the size of each granule, so by reducing it from the default of 10MB, you are increasing the total number of granules for your wide rows.  The only real effect of this is to make ClickHouse do more data reads, so it's unclear why it would significantly affect your query performance.

It's more likely that your query performance is affected by your ORDER BY key and your query filter/WHERE clause.  What is the ORDER BY and PARTITION BY of your table, and what do your "fast" and "slow" queries look like?  Are you using any secondary indexes?

title: "Connection refused" issue, with clickhouse-jdbc driver
body:
We used clickhouse-jdbc driver (ru.yandex.clickhouse, 0.2.4, 8123 port) to connect Clickhouse server, but we always get "Connection refused" issue. 

Then we used clickhouse-native-jdbc (com.github.housepower, 9000 port) to replace. Unfortunately, we found severl bugs in this driver. 

Is there any good soluction to avoid the issues?  Which driver should we use? Is there any configuration need to set? Thanks!
author: taotaizhu-pw

comments.body:
Can you reach port 8123 of your ClickHouse server from the command line via curl?  Is ClickHouse configured to run via TLS?  In that case the JDBC connection string must use port 8443 and use https instead of http.

Also is there some reason you're using an old version of the JDBC driver?  The current version is 0.3.2-patch7 (and is being migrated from yandex to clickhouse.com).

> 

Yes, most of the time, our system works fine with 8123 clickhouse. Sometime, "Connection refused" issue.  What is "VIA TLS"?

Another question, 8123 is HTTP or TCP? Thanks

TLS is an encrypted, secure connection.  The older name is SSL.  If you can connect otherwise on port 8123 then you are not using encryption/TLS/SSL.

8123 uses the standard HTTP protocol.  9000 uses the "Native" ClickHouse protocol (both protocols are based on TCP, so it can be less confusing to use the term Native).

If the connection to 8123 mostly works but you only occasionally get "connection refused" the problem is almost certainly not the JDBC driver.  That is an operating system/network level message that is just being forwarded by JDBC.  Are you using any kind of load balancer or proxy in front of your ClickHouse server?  Is it possible your ClickHouse server is occasionally crashing/restarting which would mean the port isn't open?  Is it possible that the hostname for the ClickHouse system somehow is pointing to the wrong server?

title: UDF. reduce ts data
body:
Hi!
I need to reduce time series data and keep only important point.
I proposed that UDF can be a right way for this task and have some questions.

1. Can the result of UDF be Null?
   Function decleared as `<return_type>Nullable(Float64)</return_type>`
   If script return '\n' than the result in CH is default value for type(0 in my case)
   If script return 'Null' - error: Cannot parse NaN. (CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED)
2. Can function return more than one column?
3. Is it possible to use functions to defeat a series (example: to output only even numbers).

Thx!
author: e11it

comments.body:
> Can the result of UDF be Null?

Yes. But you need to return the same string as it's used for NULL for the format you are using

Example:
```
<functions>
    <function>
        <type>executable</type>
        <name>test_function</name>
        <return_type>Nullable(UInt64)</return_type>
        <argument>
            <type>UInt64</type>
        </argument>
        <argument>
            <type>UInt64</type>
        </argument>
        <format>TabSeparated</format>
        <command>cd /; clickhouse local --input-format TabSeparated --output-format TabSeparated --structure 'x UInt64, y UInt64' --query "SELECT NULL::Nullable(UInt64) FROM table"</command>
        <execute_direct>0</execute_direct>
    </function>
</functions>
```

```
SELECT test_function(0, 1)

Query id: 009d234b-1e06-4858-8c0a-2a96614451c5

   ┌─test_function(0, 1)─┐
1. │                ᴺᵁᴸᴸ │
   └─────────────────────┘
```

> Can function return more than one column?

No. A function must return exactly one value for each input.

> Is it possible to use functions to defeat a series (example: to output only even numbers).

No. The function must return always one value.

title: What is Memory DataBase?
body:
What is Memory DataBase? I found "Memory Database" in some doc, and execute "create database memdb engine=Memory" successfully.  I also can create MergeTree table in this database. What's the difference between "Memory Database" and "Memory Table"?  Is it mean all the tables are in memory when I use memory database, even I create mergetree table? 
Thanks!
author: taotaizhu-pw

comments.body:
`Memory` database does not store tables' metadata persistently. It is an implementation part of `clickhouse-local`.
Tables' metadata is forgotten on exit, while tables data remains.

This database engine is not intended to be used explicitly.

title: Any solution for Memory Engine cluster? replicate date to slave node
body:
Is there any solution for Memory Engine cluster? Replicate the data to slave node. 
As I know that the "Replicated" function can only be used in MergeTree table/engine. Is there work around solution for Memory Engine? Thanks!
author: taotaizhu-pw

comments.body:
No, Memory engine is not for large scale storage.

In fact, it can work slower than MergeTree, due to lack of indexes, lack of sorting, lack of prewhere optimization and limited support for compression.
TLDR: In-memory != better.

> TLDR: In-memory != better.

Thanks alex. Our case is based on MergeTree engine, push some special data into memory table at 8:00AM in everyday . Each table less than 50000 lines, even most of the special tables are about 5000~10000 lines. And we found the mutation "UPDATE/DELETE" operation in memory is synchronized, it matched our requirements.  After testing, our sql queries saved 70%~80% time rather than mergetree table.

title: ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN is mutating all the parts
body:
When trying to DROP a column from a table with TB of data, it's taking a lot of time. When checking current merges, I've seen that all the parts are being rewritten to disk. Is this expected? As per the documentation, the DROP COLUMN should finish almost instantly.

* ClickHouse server version 21.12.3.32 (official build)
* Table is a ReplacingMergeTree

Expected result would be that the DROP column finishes almost instantly.
author: jaumecastell

comments.body:
Hi, @jaumecastell. First of all parts in clickhouse are immutable, so nothing can change them. `ALTER DROP COLUMN` really processes all parts on disk, because we need to remove column files from each part. Because of immutability, we create new parts instead of old ones without dropped columns. Of course, it's suboptimal to copy all the rest columns except dropped one so we use `hardlinks` to shallow copy them. 

This behavior is expected. When you need to remove terabytes of data from a disk it's impossible to do it instantly. However dropped column became invisible for queries almost immediately, because metadata changes applied quite fast.
Hi @alesapin , thank you very much for the quick response. Is there anything I can tune to speed up dropping columns?

@jaumecastell 

>thank you very much for the quick response. Is there anything I can tune to speed up dropping columns?

There are possible reasons
* you have enormous number of files in the table `parts * columns`. Check `SELECT count() FROM system.parts_columns WHERE (table = 'test') AND active`.
* you have very slow disk system or filesystem (AWS EBS with limited IOPS) and hardlinks are created very slow.
* your table is replicated and Zookeeper is very slow and new parts creation very slow.
* you excessively use Nullable(LowCardinality) types so number of files is 3 times larger than expected

Cloud disk (oracle cloud)
```sql
CREATE TABLE test
(
    `id` Int64,
    `d` Int64,
    `c` String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY intDiv(d, 10000)
ORDER BY id

set max_partitions_per_insert_block=0;

insert into test select number, number, '' from numbers(1e8);


SELECT count() FROM system.parts_columns WHERE (table = 'test') AND active
┌─count()─┐
│   30285 │ -- need to create 30k * 2(4) hardlinks
└─────────┘

alter table test drop column c;
0 rows in set. Elapsed: 66.869 sec.
```

Laptop (NVME)

```sql
SELECT count() FROM system.parts_columns WHERE (table = 'test') AND active;
┌─count()─┐
│   30285 │
└─────────┘


alter table test drop column c;
0 rows in set. Elapsed: 33.928 sec.
```

Hi @den-crane , I modified your example table `test` into a ReplicatedMergeTree table and reproduced your steps.
My queries was canceled due to `receive_timeout=300` setting.
This `alter table test drop column c` query seems to be an asynchronous operation that I checked `system.mutations` and found that this mutation is done finally.
I was wondering does it really not matter that my `drop column` alter query was canceled and some parts would eventually finish the whole columns removing process?

Only selects can be cancelled.

`alter table test drop column c` can not be canceled and will be processed in the background.

title: Details about how distribute_group_by_no_merge works
body:
I'm wondering how distribute_group_by_no_merge = 1 works. 

I'm using distribute_group_by_no_merge=1 to optimize the following query

original query: 

```
WITH Date(now()) AS in_endDate
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) AS tmp, ext_ingest_date
FROM (
  SELECT client_id
  , Date(ext_ingest_time) AS ext_ingest_date
  FROM test
  WHERE ext_ingest_time >= date_add(day, -54, in_endDate)
      AND ext_ingest_time <= in_endDate
GROUP BY ext_ingest_date
```

And I wrote two queries using distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1 as optimized versions

A:
```
WITH Date(now()) AS in_endDate
SELECT SUM(tmp) AS count_distinct, ext_ingest_date
FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) AS tmp, ext_ingest_date
    FROM (
      SELECT client_id
      , Date(ext_ingest_time) AS ext_ingest_date
      FROM test
      WHERE ext_ingest_time >= date_add(day, -54, in_endDate)
      AND ext_ingest_time <= in_endDate
    )
    GROUP BY ext_ingest_date SETTINGS distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1
)
GROUP BY ext_ingest_date
```

B: 
```
WITH Date(now()) AS in_endDate
    SELECT SUM(tmp) AS count_distinct, ext_ingest_date
    FROM (
        SELECT
            COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) AS tmp
            , Date(ext_ingest_time) AS ext_ingest_date
            FROM test_table
        WHERE ext_ingest_time >= date_add(day, -54, in_endDate)
        AND ext_ingest_time <= in_endDate
        GROUP BY ext_ingest_date SETTINGS distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1
)
GROUP BY ext_ingest_date
```

And I found the distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1 only works for B.  It seems because I imposed distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1 to a subquery in query A so it doesn't work. 

But I need professional interpretation about the difference between A and B, as well as how distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1  influences these two queries.

Besides, I have a few more questions:
1. I know distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1  can be used to optimize `count distinct`. Does it also work for other aggregations like Min, Max, Sum, and Count?
2. Can we use distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1  along with window functions?

Wait for your response! Thanks a lot!
author: catwang01

comments.body:
This is expected. Because of `( )` `select_at_initator ( select distributed ) `

Only part of the query inside `( .... )` is executed at shards.



```
WITH Date(now()) AS in_endDate
SELECT SUM(tmp) AS count_distinct, ext_ingest_date
FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT client_id) AS tmp, ext_ingest_date
    FROM (                                                          --- executed on initator
      SELECT client_id                                              --- executed on shards
      , Date(ext_ingest_time) AS ext_ingest_date
      FROM test
      WHERE ext_ingest_time >= date_add(day, -54, in_endDate)
      AND ext_ingest_time <= in_endDate
    )
    GROUP BY ext_ingest_date SETTINGS distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1
)
GROUP BY ext_ingest_date
```

by ` SELECT client_id`  you are fetching all data to initator, after that `distributed_group_by_no_merge` loses sense because all data at the iniator.

>I know distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1 can be used to optimize count distinct.
> Does it also work for other aggregations like Min, Max, Sum, and Count?

yes it works with all agg.functions, also check 

```
--optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key arg                     Optimize GROUP BY sharding_key queries (by avoiding costly aggregation on the initiator server).
```
it's the automatic mode for `distributed_group_by_no_merge`

------

>Can we use distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1 along with window functions?

No, window functions work at the query initator now. Use `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key`.
Thanks @den-crane ! That helps a lot!

title: Does async insert support WAL?
body: It seems that "async insert" does not support WAL.  It will cause data loss when a server suddenly crashes down.
author: etah000

comments.body:
>server suddenly crashes down.

CH server or hardware server / outage?

Async insert does not change MergeTree insert behavior. 
By default data inserted into MergeTree is not synced to disk and is not guaranteed to survive unexpected hardware reboot. 

You can use mergeTree setting fsync_after_insert + fsync_part_directory

```
 fsync_after_insert                        │ 0     │       0 │ Do fsync for every inserted part. Significantly decreases performance of inserts, not recommended to use with wide parts.
 fsync_part_directory                      │ 0     │       0 │ Do fsync for part directory after all part operations (writes, renames, etc.).
───────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┴─────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

"async insert" puts small inserts in its cache. If it does not write WAL, CH will loss data when a server crashed.  This feature should have no relation with CH's "fsync write".

I want to make sure whether it supports WAL or not.

It does NOT need WAL.

With "async insert" ClickHouse starts to accumulate inserted data in some internal async_insert buffer and **postpones** INSERT commands **responses** until data is written into the **real table**. 
For example by default `async_insert_busy_timeout_ms=200` and `async_insert_max_data_size=100000 (bytes)`, when one of these limits have reached, the data inserted from the async_insert buffer will be flushed/written into the real table and INSERT command will return success (OK result).

> 

But If we set `wait_for_async=0`, the client seems not to wait for this response.
Yes. With `wait_for_async=0`  you can lost some data, because a client gets immediate insert result.

> 

Thanks. By the way, is there any comparison or benchmark about `normal insert` and `async insert`. If we open `wait_for_async=1` to let client wait for the response. Can `async insert` gains better throughput than `normal insert`？

>Can async insert gains better throughput than normal insert？

It can. The purpose of `async insert` is to improve performance with small inserts.
System performance not insert throughput.

Thanks for the suggestions.

> Don't know about situation when some active duplicates will be alive.

I will test it eventually but I wanted to know the expected behaviour before the test so I can handle the situation appropriately in the tool calling clickhouse-copier.

> My proposition is to make separate tasks for partitions.

I can create different tasks in a new task file but I was under the impression that force uploading a new file to zookeeper under the same path/description overwrites the previous task file which is not what I want. And uploading it to a separate path/description will create separate workers for each task and increase the load on the system which seems sub-optimal.

Active duplicates seem to be causing the rows to be duplicated repeatedly in the destination by copying different partitions every time I run the task. Any solution or workaround to solve this problem?

The question is not quite correct.

Partitions in ClickHouse contain multiple data parts. The subset of the data parts which is called "active" is representing the table. Every partition can have up to several hundreds of active parts. clickhouse-copier needs to copy all the active parts.

The reason why you get duplicates is probably unrelated to this observation.

title: Is there a way to remove duplicate data on ReplacedMergeTable between shards when select on distributed table on cluster?
body:
Is there a way to remove duplicate data on ReplacedMergeTable between shards when select on distributed table on cluster?
Hi, I build a distributed table on cluster based on ReplacedMergeTable. However, I found the ops of remove duplicate data only happen each server inside. Is there a way to remove duplicate data on ReplacedMergeTable between shards when select on distributed table on cluster?

1. using **FINAL**: ops of remove duplicate data only happen each server inside.
2. using the sorting key as sharding key. So, there will no duplicate data between shards.

However, I still want to know, how can i do if not using sorting key as sharding key or there is already some duplicate data between shards.
author: yandongl

comments.body: This is not currently supported.  Shard data is completely independent other than when it is combined as part of a query to a distributed table.  You must either ensure that shard data is unique by controlling inserts (as you did with by creating a sharding key based on sort key), deduplicate with your query with GROUP BY and aggregate functions (which is slow), or otherwise deduplicate in your client application (also slow).

title: AggregateFunction is not backward compatible
body:
**Describe the issue**
We were upgrading our Clickhouse cluster from **21.8.3.44** to **22.1.3.7** and found a lot of our queries are failing due to an error explained below 

**How to reproduce**
Create table 1
```
CREATE TABLE test.table_1 on cluster '{cluster}'
(
  `date` Date,
  `uniques` AggregateFunction(uniqCombined64(17), Nullable(String))
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY date
```

Create table 2
```
CREATE TABLE test.table_2 on cluster '{cluster}'
(
  `date` Date,
  `id`  Nullable(String)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY date
```

Insert data in table 2
```
INSERT INTO test.table_2 (*) VALUES ('2022-04-01', null), ('2022-04-01', '1'), ('2022-04-01', '2'), ('2022-04-01', '3'), ('2022-04-01', '3'), ('2022-04-01', '4'), ('2022-04-01', '5');
```

Insert data into table 1 using table 1 data
```
INSERT INTO test.table_1 
SELECT
  date,
  uniqCombined64State(17)(id)
FROM test.table_2
GROUP BY date
```

Run aggregate query on table 1
```
SELECT
  date,
  coalesce(uniqCombined64Merge(uniques), 0) AS uniques
FROM test.table_1
GROUP BY date 
```

Version **21.8.3.44** gives result
```
┌───────date─┬─uniques─┐
│ 2022-04-01 │       5 │
└────────────┴─────────┘
```

**Error message and/or stacktrace**
Version **22.1.3.7** throws error
```
Code: 43. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Illegal type AggregateFunction(uniqCombined64(17), Nullable(String)) of argument for aggregate function uniqCombined64Merge, expected AggregateFunction(uniqCombined64, Nullable(String)) or equivalent type. (ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT)
```


**Additional context**
This is blocking us to upgrade to newer version.
author: piyushsriv

comments.body:
>AggregateFunction(uniqCombined64(17),
> uniqCombined64Merge(uniques)

This is a mis-usage which leads to incorrect results with any version.
You should use `uniqCombined64Merge(17)(uniques)` with any version of CH.
Thanks for clarifying this.

title: How to compile the clickhouse-v20.11.4.13-stable with gcc and libstdc++ instead of libc++
author: starrysky9959

comments.body: It is not possible.

The main asset of ClickHouse is our set of test suites and continuous integration system.
With our tests, including randomized tests, we find and fix bugs in most of third-party open-source libraries.

To ensure that ClickHouse is stable and secure, the only way is to build it with exactly the same versions of libraries with exactly the same patches as we do.

If you don't know, it's difficult to imagine how many bugs (race conditions, memory safety issues) exist in C++ libraries.

title: Using map in sorting key
body:
I'm trying to use map in sorting key (together with datetime). If I am reading `PLAN EXPLAIN` correctly, when I query without time, I can see the whole primary key is used. However, when I add time condition to query, only datetime key of the primary is used and query is several time slower. Is there a way to rephrase the query to get better PK utilization? Thank you.

```sql
CREATE TABLE ts
(
    `time` DateTime,
    `tags` Map(LowCardinality(String), String),
    `value` Int64
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(time)
ORDER BY (tags, time)

INSERT INTO ts (time, tags, value) VALUES (now(),{'hostname':'host_1'}, 1234)

SELECT time,tags,value FROM ts WHERE tags['hostname']='host_1' // indexes used: MinMax, Partition, PrimaryKey
SELECT time,tags,value FROM ts WHERE tags['hostname']='host_1' AND time < now() //// indexes used: MinMax, Partition, PrimaryKey / [Keys: "time"]
```
author: alespour

comments.body:
Usage of Map in sorting key does not make sense.
Data will be sorted by the arrays of key-value pairs in lexicographical order, but it does not allow to efficiently locate the data with specific map keys or values.

I understand users should not make assumptions on the order of map keys. But I find sorting the keys before insertion helps to improve compression ratio.

Here's my test:
1. Create two tables:
```SQL
CREATE TABLE mytest2
(
    `id` Map(String, String)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY tuple();

CREATE TABLE mytest3
(
    `id` Map(String, String)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY tuple();
```
2. Insert some mock data. For table `mytest2`, the keys are in arbitrary order; for table `mytest3`, the keys are sorted before insertion. Here're the data distributions:
```plain
# Run select id, count() from mytest2 group by id;
# mytest2:
┌─id────────────────────┬─count()─┐
│ {'k2':'v2','k1':'v1'} │   12555 │
│ {'k1':'v1','k2':'v2'} │   87445 │
└───────────────────────┴─────────┘

# mytest3:
┌─id────────────────────┬─count()─┐
│ {'k1':'v1','k2':'v2'} │  100000 │
└───────────────────────┴─────────┘
```

3. Count the table size:
```
SELECT
    database,
    table,
    formatReadableSize(sum(data_compressed_bytes) AS size) AS compressed,
    formatReadableSize(sum(data_uncompressed_bytes) AS usize) AS uncompressed,
    round(usize / size, 2) AS compr_rate,
    sum(rows) AS rows,
    count() AS part_count
FROM system.parts
WHERE (active = 1) AND (table in ('mytest2', 'mytest3'))
GROUP BY
    database,
    table
ORDER BY size DESC;

┌─table───┬─compressed─┬─uncompressed─┬─compr_rate─┬───rows─┬─part_count─┐
│ mytest2 │ 142.84 KiB │ 1.91 MiB     │      13.67 │ 100000 │          1 │
│ mytest3 │ 8.30 KiB   │ 1.91 MiB     │     235.35 │ 100000 │          1 │
└─────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴────────┴────────────┘
```

The ClickHouse version is 22.7.3.5. From my test, `Map(String, String)` has better compression ratio when keys are sorted before insertion.

I wonder,
1. Is this the right direction to optimize for the space taken of a Map column, or should I use arrays in this case?
2. Are there any benchmarks on the Map v.s. Array query performance comparison?

@alanhe 

> 1. Is this the right direction to optimize for the space taken of a Map column, or should I use arrays in this case?

Yes, it is reasonable to put columns in the ORDER BY for improving the compression ratio. This key will be useless for data indexing (filtering by index) but will improve the performance due to better compression and data locality.

> 2. Are there any benchmarks on the Map v.s. Array query performance comparison?

No. I expect there will be no performance difference as the Map type is using a pair of Arrays under the hood.

title: Auditing log for user log in history
body:
Hi Clickhouse team,

Looking through the Operations and Monitoring documentation I did not find anything regarding auditing my clickhouse cluster.
At this point I am interest in auditing and keeping track of user login history into my clickhouse cluster. 

On the table `system.query_log` I can have a rough understanding of when my user log in based on the timestamps of their queries, but dealing with that just to get their login would be additional work I imagine I can get around it.

Is there an mechanism implemented on Clickhouse out of the box to keep track of user log in history or that is something I would need to implement myself?

Thanks
author: thalesvon

comments.body: What do you mean by "user login history?"  ClickHouse servers do not keep track of internal user sessions, there is no user "state" kept between queries (other than raw TCP connections for the native or HTTP clients).  Accordingly the query log is the only meaningful source of interaction users and your ClickHouse cluster.

As far as I know, there is no a good way to get this information. Probably you can try to parse system.text_log.
Likely, there will be a special system table for it.

I don't think that audit to table is good enough for audit purposes. Usually audit trail requires right separation. But in case of table a malicious user with full access to Clickhouse will be able to clean trail.
There is the `system.session_log` table for this purpose.

title: Is Executable UDF considered as deterministic?
body:
**Describe the unexpected behaviour**
I've an Executable UDF that outputs input String along with the row number like this:
```sql
SELECT test_function_python(rand() % 100)       
FROM numbers(10)                                
                                                
Query id: bb9c4d1f-0897-42fc-87a9-5252e9bb7816  
                                                
┌─test_function_python(modulo(rand(), 100))─┐   
│ 0 59                                      │   
│ 1 41                                      │   
│ 2 39                                      │   
│ 3 16                                      │   
│ 4 55                                      │   
│ 5 68                                      │   
│ 6 92                                      │   
│ 7 41                                      │   
│ 8 93                                      │   
│ 9 54                                      │   
└───────────────────────────────────────────┘   
                                                
10 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.148 sec.             
```

The problem is, if the argument is a static value, then it looks like the result is cached:

```sql
SELECT test_function_python(123)              
FROM numbers(10)                              
                                              
Query id: 8467597b-57d2-4f9e-829b-900f7482d653
                                              
┌─test_function_python(123)─┐                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
└───────────────────────────┘                 
```
As you can see row numbers are all zeroes.

**Expected behavior**
```sql
┌─test_function_python(123)─┐                 
│ 0 123                     │                 
│ 1 123                     │                 
│ 2 123                     │                 
│ 3 123                     │                 
│ 4 123                     │                 
│ 5 123                     │                 
│ 6 123                     │                 
│ 7 123                     │                 
│ 8 123                     │                 
│ 9 123                     │                 
└───────────────────────────┘                 
```

**Executable UDF code**:
```py
#!/usr/bin/python3

import sys

if __name__ == '__main__':
    i = 0
    for line in sys.stdin:
        print(i, line, end='')
        sys.stdout.flush()
        i += 1
```
author: ramazanpolat

comments.body:
@ramazanpolat UDF functions are not deterministic by default, this is just optimization for Functions if defaultImplementationForConstants is enabled, and enable it by default is reasonable, because there could be a lot of use cases when you want UDF to just make some HTTP call and map some constant to some value.
That way `SELECT test_function(1) FROM table` will not create UDF for each block size. It can be fixed on client side, with `SELECT test_function(materialize(1)) FROM table`, so it makes almost no sense to provide some setting for this, client has enough flexibility.

title: Unable to send async insert query via Http Interface
body:
Hi, Team

After setting async_insert=1 and wait_for_async_insert=0, I submitted an insert query (insert into table A select * from table B) via Postman to the Clickhouse server.

However it did not instantly return 200 OK response, but still waiting the insertion progress to complete and then returned the 200 response.

Also I tried to set those 2 properties in the request url like server_address/?async_insert=1&wait_for_async_insert=0, it also did not work as expected.

Can you guide me how to submit an async insert query via Http Interface ?
author: wilsonwang213

comments.body:
async_insert is not for `insert into table A select * from table B`
async_insert should work only with `insert into table A + datastream (values/TSV/CSV ...)`

Thanks @den-crane 

Another question is that, if I submit an insert query via Http and manually stop it. Would the insert query run and complete at Clickhouse server ?

>Another question is that, if I submit an insert query via Http and manually stop it. 
>Would the insert query run and complete at Clickhouse server ?

It can complete or can partially complete.
@den-crane can async insert work for table functions? E.g. `insert into table select * from s3(...)` not sure if s3 function will be considered a datastream here

> > Another question is that, if I submit an insert query via Http and manually stop it.
> > Would the insert query run and complete at Clickhouse server ?
> 
> It can complete or can partially complete.

In what circumstance it will partially complete?
@wilsonwang213 Asynchronous inserts work for queries with explicit data, not for INSERT SELECT, not for table functions.

title: MaterializedPostgresql database does not show all tables
body:
when I use  MaterializedPostgresql as this way
CREATE DATABASE postgres_database
ENGINE = MaterializedPostgreSQL('postgres1:5432', 'postgres_database', 'postgres_user', 'postgres_password')
SETTINGS materialized_postgresql_schema = 'postgres_schema';

it only show some tables of that schema and does not  all tables . I use 22.1.3.7 version (edited) 

When I use Matrerialized_Postgresql_table_list it work But I have to do for each 50 table one by one it's so difficult to do that in each db
author: zkuser2002

comments.body:
List of tables to be replicated is defined by the following command:
```
SELECT tablename FROM pg_catalog.pg_tables WHERE schemaname = <schema>;
```
@kssenii thanks if you send an example quesry for do that, because I do every method in documentation but at the end I got error or I got only some tables for database again

> @kssenii thanks if you send an example quesry for do that

I just sent it in the previous comment above:
```
SELECT tablename FROM pg_catalog.pg_tables WHERE schemaname = <schema>;
```
Tables list is determined by this query.

If some tables are in this list and are not in MaterializedPostgreSQL database then it means that there was some error when loading them from PostrgeSQL. You can see the reason for that in logs. Most often this happens because there is no primary key/replica identity index in PostgreSQL tables or some other error. 
Such tables (which fail to be loaded) are just skipped from replication. This is an expected behaviour. See logs for more information why some tables were skipped.

author: sunny19930321

comments.body: I think that if the dictionary table does not exist and provides default values, then I plan to add this feature

This feature is questionable, because `DEFAULT` clause will be silently ignored if there's a typo in dictionary name, such behavior may be misleading. We could add a setting, but I think that this feature does not worth adding a setting. You should either create dictionary first or create table without `DEFAULT` clause in column definition and add it later using `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN`.

title: Why not allowed to change a timeout setting, sync_request_timeout?
body:
There are many settings that related to timeout, like send_timeout, receive_timeout. Some of them are configurable, like receive_timeout. However, there is a timeout for synchronous request-result protocol call (like Ping or TableStatus): **sync_request_timeout** (default is 5s), the one is not allowed to set by user. In some cases, when the servers are busy and timeout may happen in Connection::getTablesStatus(), since 5 seconds is very short.

Would you mind to explain why the "sync_request_timeout" is not allowed to be changed? Or what kind of considerations for this behavior?
author: zhangjmruc

comments.body:
sync_request_timeout – timeout for server ping. Defaults to 5 seconds.
In some cases, if the data sync request time out, it may be casued by many different reasons, basically it shouldn't take more than 5 seconds for synchronous request-result protocol call (like Ping or TableStatus) in most of the normal circumstances , thus if time out setting too long, eg. 5 minutes or longer than that , then you will run into more overall performance issues.  This is not good for any application on the server.
Thanks @sgycs

title: Breaking a source table row into multiple rows using materialized views
body:
Is it possible to create two rows in a MV from a single row in a source table?

Example:
Insert in source table:
|when | col_1 | col_2|
|-----|-------|------|
|datetime | val_1 | val_2|

I would like to end up with something like this in the Materialized view:
| when | col_x |
|------|-------|
|datetime | val_1|
|datetime | val_2|

Is it possible to do that? Thanks!!
author: a-dot

comments.body:
Yes it's possible `arrayJoin( [ col_1 , col_2 ] ) `

```sql
SELECT arrayJoin([col1, col2]) AS colx
FROM
(
    SELECT
        1 AS col1,
        2 AS col2
)
┌─colx─┐
│    1 │
│    2 │
└──────┘



create materialized view ...
...
select arrayJoin( [ col_1 , col_2 ] ) as col_x, 
from ...
```

Thanks den-crane, as always!
One follow up question if I may... the array approach is stumping me and I simply can't figure out how to do this. In my first post I gave you a simple example but what I'm trying to do is slightly more complicated.. I want to unfold col1 and col2 but I want to assign val_3 as such:

Before:
|when|col_1|col_2|col_3|
|------|-----|-----|------|
| datetime | val_1 | val_2 | val_3|

After:
|when|col_x|col_y|col_z|
|-----|-----|------|-----|
|datetime| val_1|val_3|0|
|datetime|val_2|0|val_3|

Hopefully you can still help! Thanks again!!

```sql
SELECT col_x, col_y, col_z
FROM
(
    SELECT
        'val_1' AS col_1,
        'val_2' AS col_2,
        'val_3' col_3
)
array join [col_1, col_2] AS col_x, [col_3, '0'] as col_y, ['0', col_3] as col_z
┌─col_x─┬─col_y─┬─col_z─┐
│ val_1 │ val_3 │ 0     │
│ val_2 │ 0     │ val_3 │
└───────┴───────┴───────┘
```


```sql
SELECT
    (arrayJoin(arrayZip([col_1, col_2], [col_3, '0'], ['0', col_3])) AS xx).1 AS col_x,
    xx.2 AS col_y,
    xx.3 AS col_z
FROM
(
    SELECT
        'val_1' AS col_1,
        'val_2' AS col_2,
        'val_3' AS col_3
)
┌─col_x─┬─col_y─┬─col_z─┐
│ val_1 │ val_3 │ 0     │
│ val_2 │ 0     │ val_3 │
└───────┴───────┴───────┘
```
thank you so much!

)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree()
PARTITION BY xxHash64(uid) % 8

SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 500000000, min_rows_for_wide_part = 1000000, index_granularity = 8192

)
ENGINE = Distributed('default', 'default', 'demo_user', xxHash64(uid))

```alter table default.demo_user ON CLUSTER default DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS demo,DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS demo_ts; ```

title: Adding a column (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) fails
body:
Hi all

I have the following setup:
     - Clickhouse version 21.9
     - 8 nodes in cluster ( 2 shards / 4 replicas)
     - test.XXX is a ReplicatedMergeTree table

I need to add a column to test.XXX table , the following query is executed: 
 
> ALTER TABLE test.XXX ON CLUSTER test_cluster ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS NEWCOLUMN1 String;

It fails with an error:

> [Code: 1002, SQL State: ]  ClickHouse exception, code: 1002, .... DB::Exception: There was an error on ...: Code: 517. DB::Exception: Metadata on replica is not up to date with common metadata in Zookeeper. Cannot alter. (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER) (version 21.9.2.17 (official build)). (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER) (version 21.9.2.17 (official build))

Some observations:

1. Sometimes the above ALTER works ok, but such cases are rare. 
2. Even though query ends with an error, the column is actually added
3. Checked metadata before running the query - it is exactly the same both on disk / in zookeeper

Question:

Am I doing something wrong? 

I know I can workaround by executing DDLs on each shard separately or just ignore CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER error, but this looks inconvenient. Is there a reliable way to execute DDL queries on cluster?
author: x052bb

comments.body:
@x052bb
Do you use JDBC ? 
Do you connect to a random server?
Do you run several `alter` one by one? `ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..; ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..; ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..;` ?

@den-crane 

> Do you use JDBC ? 

Yes

> Do you connect to a random server? 

No. There's a single server in JDBC connection string, like _jdbc:clickhouse://host:port_

> Do you run several `alter` one by one? `ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..; ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..; ALTER TABLE .... ADD COLUMN ..;` ?

The above error is reproduced if I run single ALTER, just as in example above
Does it reproduce from CH client ?

@den-crane 

> Does it reproduce from CH client ?

Here's how reply looks when I'm using pure HTTP:

> host1  9010    0               7       5
> host2  9010    0               6       5
> host3  9010    0               5       5
> host4  9010    0               4       4
> host5  9010    0               3       0
> host6  9010    517     Code: 517. DB::Exception: Metadata on replica is not up to date with common metadata in Zookeeper. Cannot alter. (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER) (version 21.9.2.17 (official build))     2       0
> host7  9010    0               1       0
> host8  9010    0               0       0
> Code: 517. DB::Exception: There was an error on [host6:9010]: Code: 517. DB::Exception: Metadata on replica is not up to date with common metadata in Zookeeper. Cannot alter. (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER) (version 21.9.2.17 (official build)). (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER) (version 21.9.2.17 (official build))
> 

But

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Ok, so it looks like I've found the reason:

JDBC driver (we are using 0.1.55) by default sets compress=1 property to the HTTP request. That setting breaks DDL request like this... God knows why...
This issue should be directed to the repository of the JDBC driver.

```sql
CREATE TABLE t
(

)

SELECT *
FROM t;

┌────v─┐
│   10 │
│  100 │
│ 1000 │
└──────┘

ALTER TABLE t
    UPDATE v = v / 10 WHERE 1 = 1;

SELECT *
FROM t;

┌───v─┐
│   1 │
│  10 │
│ 100 │
└─────┘
```

title: Any plans to optimize the Map type from the storage perspective?
body:
The Map type provides great syntax benefits, but the fact that all data for the Map column is stored in a single file ends up being a significant bottleneck (becoming more and more significant as the number of keys grows, especially if the dataset is somewhat sparse).

Is there any plan to optimize this and make it so that the "Map" datatype actually writes on separate files for each key? At the moment, the performance hit is just too high to use it at scale unfortunately unless the number of keys is very limited.
author: andrea-s

comments.body: Yes, there are plans to implement `Map` type that writes each key to separate column, but only after #23932 will be merged.
That's a great news, thank you!
@CurtizJ , I see that #23932 has been merged - do you know how long will it be until the Map datatype will use it? Thank you very much

title: EXPLAIN SYNTAX doesn't report more than one column in GROUP BY
body:
For instance a query like this:

```sql
explain syntax (SELECT sum(number) _number, count(), number, toDate(now()) date FROM numbers(10) GROUP BY number, date);

EXPLAIN SYNTAX
SELECT
    sum(number) AS _number,
    count(),
    number,
    toDate(now()) AS date
FROM numbers(10)
GROUP BY
    number,
    date

Query id: 985a47d6-644e-4821-8a6d-83de0925cfdd

┌─explain─────────────────────┐
│ SELECT                      │
│     sum(number) AS _number, │
│     count(),                │
│     number,                 │
│     toDate(now()) AS date   │
│ FROM numbers(10)            │
│ GROUP BY number             │
└─────────────────────────────┘

whether choosing distributed table can cause performance degrade in the query?

1. CH node gets the query -- this node became node initiator for distributed query.
2. The initiator sends queries to all shards
3. All shards execute the query
4. All shards reply to initiator with result
5. Initiator does final aggregation -- it can take a lot of time, bigger than step 3

You can disable step 5 

```
  --distributed_group_by_no_merge arg                                  If 1, Do not merge aggregation states from different servers for distributed queries (shards will process query up to the Complete stage, initiator just proxies the data from the shards). If 2
                                                                       the initiator will apply ORDER BY and LIMIT stages (it is not in case when shard process query up to the Complete stage)
```

Try to execute your query with `set distributed_group_by_no_merge=1`

title: High values of minSessionTimeout on zookeeper may lead to problems with clickhouse restart
body:
Ephemeral nodes will not be removed till `minSessionTimeout` will be reached, clickhouse during restart says: 

```
Couldn't start replication (table will be in readonly mode): Replica /tables/foo/bar/replicas/ch_4/is_active appears to be already active (host: ch-4, port: 9009, tcp_port: 9000, database: foo, table: bar scheme: http, ). If you're sure it's not, try again in a minute or remove znode /clickhouse/tables/foo/bar/replicas/ch_4/is_active manually. 

REPLICA_IS_ALREADY_ACTIVE
```

To fix it you need to reconfigure & restart zookeeper, after that you may need to drop old ephemeral nodes (you can list them using `echo dump | nc zookeeper-1 2181` ) 

P.S. OK just to close the issue (added the issue to make it indexed by search engines). Optionally we can add a note about minSessionTimeout in the exception message.
author: filimonov

comments.body: It occurs if you terminate clickhouse-server by kill (without waiting for shutdown). Then ephemeral nodes are remaining in ZooKeeper until session timeout and it is impossible to determine if the server with replica is no longer connected.

title: Access Control setup could be simpler and safer
body:
Configuring Access Control requires various steps:

1. Lock down the default user e.g. with a temporary random password
2. Give it access management right by setting  yandex > users > default > access_management to 1. [Adding a temporary override in /etc/clickhouse-server/users.d did not seem to work]
3. Restart Clickhouse
4. Run SQL to create an admin user with special grants
5. Run SQL to remove rights to the default user (e.g. prevent write operations)
6. Unlock the default user e.g. reset the password to empty
7. Reset access_management
8. Restart Clickhouse
9. Log in as admin and create users and roles as needed

A mistake might create risk to lock oneself out of the database or leave unwanted roles open for abuse. The first 8 steps could be automated to be safer.
E.g.
```
sudo clickhouse-client --create-admin
The "admin" user has been created with password "<random_password>". The "default" user is now read-only.
```

title: How can I confirm that SQL execution uses vectorized computation?
body: Does clickhouse use vectorisation for all SQL or some of it and if so, how do I know if my SQL is using vectorisation?
author: asasas234

comments.body:
Some computations are vectorized and some are not.

You can run the following commands in Ubuntu:

```
sudo apt install linux-tools-common
sudo perf top
```

Start running some queries with `clickhouse-benchmark`.
Then navigate to the top functions from ClickHouse.
Open disassembly. And find vector instructions there.

On x86 CPUs vector instructions are using vector registers, named with `xmm`, `ymm`, `zmm`.
And the instructions are named starting with `p` (packed) or `vp`.
Although some other non-vector instructions can also use vector registers.

In some cases we use JIT compilation and vectorization together - that gives maximum benefit.
If JIT compilation is used, you cannot see disassembly in perf top and you will see some addresses instead of function names.
Thank you for your answer @alexey-milovidov

comments.body: Scince we use non-blocking reading from the socket in HedgedConnectionsFactory, most likely the error `SOCKET_TIMEOUT` occures is the first connection to the socket or while writing data to socket. You can try to tune timeouts `connect_timeout_with_failover_ms`/`connect_timeout_with_failover_secure_ms` for connection to the socket and `send_timeout` for writing data to socket.

Also you can try to turn off settings `use_hedged_requests` and `async_socket_for_remote` to turn off async non-blocking reads from sockets and see if such errors will be repeated (unlikely to be a problem in these settings, but if you turn them off, we could see more precise place in the code where the error occures)

title: Is it OK to implement a direct ORC/Parquet input/output format?
body:
Now, the ORC and Parquet format are implemented by using Apache Arrow as a converter, but there is so much memory copy resulting a performance decreasing. 
The question is that it is OK to implement a direct reader/writer to process ORC/Parquet format data?
author: zhanglistar

comments.body: Yes, it will be very appreciated (if there will be performance benefit).

It's ok to use some library better suited for it. And it is even Ok to read the format manually.
For example, we do it for Protobuf :)

title: Unexpected behaviour of AggregatingMergeTree
body:
**Describe what's wrong**

> **AggregatingMergeTree** does not respect expected behaviour for fields of type `SimpleAggregateFunction(max, Array(Tuple(url String, status_code UInt16)))`. 

**Does it reproduce on recent release?**

> Tested on Clickhouse 21.13.1.1 

**How to reproduce**

* ClickHouse server version: 21.13.1.1
* Create a table 
> `CREATE TABLE test_tuple_aggreg
(
    `id` UInt32,
    `session_date` Date,
    `tuples` SimpleAggregateFunction(groupUniqArrayArray(2), Array(Tuple(
        url String,
        status_code UInt16
    )))
)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree
PARTITION BY session_date
ORDER BY id`

* Inspect created table: `SHOW CREATE TABLE test_tuple_aggreg`
> Result: `CREATE TABLE default.test_tuple_aggreg
(
    `id` UInt32,
    `session_date` Date,
    `tuples.url` Array(String),
    `tuples.status_code` Array(UInt16)
)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree
PARTITION BY session_date
ORDER BY id
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192`

We loose track of `SimpleAggregateFunction`.

* Populate the table to see if correct aggregations are used
>  * `INSERT INTO `test_tuple_aggreg` VALUES (1, '2022-01-02', ['url1'], [500])`
>  * `INSERT INTO `test_tuple_aggreg` VALUES (1, '2022-01-03', ['url2'], [404])`
>  * `INSERT INTO `test_tuple_aggreg` VALUES (1, '2022-01-04', ['url3'], [503])`

* When we inspect the data we see all 3 rows
> select * from test_tuple_aggreg

│  1 │   2022-01-02 │ ['url1']   │ [500]              │

**Expected behavior**

    `nested` SimpleAggregateFunction(groupUniqArrayArray(2), Array(Nested( <------------- nested field
        url String,
        status_code UInt16
    )))
)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree
PARTITION BY session_date
ORDER BY id

--------- when trying to insert data into it

INSERT INTO `test_nested_aggreg` VALUES (1, '2022-01-02', ['url1'], [500])

------- I get

Code: 62. DB::Exception: Cannot parse expression of type SimpleAggregateFunction(groupUniqArrayArray(2), Array(Nested(url String, status_code UInt16))) here: ['url1'], [500]): While executing ValuesBlockInputFormat: data for INSERT was parsed from query. (SYNTAX_ERROR)

```
Is it another issue or am I doing something wrong?

>Is it another issue or am I doing something wrong?

Clickhouse creates 2 different structures depending of `flatten_nested` -- **columnS** with Arrays VS a **column** with Arrays of Tuples.
So you should insert accordingly.

two columns `Array(String), Array(String)`
`INSERT INTO test_nested_aggreg VALUES (1, '2022-01-02', ['url1'], [500])` 

 one column `Array(Tuple(String,String))`
`INSERT INTO test_nested_aggreg VALUES (1, '2022-01-04', [('url1', 500)])`

title: Using Kafka engine on cluster with replicas
body:
I am confused about table creating on cluster with replicas. 
For example, the cluster has 4 nodes, config is 2 shards(node_A1, node_B1) and 2 replicas(node_A2, node_B2).
1. create kafka engine table and materialized view on all nodes and the result table using MergeTree engine on cluster
2. create kafka engine table and materialized view only on half of nodes(eg. node_A1 and node_B1), and the result table using ReplicatedMergeTree engine on cluster
What happen if the node with Kafka engine table is broken? Which is the best way about using Kafka engine table？
author: cainiaodidi

comments.body:
First, unlike some other databases, ClickHouse does not have a concept of a "primary node" versus a "replica node". Multiple nodes that hold the same copy of data are both considered replicas, and those replicas are equal in all respects.  Data written to a replicated table on any replica node will be copied to all other replica nodes for that table.

Second, shards in ClickHouse are tables on different ClickHouse nodes that have the same structure but hold different data.  Distributed tables are used to allow queries that combine the data from multiple shards.  Distributed tables require a cluster definition in the \<remote_servers> section of the ClickHouse configuration so that ClickHouse can retrieve that data from all shards of the table.  In your \<remote_servers> cluster definition you will create a list of shards, and within each shard you will add the list of ClickHouse replica nodes where the data for that shard can be retrieved.

Replication of the data for each shard can be implemented in two ways:

A)  Create the table on each replica node using a Replicated version of the appropriate MergeTree engine (such as plain ReplicatedMergeTree or ReplicatedSummingMergeTree).  Metadata about the replicated table will be stored in zookeeper under the zookeeper path set as the first parameter in the Engine definition, and the shard number is normally included in this path.  ClickHouse will automatically keep all replicas of the table in sync for each shard, and as noted above, data inserted into the table on any node will be copies to all other replicas.  In this case the \<internal_replication> element in each shard of the cluster definition must be set to `true`

B)  Create the table with a MergeTree engine that is not replicated, and set the \<internal_replication> element of each shard in the cluster definition to `false`.  In this case data will only be replicated if you insert into a distributed table.  When inserts happen to the distributed table, the node handling the insert will be responsible for inserting a copy of the data into all replicas defined in the shard.  This is less reliable than using zookeeper and Replicated tables, because if some problem happens with copying data to multiple nodes on insert, ClickHouse does not automatically ensure that the replicas hold the same data.

The recommended way to do any replication is to use a ReplicatedMergeTree table, option A above.

Now to get to the Kafka part.  If you try your option 1, create a Kafka engine table and MV and result on all nodes with a MergeTree engine for the "result" table, your materialized view will have to use the distributed table as the actual target so the data is copied to the other replicas.  This will mostly work, but it is not recommended for the same reasons that replication option B is not recommended -- Replicated tables using zookeeper are much more reliable (and also perform better) than using distributed tables for replication.

Your option 2 will also work, but if one of the nodes is down or the Kafka engine is down, all of the data will go to the other node and your shards will be unbalanced for the period that one of the nodes is down.  This imbalance might be okay if you are able to repair the broken node quickly.

Depending on your Kafka volume and number of partitions, it's also possible to add the Kafka engine and materialized view on all four shards even if you are using Replicated tables.  Because consuming multiple partitions will be split among all four nodes, data will not be duplicated.  If one of the four node goes down, data will still be unbalanced, but only half as much.  Adding your Kafka engine to all four nodes will spread the ingest processing cost and increase your reliability.

Thanks a lot, and I am a little confused about this.
> create a Kafka engine table and MV and result on all nodes with a MergeTree engine for the "result" table, your materialized view will have to use the distributed table as the actual target so the data is copied to the other replicas


If create MV on all nodes, How to use the distributed table as the actual target? Could you please write some sql connecting kafka engine table, mv and target table to explain this?


> it's also possible to add the Kafka engine and materialized view on all four shards even if you are using Replicated tables

If I use Replicated tables and four Kafka engine tables consume different partitions, then 'result' table will get different data between node_A1 and node_A2, and I think this will be against with Replicated tables

Again it's not recommended to use a Distributed Table as a target for a materialized view, but it is possible.  The syntax is the same as any other Materialized View using TO:

  ```CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW table_name [TO[db.]name] ```

where db.name is a distributed table.  The target distributed table must exist, and should use a regular MergeTree table as the source table.

If you use the Kafka engine on all four nodes, the data _initially_ inserted on node_A1 from Kafka will be different from the data _initially_ inserted on node_A2, but since they are replicas, inserted data on node_A1 will be quickly copied to node_A2, and vice versa.  Both node_A1 and node_A2 will end up with identical data, just the inserts happened on different nodes.

> If you use the Kafka engine on all four nodes, the data _initially_ inserted on node_A1 from Kafka will be different from the data _initially_ inserted on node_A2, but since they are replicas, inserted data on node_A1 will be quickly copied to node_A2, and vice versa. Both node_A1 and node_A2 will end up with identical data, just the inserts happened on different nodes.

Thanks, I try to understand that. If there are two partitions of topic, node_A1 consumes partition 0 and node_A2 consumes partition 1, and for the replicated result table on node_A1 and node_A2, it will contain data from both two partitions. I used to think that the original data on node_A2 will be deleted when the data is copied from node_A1.

Hi @genzgd thanks for your responses so far.

Would like to ask about an extension to this question assuming we adopt option A described in this thread:
- Would it be possible to optimize queries with a Distributed Table Engine by declaring a shard key that is the same as the partition key declared for the kafka topics consumed for the table targeted? 
- My main concern is about how coordination would work where instances in a shard would be able to inform zookeeper about the values of keys present in its particular shard to allow for `optimize_skip_unused_shards`

title: Does clickhouse allow to use openmp?
body:
Background is I want to do a multi threading memset to set zero of a big memory about 100MB or more, openmp can do this very easily. But I don't see any openmp code in all this project even in the contrib code, So does clickhouse allow to use openmpt to do some parallel things?
Thanks in advance.
author: zhanglistar

comments.body:
Parallelization in ClickHouse is usually done on the level of data pipeline, not for individual loops. So, no use for OpenMP.
It is better to avoid adding OpenMP. What is the place where memset has to be parallelized?

> 

In clickhouse-keeper, there is a hashtable to store all the node data which maybe 10million or billon, resizing process will have to calloc a big memory maybe 100MB 200MB even more, in one thread, this is about 100ms even more to complete, while using openmp will decrease to 30ms which I have tested in local. This code is in critical path of raft state machine running in a single thread, resulting performance decreasing when doing pressing test. After using openmp, the writing speed is much more smooth.

If we use our HashMap, it will do `mmap` for memory chunks 64MB or larger and avoid using memset from userspace, because OS kernel is already zeroing memory. And we cannot avoid this work that is done by OS kernel.

Also if we want to lower the latency (and we do) it makes sense to amortize resizes (by doing incremental data movement from old buffer to the new buffer). It will lower the latency to microseconds range.

> If we use our HashMap, it will do `mmap` for memory chunks 64MB or larger and avoid using memset from userspace, because OS kernel is already zeroing memory. And we cannot avoid this work that is done by OS kernel.
> 
> Also if we want to lower the latency (and we do) it makes sense to amortize resizes (by doing incremental data movement from old buffer to the new buffer). It will lower the latency to microseconds range.

Thanks for your reply. mmap is 30% faster than calloc, but still 2x slower than openmp version memset. OK, I will not use openmp, and using malloc and memset part of memory to reduce latency. 
BTW this is the first buffer that needed to malloc for new hashmap, and need to initialize the managing metadata, the following process is incremental.

title: Having a weird experience with duplicates?
body:
Sorry to be that guy to open an issue that is probably obvious! I have tried to figure out the issue for the last couple of hours but seems to be hitting a brick wall so thought someone with way more experience might be able to help out  😊

I have a table with the following structure:

```
CREATE TABLE test.t_table (
                    symbol LowCardinality(String),
                    ex_timestamp DateTime64(3),
                    local_timestamp DateTime64(3),
                    price Decimal(38, 8),
                    amount Decimal(38, 8),
                    size Decimal(38, 8)
) ENGINE = MergeTree()
      PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(timestamp)
      ORDER BY (symbol, ex_timestamp, local_timestamp, price, amount, size);
```
	  
	  
I then populated the table with the following:

```
INSERT INTO test.t_table
SELECT
       symbol,
       fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(CAST(toInt64(ex_timestamp) / 1000, 'Int64'), 'UTC') as ts1,
       fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(CAST(toInt64(local_timestamp) / 1000, 'Int64'), 'UTC') as ts2,
       toFloat64OrZero(price) as price,
       toFloat64OrZero(amount) as amount,
       toFloat64OrZero(size) as size
FROM test.source_table;
```

However if i run any type of SELECT query, it returns duplicate records for every row, So for example every row comes twice, to verify this i performed the following duplicate check:

```
SELECT
	count() AS cnt
FROM  test.t_table
WHERE t_table.timestamp = '2021-12-30'
GROUP BY *
HAVING cnt > 1

┌─cnt─┐
│   2 │
└─────┘ 

```

Which returns the count of 2 but if i run the exact same query on the source table it returns a count of 0.

At this point i am thinking there has to be something wrong with populating the table which has caused duplicates but what is confusing me is the fact the total count of rows in both tables are exactly the same.

Could this be an issue with the LowCardinality, Partition or the way i have the ORDER BY above?

My last resort is to delete all data from the test_table and re-insert but there is several billion rows so i thought asking for advice prior might help reduce the risk of the outcome being the same.

Thanks guys and happy new year! :-)
author: BirdyUK

comments.body:
1. CH version?
2. `timestamp = '2021-12-30'` , I guess timestamp is DateTime64 , and this comparison DateTime64 = '2021-12-30' can produce unexpected behaviour in some versions.
3. I don't see `timestamp` column in the t_table

title: when data will be merged in a same partition?
body:
I found there are 3 files in a same partition 2 days ago.and them not continuous.
 when I use
```
OPTIMIZE table xxx partition(20211221);
```
and data in 20211221 will be merged a single file and they are continuous,that seems ok,
why when I  not execute the optimize command and data will not be merged a single file
author: FunkyYang

comments.body:
Merges are eventual and may never happen. It depends on the number of inserts that happened after, the number of parts in the partition, size of parts. If the total size of input parts are greater than the maximum part size then they will never be merged.


It is very unreasonable to constantly merge up to one part.
Merger does not have such goal. In the contrary the goal is to have the minimum number of parts withing smallest number of merges. Merges consume the huge amount of disk and processor resources.

It makes no sense to merge two 300GB parts into one 600GB part for 3 hours. Merger have to read, decompress 600GB, merge, compress, write them back, after that the performance of the selects will not grow at all or will grow minimally.

author: cainiaodidi

comments.body:
You can use a multiplexing feature of Distributed table.


So you create an additional cluster `remote_serves` where all Clickhouse nodes a replicas in a single shard with internal_replication = false
Then you create a Distributed table using that new cluster.
Then you insert data into Distributed table and Distributed table multiplex inserts and write exactly the same data to all replicas (to all engine=Join tables).

Then you use `select count(1) from join` -- you don't need to use select count(1) from `_dist` because all join tables have the same data.

author: andrelec1

comments.body:
Performance reasons. CH avoids nullable types by default.

see: `  --aggregate_functions_null_for_empty arg                             Rewrite all aggregate functions in a query, adding -OrNull suffix to them`

```sql

select max(date) from (select today() date where 0)
┌──max(date)─┐
│ 1970-01-01 │
└────────────┘

select maxOrNull(date) from (select today() date where 0)
┌─maxOrNull(date)─┐
│            ᴺᵁᴸᴸ │
└─────────────────┘

select max(toNullable(date)) from (select today() date where 0)
┌─max(toNullable(date))─┐
│                  ᴺᵁᴸᴸ │
└───────────────────────┘

set aggregate_functions_null_for_empty=1
select max(date) from (select today() date where 0);
┌─maxOrNull(date)─┐
│            ᴺᵁᴸᴸ │
└─────────────────┘
```

title: Access rights changes during ALTER FREEZE
body:
### Describe the unexpected behaviour
When I make a backup of the table, the data rights are set to `0440`

```
ALTER TABLE DB.TABLE FREEZE WITH NAME 'ffff'
```

```
# ll data/DB/TABLE/202012_124_374523_16/
total 16641004
drwxr-x---  2 clickhouse clickhouse       4096 Dec  6 00:08 ./
drwxr-x--- 19 clickhouse clickhouse    1880064 Dec  6 00:13 ../
-r--r-----  2 clickhouse clickhouse   34828116 Dec  6 00:08 attr_type.bin
-r--r-----  2 clickhouse clickhouse         57 Dec  6 00:08 attr_type.dict.bin
...
```

### How to reproduce

```
ALTER TABLE DB.TABLE FREEZE WITH NAME 'ffff'
```

#### Which ClickHouse server version to use
```
SELECT version()

┌─version()──┐
│ 21.11.5.33 │
└────────────┘
```
### Expected behavior
There will be no expectation that the file permissions will change. For example, in version `21.7.7.47` this is not noticed.
author: k0st1an

comments.body: Also the problem detected in version `21.11.2.2`.

This behaviour exists since the beginning (when FREEZE command was introduced) and needed to protect files that were hardlinked and to avoid modification of backups. As all files in ClickHouse are immutable, additionally making them readonly should not be a concern.

title: Checksums of parts don't match: hash of uncompressed files doesn't match
body: <Error> dbname.tablename (ad765d86-7735-4217-ad76-5d867735b217): Code: 40, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Checksums of parts don't match: hash of uncompressed files doesn't match (version 21.7.5.29 (official build)). Data after merge is not byte-identical to data on another replicas. There could be several reasons: 1. Using newer version of compression library after server update. 2. Using another compression method. 3. Non-deterministic compression algorithm (highly unlikely). 4. Non-deterministic merge algorithm due to logical error in code. 5. Data corruption in memory due to bug in code. 6. Data corruption in memory due to hardware issue. 7. Manual modification of source data after server startup. 8. Manual modification of checksums stored in ZooKeeper. 9. Part format related settings like 'enable_mixed_granularity_parts' are different on different replicas. We will download merged part from replica to force byte-identical result.
author: wlwqq

comments.body:
There could be several reasons: 
1. Using newer version of compression library after server update. 
2. Using another compression method. 
3. Non-deterministic compression algorithm (highly unlikely). 
4. Non-deterministic merge algorithm due to logical error in code. 
5. Data corruption in memory due to bug in code. 
6. Data corruption in memory due to hardware issue. 
7. Manual modification of source data after server startup. 
8. Manual modification of checksums stored in ZooKeeper. 
9. Part format related settings like 'enable_mixed_granularity_parts' are different on different replicas. 

ClickHouse will download merged part from replica to force byte-identical result.

title: Skip index file
body: I want to know more about the skip index, but when I look at the skp_idx_[cloumn].idx file, I can't understand the contents because it is binary, is there any command to view the file?
author: zqw961025

comments.body: Unfortunately there is not a command or tool to independently view the data in a skip index file.  In addition the binary format differs by skip index type -- the values for a bloom filter index are stored differently than the simpler minmax index.  The actual serialization is controlled by the implementation of IMergeTreeIndexGranule for each index type -- see, for example, the relatively simple function `MergeTreeIndexGranuleMinMax::serializeBinary` in `MergeTreeIndexMinMax.cpp`.

title: Are select queries aware of detach?
body:
If my select query is running and I issue a detach command on a partition(which is being processed by the select query in question), will the select query still read the partition data? 

I am not able to test this because my select queries are super fast so I would like to confirm it.
author: gauravphoenix

comments.body:
I was able to experiment with this by putting a lot of data in my table and then performing a select. 
Not only I did `detach`, I went to the store directory and did `rm -rf *` to remove the detached partitions. 

so my question is no longer about "if" but rather "how". 

when select queries are being run, and I have already performed detach and removed the files, where is the data being read from?

The mystery is solved now, I did some more investigations and it seems that when `detach` command is executed, the data is **not** removed immediately from the store directory when `select` queries are running. The copy to detach directory still occurs but not the removal and hence select queries are able to see the data. 


it will be nice to have documentation updated to reflect this
Yes, the data parts are refcounted, and removed only after the latest query finished.
@alexey-milovidov does refcount apply to attach commands too? Can I safely run attach commands when select queries are being run?

Yes, you can.

The same mechanics allows to run multiple INSERT and SELECT queries concurrently and multiple background merges without locks. This is fundamental for ClickHouse.

And even more... if you use Atomic database (by default), you can DROP table during SELECT without any locks and waiting :)
It's magic.

title: Can a properly set partition key speed up the SELECT query?
body:
Hi All,
When I encountered too many parts error, I noticed that there was such a sentence in the error report: **Please note, that partitioning is not intended to speed up SELECT queries (ORDER BY key is sufficient to make range queries fast). Partitions are intended for data manipulation (DROP PARTITION, etc).. (TOO_MANY_PARTS)**
This is somewhat inconsistent with my view of partition keys all the time. If CH will divide the data into different directories according to the partition key, then the correctly set partition key should greatly improve the SELECT query speed, because this allows CH to skip a lot unwanted directory according to the partition key. In my opinion, the biggest impact on performance is the partition key, followed by the ORDER BY key, and finally the index. Am I right? (May be I should read the source code)
author: fsgdgsdfgsgd

comments.body:
There is no contradiction. 
The main goal of partitioning is to manage data retention (drop old data). Also partition pruning speed ups queries. 
BUT you should choose partitioning based to satisfy data retention requirements.
