title: RepliactedMergeTree is readonly if one zookeeper in the cluster in not available, stopped servers do not start
body:
Hi,

I have come across an odd behavior of the clickhouse-server when one zookeeper from an otherwise healthy cluster becomes unavailable. The behavior in case of zookeeper failure is not covered by the documentation and I am not sure if this is working as intended.

I have set up replication with a cluster of 5 zookeepers. If I shut down only 1 of the 5 zookeepers, the replication stops working, although the 4 remaining zookeepers are healthy and functioning. The effects are:

* replicated tables on running servers become read only
* stopped clickhouse-servers fail to start.

Only after I manually remove the missing zookeeper from the clickhouse-server config the write requests start working again and the shut-down server can start without failure. No need to bring back the missing zookeeper node.

So it seems that when you set up replication following the documentation, every one of the zookeepers is a single point of failure, although the zookeepers themselves are set up for high availability.
Am I missing something e.g. undocumented configuration or is this the intended behavior?

**How to reproduce**

1. ClickHouse version 21.10.2.15 (official build)
2. Configure zookeeper nodes
3. Shut down one of the zookeepers while still having a number of functional nodes > quorum
4. Try to insert data into a replicated table or (re-)start a clickhouse-server


**Expected behavior**
If at least one of the configured zookeeper nodes answers requests, it means that it fulfilled its configured criteria to be considered healthy (meaning a the configured quorum was reached). So the clickhouse-server should try ALL configured nodes before failing. 

**Error message and/or stacktrace**
When I shut down the zookeeper then the clickhouse-server logs:

1. `<Error> [...]: void DB::StorageReplicatedMergeTree::queueUpdatingTask(): Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Session expired (Session expired). (KEEPER_EXCEPTION)`
2. `<Warning> [...]: ZooKeeper session has expired. Switching to a new session.`
3. `<Error> zkutil::EphemeralNodeHolder::~EphemeralNodeHolder(): Cannot remove /clickhouse/tables/01/[...]/replicas/[...]/is_active: : Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Session expired (Session expired). (KEEPER_EXCEPTION)`
4. `<Information> [...]: Stopped being leader`
5. `<Error> [...]: void DB::ReplicatedMergeTreeRestartingThread::run(): Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: All connection tries failed while connecting to ZooKeeper. nodes: [... missing nodes IP:PORT ...]`
6. `<Error> executeQuery: Code: 242. DB::Exception: Table is in readonly mode (zookeeper path: /clickhouse/tables/01/[...]). (TABLE_IS_READ_ONLY) (version 21.10.2.15 (official build)) (from 192.168.28.159:54816) (in query: INSERT INTO [...] VALUES)`

(Re-)starting a clickhouse-server with the zookeeper node missing leads do the clickhouse-server logging timeouts to the zookeeper node and shutting down again.
author: mgehlmann

comments.body:
It's really unexpected. I turned off one of 3 ZK node hundreds of time, no impact on CH.

Can you show how zookeeper is configured in your CH.

Now:

```
All zookeepers up:

title: How to add versioning column for existing ReplicatedReplacingMergedTree-engine table
body:
Hi guys,

I created a table with ReplicatedReplacingMergedTree engine (no versioning column specifed).

I would like to ask if there is a way to ALTER the table and add a versioning column? 

I have 500GB of data on the table already so it would be not easy to create a new table and insert everything again.

Many thanks!
author: tranvinhthuy

comments.body: ReplacingMergedTree or ReplicatedReplacingMergedTree ?

> ReplacingMergedTree or ReplicatedReplacingMergedTree ?

sorry I specified more, it's ReplicatedReplacingMergedTree

There is no easy/safe way for Replicated. 

You can use `attach partition from`. This command almost instant and almost free and does not copy data on a disk, but clones the data using hardlinks (it's possible with tables with any size).

```sql
-- test data
CREATE TABLE test (key Int64, ts DateTime, s String)
ENGINE = ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree ('/clickhouse/{cluster}/{database}/tables/{shard}/sometest','{replica}')
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(ts)
ORDER BY (key);

insert into test select number, today(), '' from numbers(10000);

-- new table with ver column
CREATE TABLE new on cluster .... (key Int64, ts DateTime, s String)
ENGINE = ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree ('/clickhouse/{cluster}/{database}/tables/{shard}/sometest_v2','{replica}', ts)
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(ts)
ORDER BY (key);

-- generate alters
select concat('alter table new', ' attach partition id \'', partition_id, '\' from test;')
from system.parts 
where active = 1 and table like 'test' 
group by database,table,partition_id
order by database,table,partition_id 

alter table new attach partition id '202110' from test;

select count() from new
--
10000

rename table test to old, new to test;

--eventually
drop table old.
```

> ```sql
> partition_id
> ```

Thank you very much for your answer.

I would like to ask what could be unsafe during the `attach partition from` operation? So we could prepare before executing this.

(FYI, in our setup we only have 1 main CH instance and 1 replica instance + zookeeper. We can stop the replication any time and/or recreate the replica instance during table altering).

>I would like to ask what could be unsafe during the

Nothing unsafe in this way. And you can make a backup just in case `alter table test freeze`.
Obviously you need to stop ingestion because you will insert into the old table and the new table will miss these during maintenance inserts.

------

>There is no easy/safe way for Replicated.

I meant there is another way. Edit .sql files and all ZK metadata records for existing table. 
For example for non-replicated tables IN THIS CASE you can execute `detach table`, edit .sql file, `attach table`. No need for the second table and attach ... and other.

>(FYI, in our setup we only have 1 main CH instance and 1 replica instance + zookeeper. We can stop the replication any >time and/or recreate the replica instance during table altering).

If you create the new table on all replicas then everything will be consistent.  Replicated table executes `alter table attach from` on all replicas. After that you need to execute `rename table test to old, new to test;` on all replicas or on_cluster (not sure is it possible with rename multiple tables or not. Probably `rename table xxx to yyy on cluster; rename table zzz to qqqq on cluster ` should work.

Thank you so much for the help!

I will proceed with this and close this issue when it is done.

title: Questions about clickhouse-copier
body:
We would like to use clickhouse-copier tool to copy data between clusters as part of a production workflow. I appreciate if you can answer the following questions:
1. Would clickhouse-copier ever drop partitions or remove data from destination table? If so, how to guarantee this wouldn’t occur? It's mentioned in the documentation page that skipping `<enabled_partitions>` config can cause deletion of destination partitions:
> This section specifies partitions that should be copied, other partition will be ignored. … Since partition key of source and destination cluster could be different, these partition names specify destination partitions.
>
> NOTE: In spite of this section is optional (if it is not specified, all partitions will be copied), it is strictly recommended to specify them explicitly.
>
> If you already have some ready partitions on destination cluster they will be removed at the start of the copying since they will be interpeted as unfinished data from the previous copying!!!
2. What kind of inconsistencies are expected if source table changes? In case of insertion into source table, is it guaranteed that all rows already existing before starting copying process will be copied? Could insertion of new rows into destination table during the process lead to any inconsistencies?
3. How to make sure that copying process completed successfully (i.e. all rows are copied to destination table and helper tables are cleaned up)? In some cases `ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM *_piece_* ...` and `DROP TABLE ... *_piece_*` fail because of `max_partition_size_to_drop` limitation.

Update 2: Even though it failed to attach some partitions/pieces to destination table, it proceeds as if there are no errors then it drops helper tables. Also, getting status of the task doesn't indicate any errors (i.e. `{"table_page_data_copy_local":{"all_partitions_count":4,"processed_partitions_count":4}}`), that's why I'm asking if there is a reliable way to know whether it completed successfully.
HI @den-crane. Can you help us get answers to these questions? Thanks in advance.
A kind reminder @den-crane @nikitamikhaylov

> 1. Would clickhouse-copier ever drop partitions or remove data from destination table? If so, how to guarantee this wouldn’t occur? It's mentioned in the documentation page that skipping `<enabled_partitions>` config can cause deletion of destination partitions:
> 
> > This section specifies partitions that should be copied, other partition will be ignored. … Since partition key of source and destination cluster could be different, these partition names specify destination partitions.
> > NOTE: In spite of this section is optional (if it is not specified, all partitions will be copied), it is strictly recommended to specify them explicitly.
> > If you already have some ready partitions on destination cluster they will be removed at the start of the copying since they will be interpeted as unfinished data from the previous copying!!!
> 

This is true for clickhouse-copier 20.3 and earlier.
Since 20.4 clickhouse-copier does not drop partitions in destination tables.

> 2. What kind of inconsistencies are expected if source table changes? In case of insertion into source table, is it guaranteed that all rows already existing before starting copying process will be copied? Could insertion of new rows into destination table during the process lead to any inconsistencies?

clcikhouse-copier simply runs INSERT INTO ... SELECT FROM queries.
If you continue to modify data in source or destination tables, all kinds of inconsistencies are expected.

> Since 20.4 clickhouse-copier does not drop partitions in destination tables.

Correction: since 21.7 there is a flag to drop partitions in destination tables (`allow_to_drop_target_partitions`)

title: Session expired with zookeeper
author: zhangjmruc

comments.body: I remember seeing similar errors in production, however it's recoverable in less than several minutes. I'm not sure if it's indeed a bug.

> I remember seeing similar errors in production, however it's recoverable in less than several minutes. I'm not sure if it's indeed a bug.

The comment in enterLeaderElection() indicates that there is an assumption that the current_zookeeper is not changed and is alive. I don't know many detail in the leader election logic. So whether this will happen when the CK server is slow and session expired before exitLeaderElection() is called.

"current_zookeeper lives for the lifetime of leader_election, since before changing `current_zookeeper`, `leader_election` object is destroyed in `partialShutdown` method"

> CH do automically establish a new session with ZooKeeper, but some underlying class cannot see or use it, but only the old expired one.

It's intended, and it's correct behavior, not a bug. Usually it's bad idea to just switch to another session while executing some complex operation (especially, when ephemeral nodes are involved), because it may cause tons of consistency issues.

> > CH do automically establish a new session with ZooKeeper, but some underlying class cannot see or use it, but only the old expired one.
> 
> It's intended, and it's correct behavior, not a bug. Usually it's bad idea to just switch to another session while executing some complex operation (especially, when ephemeral nodes are involved), because it may cause tons of consistency issues.

@tavplubix I also found that in ReplicateMergeTree logic, CH just get the current_zookeeper via getZooKeeper() and no valid check on it. If the zk session in current_zookeeper is already expired, then wrong zookeeper will be passed to undering methos for complex operations.
It's really not friend to customer that when this happens always, what we can do is only wait or restart the server. 
Since now All the Replicated MergeTree engines share ONE zookeeper session, but they may be not aware of the changes of current_zookeeper due to expire. Why don't they share a reference to the pointer of zookeeper object, so all usages can see the latest, VALID zookeeper session.

	`vehicle_no` String,

ORDER BY (vehicle_no, alarm_code, alarm_time)

title: question about license

Hi, i'm thinking about this.

author: wzisheng

comments.body:
Our usage of the libraries that are under LGPL is compliant with the terms of their respective licenses.
That's how we can use them.

You can read the licenses in `SELECT * FROM system.licenses` and check that ClickHouse complies with all the license terms.

If you want to create a derivative product on top of ClickHouse, you must also make sure, that your product comply with the terms of all licenses.

title: Difference between optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key and distributed_group_by_no_merge
body: What is the difference between  optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key and distributed_group_by_no_merge ?
author: DipalPrajapati

comments.body:
Basically the same, but `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` is smarter and works only if sharding key is appropriate. 

distributed_group_by_no_merge -- is a directive it's applied to a query unconditionally.

 optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key -- basically the same but it's works only if `optimize_skip_unused_shards=1` and `sharding expression matches groupby section`.

title: system.numbers get timeout when where clause is specified
body:
My clickhouse version is 21.7.6.39

In my case I need to get some sequences from specified number.
I use `numbers(1000)` at first,but it can't be used in read only mode.

So I follow #18854 and turn to use ` system.numbers `.
But I found that I can only get `read timed out` when the `where` clause is specified.

Is this a bug?

Here is my SQL 
```
 SELECT * FROM system.numbers where number>10 and number<20;
```
author: wolgy

comments.body:
`WHERE` conditions aren't pushed into `system.numbers` so you need to provide a `LIMIT` clause so it knows when to stop generating numbers.

For example:
```
 SELECT * FROM system.numbers LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10;
```

title: Query result column name problem
body:
clickhouse version
```
SELECT version()

Query id: 4b24f690-5c72-4c64-81ad-ffaa5b8cd918

┌─version()─┐
│ 21.9.4.35 │
└───────────┘

```
table structure
```sql
CREATE TABLE t1
(
    `id` Int,
    `name` String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

CREATE TABLE t2
(
    `id` Int,
    `name` String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY id
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

insert into t1 values(1, 'fan1');
insert into t1 values(2, 'fan2');
insert into t1 values(3, 'fan3');
insert into t1 values(4, 'fan4');
insert into t1 values(5, 'fan5');
insert into t1 values(6, 'fan6');
insert into t1 values(7, 'fan7');
insert into t1 values(8, 'fan8');
insert into t1 values(9, 'fan9');


insert into t2 values(2, 'dba');
insert into t2 values(3, 'rd');
insert into t2 values(4, 'sre');
insert into t2 values(5, 'ops');

insert into t2 values(7, 'rd');
insert into t2 values(8, 'sre');
insert into t2 values(9, 'ops');

insert into t2 values(13, 'ops');


```
t1,t2 both have column `name`

```sql
SELECT
    t1.id,
    t2.name
FROM t1
INNER JOIN t2 ON t1.id = t2.id
WHERE (t1.id > 2) AND (t1.id < 5)

Query id: 0a847a1b-9fd7-493e-b3d3-7f65e2657d74

┌─id─┬─t2.name─┐
│  3 │ rd      │
│  3 │ rd      │
│  4 │ sre     │
│  4 │ sre     │
└────┴─────────┘
```
It is common knowledge that the column names in the query results should be `id`, `name`
but in clickhouse, `name` become `t2.name`
This causes the following sql to also report an error
```sql
SELECT *
FROM
(
    SELECT
        t2.name,
        sum(t1.id) AS sum_id
    FROM t1
    LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.id = t2.id
    WHERE (t1.id > 2) AND (t1.id < 5)
    GROUP BY t2.name
) AS tt
WHERE tt.name = 'sre'

Query id: bdf23dae-1e15-4243-afeb-3aedf78848f1


0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.003 sec. 

Received exception from server (version 21.9.4):
Code: 47. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: There's no column 'tt.name' in table 'tt': While processing tt.name: While processing SELECT * FROM (SELECT t2.name, sum(t1.id) AS sum_id FROM t1 LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE (t1.id > 2) AND (t1.id < 5) GROUP BY t2.name) AS tt WHERE tt.name = 'sre'. (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)

```
The problem lies in t2.name, which needs to be changed to this
```sql
SELECT *
FROM
(
    SELECT
        t2.name,
        sum(t1.id) AS sum_id
    FROM t1
    LEFT JOIN t2 ON t1.id = t2.id
    WHERE (t1.id > 2) AND (t1.id < 5)
    GROUP BY t2.name
) AS tt
WHERE tt.t2.name = 'sre'

Query id: 2c1f53e8-6d5f-4300-b9d1-d6d564188dc6

┌─t2.name─┬─sum_id─┐
│ sre     │      8 │
└─────────┴────────┘
```
>tt.t2.name looks rather strange


This problem leads to complex subquery associations where all columns must be aliased, otherwise all sorts of strange errors or query results are reported
author: Fanduzi

comments.body:
>It is common knowledge that the column names in the query results should be id, name

Clickhouse way of naming query columns is simply different from your expectations. Use aliases.

> > It is common knowledge that the column names in the query results should be id, name
> 
> Clickhouse way of naming query columns is simply different from your expectations. Use aliases.

Indeed, this is a problem that can be explained in one sentence: clickhouse's sql dialect features. However, this results in users having to use aliases repeatedly in self-associative and complex subquery scenarios, and I have encountered problems when only some subqueries use aliases and the sql still works but with incorrect results. 

And is there any information about this in the official documentation? I didn't find any. I think It may not be a technical problem, but it is a user experience problem 🙃

title: Is it possible to calculate number of distinct keys in map?
body:
I have a map type field. Is there a way to calculate how many times each of distinct keys encounter in the whole table?

Say I have a table from the example in the docs:

`CREATE TABLE table_map (a Map(String, UInt64)) ENGINE=Memory;`
`INSERT INTO table_map VALUES ({'key1':1, 'key2':10}), ({'key1':2,'key2':20}), ({'key1':3,'key2':30});`

Can I write a query like this?

`SELECT
    a.keys,
    count(a.keys) AS cnt
FROM table_map
GROUP BY a.keys
ORDER BY cnt DESC`

This query counts distinct set of keys, but can it be rewritten to count keys?
author: sogawa-sps

comments.body:
You can use `arrayJoin` for that

```sql
SELECT arrayJoin(a.keys) as keys, count() as cnt FROM table_map GROUP BY keys ORDER BY cnt DESC;
```

```
┌─keys─┬─cnt─┐
│ key2 │   3 │
│ key1 │   3 │
└──────┴─────┘
```

Reopen this issue if this solution is not suitable for your case
Thanks a lot!

title: Big mutation count stops updates?
body:
I have seen if table mutation count is greater than above 100 - 1000 (aprox.) they suddenly stop progressing.

And this is very inconvenient.

What is happens?

Is there way to change this behavior?

```
author: Grian

comments.body:
ClickHouse is designed for immutable data.  Its high performance is dependent on sparse indexes (in the default case there is only a single index value for every 8192 rows), and keeping all of the columnar data in the table sorted by those indexes.  Accordingly mutations are very expensive, and in many cases require resorting and rewriting one or more columns for all the data.  If there are a 100+ mutations running at once, this will definitely degrade ClickHouse performance.

In general you should only run mutations in exceptional circumstances, they should not be part of a regular business process.  Also mutations lock the affected table while processing, so only one mutation should be executed at a time in any case.

Lightweight mutations are on the roadmap for 2022, so this situation could change in the future.

you can use alter and change  fields length.

title: Slower uniq in materialized view compared to normal query on base table
body:
Title says it all..

Reproducable by following this:
(using ClickHouse server version 21.9.1 revision 54449)

```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nf
(
    `clientIP` String,
    `serverIP` String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY (serverIP, clientIP)
```
```
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW nf_uniq_mv
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree
ORDER BY (serverIP)
AS
SELECT
    serverIP,
    uniqState(clientIP) as uniq_clientIP
FROM nf
GROUP BY (serverIP)
```

```
INSERT INTO nf (clientIP, serverIP)
SELECT
    IPv4NumToString(toUInt32(toUInt32(16777216 + rand(2) % 16777215))),
    IPv4NumToString(toUInt32(toUInt32(16908288 + rand(2) % 65535)))
FROM numbers_mt(100000000)
```

Query the materialized view:
`select serverIP, uniqMerge(uniq_clientIP) as uniq_cips from nf_uniq_mv GROUP BY (serverIP);`
Result: 65535 rows in set. Elapsed: 33.561 sec. Processed 131.07 thousand rows, 20.30 MB (3.91 thousand rows/s., 604.81 KB/s.)

Query the base table:
`select serverIP, uniq(clientIP) as uniq_cips from nf GROUP BY serverIP;`
Result: 65535 rows in set. Elapsed: 5.259 sec. Processed 100.00 million rows, 3.99 GB (19.01 million rows/s., 757.75 MB/s.)

Querying the base table results in processing 99,868,930 more rows than querying the materialized view. Yet, it takes 28.302 LONGER to get the same results back.

I would expect the materialized view to be faster than querying the base table.

```

SETTINGS index_granularity = 512 AS

    serverIP,
    uniqHLL12State(clientIP) AS uniq_clientIP

select serverIP, uniqHLL12Merge(uniq_clientIP) as uniq_cips from nf_uniq_mv GROUP BY (serverIP) format Null;

Is there a ratio where it would be more performent to use the Merge notation instead of just querying the raw data?

@PyCht

In both cases processes is about the same number of rows and the same amount of data. Why do you expect that MatView will be faster? Your matview should be 100 times smaller in number of rows, then you can expect improvement.

title: Non standart aggregation with GROUP BY
body:
** SQL **
```
SELECT MAX(1)  FROM (SELECT 1) one WHERE 1 = 0 GROUP BY NULL;
```
Current result:

```
┌─max(1)─┐
│      0 
└──────┘
```

Expected SQL Standart behavior (MySQL, sqlite, etc):

```
mysql> SELECT MAX(1)  FROM (SELECT 1) one WHERE 1 = 0 GROUP BY NULL;

title: Enable to run aggregations in TTL without GROUP BY
body:
**Use case**

We are syncing MySQL to Clickhouse, but Clickhouse does not support well mutations (UPDATE, DELETE) that's why we came with a snapshot strategy in order to keep the data sync. 


We create two tables for each MySQL table: snapshot and landing.
The schema of the process is the following:

- Initial dump of the tables is inserted in the snapshot table
- Changes are being inserted in the landing table
- Periodically, a script will generate a new snapshot by merging the last changes with the last snapshot

When we want to get the data, we just need to query the last snapshot and everything is fine.

This approach works great as everything is just inserts and selects, no mutations. Less problems.
But there is a catch, the disk. 

The less lag (time needed to have a change inside the snapshot ), we want. The more frequent the script needs to run and the more disk we will need. For this, we could add a TTL to the table. 

But on the other hand, the less TTL time, the less time window we have to fix issues if something breaks. Having a small TTL could lead to losing data, so we need to have a balance.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

In this situation, it would be great to be able to define a TTL like 

```sql
TTL snapshot_time + 1 INTERVAL HOUR WHERE max(snapshot_time) != snapshot_time
```

If we would be able to define a TTL like the one above if the script would stop working, we will always keep the last snapshot. Avoiding losing data and being able to reduce TTL time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Any idea or approach to dealing with real-time synchronization with MySQL is appreciated. We have checked the other MergeTree engines, but we have had no luck.
author: alexon1234

How you can find max(snapshot_time) ?
`select max(snapshot_time) from snapshot_table` ?
Yes.

So you can make a dictionary, with a query `select 1 id, max(snapshot_time) x from snapshot_table`

And then TTL rule `TTL snapshot_time + 1 INTERVAL HOUR WHERE gictGet(..., 'x', 1) != snapshot_time`

title: Mutations performance characteristics
body:
Hi ClickHouse team,

I have some questions about the CH delete mutations:
1. Does the mutation processing time depend on the complexity of the mutation query?
2. Do update mutations perform significantly faster than the delete ones?
3. We noticed an increase in the query processing time during the mutations (like 2x). Is this expected? The metrics do not show a significant drop in CPU or memory during the mutation time?

Thank you!
author: ibradwan

comments.body:
1. maybe.
2. Yes. If you have 400 columns in a table, update of a single column can be ~400 times faster than delete.
3. yes. Mutations cause high disk i/o -> cache spoiling. Basically mutation reads all data from related partitions and uncompresses all data / mutates / compresses and writes data back.

Mutations are admin operation implemented to satisfy GDPR. You should not use them on daily basis.

I see. So to give some context, our mutation query is just a plain filtering delete query, but the `WHERE` condition could get complex in terms of the number of conditions (but every condition is just equal, greater, ...etc). Also, the fields on which we filter could be non-primary or sort keys. Please check the sample query below for reference.

So in light of this, let me ask other questions regarding point one:
* In the mutation execution plan, I believe you apply the select query in order to know which parts & blocks to mutate. The effect of the query complexity on this part should be negligible compared to the total mutation time.
Now I suppose you check the filtering condition for every row you scan to see if it's going to be changed or not. The cost for this step should be almost equivalent to the step of running the query on the whole table (`Sum(applying a filter on one row) ~= applying the filter of the whole table`). If this is the case, then the query complexity should not be a big factor in the mutation time. This is probably a naive way of thinking about the mutations internals, but is there a reason that makes the query complexity contribution to the total mutation time significant? If yes, then do you have any recommendations for a query similar to the one below?
* Would it make a difference if we filter on primary/sort key fields only?
* Would it make a difference to add data-skipping indexes on non-primary/sort keys fields?

For debugability, is there a way to know if a mutation got stuck, or if it is still processing?

title: CSV parsing failure in case of nested double quotes
body:
**Describe what's wrong**
CSV parsing fails if there are nested double quotes.

**Does it reproduce on recent release?**
Yes

**How to reproduce**
Table:
```
CREATE TABLE test.test
(
    `id` Int,
    `task` String,
    `hours` Float32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PRIMARY KEY id
ORDER BY id
```

File:
`1,"Build - '"Products'" tab",1`

Import:
`clickhouse-client --query "INSERT INTO test.test FORMAT CSV" < /mnt/c/temp/test.csv`

**Expected behavior**
Import processed successfully. Parser is able to identify nested double quotes.

**Error message and/or stacktrace**
```
Code: 27. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected , before: Products\'" tab",1: (at row 1)

Row 1:
Column 0,   name: id,    type: Int32,   parsed text: "1"
Column 1,   name: task,  type: String,  parsed text: "<DOUBLE QUOTE>Build - <SINGLE QUOTE><DOUBLE QUOTE>"
ERROR: There is no delimiter (,). "P" found instead.
```

**Additional context**
OS: Windows
Version: 21.9.3.30
Server: Docker over WSL2
CLI: Ubuntu over WSL2
author: sogawa-sps

comments.body:
CSV does not support nested quotes without proper escaping and there is no theoretical way to implement this support.

Example:

Suppose we have a table with two fields: `a String, b String` and a CSV data:
```
"Hello","World","Goodbye"
```

Then it can be parsed as:

`"Hello","World"`, `"Goodbye"`
or
`"Hello"`, `"World","Goodbye"`

The proper way is to escape quotes like this:

```
"Hello"",""World","Goodbye"
```

@alexey-milovidov thank you for you answer but it I think it's totally valid case if there are no commas inside. For example PostgreSQL processes such a file correctly. And OpenCSV is also able to properly parse such a file.

Actually it was an export from PostgreSQL. I tried to migrate my data from it to ClickHouse and it failed so I can't start working with this DB. PostgreSQL can ingest it back properly.

@sogawa-sps Clickhouse does not support this escaping. There is no strict standard for CSV escaping. Clickhouse has own datatypes and own rules for escaping.

You can use `"Build - ""Products"" tab"`  or `'Build - "Products" tab'`.

```bash
psql > \copy (select 'Build - "Products" tab' x) to 'temp.csv' with csv ;

$ cat temp.csv
"Build - ""Products"" tab"
```
Thank you @den-crane, will try.

title: How to rebalance data in clickhouse cluster after adding new nodes
body: I could find a lot of documentation on how to setup clickhouse cluster; but none on expanding existing cluster and rebalance data. Can someone help me with pointers on the same. Is there any best practices on this from clickhouse?
author: abhilash-radhakrishnaru

comments.body:
There is no good and easy solution. 
Moreover there is no way magically extract part of rows from old shards and move them to the new.

You can define the new shard with bigger weight then this shard will get more data and eventually all shard became even. 

If you need row-level resharding you can only reinsert data. (by any tool: inset / select ; clickhouse-copier ...)
If you don't you can detach some old part from the old shards and copy them to the new nodes and attach them there.

body:
If you execute this commands
```
create table TestBudaBest
(
    id        UInt64,
    name      String,

) ENGINE = MergeTree primary key id;

insert into TestBudaBest
values (1, 'Bob', 1),
       (2, 'Job', 2),
       (3, 'Jim', 3);

(
    id   UInt64,
    name String
) engine MergeTree primary key id;

insert into Country (id, name)
values (1, 'Moscow'),
       (2, 'London'),
       (3, 'Tokyo');

create dictionary CountryDict
    (
    id UInt64,
    name String
    )
    PRIMARY KEY id
    SOURCE (
        Clickhouse(
        PORT 9000
        USER ''
        HOST '127.0.0.1'
        PASSWORD ''
        DB 'test_db'
        TABLE 'Country'
        FAIL_ON_CONNECTION_LOSS 'false'
        )
        )
    LIFETIME (MIN 0 MAX 1800)
    LAYOUT (HASHED());

create view TestBudaBestAndCountryView
as
    select id, name, dictGet('CountryDict', 'name', countryId) as countryName from TestBudaBest;

create dictionary TestBudaBestAndCountryDict
(
    id        UInt64,
    name      String,
    countryName String
    )
    PRIMARY KEY id
    SOURCE (
        Clickhouse(
        PORT 9000
        USER ''
        HOST '127.0.0.1'
        PASSWORD ''
        DB 'test_db'
        TABLE 'TestBudaBestAndCountryView'
        FAIL_ON_CONNECTION_LOSS 'false'
        )
        )
    LIFETIME (MIN 0 MAX 1800)
    LAYOUT (HASHED());


select * from TestBudaBestAndCountryDict; -- Oops
```
You will get error: Dictionary (`CountryDict`) not found: While processing id, name, dictGet('CountryDict', 'name', countryId) AS countryName

But if you create view like this
```
create view TestBudaBestAndCountryView
as
    select id, name, dictGet('test_db.CountryDict', 'name', countryId) as countryName from TestBudaBest;
```
It should work.

Version: 21.8.4.51
author: Aleksandr-yask

comments.body: It is not a bug, when you use dictGet specified dictionary name is searched in scope of context default database. It could not find dictionary that was created in non default database, so database must be explicitly specified.

title: How to understand ClickHouse explain
body:
I'm using explain to get SQL plan, there is one like the following:
```
┌─explain─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Expression (Projection)                                                                         │
│   Expression (Before ORDER BY and SELECT)                                                       │
│     MergingAggregated                                                                           │
│       SettingQuotaAndLimits (Set limits and quota after reading from storage)                   │
│         Union                                                                                   │
│           Expression (Convert block structure for query from local replica)                     │
│             CreatingSets (Create sets before main query execution)                              │
│               Aggregating                                                                       │
│                 Expression (Before GROUP BY)                                                    │
│                   Filter (WHERE)                                                                │
│                     Join (JOIN)                                                                 │
│                       Expression (Before JOIN)                                                  │
│                         SettingQuotaAndLimits (Set limits and quota after reading from storage) │
│                           ReadFromStorage (MergeTree)                                           │
│               CreatingSet (Create set for JOIN)                                                 │
│                 Expression (Projection)                                                         │
│                   Expression (Before ORDER BY and SELECT)                                       │
│                     SettingQuotaAndLimits (Set limits and quota after reading from storage)     │
│                       ReadFromStorage (MergeTree)                                               │
│           ReadFromPreparedSource (Read from remote replica)                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
However I don't understand each step means, for example SettingQuotaAndLimits, Expression, CreatingSets, Union and so on, And I can't get detail documents. Is there any way I can get to understand each step means?
And the second questions is what the indent means? I can see some indents in each line for Explain output, Is there any hints using intent?
author: ggchangan

comments.body:
Query plan is a tree which represents decomposition of a query into basic steps.
Usually, each step represents some logical transformation over a set of columns. There is no documentation about it because query plan is still in development stage, and may be changed over versions. Its main reason for now is to give some introspection, more to developer than to user.

Let me describe each step a little bit:
* `ReadFromStorage` reads a set columns from table (in recent version, there will be `ReadFromMergeTree` for merge tree engine).
* `SettingQuotaAndLimits ` is a technical step which does actually nothing with data, but responsible for checking quota and limits (like checks for `max_rows_to_read`). I will try to remove it later.
* `Expression` calculates functions over columns, like `x, y -> x + 1, y * 2`. Use `explain actions = 1 select ...` to see more details.
* `Join` executes join. For this query, it is a hash join, which adds joined columns from hash table (which is filled in `CreatingSet`)
* `Filter` is an implementation of `WHERE` or `HAVING`. Removes rows buy some expression.
* `Aggregating` is responsible for `GROUP BY`. See `actions = 1`.
* `CreatingSets` fills hash table for `IN (subquery)` or hash join (in this query).
* `ReadFromPreparedSource` here is actually reading from remote table (changed in recent versions).
* `Union` is an implementation of `UNION`, or just a fusion of data from several sources (`Expression` and `ReadFromPreparedSource ` here).
* `MergingAggregated ` is also a part of `GROUP BY`, which merges aggregate function states from different sources (remote and local here) together.

About indentations, it is all about a tree representation. Every tree node adds the same ident to its children. Here, for `CreatingSets` children are `Aggregating` and `CreatingSet`, and for `Union` are `Expression` and `ReadFromPreparedSource`. Other steps have no more than one children.

title: When to use skipping index vs ORDER BY for a column
body:
#### A few questions regarding this topic:

1. What is the characteristics of a column that makes it suitable to be included in `ORDER BY` or as a `Skipping Index`?

2. I'm under an impression that generally the columns in `ORDER BY `should be from low cardinality to high cardinality, is this correct?


#### Follow-up question:

I have a set of hierarchical columns, let's say `parent_id`, `child_id`, `grandchild_id`, where their cardinalities are like this - `parent_id` is under 100, `child_id` is under 500, `grandchild_id` is under 50,000.

I could use dictionary for the relationship if the relationship doesn't change at all, however it's rare but does change time to time, so I'm saving these along with the main id, `grandchild_id`

The table is partitioned by the `toStartOfDay(timestamp)`, `timestamp` itself is in `5-minute` segments and the total number of rows per daily partition is about `100 million` rows (there are other fields that make the row count higher, but omitted to make the question simple)

What should the ORDER BY look like? 

#### Characteristics of each columns:
- `parent_id`: 
  - **CAN** be used in `WHERE` and **NEVER** used by `GROUP BY`
  - cardinality < 100
- `child_id`: 
  - **CAN** be used in `WHERE` or `GROUP BY` with `parent_id` in WHERE
  - cardinality < 500
- `grandchild_id`: 
  - **CAN** be used in `WHERE` or `GROUP BY` with `parent_id` or `child_id` in `WHERE`
  - cardinality < 50,000
- `timestamp`: 
  - **MUST** be used in `WHERE` and **CAN** be used in `GROUP BY`
  - cardinality == 288 within a partition (`5-minute` chunk, partitioned by `toStartOfDay(timestamp)`)


1. `parent_id`, `child_id`, `grandchild_id`, `timestamp`?

2. `timestamp`, `parent_id`, `child_id`, `grandchild_id`?

3. `grandchild_id`, `timestamp` with skipping index on `parent_id` and `child_id`?

4.  `timestamp`, `grandchild_id` with skipping index on `parent_id` and `child_id`?

5. something else?

I tested 1 ~ 4, and 3 is coming out with the least `marks to read and ranges`, and I'm not sure if it's due to the small size of the sample (1.5 billion rows) or not.
author: iameugenejo

comments.body:
The goal of both the primary key and data skipping indexes is to reduce the number of granules to read (blocks by default of  8192 row/key values).  In general query patterns are more important than cardinality.   It would also be beneficial to actually run the queries rather than just relying on the EXPLAIN plan to see the actual amount of data read.

Because timestamp is always used in your WHERE clause, it should normally be the first element of your ORDER BY/primary key since it allows limiting the number of blocks read.   The main exception to this is if your queries normally span more than one partition (assuming the PARTITION BY expression is based on the timestamp), so that further filtering by timestamp beyond the partition level does not result in excluding any more data.

If your data is sorted such that most blocks contains only a handful of grandchild_id values, that will permit skipping a larger number of blocks that don't contain the requested values, so that could be improving your estimated performance in combination with partition level filtering.

Skipping indexes are only useful if there is a high correlation between the primary key and the index value or if the data is naturally grouped.  If your parent_id and child_id are evenly scattered among your rows such that each block of 8192 rows contains the parent_id or child_id, reading those blocks cannot be skipped and the skipping index provides no benefit.

Again selecting the correct primary key and skipping indexes is not easy to do based on broad principles like cardinality; the query pattern is more important.  Over the next few months ClickHouse Inc. will be developing more in depth articles to cover partition key, primary key, sorting key, and skip index tuning.

title: How to watch the progress when I receive data from MySQL using MaterializeMySQL
body: Clickhouse can synchronize data from MySQL using MaterializeMySQL. But i don't konw how much data have been synchronized currently. So how to make sure that the data in CH is consistent with that in mysql ?
author: Fire-DB

comments.body: I also want to know

Currently, the only way is to do this manually:

1. Count the number of rows in MySQL, either by doing `ANALYZE TABLE ...` and querying `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, or by `SELECT COUNT(*)` in all the tables. If you are using the `materialized_mysql_tables_list` setting, adjust accordingly.
2. While MaterializedMySQL is in full sync, you can monitor the progress by querying `system.parts` in ClickHouse: `SELECT sum(rows) FROM system.parts WHERE database = 'yourdb' AND active`.

title: Simple questions about master node and optimize query
body:
Hi! I have two questions (with subsections), sorry if there are some answers but I didn't found them.

1. I want to create a cluster only with shards (without replication/zookeeper), didn't find any description regarding the master node. 
  1.1 The good solution is to place the Distributed table on a separate node - the master node?
  1.2 If 1.1 is true, is there any recommendation for CPU/RAM? as far as I understood, in the master node we don't need to have the same RAM as in the data node, because we simply combine the result from the shards, is it true?
  1.3 If 1.1 is true, is it possible to scale master nodes and this solution doesn't create any problems with parallel aggregation results for n master nodes? for example configuration - 

```
load balancer, 3 master nodes with Distributed tables, and `n` data nodes 
```

or is this a weird solution and it's easier to create a distribution table for each data node without master nodes :)

2. I have one unusual metric and I hope someone help to find the solution. For example, I have these tracks from fronts - 

```
date, event_type: progress, session_id, progress_percent

date, progress, '1', 31
date, progress, '1', 52
date, progress, '1', 78
date, progress, '2', 30
date, progress, '3', 100
```


I need to calculate the maximum percentage for each session and then display it in groups. So, I need to return something like this by one request to Clickhouse - 
`[1,0,1,1]` - `countResample(0, 100, 25)(max progress_percent group by session_id)`

Somehow a better solution could there be? except that front sends 1 more event(something like progress_last to avoid `argMax`) and of course `update percent` in record because this is bad practice

I thought about creating 1 more table - AggregatingMergeTree and store max percent by session there, but I'm not sure if this is a good solution since 1 more table is being created

Thanks
author: Aristat

comments.body:
>or is this a weird solution and it's easier to create a distribution table for each data node without master nodes :)

1) It's uncommon solution. In 99% cases easier to create a distribution table for each data node without master nodes. In 1% cases people use this uncommon solution because they need a lot of memory for their "Master" (query-initator) nodes. So they have i.e. 1TB RAM at two nodes (two "Master" nodes) + 20 (n) data nodes with i.e. 64GB RAM. It allows them to save money and be able to do huge in-memory JOINs or/and FinalAggregations.
It has zero relation to Replication/Sharding.


2) I prefer to answer to separated questions in separated issues.
@den-crane thanks 🚀

create table default.tbl on cluster mycluster (name String) engine=Memory;

title: "Aggregator: Merging aggregated data" process is very slow when many rows
body:
When the ClickHouse single-node system is used to perform a group by aggregation query on detail data tables, when the query result set contains a large amount of data (such as more than 1 million), I find that the "merging aggregated data" process of the final result set is slow. I haven't found an effective optimization, and I think we can consider supporting the intra-node shuffle mechanism so that the "merging aggregated data" process can be parallelized,which may improve the query performance in this scenario. In the distributed table scenario,the execution of each local table has same performance problems.
So do we have any similar considerations and plans to optimize the problem for this scenario?
author: wallace-clickhouse

comments.body:
Do you know an algorithm how to do aggregation faster? 
Can you point some whitepaper or a wiki article? 
Do you know other database / tool which can do it faster than Clickhouse?

It has no sense to ask the same question again and again. What you want is the magic.

Here an example for 100mil

```
SELECT x
FROM
(
    SELECT cityHash64(number) AS x
    FROM numbers_mt(100000000)
)
GROUP BY x
FORMAT `Null`

Elapsed: 3.552 sec. Processed 100.00 million rows
```

Please show the database which can do it faster.

title: Как корректно добавить новый диск ?

Далее прописал
sudo chown -R clickhouse:clickhouse clickhouse/
sudo  chmod -R 755 clickhouse/

config
....
<path>/var/lib/clickhouse/</path>

    <storage_configuration>
    	<disks>
     
		<default>
		   <keep_free_space_bytes>50387208960</keep_free_space_bytes>
		</default>

        	<dop>
            	   <path>/media/nikolai/tom870/clickhouse/</path>
        	</dop>

 	<policies>
 			<default>
 			  <volumes>
 			     <default>
 	  		       <disk>default</disk>
 	  		       <disk>dop</disk>
 			     </default>
 			   </volumes>
 			  <move_factor>0.2</move_factor>
 	
 			</default>
 	
        </policies>
    </storage_configuration> 
   ...

title: Predicate pushdown for view with aggregation performance. Pushdown through group by.
body:
CH 21.5.6.6

Given view and select query: 

```sql
CREATE VIEW view AS (
    SELECT
        created_at,
        column1,
        argMaxMerge(column2) AS column2,
        argMaxMerge(column3) AS column3
    FROM my_big_materialized_view
    GROUP BY created_at, column1
)
```

```sql
SELECT *
FROM view
WHERE created_at BETWEEN '1970-01-01' AND '2022-01-01' AND column1 = 1
```

According to ```EXPLAIN SYNTAX```, after AST-level optimizations, predicates from select query will be pushed down to view subquery.

But it's:

```sql
SELECT
    created_at,
    column1,
    argMaxMerge(column2) AS column2,
    argMaxMerge(column3) AS column3
FROM my_big_table
GROUP BY created_at, column1
HAVING (created_at >= '1970-01-01') AND (created_at <= '2022-01-01') AND (column1 = 1)
```

Why is that ```HAVING``` and not ```WHERE```? All predicates are for group by keys, which are created_at and column1.
Will CH aggregate full table and then filter the result?

title: difference between truncate table default.SampleTable vs delete /var/lib/clickhouse/data/default/SampleTable
body:
Hello all,

To remove all data from a table(i.e.  default.SampleTable),

```
truncate table default.SampleTable;

rm -fr /var/lib/clickhouse/data/default/SampleTable/*
```

Is there any difference between the above two operations?

Thank you
author: Jack012a

comments.body:
Second operation is illegal - server will be unaware that the files are gone.
It works only for very basic table engines: Log, TinyLog, StripeLog.
If you do this for MergeTree, server will throw exception on next query and you will have to restart server to apply changes.
If you do this for ReplicatedMergeTree, server will notice that the data is gone and repair itself from replica.
Also manual files removal is not atomic in presense of concurrent writes and background merges.

I only do the second operation while I turn off the clickhouse-server. The main reason I need to do this is to transfer some data from one machine to another machine so I don't have to import all data again.

Thank you

Yes, you can manually move data between offline servers - it is legal :)
And to online server as well (with moving to detached directory and ATTACH PART queries).

title: [PART AND PARTITION] Would all the parts of one partition be merged into a single part finally?
body:
We are trying to use  clickhouse-local to do pre-computing of part。 

As we all know，one partition has many parts， but will all the parts in one partition be merged into one part finally？

If they will  be merged into one part some how,  will single execution of  "OPTIMIZE TABLE [db.]name [ON CLUSTER cluster] [PARTITION partition | PARTITION ID 'partition_id'] [FINAL]" command give the final result ?

Thx!
author: mo-avatar

comments.body:
Merges are eventual and may never happen. 
It depends on the number of inserts that happened after, the number of parts in the partition, size of parts.
If the total size of input parts are greater than the maximum part size then they will never be merged.

OPTIMIZE ... FINAL tries to merge all part into a single part if it has enough resources in a merge pool (free disk space) without noting maximum part size limit.

title: Write distributed table, no ZK, how to avoid data inconsistency between replic
body:
In our cluster, the query results are inconsistent for many times. After investigation, it is found that the reason is that the query is executed on different copies and the returned results are inconsistent.

Comparing the data of two replicates, there are some differences.

Write method: write distributed table, randomly to each local table.

Read mode: read distributed table.

config:
insert_distributed_sync :default 0；
internal_replication: default false;

how to fix it。thanks~
author: shadowDy

comments.body: Use replicated tables / zookeeper

> Use replicated tables / zookeeper

Why do distributed tables have this problem

I understand that if local is written first and then distributed to other nodes or replicas in the form of files, the short-term data will be delayed (inconsistent), but it should be the same in the end.

>Comparing the data of two replicates, there are some differences.

Distributed table does an insert-retry in case of an error.
MergeTree table does not have a deduplication feature.

There is a scenario possible:
1. Distributed table inserts into the shard
2. Shard successfully applies the insert.
3. Distributed gets the insert timeout because of a network error.
4. Distributed table repeats the same insert from the step 1.
5. You got double data.

`rename table table_B to table_A;`

`Table is in readonly mode (zookeeper path: /clickhouse/tables/01/default/table_B)`

I have tried to find some command to fix the zookeeper path for this table as alter table and etc. but nothing found.

Is it a solution to make it out?
author: lucasguo

comments.body:
There is no good solution. ZK does not allow to rename znodes. 
You can manually fix table_A.sql file in metadata folder. 

This is the impossible situation in the latest CH versions. Because CH now expands {database}/{table} macros on a create command, so in the table's metadata (.sql) will be the real name `table_B`, instead of `{table}` macro.

Also the latest CH versions allow to use Atomic databases and uuid as ZK path. You  can simply omit ZK path parameter `ReplicatedMergeTree()`

title: When there are duplicate nodes in different clusters, insert a piece of data based on the distributed table of the replicated table, and query two pieces of data
body:
I tested a distributed table with replicated table as local table.

Now there are 4 CK servers A, B, C, D, 
where A, B, C are a cluster (3shards_1replicas), and A, B, C, D are the second cluster (2shards_2replicas: s1{A,B}, s2{C,D})

When I use the following sql to build a table

create table t on cluster 3shards_1replicas (...) engine = ReplicatedMergeTree(...) ...
create table t_all on cluster 3shards_1replicas as t engine = Distributed(.., rand())

Insert 1 piece of data into t_all, query t_all to find 2 pieces of data

When the cluster of the above table creation statement is changed to 2shards_2replicas,  same insert, the query is normal;
The local table engine of the table creation statement is changed to MergeTree, same insert, and the query is normal.

So, when there are duplicate nodes in different clusters, does the replicated table engine not work properly?
author: HavAnIdea

comments.body:
Replication depends on ZK path and macros (ReplicatedMergeTree(zk_path)).
You need to have 2 sets of macros shard.

Please provide EXACT command `create table t on cluster 3shards_1replicas (...) engine = ReplicatedMergeTree(...) `
and `select * from system.macros` from all 4 nodes.

local table DDL like ' create table t on 3shards_1replicas (columns) engine = ReplicatedMergeTree('clickhouse/table/{shard}/default/t', {replica}) '
A,B,C,D four nodes have the same macros (shard and replica), but different value

A shard = 01, replica = 01
B shard = 01, replica = 02
C shard = 02, replica = 01
D shard = 02, replica = 02

only 2shards_2replicas's macros , no 3shards_1replicas's macros

so, even if I specify the cluster name as 3shards_1replicas，
when doing macro replacement，ClickHouse cannot tell whether the replaced macro belongs to this cluster

It is undeniable that the configuration of multiple clusters is very flexible，but does it bring additional learning costs, because not everyone knows the cluster configuration (such as macros and node belongs to which cluster), and these people cannot use it correctly

forget about `on cluster`. `on cluster` is a simple helper to execute queries on each node. It has no relation to replication.

remote_servers section -- aka cluster description has 0 ZERO relation to replication.

You need to define one more macro and name it for example myshardXXX.

A shard = 01, replica = 01, myshardXXX=01
B shard = 01, replica = 02, myshardXXX=02
C shard = 02, replica = 01, myshardXXX=03
D shard = 02, replica = 02

After that create a table using that new macro

`ReplicatedMergeTree('clickhouse/table/{myshardXXX}/default/t', {replica}) '`

    `updated` AggregateFunction(max, DateTime) DEFAULT initializeAggregation('maxState', now())
)
ENGINE = SummingMergeTree
ORDER BY app
```

body:
**Describe the bug**

Appears that _timestamp and _timestamp_ms virtual columns are returning 0 for kafka. Perhaps it is somehow due to JSONEachRow format?

Issue is in docker 21.6.4.26 and 21.2.2.8 at least.

I'm using amazon MSK 2.6.1

**How to reproduce**

```
create table kafka ( name String ) ENGINE=Kafka() SETTINGS kafka_broker_list = '...', kafka_topic_list = 'test-events', kafka_group_name='test', kafka_format='JSONEachRow';
create table t (time DateTime64(3), name String) ENGINE=MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple();
create materialized view kafka_mv to t AS select _timestamp_ms, name FROM kafka;
```

```
echo '{"name":"test"}' | bin/kafka-console-producer.sh ...
```

Clickhouse table just looks like:

```
┌────────────────────time─┬─name─┐
│ 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000 │ test │
...
└─────────────────────────┴──────┘
```

If checking with kafka consumer:

```
bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh ... --from-beginning --property print.timestamp=true
CreateTime:1623839664050        {"name":"test"}
CreateTime:1623839989619        {"name":"test"}
CreateTime:1623840562909        {"name":"test"}
CreateTime:1623840285113        {"name":"test"}
```

I see the same with _timestamp col
author: mzealey

comments.body:
Mapping of columns in mv happens by names, not by positions.

So that should help:
```
create materialized view kafka_mv to t AS select _timestamp_ms as time, name FROM kafka;
```
Gah yes that fixed it. Normally I thought there were errors when creating a mv or inserting into it like this, but I did not see anything on console or in the logs :-/

title: How to realize data synchronization when adding a new replica to a Clickhouse
body:
Cluster status:

Currently, ZK is not introduced into the cluster, and reading and writing are realized through distributed tables; The configuration mode of multi slice and double copy is adopted.

The data quality of each replica is about 800g, using HDD storage

Problems encountered:

How to quickly synchronize historical data to a new replica instance when a single replica is down, an instance is migrated, or a new replica is added; How to ensure the consistency of historical data and delta data on the new replica with other replicas.

Does Clickhouse have any good suggestions on data consistency?

thanks~
author: shadowDy

comments.body:
You can

1. stop ingestion
2. alter table freeze (make snapshot)
3. add a new server into cluster
4. start ingestion (new data will be added on both nodes)
5. copy / rsync snapshot , attach parts from the snapshot at the new replica.

Of course it's not possible for Replacing / Collapsing.

>How to ensure the consistency of historical data and delta data on the new replica with other replicas.

No good ways. Use replication (Zookeeper)

>Does Clickhouse have any good suggestions on data consistency?

Of course not. There is no easy way to compare 800g of data in two tables.

title: Metadata storage path for Atomic database engine

Are there any setting or possibility to store Clickhouse's metadata physically at specified location?

comments.body: I guess `<path>/var/lib/clickhouse/</path>` in config.xml
I'm looking only for **metadata** storage, not the full clickhouse data...

I recommend setting up replication because RAID (including RAID-1) does not provide good guarantees if only a single server is used.

gives the result:

author: zav379

comments.body:
when you use native clients (clickhouse-client, golang driver etc) the conversion of timestamps to human-readable strings happens on the client side, according to client timezone and preferences. See the setting `--use_client_time_zone` and similar.

toString happens on the server. 

If you want to use some fixed rules of converting timestamp to human readable format - just pass the timezone explicitly. 

```
WITH now() AS ts
SELECT
    timezone(),
    ts,
    toTimeZone(ts, 'UTC') AS ts_utc,
    toTypeName(ts),
    toTypeName(ts_utc),
    toUnixTimestamp(ts),
    toUnixTimestamp(ts_utc)

title: Issues querying foreign tables with functions in where statements
body:
When using a foreign table (e.g. a mysql table) clickhouse doesn't seem to properly send the result of functions if they are called inside `WHERE` statements.

Executing `SELECT foo FROM foreign_table WHERE a=10 AND b='2019-10-05'` will send a statement like:

```
SELECT `foo`, `a`, `b` FROM `db`.`foreign_table`  WHERE (`a` = 10) AND (`b` = '2019-10-05')
```

But executing `SELECT foo FROM foreign_table WHERE a=10 AND b=toDate('2019-10-05')` will send:

```
SELECT `foo`, `a`, `b` FROM `db`.`foreign_table`  WHERE (`a` = 10)
```

I assume that the function is executed afterwards and `b` is parsed clickhouse-side.

I'm not sure if there is an easy fix for this, but I assume this would help with the efficiency of mysql foreign tables and might be critical in some high-load scenarios where one wants to filter on indexed columns.

My specific issue here is different and relates to the clickhouse mindsdb integration, but I think this "bug" (if you'd call it such) is more generic.

**Additional context**
From the --send_logs_level=trace message,I found when querying distributed table,subqueries to local table on each shard are fast,the bottleneck is at the aggregating merge stage on the 1st shard which distributed query is submitted,aggregating merge takes a long time and I found only 1 cpu core is working during aggregating merge.
author: wallace-clickhouse

comments.body:
Expected behavior. In some cases initiator spends more time for final aggregation.

For example:
```
initiator sends queries to shard
    shard1 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds
    shard2 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds
    shard3 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds
         initiator aggregates 3  millions unique groups for 15 seconds

Total time 10+15 = 25 seconds.
```

VS
```
initiator aggregates 3  millions unique groups for 15 seconds

Total time = 15 seconds.
```

This can be solved by sharding by expression + distributed_group_by_no_merge

--distributed_group_by_no_merge   If 1, Do not merge aggregation states from different servers for distributed query processing - in case it is for certain that there are different keys on different shards. If 2 - same as 1 but
                                                                   also apply ORDER BY and LIMIT stages

In this case :
```
initiator sends queries to shard
    shard1 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds
    shard2 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds
    shard3 aggregates 1 million unique groups for 10 seconds

Total time = 10 seconds.
```

title: Should uniq or uniqCombined be used for sharded, aggregated uniques?
body:
the documentation for uniqCombined says:

```
Compared to the uniq function, the uniqCombined:
Consumes several times less memory.
Calculates with several times higher accuracy.
Usually has slightly lower performance. In some scenarios, uniqCombined can perform better than uniq, for example, with distributed queries that transmit a large number of aggregation states over the network.
```

The documentation for uniq says:

```
We recommend using this function in almost all scenarios.
```

We have "distributed queries that transmit a large number of aggregation states" -- so should we be using uniqCombined?  If so should the "uniq" recommendation be updated to reflect that?  Or is the uniqCombined documentation out of date?

(On a side note, I don't suppose there's a way to convert uniqState to uniqCombinedState for existing data?)
author: genzgd

comments.body:
>If so should the "uniq" recommendation be updated to reflect that? 
>Or is the uniqCombined documentation out of date?

Milovidov: 
uniqCombined with default values is somewhat more accurate than uniq.
uniqCombined is more accurate and takes up less memory and disk space. But usually slower.


I (Denis) suggest to try `uniqCombined64(15)` -- it boosts queries up to 10 times for my distributed queries (1Gbit network).
And the error is <2% in comparison with uniqExact.

Also about states:
```
disk space for example
2.2M    uniqHLL12State
58M   uniqCombinedState(20)
15M   uniqCombinedState(15)
140M    uniqState

Speed
SELECT uniqMerge(us) AS unique FROM mvz WHERE z = '555' GROUP BY d
┌─unique─┐
│ 297580 │
└────────┘
1 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.031 sec.

SELECT uniqHLL12Merge(uh) AS unique FROM mvz WHERE z = '555' GROUP BY d
┌─unique─┐
│ 297323 │
└────────┘
1 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.002 sec.

SELECT uniqCombinedMerge15(uc) AS unique FROM mvz WHERE z = '555' GROUP BY d
┌─unique─┐
│ 298636 │
└────────┘
1 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.003 sec.
```


>(On a side note, I don't suppose there's a way to convert uniqState to uniqCombinedState for existing data?)

No way. 
AMilovidov thinks that it's possible in theory, he can do it :) (select states into application / recalculate / insert into another table).
I'll give uniqCombined(64) a shot.  Thanks for the detailed response!

title: GRANT SELECT if column not in restricted tuple
body:
According documentation : 

```
GRANT SELECT(x,y) ON db.table TO john WITH GRANT OPTION
It means that john has the permission to execute:

SELECT x,y FROM db.table.
SELECT x FROM db.table.
SELECT y FROM db.table.
john can’t execute SELECT z FROM db.table. The SELECT * FROM db.table also is not available. Processing this query, ClickHouse doesn’t return any data, even x and y. The only exception is if a table contains only x and y columns. In this case ClickHouse returns all the data.
```

Is there a way to return column z empty, filled with null, or not return during processing? 
`SELECT x,y,z FROM db.table` now returns exception. 
This behavior is incomprehensible
author: bralbral

comments.body:
Hi @bralbral,

The current behavior is to return an error when columns selected are not included in the `GRANT SELECT`:
i believe this is the exception you are referencing:
```
Code: 497. DB::Exception: user_xy: Not enough privileges. To execute this query it's necessary to have grant SELECT(id, x, y, z) ON db1.table4. (ACCESS_DENIED) (version 22.1.3.7 (official build))
```
this is produced when using something like `SELECT * FROM db1.table4` is used.

The behavior is designed to be similar to what is implemented in other database systems.
**Examples**
PostgreSQL behavior:
```
db1=> select * from table4;
ERROR:  permission denied for relation table4
db1=> select x,y from table4;
  x  |  y
-----+-----
 abc | def
(1 row)
```

MySQL behavior:
```
mysql> select * from db1.table4;
ERROR 1143 (42000): SELECT command denied to user 'user_xy'@'localhost' for column 'id' in table 'table4'
mysql> select x,y from db1.table4;
+------+------+
| x    | y    |
+------+------+
| abc  | def  |
+------+------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

if you would like to suggest a different behavior, please submit an enhancement request using the template "Feature Request" when creating a new issue.

thanks.

There are six values for field wealth_level, which are '0', '1', '2', '3', '4', and '5'.
The corresponding number of data is about 400 million, 4 million, 4 million, 4 million, 4 million, 4 million.
sql:
select bitmapCardinality(
(select groupBitmapMergeState(user_id_bit)
from database.table_bit
where  wealth_level in ('3','4','5')));

When modifying the value condition of field wealth_level , the corresponding SQL time consumption is:
wealth_level in ('5')                  :0.36s
wealth_level in ('4','5')              :1s 
wealth_level in ('3','4','5')          :1.2s
wealth_level in ('2','3','4','5')      :4.5s
wealth_level in ('1','2','3','4','5')  :4.8s

In my usage scenario, there are many cases with multiple value ranges.
author: ustcrczhang181

comments.body:
Also you may ask why when changing from two to three values, the time changes from 1s to just 1.2s - less that 50%.
Most likely this is because the dependency between time and the amount of data is not strictly linear.

Roaring bitmap is not a simple data structure. There can be some steps in query execution time due to resizes. There can also be some "phase changes" in the data structure depending on the data volume.

I don't see anything paradoxical in these timings.

title: Create functions queryID and initialQueryID
body:
Goal is to find out (initial_)query_id of INSERT query that triggered this (current) Materialized View execution, in order to register this initial_query_id in statistics table.
Why? It would enrich statistics/monitoring/troubleshooting and provide significant information both about origins of insert to ClickHouse and about propagation of insert through ClickHouse derived objects (e.g. in-ClickHouse latency).

The point is that system.query_log with all its useful information knows nothing about data.
At the same time manual statistics table(s) that are filled by adjacent MV potentially know everything about incoming data, but lack information about initial IP's, queries etc.
These two statistic's sources are crying to be linked together.

This use case and this desire look general enough, so there is probably some general solution.

+++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Details
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++

Input data stream enters my ClickHouse cluster through input Null table (on every node). 
Several Materialized Views over this Null table are performing some processing and propagating data further (there are distributed tables and more MV's there). 
In order to reduce in-ClickHouse latency: parallel_view_processing=1

One of derived tables (stat2.inserts_v02) contains statistics about input flow  (count(), quantiles, delays) over some data-related dimensions.
It is basic ReplicatedMergeTree that is filled via MV from inserts to initial Null table data2.input_null like:
`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW data2.inserts_v02_MVst2 ON CLUSTER ch_sNr1 TO stat2.inserts_v02
AS SELECT
  <data dimensions>,
  hostName(),
  count(), median(), etc
  FROM data2.input_null GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ...`

I'm trying to somehow find out/evaluate (initial_)query_id of parent's insert inside Materialized View's query.
It would be very helpful for monitoring/troubleshooting/statistics. 
If query_id or initial_query_id were known, it would have been possible to obtain a lot of additional information from system.query_log tables - both about origins of ETL data flow (IP addresses, http_user_agent) and about further destiny of this insert (whole picture of latencies within ClickHouse, additional checks that everything works as intended).

But all my attempts failed.
There are seemingly no inherent functions to receive initial_query_id that triggered MV during MV execution (however modern ClickHouse versions do display query's query_id in clickhouse-client).
I tried to fill initial_query_id via lookup into system.processes table, but the problem is that these are large inserts (500k-1M events) that are executed several seconds, and there are usually many simultaneous inserts of such kind. 
So Materialized View (when it is executed) can't find out which of existsing system.processes INSERT queries is its parent. 
`(SELECT arrayStringConcat(groupArray(initial_query_id), ',') FROM system.processes WHERE substr(query,1,37)='INSERT INTO data2.stage2_null_events') AS possible_query_ids,`
author: krebrikov

comments.body:
In other words you want to make things like query_id and initial_query_id available as functions, and use them inside your materialized views? 


Something like: 

```
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW foo AS SELECT hostName(), count(), median(), queryID(), initialQueryID() from bar;
```

?

If there were direct functions like this it would be a perfect outcome !

Actually I didn't intend this Issue to be a feature request, but rather hoped that there is already some workaround to enrich inserts-related statistics (counted within derived MV) with audit data from system.query_log. 
If it was a function - even better!

What is more important is that I assume it is not my personal issue, but rather a feature that would meet certain demand from ClickHouse users in a whole. 
It looks like an implementation of final "Load" phase of non-trivial ETL processes on the side of ClickHouse not in some particular table, but rather in a small tree of several tables (linked by Materialized Views) is quite a mainstream approach. 
And additional MV (to main data flow) that evaluates insert's statistics for monitoring looks very natural solution here. An opportunity to link to system.query_log would make this pattern more useful.

> workaround to enrich inserts-related statistics (counted within derived MV) with audit data from system.query_log.

You can try joins (of course later, it is not possible at insert / MV time) . But it would be quite painful, non reliable  and and non efficient.

Addind such function should be trivial.

title: Modifying clickhouse configuration parameter not working!

comments.body: What exactly do you modify? How to reproduce the issue?

> What exactly do you modify? How to reproduce the issue?

Modify the 'max_partitions_per_insert_block' parameter and insert partitions greater than this value to reproduce

Most probably you are doing something wrong. It is a user-level setting, you need to put it into users.xml inside the default profile. 
If it does not help - please show what exactly did you do, and how the file looks like. 

P.S. Relaxing that limitation (`max_partitions_per_insert_block`) is typically a very bad idea. Or not: it's VERY-VERY bad idea :) Rethink your partitioning schema instead - you want to do inserts in one or a few partitions at a time.

title: Whether all replicas are single-threaded the processQueueEntry？
author: Sallery-X

comments.body: The StorageReplciatedMergeTree processQueueEntry is not single threaded, multiple threads from the background pool will be used to process multiple queue entries.  The number of threads is controlled by the `background_pool_size` parameter, and defaults to 16.  The queue is maintained in zookeeper and modifications are protected by a mutex.  In real world situations many merges and fetches for the same replicated table will happen in parallel.

I am trying to figure out how to model this so that the table has one row (after an `OPTIMIZE`) to represent that entity (even though there are multiple events per entity).

My data is something like this, where event D is the one that can occur multiple times:
```
Event type A:
{
  "id": <string identifier>,
  "a": <data for field a>
  "aa": <data for field aa>
}

Event type B:
{
  "id": <string identifier>,
  "b": <data for field b>,
  "bb": <data for field bb>
}

Event type C:
{
  "id": <string identifier>,
  "c": <data for field c>,
  "cc": <data for field cc>
}

Event type D:
{
  "id": <string identifier>,
  "d": <data for field d>,
  "dd": <data for field dd>
}
```

What I want a table in Clickhouse to look like is something like this:

```
CREATE TABLE events
(
  id String,
  a Nullable(String),
  aa Nullable(String),
  b Nullable(String),
  bb Nullable(String),
  c Nullable(String),
  cc Nullable(String),
  d Nullable(Array(String)),
  dd Nullable(Array(String))
)
```
where the elements of column `d` and `dd` are ordered the same, e.g. `d[1]` and `dd[1]` should be from the same instance of event D.

What I am having trouble with is coming up with the correct engine that would give me this. I naturally went to the `AggregatingMergeTree` for this and using `id` as the sort key, but I don't know how to aggregate the fields from event D. I think it might be because of the apparent lack of an aggregate function that would aggregate values into an array of that type (e.g. aggregating `Nullable(String)` into `Array(String)`). 

Is there such a function or table engine that would accomplish what I'm trying to do or am I even thinking about this correctly? I realize I could write the D events to a separate table but I want to avoid a join if possible.

comments.body: groupArray()

I did see that but the first line in the docs says `Values can be added to the array in any (indeterminate) order.` which I need the columns from event D to match in order. Is there away to use Nested types with groupArray? It was kind of confusing to me because from what I understand, Nested types are arrays themselves?

groupArray 
Syntax: groupArray(x) or groupArray(max_size)(x)

Creates an array of argument values.
Values can be added to the array in any (indeterminate) order.

The second version (with the max_size parameter) limits the size of the resulting array to max_size elements. For example, groupArray(1)(x) is equivalent to [any (x)].
**In some cases, you can still rely on the order of execution. This applies to cases when SELECT comes from a subquery that uses ORDER BY.**

eg.

with t as (select number n from system.numbers limit 100000),
t1 as (select n%20 x,count(*)c from t group by x),
t2 as (select toUInt8(x/4)x1,groupArray(c)ac from t1 group by x1)
--select t2.*,2 from t2

select x1% 3 x2,groupArray(ac) ac,3 from t2 group by x2
;

title: A "versioned" version of AggregatingMergeTree
body:
We have a very specific criteria for storing data which we cannot find a very good solution for. We would like to do something like a versioned AggregatingMergeTree but it doesn't exist so is there maybe a different solution?

We have a setup that looks like this:
```
create table if not exists test.test
(
    country        LowCardinality(String),
    text           String CODEC (ZSTD(3)),
    number         SimpleAggregateFunction( max, UInt32),
    related_number Float32,
    first_seen     SimpleAggregateFunction( min, Date)
)
    engine = AggregatingMergeTree()
        PARTITION BY country
        ORDER BY (country, text)
        SETTINGS index_granularity = 256;

insert into test
values ('us', 'foo', 1, 30, '2020-01-01'),
       ('us', 'foo', 2, 20, '2021-01-02'),
       ('us', 'foo', 3, 10, '2021-01-03');
```
If we do select all data with final (`select * from test final`) we get:

| country | text | number | related_number | first_seen |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| us | foo  | 3  | 30 | 2020-01-01  |

which is what one would expect. 

But we would like "save" the `related_number` that correspond to max `number` while maintaining the lowest `first_seen` date as shown in the table below (with the _**bold italic records highligthed**_).

(`select * from test`)
| country | text | number | related_number | first_seen |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| us | foo  | 1  | 30 | **_2020-01-01_**  |
| us | foo  | 2  | 20 | 2020-01-02  |
| **_us_** | **_foo_**  | **_3_**  | **_10_** | 2020-01-03  |
| us | foo  | 1  | 30 | 2020-01-04  |

So essentially we are looking for the behavior of the combination of a ReplacingMergeTree (with `number` as the version column) and a AggregatingMergeTree -> a VersionedAggregatingMergeTree.

Any idea how we could solve this?

edit: changed the last table to better show what we want
