title: I found that when I turn off a replica, the file of zookeeper "/is_active" does not change the state, and the "/is_lost" either.
author: Sallery-X

comments.body: Looks like expected behavior. Replica does not become lost if it just turned of, so it's `/is_lost` should not be changed. It's changed only when other replicas consider inactive replica as staled according to its log pointer. As for `/is_active` node, it's ephemeral and it disappears when replica is turned off, but it may happen not immediately and may take from seconds up to 1 minute (depends on ZooKeeper configuration)

title: Is it the best way to create a Clickhouse table and place the columns with low cardinality on the left in order by primary key order？？
body: For example, there are year, month, day, hour and time stamp in order by. The year should be on the far left and the hour should be on the far right.
author: shadowDy

comments.body:
In the most cases it's correct. 
In some cases it's not. For example you have a multi-tenant system and you have 10 000 tenants. You need to divide tenants because all queries have `where tenant = ... `  then you put tenant_id to first position in order_by.

Good ORDER BY typically contains 3 to 5 columns. 
The most important for filtering (and/or the lowest cardinal) on the left-most position. 
Later importance is getting lower, and column cardinality - higher.  

Ideally, if you can organize the data in the natural hierarchy order, for ex. `(continent, country, region, city, street)`

title: Live view vs interval query efficiency
body:
Hi @vzakaznikov,

I have a question, hope you can help me.
Let assume I have some query (`SELECT * FROM table WHERE updated_at > NOW64()- INTERVAL 1 second`) that select data updated within last second. I don't need every update, just snapshot every second.
What's going to be more efficient LIVE VIEW or just direct query every second?

Thank you
author: sasha-id

comments.body: Hi @alex-klepa, efficiency will depend on how fast it takes to execute the query itself and the overall insert rate. If the result can be calculated fast you can use polling method and resend the query every second. Now, if you have 100's of clients sending the exact same query then a LIVE VIEW might be much more efficient as it will store the cached result in memory but might be more inefficient if you have many updates going into the source table as LIVE VIEW will try to be in sync with the source table and calculates new result for each insert block. In this case it really depends on your INSERT rate. The best way to find out what works for your specific case is to prototype both solutions. You also have to keep in mind that LIVE VIEW tables are still an experimental feature. Hope this helps.
Thank you for detail explanation!

If don't need real-time updates then you can also try a solution using LIVE VIEW table but not using WATCH query. Instead you can use plain select on the LIVE VIEW. In this case what will happened is that you will still use polling method and resend your query to the LIVE VIEW every second. Now if the insert rate is not high and many clients send the same query to this LIVE VIEW at this very same second then they will all get an instant result as the result will be in the cache of the LIVE VIEW.
Got it, I think I read your article regarding this, using LIVE VIEW as caching layer.
You are most welcome!

title: when will clickhouse materialized view update the data?
body: when will clickhouse materialized view update the data? How long source table update the materialized view table data
author: melin

comments.body:
Hi.
Data insertion into MV table happens at the same time you insert data into source table.
If insertion into source table returns `ok`, new data is inserted in both source and MV table. This insert is not transnational, however. It means, there could be a moment when `select` can get not consistent data while reading from source table and MV (e.g. it can see MV before insertion, but source table after).

title: Top N of unique string
body:
Hi,

In the main table, there is a string column for `ip` which is unique (mostly) per document. I want to return the top 10 IPs for this table (few billions of documents). Is there any performant way to do so?
author: hatrena

comments.body: What do you mean top10 if they are uniq?
something similar to `topK(N)` with count as well but performant.

Naive solution is:

```
SELECT click_ip, count() AS c FROM table GROUP BY click_ip ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10
```

It may not fit in memory, but you can raise `max_memory_usage` and enable `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`.
Then the query will be able to proceed even with multiple billion records. But it can be slow.

Optimized variant is:

```
SELECT click_ip, count() AS c FROM table
WHERE click_ip IN
(
    SELECT click_ip FROM table ORDER BY rand() LIMIT 1000000
)
GROUP BY click_ip ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10
```

It relies on assumption that top 10 IP addresses most likely will be present in random sample of a million records from a table. It's not guaranteed to be true but it is almost always true.

This query can be slightly more optimal:

```
SELECT click_ip, count() AS c FROM table
WHERE click_ip IN
(
    SELECT click_ip FROM table WHERE rand() % 10000 = 123
)
GROUP BY click_ip ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10
```

And if data in your table is uniformly distributed, you can also use this trick:
```
SET max_rows_to_group_by = 1000000, group_by_overflow_mode = 'any';
SELECT click_ip, count() AS c FROM table GROUP BY click_ip ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10;
```

The average response from the naive solution is `10 rows in set. Elapsed: 15.929 sec. Processed 204.23 million rows, 20.28 GB (12.82 million rows/s., 1.27 GB/s.)` which is much better than the other solutions somehow. those take minutes.

Great!

By tuning the constants of the optimized variants (with subqueries) you can get better response time.

title: I think the merge operation will be excute when i insert、alter or optimize, Besides will the merging be executed regularly when the storage start up？And how often？
author: Sallery-X

comments.body: Merges are executed regularly even when there are no writing queries (such as INSERT, ALTER or OPTIMIZE). There are several kinds of merges (ordinary merges, TTL merges, recompression merges) and a lot of heuristics are used to determine if some parts should be merged or not, so it's hard to tell how often background merges are executed, because it depends. If you are interested in implementation details, you can start from `MergeTreeDataMergerMutator::selectPartsToMerge(...)`.

Duplicate of #21554 and #21555 and #21625

Please, do not create duplicate issues.

title: Generate data part for each partition during updating
body:
main process includes: 
- create table with:
```sql
CREATE TABLE class
(
    `level` String,
    `status` String,
    `class` String,
    `name` String,
    `create_time` datetime DEFAULT now()
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY (level, status)
ORDER BY (level, status)
```
- add values:
```sql
INSERT INTO class(level,status,class,name) VALUES
('high','open','c1','lee'),
('high','close','c2','smith'),
('high','close','c3','kyo'),
('high','open','c4','kim'),
('high','close','c5','wong');
```
- check partition
 ```
┌─partition────────┬─name───────────────────────────────────┬─active─┐
│ ('high','close') │ 6c5a0a8f77a1afb8aba98e946d1ff7cc_2_2_0 │      1 │
│ ('high','open')  │ 6f727efd83659398a5e8e77967a7022c_1_1_0 │      1 │
└──────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┘
```

- update value `alter table class update name='tim' where class='c1'`

- check partition again and find two new data parts.
```
┌─partition────────┬─name─────────────────────────────────────┬─active─┐
│ ('high','close') │ 6c5a0a8f77a1afb8aba98e946d1ff7cc_2_2_0   │      0 │
│ ('high','close') │ 6c5a0a8f77a1afb8aba98e946d1ff7cc_2_2_0_3 │      1 │<- how it is generated?
│ ('high','open')  │ 6f727efd83659398a5e8e77967a7022c_1_1_0   │      0 │   
│ ('high','open')  │ 6f727efd83659398a5e8e77967a7022c_1_1_0_3 │      1 │<- the updated data should be in here
└──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┘
```

Question:
The record of class='c1' should be located in partition ('high','open'). Why during updating, new data part is built in ('high','close')?
author: SE2AI

comments.body:
Mutation always mutate all parts. But executes only renaming (using hardlinks) for parts which no need to mutate.
You can check files inodes.

hashsum unchanged:
```
┌─name─────────────────────────────────────┬─active─┬─hash_of_all_files────────────────┬─hash_of_uncompressed_files───────┬─uncompressed_hash_of_compressed_files─┐
│ 6c5a0a8f77a1afb8aba98e946d1ff7cc_3_3_0   │      0 │ a6b96dff78e99201a8fb83c53dc065ef │ b02202c65d46e0c4091f71b5aa59b1de │ a85591fa0fa5bbcae85394a1c87fea6c      │
│ 6c5a0a8f77a1afb8aba98e946d1ff7cc_3_3_0_4 │      1 │ a6b96dff78e99201a8fb83c53dc065ef │ b02202c65d46e0c4091f71b5aa59b1de │ a85591fa0fa5bbcae85394a1c87fea6c      │

Also you can use ` in partition ` for **replicated** tables if you have concern about zookeeper performance.

title: How to accelerate update querys
body:
In my case, I build a table with 12M data and 600 partitions，and test the performance of single-record update per second.

I try both situations:

1. 100 concurrent single-update in one partition, only one column value changed for each update.
2. 100 concurrent single-update in 100 partition(1 update for 1 partition), only one column value changed for each update.

In both situations, the 100 update could be completed after about 3~4min, which means update efficiency is about ~0.3 record per second. 

So, how to improve update performance? actually 100 single-record-update per second would be ok for me. Are there any important configurations or best practice guide?
author: SE2AI

comments.body:
You do understand that Clickhouse does not support updates as daily-basis operations?
Alter update / delete are designed for rare admin operations like GDPR.
Try ReplacingMergeTree / CollapsingMErgeTree / external dictionaries instead of alter.

Setup:

Our code writes to a Distributed table on either server, and then clickhouse writes the record to the underlying real tables on both servers.

To get multivolume support, I upgraded from 18.14.19 to 20.8.12.2. I had a number of problems, and ran out of time to debug/fix, so I rolled back to 18.14.19. My problem probably started then.

title: Parse exception for Dictionary with JSONEachRow
body:
(you don't have to strictly follow this form)

**Describe the bug**
There is a parsing exception when reading a dictionary from json file formatted as JSONEachRow:
`Code: 27. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '"' before: 'abc", "foo": "1" }\n{ "id": "def", "foo": "2" }\n': (while reading the value of key id).`

**Does it reproduce on recent release?**
Reproduced on version 21.3.2

**How to reproduce**
Create file test.json:
```
{ "id": "abc", "foo": "1" }
{ "id": "def", "foo": "2" }

```

Create dictionary:
```
clickhouse-client --query "
CREATE DICTIONARY test
(
    id String,
    foo String
)
PRIMARY KEY id
SOURCE(FILE(path '/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/test.json' format 'JSONEachRow'))
LAYOUT(HASHED())
LIFETIME(MIN 5 MAX 15);
"
```

Run test query:
`clickhouse-client --query "SELECT id from test"`

Output:
`Code: 27. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '"' before: 'abc", "foo": "1" }\n{ "id": "def", "foo": "2" }\n': (while reading the value of key id).`

For sanity check, the following query works as expected:
```
clickhouse-client --query "SELECT id FROM file('/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/test.json', 'JSONEachRow', 'id String, foo String')"
abc
def
```

**Expected behavior**
Parsing of JSONEachRow should work for dictionary the same as it is for table.
author: kfirdado

comments.body:
HASHED  -- layout supports only UInt64 as PRIMARY KEY

You need to use -- COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED
```sql
 CREATE DICTIONARY test
 (
     id String,
     foo String
 )
 PRIMARY KEY id
 SOURCE(FILE(path '/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/test.json' format 'JSONEachRow'))
 LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED())
 LIFETIME(MIN 5 MAX 15);


SELECT * FROM test;
┌─id──┬─foo─┐
│ abc │ 1   │
│ def │ 2   │
└─────┴─────┘


SELECT dictGet('default.test', 'foo', tuple('abc')) AS r
┌─r─┐
│ 1 │
└───┘
```

title: process has no CAP_IPC_LOCK capability, binary mlock will be disabled
body: 2021.03.11 13:43:14.558479 [ 1 ] {} <Information> Application: It looks like the process has no CAP_IPC_LOCK capability, binary mlock will be disabled. Note that it will not work on 'nosuid' mounted filesystems.
author: Sallery-X

comments.body: The message is correct.

> binary mlock will be disabled

binary mlock = put whole clickhouse binary in ram and forbid paging.

To be enabled the Linux capability CAP_IPC_LOCK is needed. (The log message is relevant and help you to fix the issue).

When you don't have such a capability the feature can not be enabled, that potentially may to less stable performance due to paging of the execuatable. That is the only side-effect.

title: When i use the storage of replicatedReplicaingMergeTree, i found the parts haven't merge parts for too long
author: Sallery-X

comments.body:
Clickhouse merge scheduler does not have the goal to merge everything. 
Merge scheduler balance number of parts in a partition with an amount of resources needed to merge them and plans merges if there are free resources available. 


Merges are eventual and may never happen. It depends on the number of inserts that happened after, the number of parts in the partition, size of parts.
If the total size of input parts bigger than the maximum part size then they are never will be merged.

It's not bug. It's normal behavior. CH checks memory required for a query execution and available memory. 
This check is implemented to prevent OOM.

you can configure `<max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>5</max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>`

```
config.xml
    <!-- Maximum memory usage (resident set size) for server process.
         Zero value or unset means default. Default is "max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio" of available physical RAM.
         If the value is larger than "max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio" of available physical RAM, it will be cut down.

         The constraint is checked on query execution time.
         If a query tries to allocate memory and the current memory usage plus allocation is greater
          than specified threshold, exception will be thrown.

         It is not practical to set this constraint to small values like just a few gigabytes,
          because memory allocator will keep this amount of memory in caches and the server will deny service of queries.
      -->
    <max_server_memory_usage>0</max_server_memory_usage>

    <!-- On memory constrained environments you may have to set this to value larger than 1.
      -->
    <max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>0.9</max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>

```

title: I would like to know a more detailed explanation of interserver_http_host
body:
My team recently had a problem with the operation of the replica table, and it turned out to be a problem with the interserver_http_host.
After choosing an appropriate host, the problem was solved.
However, there seems to be insufficient explanation for this. I've looked into the official docs or git issues, but there seems to be a lack of explanations to understand in detail
I initially thought that Zookeeper would check all data changes between the replica nodes and sync them.
And even at first it worked fine. The cloning was good and the sharding was good.
However, after some time, the replica node had a "host not found" problem, so I had to fix the interserver_http_host.
Why didn't the problem arise from the beginning of cloning?
Will clickhouse only use interserver_http_host in certain situations?
author: cokepizza

comments.body:
`interserver_http_host` and `interserver_http_port` are used for data replication between servers. `interserver_http_host` defaults to the output of `hostname -f`.

Some `interserver_*` related settings and comments in `config.xml` are as follows
```
    <!-- Port for communication between replicas. Used for data exchange.
         It provides low-level data access between servers.
         This port should not be accessible from untrusted networks.
         See also 'interserver_http_credentials'.
         Data transferred over connections to this port should not go through untrusted networks.
         See also 'interserver_https_port'.
      -->
    <interserver_http_port>9009</interserver_http_port>

    <!-- Port for communication between replicas with TLS.
         You have to configure certificate to enable this interface.
         See the openSSL section below.
         See also 'interserver_http_credentials'.
      -->
    <!-- <interserver_https_port>9010</interserver_https_port> -->

    <!-- Hostname that is used by other replicas to request this server.
         If not specified, than it is determined analogous to 'hostname -f' command.
         This setting could be used to switch replication to another network interface
         (the server may be connected to multiple networks via multiple addresses)
      -->
    <!--
    <interserver_http_host>example.yandex.ru</interserver_http_host>
    -->

    <!-- You can specify credentials for authenthication between replicas.
         This is required when interserver_https_port is accessible from untrusted networks,
         and also recommended to avoid SSRF attacks from possibly compromised services in your network.
      -->
    <!--<interserver_http_credentials>
        <user>interserver</user>
        <password></password>
    </interserver_http_credentials>-->
```

See if the 'host not found' problem is related to the output change of `hostname -f`.

title: create table not use non-deterministic functions
body:
Partition key cannot contain non-deterministic functions:

old clickhouse 20.10 stable
`create table app.user_test(id Int32,day Date,s_t Nullable(DateTime))ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY ifNull(day,today()) ORDER BY ifNull(s_t,now()) TTL day + toIntervalDay(7)`
create table is ok 
new clickhouse version 21.2 stable
`create table app.user_test(id Int32,day Date,s_t Nullable(DateTime))ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY ifNull(day,today()) ORDER BY ifNull(s_t,now()) TTL day + toIntervalDay(7)` 
create error 
DB::Exception:Partition key cannot contain non-deterministic functions, but contains function today. 
the same create sql but not use in new version clickhouse.
author: maimaip

comments.body:
This behaviour is correct - it protects you from mistakes in table definition.
`PARTITION BY today()` can lead to surprising results - some queries won't be able to find records in table.

Instead you should create `insert_date DEFAULT today()` field in table and `PARTITION BY ifNull(day,insert_date)`

title: design table for customer
body:
hi team
I have a customer table like
```sql
create table customer (
storeId  String,
customerId String,
createDate UInt64,
updateDate UInt64,
type UInt8,
status UInt8,
birthDay UInt64,
date Date default toDate(createDate/1000)
) engine = MergeTree ...
```
I have more than 10000 stores and much more customers, I will query the customer with storeId or type but not createDate or some other date.

I'm confused how to design partition key for the table. I don't use date to query and the number of stores is to much.
And I can't use a single partition because of much data

Have any suggestions? thanks
author: peaksnail

comments.body:
> I don't use date to query and the number of stores is to much.

It does not matter. Just use `partition by toYYYYMM(toDate(createDate/1000))`
First of all partitioning is about insert --> create minimum parts during inserting and about data retention.
Partitioning can speed up queries but it's not mandatory.

It will read all partition if using partition by toYYYYMM(toDate(createDate/1000)),
Is there any way to speed up queries using storeId to query like 
```
select ... from customer where storeId='xxx'
```
otherwise it will be slow when the data is big

partition by toYYYYMM(toDate(createDate/1000))
order by (storeId, toDate(createDate/1000))

title: Considering to remove broken part ... because it's impossible to repair.
body:
Scenario: 
create a table, edit columns.txt file, detach table,  attach table  back

Result:
The part removed completely.

Expected:
part moved to detached.
author: filimonov

comments.body: Part is removed if its level is zero and if sanity threshold is passed.
Users are not supposed to manually edit columns.txt file.

File can be damaged other way (w/o manual interventions).

Dosn't it break the documented invariant? 

> If the system detects broken data parts (with the wrong size of files) or unrecognized parts (parts written to the file system but not recorded in ZooKeeper), it moves them to the `detached` subdirectory (they are not deleted).
@filimonov Let's submit a patch.

> File can be damaged other way (w/o manual interventions).

If table is replicated - the part will be repaired from replica.
If table is not replicated - the damaged part cannot be repaired automatically if there are no covered parts, and it's in doubt you can do anything.

> it's in doubt you can do anything.

The same is true for parts with level > 1, which we just detach w/o removing. Imho it's better to have the same behaviour in similar use cases.

title: Select * memory usage optimization
body:
I use ClickHouse 20.12.3.3 to store normalized logs. A table consists of 160 columns, primary key and order by key is Timestamp (int64).

Often I need to find some logs extracting all table columns. When I use the following query to find logs in 1 month period (approx. 2 TB of compressed data) on a single node - it consumes 20+ GB of memory:

SELECT * FROM events WHERE Column1 = 'value1' AND Column2 = 'value2' AND Timestamp > [START] AND Timestamp < [END] ORDER BY Timestamp DESC LIMIT **250**;

The wider search period is, the more RAM is consumed. The less columns appear in SELECT, the less memory consumed.

Folks from CH telegram group told me that part of this memory is allocated for column buffers (1MB for each column that appears in SELECT) by each thread. Let's say query is executed by 32 threads: 32t * 160c * 1MB = 5 GB RAM. So it is not clear why CH needs another 15 GB to execute this query. 

Is there a way to use a pipeline like the following one?

1. Read only columns that appear in WHERE and ORDER BY clauses from disk;
2. Mark locations of each row that satisfy WHERE clause, heap sort on-the-fly;
3. Extract marked rows after scan is finished.

This way I wouldn't need tens of GB of RAM to perform deep "historical" searches.

If that is not possible at the moment, are there any plans to introduce such a pipeline in a future releases?

comments.body:

```
Is there a way to use a pipeline like the following one?

    Read only columns that appear in WHERE and ORDER BY clauses from disk;
    Mark locations of each row that satisfy WHERE clause, heap sort on-the-fly;

title: how to kill long query?
body:
KILL QUERY WHERE query_id='xxx' doesn't work, it just return waiting. 

Is it true that a sql cannot be killed unless it is executed? But what is the point of killing if all executions are completed? The CPU is full, and the purpose of kill query is to immediately stop the executing sql and reduce the CPU usage
author: Fanduzi

comments.body:
Unfortunately not all queries can be killed.
KILL QUERY only sets a flag that must be checked by the query.
A query pipeline is checking this flag  before a switching to next block. If the pipeline has stuck somewhere in the middle it cannot be killed.
If a query does not stop, the only way to get rid of it is to restart ClickHouse.

title: Current recommendations around partition size?
body:
We have two MergeTree tables looking like:

```
CREATE TABLE logs (
    time DateTime64(3) CODEC(DoubleDelta, ZSTD(1)),
    ...
) ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toStartOfInterval(time, INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
PRIMARY KEY (cust id, some other cols, toDateTime(time))
```

these get roughly 2b and 8b rows/day into them respectively.

We typically want quite short-range queries (eg past hour or so) but on occasion want to do scans over month- or year- long periods. Is it best to use hour-long partitions for this as at present (but this means many partitions over the course of a year), or to use day partitioning, however this probably makes most of our queries slower as they have to scan the whole day? What are the current downsides of having many partitions with the ATOMIC engine?
author: mzealey

comments.body:
CH recommends monthly (toYYYYMM) partitioning.

With hourly partitioning you'll have (24*365) 8760 partitions per year, and > 10000 parts.
Your queries (over month/year) will be slowed down because they need to read many partitions.
CH start will take some time (could be hours for HDD , need to read each part metadata).
If you use replicated tables then you need to configure ZK -Djut to be able to handle big transactions otherwise alters of this table will be impossible.

I recommend to consider/test this:
```
PARTITION BY toDate(time) -- or toYYYYMM(time) 
PRIMARY KEY (toStartOfHour(time), cust id, some other cols)
```

Optimal partition size is between few gigs and 150 Gb (may also be bigger / smaller, if there are more pros than cons).
Optimal partition in a single table up to hundreds.

So if you collect 150 Gb of data per hour and you data retention is limited to couple of days then you can keep hourly.

title: Do we need to still use GROUP BY in MATERIALIZED VIEWS?
body:
Following on from #16954, does it still make sense to write:

```
CREATE TABLE agg (
) ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree()

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv TO agg AS SELECT ... FROM src GROUP BY ...
```

is it basically identical performance-wise to write it without the `GROUP BY` without any overheads or other costs (and probably making it much easier to insert bulk data without having to go via a Null table per #17239) ?
author: mzealey

comments.body: Yes, after `optimize_on_insert` is enabled there is no reason to write GROUP BY in mat.view definition.

Maybe it is still good for illustrative purposes.

Also maybe there are cases when GROUP BY in mat.view differs to the ORDER BY key of AggregatingMergeTree but I cannot imagine if they are useful.
Seems to work perfectly in my testing - no need for Null engines or GROUP BY's any more. Great work!

Hm actually I just came across a case where this is not working so well. I'm using cloudflare goflow and have an agg table like:

```
CREATE TABLE netflow_sum_proto_port (
    Time DateTime CODEC(DoubleDelta, LZ4),
    SamplerAddress IPv4 CODEC(ZSTD),
    ProtoName Enum8('ICMP'=1,'TCP'=6, 'UDP'=17,'other'=0),
    Port Int32,
    Flows SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, Float64),
    Packets SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, Float64),
    Bytes SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, Float64)
)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree()
PARTITION BY toDate(Time)
ORDER BY (Time, SamplerAddress, ProtoName, Port);

drop view if exists netflow_sum_proto_port_mv;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW netflow_sum_proto_port_mv TO netflow_sum_proto_port
AS SELECT
    toStartOfInterval(time, INTERVAL 30 SECOND) AS Time,
    reinterpretAsUInt32(reverse(SamplerAddress)) AS SamplerAddress,
    ProtoName,
    IF(Port in (443,80,0,445,993,143,2003,1443,3306,110,3389,22,21,23,995,25,53,19,587,2083,7000,1194,5060,4001,1198,389,123,1900,161,623,11211,131,132,133,134,135,136,137,138,139), Port, -1) Port,
    sum(Flows) AS Flows,
    sum(Packets) AS Packets,
    sum(Bytes) AS Bytes
FROM (
    SELECT
        toUInt32(TimeFlowEnd-TimeFlowStart+1) AS duration
        , arrayJoin(timeSlots(TimeFlowStart, duration, 1)) AS time
        , SamplerAddress
        , IF( Proto in (1,6,17), Proto, 0 ) AS ProtoName
        , arrayJoin([SrcPort, DstPort]) AS Port
        , 1.0 / 2 / duration AS Flows
        , toFloat32(Packets) / 2 / duration AS Packets
        , toFloat32(Bytes) / 2 / duration AS Bytes
    FROM netflow_flows
    WHERE Type = 'Netflow_9'
) t;
```

This is working fine, but if I truncate + insert historic data it goes very slow without the group by - if I add `GROUP BY Time, SamplerAddress, ProtoName, Port` on the end it goes about 20* faster inserting. I'm only using `max_insert_threads=1` so perhaps that is the difference as when doing the GROUP BY it seems to use quite a bit more CPU.
Yes, it is expected: GROUP BY implementation (it's the same as used for SELECT queries) is faster than merging (including merge-on-insert).
So, the answer is: it still makes sense :)

title: Cascade view prevents kafka from committing
body:
ClickHouse server version 20.8.9 revision 54438

Imagine we have the following structure of tables

kafka_queue ->  mv1 -> mergetree1 -> mv2 -> mergetree2

If we push to kafka message which cannot be processed by mv2(for example wrong data type) message will be inserted to mergetree1, but CH will not commit to kafka that message was processed. So in the end message will be inserted to mergetree1 infinite amount of times

How to reproduce

Create all tables
```SQL
CREATE TABLE dummy_queue (
  app_id String
) ENGINE = Kafka('{kafka_brokers_stage}', 'dummy_queue', 'stage-dummy_ch_queue', 'JSONEachRow');

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dummy_mv TO dummy (
  app_id String
) AS SELECT app_id FROM dummy_queue;

CREATE TABLE dummy (
  app_id String
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (app_id);

CREATE TABLE dummy_cascade (
  app_id UInt32
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (app_id);

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dummy_cascade_mv TO dummy_cascade
AS SELECT toUInt32(app_id) * 2 AS app_id FROM dummy;
```
Insert record that can be parsed
```
kafkacat -b kafka -t dummy_queue -P
{"app_id":"2"}
```
Watch that dummy_cascade table filled
```SQL
SELECT *
FROM dummy_cascade

┌─app_id─┐
│      4 │
└────────┘
```
Insert record that cannot be parsed
```
kafkacat -b kafka -t dummy_queue -P
{"app_id":"test"}
```
dummy_cascade table don't have new records, because of parsing error `DB::Exception: Cannot parse string 'test' as UInt32: syntax error at begin of string`
```SQL
SELECT *
FROM dummy_cascade

┌─app_id─┐
│      4 │
└────────┘
```

However in intermediate table dummy will be a lot of duplicate records, and the number of records will be growing and growing

```SQL
SELECT *
FROM dummy

┌─app_id─┐
│ 2      │
│ test   │
│ test   │
│ test   │
│ test   │
│ test   │
└────────┘
┌─app_id─┐
│ test   │
└────────┘
┌─app_id─┐
│ test   │
└────────┘
author: simpl1g

comments.body:
By design.

Insert is successful only all inserts into dependent materialized views succeeded.
Then commit into kafka happen.

It's a strange design, I would expect such behavior if mv2 was connected to kafka_queue directly. However in this case mv2 doesn't care how data is written to mergetree1, why should queue fail. Also in case of problem it is easier to write data from mergetree1 to mergetree2 from scratch, than to think how to deduplicate it in mergetree1.

I expect that data is written to mergetree1 and committed if all mv connected to queue directly worked
Kafka don't know if the first level table is real MergeTree, or for example engine=Null (then only second level MVs matter).

--min_bytes_to_use_direct_io arg                                 The minimum number of bytes for reading the data with O_DIRECT option during SELECT queries execution. 0 - disabled.

```
create table table10kRows(A Int64) Engine =MergeTree() order by A;
insert into table10kRows select number from numbers(10000);

QPS: 4983.314


clickhouse-benchmark -c 16 --optimize_trivial_count_query=0 --database=default <<< 'select count() from table10kRows' 
QPS: 10597.303

clickhouse-benchmark -c 16 --optimize_trivial_count_query=0 --min_bytes_to_use_direct_io=1 --database=default <<< 'select count() from table10kRows'
QPS: 11212.843
```

funny that optimize_trivial_count_query=0 gives a boost, probably it's only for a small tables.
So if I don't want to use the cache for testing disk io, can I use it `--optimize_trivial_count_query=0 --min_bytes_to_use_direct_io=1`, and why it is faster? @den-crane

Yes.

Because of my hardware + table table10kRows is too small.

title: Altering Enum in ordering key doesn't work on ReplicatedMergeTree
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reproduces at 20.8.12.2 Clickhouse version.

```
CREATE TABLE t ON CLUSTER replicated
(
    `a` UInt64,
    `b` Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2)
)
ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/default/{shard}/t', '{replica}')
ORDER BY (b, a)

INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,1),(2,2)

ALTER TABLE t ON CLUSTER replicated MODIFY COLUMN b Enum8('a' = 1)
```
The last statement falls into error: `Cannot execute replicated DDL query, maximum retires exceeded`

In case of local alter: 
`ALTER TABLE t ON CLUSTER replicated MODIFY COLUMN b Enum8('a' = 1)`

the error is next:
```
Received exception from server (version 20.8.12):
Code: 524. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9100. DB::Exception: ALTER of key column b from type Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2) to type Enum8('a' = 1) must be metadata-only.
```


**Expected behavior**
The same as on non-Replicated MergeTree
author: Blackmorse

comments.body:
Hi!

Alter of the key columns in ClickHouse is quite limited. You can alter enums but only add new values. Removing old values can change the representation of the primary key. 
```
:) ALTER TABLE t
    MODIFY COLUMN `b` Enum8('a' = 1)

Received exception from server (version 21.2.1):
Code: 524. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: ALTER of key column b from type Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2) to type Enum8('a' = 1) is not safe because it can change the representation of primary key. 
```
but the extension is allowed:
```

ALTER TABLE t
    MODIFY COLUMN `b` Enum8('a' = 1, 'b' = 2, 'c' = 3)

Ok.

```

> The same as on non-Replicated MergeTree

But how it's related to Replicated / non-Replicated MergeTree?

@alesapin , 

>  You can alter enums but only add new values

But documentation says:

> The Enum type can be changed without cost using ALTER, if only the set of values is changed. It is possible to both add and remove members of the Enum using ALTER (removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table)

> @alesapin ,
> 
> > You can alter enums but only add new values
> 
> But documentation says:
> 
> > The Enum type can be changed without cost using ALTER, if only the set of values is changed. It is possible to both add and remove members of the Enum using ALTER (removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table)

As the documentation says:
`> removing is safe only if the removed value has never been used in the table`

We restrict unsafe operations for the primary key columns because it can lead not only to the single-column corruption but to the whole table became broken.
@alesapin , So , It is correct behaviour, right?

> @alesapin , So , It is correct behaviour, right?

Yes, it's expected, maybe we have to improve docs.
Thanks

title: Materialized view with AggregatingMergeTree has different rows count on every select
body:
Hello.
I have a table:
```
CREATE TABLE user_locations
(
    user_id                        UInt64,
    latitude                       Float64,
    longitude                      Float64,
    created_at                     DateTime
)
    engine = MergeTree()
        PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(created_at)
        ORDER BY (user_id, created_at)
        TTL created_at + toIntervalMonth(3)
        SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;
```
It has about ~30 billions rows and ~100 inserts per second (using bulk inserts). There are no rows older than 1 month, data never being updated or deleted (insert only).
I need to get latest records per user, so i tried to use materialized view:
```
CREATE MATERIALZED VIEW user_locations_latest
engine = AggregatingMergeTree() PARTITION BY tuple() ORDER BY (user_id)
POPULATE AS
SELECT
    user_id,
    maxState(created_at) AS created_at
FROM user_locations
GROUP BY user_id;
```
The problem is this materialized view has different rows count on every `SELECT`:
```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_locations_latest;
5272
5233
5263
5248
5143
5277
```
If i stop to insert data, the count is always the same:
```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_locations_latest;
5279
5279
5279
```
I expect that rows count should be always the same or higher, but not less, regardless of inserting data or not. Documentation tells nothing about such behaviour.
Clickhouse 20.8.

Case 2: Key-value dictionaries like `cache`, `direct`:
\- ClickHouse will run the script, pipe the requested keys to its stdin and read the corresponding records from it's stdout.

It's because `SET` query changes setting value in current session. Distributed DDL queries are executed in separate session and `SET` query does not affect it. You should enable `allow_experimental_database_materialize_mysql` setting globally in server config to make it work with `ON CLUSTER` queries. Example:
```
    <profiles>
            <default>
                    <allow_experimental_database_materialize_mysql>1</allow_experimental_database_materialize_mysql>
                    ...
            </default>
            ...
    </profiles>
```

Another option is to configure distributed DDL queries to use separate settings profile with all settings you need:
```
    <profiles>
            <default>
                    ...
            </default>
            <dddl>
                    <allow_experimental_database_materialize_mysql>1</allow_experimental_database_materialize_mysql>
            </dddl>
            ...
    </profiles>

        <path>/clickhouse/task_queue/ddl</path>
        <profile>dddl</profile>

```

title: what kind of optimization interpreter CK used? cost-based or rule-based?
author: tenderisthenightGM

comments.body:
Mostly rule-based. Also simple cost-based for one case ("move-to-prewhere" optimization).
Also optimization with bayesian bandits for lz4 decompression and for some functions dispatch.
Thanks, but could you please tell me why it did not introduce the cost-base optimizer likes GPDB or Spark.

@tenderisthenightGM
1. because mostly CBO is needed for choosing of the most efficient access path: indexes / joins (choosing what type of join to use. Right now CH does not support inverted indexes and supports mostly only HJ. So the access path is straightforward and does not require even RBO.
2. there are tons of more important tasks.   
3. CH is opensource. Nobody implemented CBO yet.
@den-crane Thanks very much.

title: How to deal with the setting of primary key and index in new business table creation
body: When creating a new business table, we don't know the query latitude, query scenario, query mode and other information. However, the setting, order and index configuration of primary key and sorting construction have a great impact on the query performance of Clickhouse. At present, the cluster does not support the change of primary key and sorting construction order. How to guarantee the query performance in this scenario? Or do you have any good suggestions for new business, sorting and primary key setting when creating tables?
author: shadowDy

comments.body:
>Or do you have any good suggestions

No. We still unable predict the future. Just test on a daily data, choose some suitable table structure. Re-work / reload data later if needed.

> Re-work / reload data later if needed.

In this mode, when adding columns to the table that need high-frequency query, you need to adjust the order of the sort key, and you need to replay all the data. It's too troublesome

> > Re-work / reload data later if needed.
> 
> In this mode, when adding columns to the table that need high-frequency query, you need to adjust the order of the sort key, and you need to replay all the data. It's too troublesome

The problem that you don't not have options with CH. 
There is no magic. Terra-bytes of data cannot be reordered for free. It needs to read/uncompress/sort/compress/write.

hi, 

#11996 is addressed MySQL engine enum type.
MaterializedMySQL enum is not releated to it.

Maybe someone has an idea what caused this error?

SQL Error [50]: ClickHouse exception, code: 50, host: ***, port: 8123; Code: 50, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Unknown data type family: enum. Maybe you meant: ['Enum','Enum8'] (version 20.13.1.5273 (official build))

> Maybe someone has an idea what caused this error?

Short answer: MaterializeMySQL does not support ENUM data type.

Long answer:
The error happens because data type names in ClickHouse are case-sensitive, and data type names in MySQL are case-insensitive, so ClickHouse does not have `enum` or `ENUM` data type, but it has `Enum`. We could add case-insensitive alias for `Enum` data type name (like we added `BIGINT` alias for `Int64`, for example), but there is another issue. ClickHouse requires Enum values to be declared as `'name' = value`, but MySQL assignes values to names implicitly. We also need support of syntax like `Enum('a', 'b', 'c')` in ClickHouse.
It's a good idea to do both :)
HI! when can we expect support for this functionality (enum)?)

It seems that there are two approaches that could be explored to implement this, either mapping to ClickHouse enums, or mapping to LowCardinality(String).

In both cases one has to account for MySQL's case insensitivity, which means either upper- or lower-casing the enum values when passed as strings.

Keeping the numerical values in sync seems doable (since MySQL won't let you remove an enum field that is present in a row), but one has to parse the enum type from information_schema.columns and implicitly assign numeric values from their order. This may cause funkiness down the line if there are materialized views that have outdated enum values, but that could be documented with a caveat.

The LowCardinality(String) approach seems more generic, but AFAIK it's going to consume more space, and you will lose the ability to do numerical comparisons.

@tavplubix what do you think about adding optional case-insensitivity for enum value lookups in CH, and enable this transparently in StorageMaterializeMySQL::read()? We have a summer intern who can implement this.
This issue is addressed by #25676

author: gj-zhang

comments.body: `ALTER DELETE` need extra disk space to reserve  intermediate result. Maybe you can consider `ALTER DROP PARTITION`, which drop a partition each time.

> `ALTER DELETE` need extra disk space to reserve intermediate result. Maybe you can consider `ALTER DROP PARTITION`, which drop a partition each time.

Is that the only way?

@gj-zhang You can DETACH some old partition, then manually move it out to some other server. Then perform ALTER DELETE to delete some data. When disk space will be freed, move partition back and ATTACH.

TLDR: You need to temporary free some space to do ALTER DELETE.
If you are using cloud service, just increase the disk size or move all data to another VM with larger disk.
If table is replicated, you can also migrate to another server with zero downtime by creating a new replica on larger server and then dropping the old replica.

title: Extraction float64 value from JSON fails
author: cetver

comments.body:
`JSON` format does not have `float64` data type, it has implementation-defined `Number` data type. The number `99999999999999999999` is not representable as `Number` in some implementations, so the first row is invalid and `JSONExtract` returns empty string.

```
:) SELECT isValidJSON(json), type FROM (SELECT '{"value":99999999999999999999}' json, 'float' type UNION ALL SELECT '{"value":"99999999999999999999"}' json, 'string' type)

SELECT
    isValidJSON(json),
    type
FROM 
(
    SELECT
        '{"value":99999999999999999999}' AS json,
        'float' AS type
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        '{"value":"99999999999999999999"}' AS json,
        'string' AS type
)

┌─isValidJSON(json)─┬─type──┐
│                 0 │ float │
└───────────────────┴───────┘
┌─isValidJSON(json)─┬─type───┐
│                 1 │ string │
└───────────────────┴────────┘

```

I still think that this is a bug, or the behavior is not specified in the documentation.

Max "true" int is `Int64`, if the value between -9223372036854775808 : 9223372036854775807 extract functions works as expected

title: What is the difference between attach/detach and move partition
body:
Hi Team,
My requirement is move partition from one table and another table. 
Both `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` and `MOVE PARTITION TO TABLE` could meet my requirement, but what is the difference and which one has better performance?

Thanks!
Wenjun
author: RangerWolf

comments.body:
These queries are almost identical, except the following details:
 - `MOVE PARTITION TO TABLE` deletes partition from the source table, `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` doesn't.
 - It's not possible to `MOVE` partitions between replicated and not-replicated tables, `ATTACH` should work fine with `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`.

There is also `REPLACE PARTITION` query, it's similar to `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`, but it deletes partition from the destination table before  attaching.

> These queries are almost identical, except the following details:
> 
> * `MOVE PARTITION TO TABLE` deletes partition from the source table, `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` doesn't.
> * It's not possible to `MOVE` partitions between replicated and not-replicated tables, `ATTACH` should work fine with `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`.
> 
> There is also `REPLACE PARTITION` query, it's similar to `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`, but it deletes partition from the destination table before attaching.

Thanks, but which one has better performance?  @tavplubix
All of them are almost identical, so performance is the same

> All of them are almost identical, so performance is the same

Thanks!

> All of them are almost identical, so performance is the same

Not at all true.
MOVE has some replication queue magic under the hood. MOV'ing a partition with lots of parts dumped tens of thousands of entries into replication_queue, after which the replication queue stopped processing and data was eventually lost. (Seems like the replication magic has lots of race conditions and bugs.)

ATTACH FROM just copied parts into the table. Not sure if the parts will be replicated eventually or not.

(Both tables are replicated in this case.)

groupArrayMovingSum  groupArrayMovingAvg ?

`neighbor` function is tricky to use - it can obtain neighbour values only within a block.

```

  columnName

group by

Distinct and Groupby use different algorithms.
Distinct produces the first row faster. For example compare the same queries with LIMIT 1.

Now the difference is just an implementation detail.

title: Dropping insignificant (tail) items from an AggregatingMergeTree ?
body: I'm sure there must be a solution to this, but if we have an `AggregatingMergeTree` collating details of something like path hits by `toStartOfInterval(time, xxx)`, is it easily possible to make it so that it only keeps the top X per time interval where X is in the order of 10k-100k and drop all the tail stuff? So something like a TTL but for a `select item, count() total where time = xxx order by total desc limit 10000` drop anything that isn't in that query? Obviously this is possible to automate using periodically executed manual sql to only copy top items to another table but is there an in-clickhouse way?
author: mzealey

comments.body:
The main difficulty is that CH collapses/evaluates AggregatingMergeTree during the merge process. But the merge merges only some part of data at a time.

Try TTL where. 
It will not give pure result because it operates in a scope of parts in the merge. But eventually it will.

I remember similar use case that we faced in Yandex.Metrica when we were storing aggregated data.
E.g. keep only top 1000 URLs for every website for every batch of inserted data.

But it was before we started using ClickHouse.
After migrated to ClickHouse, we just decided to not aggregate data at all :rofl: 

Nevertheless, it is possible to solve this task with periodic ALTER DELETE.

title: Import to CSV - How to escape LINE FEED
body:
Can't import CSV file when a (string) field contains LF. ### Case prostgreSQL - Table system pg_stat_statements ( execution statistics of SQL statements executed by server ) We want copy its content to CH. `query` column stores texts of statements. ### Problem Some of SQL statements are splitted by LF. When generating CSV file to import in CH, lines are so splitted. Ex. (separator is '|") : 
"...|"SELECT 
     ...
     relid,                         --  - long
     schemaname,           --  - string
     relname,                   --  - string
     ...
     tidx_blks_read,          --  - long
     tidx_blks_hit             --  - long
FROM  pg_statio_all_tables"|3|...|....
CH complains : `Cannot parse input: expected | before: ...` We hoped that CH would continue to read from the first delimiter (double) quote to the other one. It would be nice not to have to substitute `LF `for `` (for example).
author: XavierQuiniou

comments.body:
I'm using CLICKHOUSE4J (cc.blynk.clickhouse) It's based upon HTTP client. I proceed like that : 
 
String sql = "INSERT INTO my-base.my-table FORMAT CSV settings format_csv_delimiter='|'";
copyManager.copyToDb(sql, my-file);
How to place with csv force quote *; ? As a setting ?
Do I understand that we can not use this feature, when writing sql statement : INSERT INTO ... ?

I'll try to explain. **The problem is not related to CH!!!!!**
CSV format defines that **ROWS**!!! are separated by new_line character. Multiline STRING VALUES MUST BE surrounded by " (double quotes) otherwise it's impossible to distinguish rows.

Here is an example:

```
very
long 
row
```
VS
```
"very
long 
row"
```

PG allows you to surround long STRING values by " in the copy command by "with csv force quote *;"

> Hi @yi , we've met the same issues, have you finally figured out a solution?

Kindly worked out. it was really painful due to the large size of that table. 

Solutions:
 1.  DROP unused/outdated PARTITIONs or parts of that table on the current cluster node(A)
 2. Setup a new clickhouse cluster node(B)
 3. Create that table in the new cluster, and the newly created table will be synced with new TTL setting from zookeeper
 4. DROP  that table on cluster node(A)
 5. re-create that table on cluster node(A)

author: ralphM78

comments.body:
> after restoring a replicated table,

Most probably you did backup recovery from the same backup on 2 replicas (some ATTACH / part / partition manipulation commands). You need to recover single replica from backup, on other replicas you need only to recreate the table and it will sync the data from the other one. 

> Is it possible to delete one of these parts ?

No cheap / easy way. You can try OPTIMIZE DEDUPLICATE (but it's quite heavy operation, will dedup on row level).

It is not safe (it's hard to do it w/o braking some invariants), beside that i guess lot of those parts were merged together already.

If the schema (set of columns / keys / partitioning etc) is the same - then the answer is yes, definitely. You can move the partitions between Replicated and non-Replicated tables.

title: Last in the selection ReplacingMergeTree.
body: I use ReplacingMergeTree, after a while old data versions lose. I want to ask how to configure that time? And I want to configure ReplacingMergeTree every time I push data to save only the latest version?
author: vladimirteddy

comments.body:
> I use ReplacingMergeTree, after a while old data versions lose. I want to ask how to configure that time?

No way for that. If you need to preserve all versions of your data row - use plain MergeTree (may be with some TTL expression), and argMax aggregate functions go access last values (or create materialized view to access last values using Replacing / Aggregating)

> And I want to configure ReplacingMergeTree every time I push data to save only the latest version?

Not possible. It's eventual. If your inserts happens very rare (like once per day) you can use OPTIMIZE FINAL command after your inserts. But it will not work with real-time ingestion.
Thank you @filimonov .

title: Storing huge amount of log entries
body:
Hello,

I would like to use ClickHouse for storing huge amount of log entries (sorted without ORDER BY) and after some time dump it to disk and send to the clients. 
I have tried to use tables with mergetree table engine but, as the description of mergetree engine says it was not sorted, because not all parts were merged. 

Is there a way how to achieve desired behavior? I would like to have sorted logs without ORDER BY expression. Is it even possible with some engines?
I have look into Log engine but it does not support TTL and replication.

Thank you for help
author: wutchzone

comments.body:
You should use *MergeTree. Other engines is not suggested for permanent data.
Can you show "create table xxx" for MergeTree ?
You can use MergeTree without ORDERBY (`order by tuple()`), but usually it has no sense. At least you can add fake column with insertion date.

```sql
CREATE TABLE mylogs
(
    `Log` String,
    `created_at` Date MATERIALIZED today()
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(created_at)
ORDER BY created_at
```

Can you show your supposed selects ?

> Is there a way how to achieve desired behavior? I would like to have sorted logs without ORDER BY expression. Is it even possible with some engines?

Logs are typically stored in MergeTree table with ORDER BY time column.

@den-crane @alexey-milovidov 
Thank you both for help. Firstly I was very confused when I used the MergeeTree engine, because I tried to dump the data too early. Propably many parts were not merged and it consumed a lot of RAM when used with ORDER BY. When I try to dump after hour when they were inserted, it does not consumed RAM at all and it performs smoothly. I was just afraid that this cannot be solved with mergee tree, but it can. Now everything is working perfectly, thank you once more.

title: RBAC - KILL MUTATION requires 0 grants, but KILL MUTATION ON CLUSTER requires 4 ALTER grants.
body:
A user doesn't need any grants to execute `KILL MUTATION` , but needs `ALTER UPDATE`, `ALTER DELETE`, `ALTER MATERIALIZE INDEX`, and `ALTER MATERIALIZE TTL` to execute `KILL MUTATION ON CLUSTER`.

**How to reproduce**
* ClickHouse server version 20.12.1

* Queries to run that lead to unexpected result
```
clickhouse1 :) kill mutation where 1

KILL MUTATION WHERE 1 ASYNC

Query id: e7a0a643-28d1-40bd-a0fe-45137868f0aa

Ok.

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.006 sec.

clickhouse1 :) kill mutation on cluster sharded_cluster where 1

KILL MUTATION ON CLUSTER sharded_cluster WHERE 1 ASYNC

Query id: e3be7b71-03f7-410c-9b40-7761d9a92fcd

Received exception from server (version 20.12.1):
Code: 497. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: user0: Not enough privileges. To execute this query it's necessary to have the grant ALTER UPDATE, ALTER DELETE, ALTER MATERIALIZE INDEX, ALTER MATERIALIZE TTL ON *.*.

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.023 sec.
```
author: MyroTk

comments.body:
@MyroTk 

Most likely you are being able to execute your KILL MUTATION query because there are no mutations and there is nothing to kill.

To execute `KILL MUTATION` (without `ON CLUSTER`) for a mutation you must have the exact grant which was required to start that mutation. It means e.g. to kill `alter delete` mutation you must have the `ALTER DELETE` grant.

To execute `KILL MUTATION ON CLUSTER` you must have all the grants `ALTER DELETE, ALTER UPDATE, ALTER MATERIALIZE TTL ON *.*` because it's executed on cluster and while we're checking the access righs we don't know yet which mutations we're actually going to kill.
@MyroTk Please update the documentation.

> In my docker , i only just run one "mysql" , it means that i need to set up mysql cluster? Can the 'ch' synchronize one "mysql"?

Yes, MaterializeMySQL supports replication from single MySQL server, you don't need to setup a cluster.

>  i update the data of mysql ... and the tables of clickhouse has not change

MaterializeMySQL replicates tables from one database in MySQL, changes in other databases are ignored.  If you want to replicate data from several databases in MySQL, you should create several corresponding MaterializeMySQL databases in ClickHouse. To enable replication from some database, you should specify correct name of database in MySQL when creating MaterializeMySQL database in ClickHouse. For example, if you have database named `some_db_name` in MySQL, then you should create database in ClickHouse with `engine=MaterializeMySQL('hostname:port', 'some_db_name', 'user', 'password')`. Most likely there is no changes in ClickHouse tables because you specified name of wrong database.

title: [proposed bug] Join Table Engine limitation
body:
Стоит следующая задача: необходимо мапить одно значение на другое во множестве запросов, таблица мапинга достаточно большая, 100-500М записей, для этого была создана таблица с движком Join с последующим мапингом через joinGet
`CREATE TABLE lookup (key UInt64, id UInt64) ENGINE = Join(ANY, LEFT, key)`

Но вот дальше стали происходить какие-то странности, при вставке данных в эту таблицу вылетает сообщение
` DB::Exception: Memory limit (total) exceeded: would use 1.92 GiB (attempt to allocate chunk of 402654352 bytes), maximum: 1.75 GiB: While executing SinkToOutputStream (version 20.9.2.20 (official build))`

Для вставки использовалась либо обычная таблица MergeTree с исходными данными, либо генерация
`INSERT INTO lookup (key, id) SELECT rand64() + arrayJoin(range(1000000)), 0`

Странность заключается в том, что каждый раз при пересоздании таблицы лимиты на количество записей разные, 8388608, 16777216, 33554432, а иногда и нормально без ограничений, ну или не удалось их достигнуть.

Значения параметров max_rows_in_join, max_bytes_in_join по умолчанию 0.
Проверял на разных серверах и версиях 19.4.5.1 и 20.9.2.20, ситуация везде повторяется.

Соответственно 2 вопроса:
1. может есть иной механизм реализации подобного мапинга, сопоставимый по скорости?
2. откуда берутся лимиты на таблицы типа Join и как их контроллировать?
author: Fallenyasha

comments.body:
Чуть больше исследовал, посмотрел потребление памяти при выполнении запросов инсерта, вставлял блоками по ~2М записей, получается следующая картина

Т.е. похоже на то, что при достижении некоторого лимита записей происходит удвоение алоцируемой для таблицы памяти, при этом эта память поедается из max_memory_usage, что немного странно, т.е. получается что обычную таблицу типа MergeTree можно иметь с неограниченным количеством записей, а типа Join с непонятным ограничением, завязанным на max_memory_usage. Можно ли это обойти?

@Fallenyasha Лимиты берутся из ограничения на запрос, вставляющий данные.
Аллокация данных для таблицы типа Join происходит в контексте запроса на вставку.

Аллокация одной из структур данных требуется не на каждый запрос, а только если места в буфере таблицы недостаточно - в этом случае выделяется в два раза больше памяти, чем было ранее. Это объясняет наблюдаемые вами результаты.

Для того, чтобы обойти ограничение, выставите:
```
SET max_memory_usage = 0
```
перед вставкой.

When I executed a query, ClickHouse utilizes only one CPU core. There are 40 CPU cores.

Is it possible to parallelize this query to speed up?

To reproduce my problem, refer to the below queries.

Thank you.

**Prepare test data**
```SQL
CREATE TABLE test_merge
(
    `date` Date,
    `action1` LowCardinality(Nullable(String)),
    `action2` String,
    `uv` AggregateFunction(uniq, UInt64),
    `session` AggregateFunction(uniq, UInt64)
)
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree()
PARTITION BY date
ORDER BY (action1, action2)
```

```SQL
INSERT INTO test_merge SELECT 
    now(),
    CAST(number % 20000, 'String') AS action,
    action AS action2,
    uniqState(number),
    uniqState(number)
FROM 
(
    SELECT number
    FROM system.numbers
    LIMIT 100000000
)
GROUP BY 
    action,
    action2
```

**This query uses only one CPU core.**
```SQL
SELECT 
    action1,
    uniqMerge(uv) AS uv,
    uniqMerge(session) AS session
FROM test_merge
GROUP BY action1
ORDER BY uv DESC
LIMIT 10
```

ClickHouse Version: 20.8.2
author: achimbab

explain SELECT 
    action1,
    uniqMerge(uv) AS uv,

FROM test_merge

LIMIT 10
```
to see the execute plan

my plan

title: `select countMerge from ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree` get doubled results
body:
Hi all.
Recently I started using clickhouse and I have some troubles.
I create local MV on local table containing complete data (called it tbl), and create distributed MV based on local MV.
I use cluster with 3 shards and each shard has an extra replication, thus there are 6 servers in total.

Local table containing complete data, or tbl uses ReplicatedMergeTree as engine. Local MV uses ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree as engine.
In addition, I recreated every MVs on test database with POPULATE. In this way, there is no possible of duplicated insertion.

The problem is that,
when I select countMerge from distributed MV, I got twice the correct answer (i,e., if the correct answer is 50, I got 100.), 
while select uniqExactMerge from distributed MV will give a correct result.

Here is the script:
```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS test ON CLUSTER cc_cluster;
-- local MV
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW
IF NOT EXISTS
test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_local_test_v2
ON CLUSTER cc_cluster
ENGINE = ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{layer}-{shard}/test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_local_test_v2', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY (dt)
ORDER BY (dt, scene)
POPULATE
AS select
    countState(1) as expos,
    countState(if(click>0, 1, null)) as clicks,
    sumState(if(click=1, watch, 0)) as dr,
    countState(if(click=1 and tbl.cost_cnt>0, 1, null)) as cost_cnt,
    sumState(if(click=1, tbl.cost_total, 0)) as cost_total,
    countState(if(click=1 and tbl.chat_cnt>0, 1, null)) as chat_cnt,

    uniqExactState(recom_token) as item_expos,
    uniqExactState(if(click=1, recom_token, null)) as item_clicks,
    uniqExactState(uid) as user_expos,
    uniqExactState(if(click=1, uid, null)) as user_clicks,
    uniqExactState(if(click=1 and tbl.cost_cnt>0, uid, null)) as user_costs,
    uniqExactState(if(click=1 and tbl.chat_cnt>0, uid, null)) as user_chats,
    scene,
    toFixedString(dt, 8) as dt
FROM recom_stats_dws.user_event_log_day_local as tbl
GROUP BY dt, scene;

-- distributed MV
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_all_test_v2
ON CLUSTER cc_cluster
AS test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_local_test_v2
ENGINE = Distributed(cc_cluster, test, user_event_stat_scene_mv_local_test_v2, rand());


-- query
select  \
    countMerge(expos) as expos,  \
    countMerge(clicks) as clicks, \
    sumMerge(dr) as dr, \
    countMerge(cost_cnt) as cost_cnt, \
    sumMerge(cost_total) as cost_total, \
    countMerge(chat_cnt) as chat_cnt, \
    uniqExactMerge(item_expos) as item_expos, \
    uniqExactMerge(item_clicks) as item_clicks, \
    uniqExactMerge(user_expos) as user_expos, \
    uniqExactMerge(user_clicks) as user_clicks, \
    uniqExactMerge(user_costs) as user_costs, \
    uniqExactMerge(user_chats) as user_chats, \
    scene, \
    dt \
FROM test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_all_test_v2 as tbl \
GROUP BY dt, scene \
order by dt, scene;
```
PS: 
local MV = test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_local_test_v2
distributed MV = test.user_event_stat_scene_mv_all_test_v2
local table containing complete data = recom_stats_dws.user_event_log_day_local

Which part may I did something wrong?
hope to get your help XD
author: DouMiaoO-Oo

comments.body:
You have executed POPULATE twice. At each replica. It doubled the data.

You need to run POPULATE only at one replica.

on_cluster -- is just a helper. It executes this CREATE MAT.... at all nodes. 

then CREATE MAT.... POPULATE is executed at node N1 it does POPULATE over all data 
then CREATE MAT.... POPULATE is executed at node N2 (which is replica for N1) and it does POPULATE over all the same data as N1
and you get all duplicated in MV

I never use POPULATE becase it is unusable. You can insert data into MV by yourself.
@DouMiaoO-Oo I think you can close issue ;)

author: qinglok

comments.body:
>  this scheme can not be successfully implemented

what do you mean? 

For large insert ... select you may want to adjust several settings:

```
set
   max_insert_threads=4, /* flush to target table in parallel */ 
   max_threads=4,  /* don't use too many thread during select */
   min_insert_block_size_bytes = 536870912, /* combine smaller data blocks coming from select into larger */ 
   min_insert_block_size_rows = 16777216     /* that way insert will create fewer parts, but each one will be quite big */,
   max_bytes_before_external_group_by = '8G' /* allow on disk group by if your group by don't fit into memory */;
```


After that - just do your:
```
INSERT INTO table_1 SELECT ... FROM table_2 GROUP BY ...
```

Or (bit better/cheaper) - do a lot of INSERT ... SELECT slicing data every time by some condition to pick single (or few) groups at once, or single (of few) partitions at once.

P.S. Those setting are quite aggresive, and suitable only for moving bigger amounts of data. So defaults have more 'convervative' values.

This SQL has two parts.

JOINs and primary keys are not related. CH does not use indexes or keys for joins. There is no restrictions which columns can be used.

```sql
1)
SELECT DISTINCT name
FROM test_all AS a
GLOBAL INNER JOIN credit_ga.test_all_2 AS b ON a.name = b.name
ORDER BY name ASC

2)
SELECT DISTINCT name
FROM test_all AS a
INNER JOIN credit_ga.test_all_2 AS b ON a.name = b.name
ORDER BY name ASC

SQL1  An initiator executes `SELECT credit_ga.test_all_2 AS b` into temporary table. Then propagates this temporary table to shard of the table `test_all AS a`. Then shards do join with this temporary table. Table  `credit_ga.test_all_2` is read 1 time.

SQL2 executes double-distributed join. Each shard of the table `test_all AS a` selects data from `credit_ga.test_all_2 AS b` and do join. Table `credit_ga.test_all_2 AS b` is read by each shard.

title: How to grant CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE to a user
body:
When I execute the following sentence, I get an error

GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE on app.* to bigdata

Exception on client:
Code: 509. DB::Exception: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE cannot be granted on the database level
author: yanchaoguo

comments.body:
> When I execute the following sentence, I get an error
> 
> GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE on app.* to bigdata
> 
> Exception on client:
> Code: 509. DB::Exception: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE cannot be granted on the database level

@den-crane

`CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` is a privilege which can be granted only globally, i.e.

```
GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO user1, role2;
```

That's because temporary tables (unlike ordinary tables) aren't stored in databases. Temporary tables are identified only by name (not by `database_name + '.' + table_name`).

title: tokenbf_v2 index does not drop rows in aggregation query
body:
The tokenbf_v2 index does not drop rows when used in an aggregation query. That is, according to the query trace, it is used and rows are said to be dropped, but eventually all rows are scanned anyway as if the index didn't exist.

In my case I have a (large) table like:

```
CREATE TABLE MY_TABLE
(
    `Year` LowCardinality(String),
    `Route` String,
    `Count` Float64
)
ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree
PARTITION BY Year,
ORDER BY (Month, Route, Count),
INDEX route_index (Route) TYPE tokenbf_v1(256, 2, 0) GRANULARITY 1,
SETTINGS index_granularity = 128;
```

Route is a comma separated string of id's, like '242341,345223,12341'. There can be hundreds of id's in a Route.

When I query: 

`select Count(*) from MYTABLE where Year = '2020' and hasToken(Route, '12341')`

the query trace shows this:

Key condition: (column 2 in ['2020, '2020']), unknown, and
MinMax index condition: (column 0 in ['2020', '2020']), unknown, and
Index `route_index` has dropped 254959 granules.
Selected 1 parts by date, 1 parts by key, 17961 marks to read from 7839 ranges
Reading approx. 2299008 rows with 2 streams

which looks good, but then it proceeds to read all rows anyway:

Aggregated. 233990 to 1 rows (from 0.225 MiB) in 5.498 sec. (42560.946 rows/sec., 0.041 MiB/sec.)
Aggregated. 104612 to 1 rows (from 0.102 MiB) in 5.774 sec. (18119.055 rows/sec., 0.018 MiB/sec.)
Aggregated. 130101 to 1 rows (from 0.127 MiB) in 5.775 sec. (22529.594 rows/sec., 0.022 MiB/sec.)
Aggregator: Merging aggregated data
executeQuery: Read **34925324** rows, 16.27 GiB in 5.966 sec., 5853956 rows/sec., 2.73 GiB/sec.

Actually if I run the query like this, which does not invoke the route_index:

`select Count(*) from MYTABLE where Year = '2020' and Route LIKE '%12341%'`

in this case the query will be faster! The reason is it also scans all rows but does not have the extra first step of the tokenbf index.

Expected behaviour:

Since the tokenbf_v2 filter was able to skip 34925324 - 2299008 rows, which is 93% of the total number of rows, I expected the hasToken query to be faster than the LIKE query which didn't use any index.
I don't understand why the hasToken query, after initially dropping all those rows, proceeds to scan all rows anyway.

`route_index` analysis takes 200ms -- and this is expected.

Thanks, I checked and you are right. I don't know what went wrong the first time but I recreated the table and now things seem to work correctly. Also nice that the index can also be used in LIKE queries, as long as I add the comma's.

However, I noticed that the difference starts to become smaller when there are more partitions filled in my table. In your example there is no partitioning but my table has partitioning by YEAR. When there is only one partition filled, the query is a lot faster with the route_index. But if I add more years, the difference in speed becomes much smaller until it actually becomes much slower to query with index than without.

(to be clear, querying without index I do like:

`select Count(*) from MY_TABLE where Year = '2020' and Route like '%3119550599%'`

and to invoke the index I add the comma's to the like )

Actually I noticed that the difference only appears if I call another optimize after adding the data to my table with the index.
If I only add the data and don't call optimize, the query with index remains faster.

@den-crane I just reported what I was seeing. I also don't quite understand why the index query slowed down when filling more than one partition. But I have a feeling that it might just be the amount of data that made the index grow so large that it didn't fit into memory anymore.
To test this I tried making the index_granularity larger and the index queries started to be fast again, also with multiple partitions. This despite the fact that with larger index granularity the bloom filter cannot be as precise in dropping granules.

>This despite the fact that with larger index granularity the bloom filter cannot be as precise in dropping granules.

Analyzing skip indexes is a super-slow process and they are heavy and need to read them from disk.
When an index granula covers many rows it speeds up the index analyzes but decreases number of dropped rows.

title: Connecttion refused after kill the clickhouse server process
body:
I have a clickhouse table containing more than 40 billion records.  One day I want to modify a parameter in my config.xml. So I attempted to stop the server but it was stuck. I guess there were many background processes working. Then I kill the clickhouse server with "kill -9".
However when I tried to restart the server and run clickhouse-client again, I got "connection refused". 
If I remove all data partitions and the corresponding table metadata (sql), it works fine again. Once I move the table data back to its position, I got the same error "connection refused" again.

**How to reproduce**
if I tried to stop the clickhosue server process with "kill -9", but not "clickhouse-server stop". the error occurs. Especially when its a massive table.

version 20.0.10

If any ideas? Thanks.

comments.body:
40 billion records -- it's not big table. There are installation with 40 trillions.
CH start time depends on number of parts (table partitioning).

Can you show 
`select count() from system.parts`?
`select count() from system.columns where tables = ....` ?

Thanks for your reply @den-crane 
the table contains 14521 partitions and 119 columns.
do i have to wait for longer time after restart the server before trying to connect? have no idea...

>The table contains 14521 partitions and 119 columns.

Then slow start is expected. Especially on slow HDD or IOPS limited cloud disks (like AWS EBS GP1)
You should wait longer  for a start minutes. I've heard that in case of 100000 CH can start up to 40 minutes.
This is expected by design. Because CH reads reads every part (metadata) on start. 

You can use disks with low latency (SSD/NVME) or reduce number of partitions (by re-desingning your table -- partition by section).

title: For tables without a primary key, it is recommended to automatically add a hidden primary key when synchronizing to clickhouse, so that the synchronization can pass.
body: For tables without a primary key, it is recommended to automatically add a hidden primary key when synchronizing to clickhouse, so that the synchronization can pass.
author: dbawangwei

comments.body: And your question is ?

When the MySQL database is synchronized to clickhouse, the MySQL tables cannot be synchronized without a primary key. In production, many MySQL tables do not have a primary key for various reasons, so data cannot be synchronized to clickhouse.

This is impossible. Try to consider the following use cases
```
in mysql:> CREATE TABLE test(a int);
in mysql:> INSERT INTO test VALUES(1)(1)(2)(2)
in mysql:> UPDATE test SET a = 2 WHERE a = 1; /// ClickHouse will not know how to merge.
```

title: Question about ceil rows to complete granule
body:
In `MergeTreeRangeReader::startReadingChain`, there is the logic of `stream.ceilRowsToCompleteGranules(space_left)`,
May I know in which case we need to read part of granule?

Can provide some sql case for to produce this case? Thanks.
author: hustnn

comments.body:
Reading less than one granule is needed when granule is large and we don't want to create large blocks in memory.
As far as I remember, it's controlled by `preferred_block_size_bytes` setting.

Set it to lower value, make a table with wide rows, do SELECT *, and you will notice reading less than one granule.
@alexey-milovidov May I know why some reader (like `MergeTreeReaderCompact`) does not support reading of incomplete granule?

It's expected that only small portion of data is in compact parts - so reading less than one granule is not worth development for compact parts.
Also now we are using "adaptive granularity" - if table rows are heavy, granules will have less amount of rows automatically (it makes reading less than one granule partially obsolete, thought it still makes sense).

title: add clickhouse version to system.trace_log
body: It's hard to know if stacktraces don't match current clickhouse version.
author: filimonov

comments.body: OK, i see `revision` there, is it enough to idenify the version?

When version need to be changed with keepeing possibility to use tracelog:
```sql
CREATE TABLE system.addresses_dict
(
    `revision` UInt32,
    `address` UInt64,
    `line` String,
    `symbol` String,
    `demangle` String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY (revision, address)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 128;

INSERT INTO system.addresses_dict
select
    revision,
    address,
    addressToLine(address) as line,
    addressToSymbol(address) as symbol,
    demangle(symbol) as demangle
from 
(
    select
     revision,
     arrayJoin(trace) as address
   from system.trace_log
   group by revision, address
);
```
Revision is enough to distinguish two versions.
BTW - build can also differ. Maybe some kind of build id / binary checksum?
