title: system.parts.hash_of_uncompressed_files
body:
Hello. 

How is computed the field system.parts.hash_of_uncompressed_files ? 

What is its purpose ?

Regards.

nikk0
author: nikk0

comments.body:
There are some files that we don't compress, like `.idx`, `.mrk`.
But we still calculate hash of the data in these files, accumulate it and present in the `hash_of_uncompressed_files` field.

The purpose is the same as for other hashes - to compare them to find possible difference.

If table is replicated, hashes will be used to ensure that data on replicas will be byte-identical after replication. It protects from bit-flip errors in HDD (bit rot), bit flips in RAM on the server, RAM on the network controller, RAM on the network switches, data corruption during network transfer, memory stomping bugs in software, etc...
It is computed with `HashingWriteBuffer`, non-cryptographic hash function `CityHash_v1_0_2::CityHash128WithSeed` is used.

title: Can I create MaterializedView over remote table?
body:
There are 2 clusters.
I create table `base` and table `destination` on `cluster_1`.
```
create table base (id Int8, name String) ENGINE=MergeTree() order by id;
create table destination (id Int8, cnt Int8) ENGINE=MergeTree() order by id;
```
I create materialized view `view` on `cluster_1` and it's working as expected.
```
create MATERIALIZED VIEW view to destination as select id,count(name) as cnt from test;
```
**And here is the problem**. I create table `destination` and materialized view `view` on `cluster_2` which is based on table `test` from `cluster_1`.
```
create table destination (id Int8, cnt Int8) ENGINE=MergeTree() order by id;
create MATERIALIZED VIEW view to destination as select id,count(name) as cnt from remote('cluster_1',default.test,'default','') group by id;
```
I get exception:
```
Received exception from server (version 20.4.4):
Code: 49. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Logical error while creating StorageMaterializedView. Could not retrieve table name from select query..
```
It seems like materializedView source cannot be a remote table. And then I try to create a remote materializedView on `cluster_1`.
```
create MATERIALIZED VIEW remote_view to remote('cluster_2',default.destination,'default','') as select id,count(name) as cnt from test
```
Fail again:
```
Syntax error: failed at position 48:
Expected one of: CONSTRAINT, identifier, column declaration, INDEX, list of elements, columns or indices declaration list, table property (column, index, constraint) declaration
```

Do you know how to create MaterializedView over remote tables?
author: winter7

comments.body: The reason I ask this question is that I want to use Kafka Engine. I wonder if I should temporarily add some ClickHouse instances with kafka engine table as consumers when Kafka traffic surges and convert data by materialized View to the original (remote) Clickhouse instances. Is this a good way to deal with the sudden increase in Kafka traffic?

MaterializedView is an insert trigger. 

It gets data from **INSERT**. 

It **never** reads (selects) from table.

You must create MaterializedView at a server where inserts happen. You can re-route MaterializedView output to remote server. `create table xxx as remote(); create Materialized View .... to xxx as select .....`
Thank you! I think `create table xxx as remote();` is what I missed in my second attempt.

title: Table system.query_log does not exist for few systems
body:
Hi,
We are using clickhouse on our production servers. I have noticed that query_log table sometimes exist on some server and on some it does not exist.
Like I am running clickhouse on two servers with same default configs, no changes except for clickhouse version:
1)Clickhouse version 20..6.3 (here the table exists) 
2)Clickhouse version 20..4.6 (here the table does not exist)
Question: 
1) does query_log is enabled by default in latest version??
2) Does it depend on disk space also?? i mean the table will grow over time and does it get deleted afterwards or something like that?? When does the table flushes??
author: John-belt

comments.body:
It is enabled by default for all queries since version 20.5.
In older version you can enable it manually with the `log_queries` setting.
In new version, you can disable it with the same setting...
That's consistent with your report :)

> Does it depend on disk space also?? i mean the table will grow over time and does it get deleted afterwards or something like that?? 

No, there is no cleanup, it will grow indefinitely.
Usually it is quite small nevertheless and there is no issue.
Otherwise you can manually `TRUNCATE`, `ALTER ... DROP PARTITION` or `ALTER MODIFY TTL` to set automatic cleaning.

> When does the table flushes??

The data is flushed from in-memory buffer to the table every 7 seconds by default.
Yup that makes sense, thanks

когда в поле могут быть любые допустимые значения, без nullable не обойтись.

>Речь не идет о хранении, речь идет о том, что при создании view поверх
> селекта CH по умолчанию делает ненулевым поля которые по логике должны быть nullable.

я ничего не понял вообще. Пример есть?

>когда в поле могут быть любые допустимые значения, без nullable не обойтись.

это конечно так. 
! **Но у тысяч пользователей КХ нет ни одного Null в их БД и все просто сломается если они появятся после внезапного join_use_nulls = 1. Я не говорю про хранение, я про то что SQL запросы написаны таким образом что они ожидают 0 и '' , а не Null. Бекэнды просто не поддерживают Null и не умеют их отображать. Моя система просто сломается вся, и исправлять под Null надо несколько месяцев в нескольких командах, включая фронтэнд.**

select test.id, test.val, test2.val2 
from test 
left join test2 using id

подключаюсь с настройкой join_use_nulls = 1 
выполняю запрос - работает
создаю view
create or replace view tst as 
select test.id, test.val, test2.val2 
from test 
left join test2 using id

делаю 
select * from tst
Code: 349. DB::Exception: . DB::Exception: Cannot convert NULL value to non-Nullable type: while converting source column val2 to destination column val2.

если у них нет null то ничего и не сломается. их же нет :)

у запроса и у представления не должно быть разного поведения, но запрос работает, спокойно возвращает null, а представление нет.

это ожидаемое поведение view. Используйте settings join_use_nulls = 1

create or replace view tst as select test.id, test.val, test2.val2
from (select 1 id, 1 val) test
left join (select 2 id, 2 val2) test2 using id settings join_use_nulls = 1;

>если у них нет null то ничего и не сломается. их же нет :)

SQL запросы написаны таким образом что они ожидают 0 и '' , а не Null

```sql

select test.id, test.val, test2.val2, renamed
from (select 1 id, 1 val) test
left join (select 2 id, 2 val2, val2 renamed) test2 using id
where renamed = 0;
┌─id─┬─val─┬─val2─┬─renamed─┐
│  1 │   1 │    0 │       0 │
└────┴─────┴──────┴─────────┘
```

если внезапно установить set join_use_nulls = 1

```sql
set join_use_nulls = 1;

select test.id, test.val, test2.val2, renamed
from (select 1 id, 1 val) test
left join (select 2 id, 2 val2, val2 renamed) test2 using id
where renamed = 0;

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.001 sec.

```

плюс ко всему мои некоторые запросы вместо 4 минут, начинают работать 8 минут и это ожидаемое поведение, потому что делается group by по колонке которая результат join-а и нее меняется тип с UInt64, становится Nullable(UInt64)

title: How to use redis to create an external dictionary？
body:
According to the document, Clickhouse supports the use of redis to build an external dictionary, but there is no actual example to show how to use it.
There is a redis instance, hash_ map structure.(hmset key 1 a 2 b ),about 100 million keys
How should I use it？
I hope to get some examples.
Thanks!
author: IVitamin-C

comments.body: Hope to get help. Thank you very much
@CurtizJ  Can you give me an example? Thank you very much.

You can create a dictionary with complex key by using DDL:

```sql
CREATE DICTIONARY default.dict_redis
(
    `Key` String,
    `Field` String,
    `Value` String
)
PRIMARY KEY Key, Field
SOURCE(REDIS(HOST '127.0.0.1' PORT 6379 STORAGE_TYPE 'hash_map' DB_INDEX 0))
LIFETIME(MIN 1 MAX 10)
LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED())
```

To use Redis `hash_map` dictionary should have 3 columns,  primary key of 2 columns (key and field in terms of Redis), `STORAGE_TYPE 'hash_map'`, layout type started with `complex_key`. Currently for Redis with `hash_map` supported only `complex_key_hashed` and `complex_key_direct`, but not `complex_key_cached`.

Then you can get values by regular `dictGet` function. Example:
In Redis ```> hmset key1 field1 1 field2 2```
```
SELECT dictGet('default.dict_redis', 'Value', ('key1', 'field1')) AS value

┌─value─┐
│ 1     │
└───────┘

SELECT dictGet('default.dict_redis', 'Value', ('key1', 'field2')) AS value

┌─value─┐
│ 2     │
└───────┘
```

> You can create a dictionary with complex key by using DDL:
> 
> ```sql
> CREATE DICTIONARY default.dict_redis
> (
>     `Key` String,
>     `Field` String,
>     `Value` String
> )
> PRIMARY KEY Key, Field
> SOURCE(REDIS(HOST '127.0.0.1' PORT 6379 STORAGE_TYPE 'hash_map' DB_INDEX 0))
> LIFETIME(MIN 1 MAX 10)
> LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED())
> ```
> 
> To use Redis `hash_map` dictionary should have 3 columns, primary key of 2 columns (key and field in terms of Redis), `STORAGE_TYPE 'hash_map'`, layout type started with `complex_key`. Currently for Redis with `hash_map` supported only `complex_key_hashed` and `complex_key_direct`, but not `complex_key_cached`.
> 
> Then you can get values by regular `dictGet` function. Example:
> In Redis `> hmset key1 field1 1 field2 2`
> 
> ```
> SELECT dictGet('default.dict_redis', 'Value', ('key1', 'field1')) AS value
> 
> ┌─value─┐
> │ 1     │
> └───────┘
> 
> SELECT dictGet('default.dict_redis', 'Value', ('key1', 'field2')) AS value
> 
> ┌─value─┐
> │ 2     │
> └───────┘
> ```
I create the dictionary table：
```
CREATE DICTIONARY IF NOT EXISTS test.test1 
( `Key` String
    ,`Field` String  
    ,`Value` String DEFAULT ''
    ) 
PRIMARY KEY Key,Field
SOURCE(REDIS(HOST 'redis-123' PORT 50072 STORAGE_TYPE 'hash_map' PASSWORD 'test123' DB_INDEX 0)) 
LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_DIRECT());
```
Received exception from server (version 20.6.3):
Code: 489. DB::Exception: Received from 9.151.19.223:19000. DB::Exception: Primary key for simple dictionary must contain exactly one element.

It's a bug. #16007

BTW, I also implemented support of cache layout for Redis dictionaries. #15985

Export data from RocksDB to CSV file and import to CH as CSV

1. More than 10 billion lines

2. Close to 500GB

3. Import takes 5 hours or more

1. You can transform CSV to Native using clickhouse-local

   but I don't believe that it has sense. Because it's the same amount of job.

   CSV -> native( clickhouse-local ) -> clickhouse

   CSV -> clickhouse

2. Check the speed difference. 
   Download 1bil rows from CH `clickhouse-client -q 'select * from T limit 100000000 format Native'` > test.native

   clickhouse-client -q 'select * from T limit 100000000 format CSV'` > test.CSV

   Create test table `create table test as T`

   try load and compare the speed.  `clickhouse-client -tq "insert into T format Native" < file.native`
 
3. Try load in parallel by running multiple clickhouse-client (with disabled parallel parsing --input_format_parallel_parsing=0)

Native export time used 3090s, file size 460,223,132 KB.
Native import time used 4423s.

RowBinary export time used 3519s,  file size 460,706,927 KB.
RowBinary import time used 4673s.

   You can get a description of RowBinary format from CH documentation and Native almost the same as RowBinary the same value encodings but in columns not rows. You can copy Native implementation from JDBC driver or GO-driver.

2. you can use `clickhouse-local` and convert from CSV into Native.

3. You can load CSV in parallel by running multiple clickhouse-client (with disabled parallel parsing --input_format_parallel_parsing=0)

title: Count in AggregateMergeTree
body:
Hi Guyz,
I wanted to understand that how we can keep track of counts for a groupby keys. As In clickhouse, data is not anytime in its final form And when the parts get merged in background then columns for which no aggregate function is specified Any random values is taken.

For Example:
create table exp_raw(
	id UInt64,
	data String
)Engine=Log

create table exp_mergetree(
	id UInt64,
	eval UInt64,
	data SimpleAggregateFunction(max, String)
)
Engine = AggregatingMergeTree()
order by id

create materialized view exp_mv to exp_mergetree
AS select
id,
count() as eval,
max(data) as data
FROM exp_raw
Group BY id
order by id

INSERT INTO exp_raw values(12, 'hey')
INSERT INTO exp_raw values(12, 'Fine')

***************************************
select * from exp_mergetree;
It contains both of these records
┌─id─┬─eval─┬─data─┐
│ 12 │    1 │ Fine │
└────┴──────┴──────┘
┌─id─┬─eval─┬─data─┐
│ 12 │    1 │ hey  │
└────┴──────┴──────┘

When I run optimize table command, The result is
┌─id─┬─eval─┬─data─┐
│ 12 │    1 │ hey  │
└────┴──────┴──────┘

But Thats not what I want. I wanted the eval count to be 2.
Is there a way we can use count as an aggregate function in Aggregate merge tree table?
I can always keep one more column in raw table which has a value 1. But I am looking to solve this with aggregate function.
author: shubham721

comments.body:
SummingMergeTree -- does automatic summing of numeric columns, AggregatingMergeTree does not.

AggregatingMT require AggregateFunction   or SimpleAggregateFunction .

eval **SimpleAggregateFunction**(sum,UInt64)


```sql

create table exp_mergetree(
   id UInt64,
   eval SimpleAggregateFunction(sum,UInt64),    <---------------
   data SimpleAggregateFunction(max, String)
)
Engine = AggregatingMergeTree()
order by id
```

I can do that, But I won't be able to write populate query
As I can't give a aggregate function inside another one
sum(count()) is not supported.

>But I won't be able to write populate query

Not true. Give me example.

>sum(count()) is not supported.

You are mistaken. You don't need `sum(count())`. Try with only `count()`. MV will calculate count. Let's say 301. And will write 301 into a `eval SimpleAggregateFunction`. SimpleAggregateFunction does not require state or function. It works with simple values `301` during merges. 

In any case you can use sum(1) instead of count()  -- but it's overkill.

title: RBAC Materialized Views - User is required additional privileges to INSERT into the source table.
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a materialized view is created using a table as a source table, in order to insert on that table, the user is required INSERT and SELECT privilege on the source table, and INSERT privilege on the target table.

**How to reproduce**
* ClickHouse server version 20.9.1 revision 54439.
* `CREATE TABLE` statements for all tables involved
```
clicktest :) create materialized view mat1 to target0 as select * from table0

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mat1 TO target0 AS
SELECT *
FROM table0

Ok.

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.009 sec.
```

After granting INSERT on table0
```
#clickhouse-client -u user0
ClickHouse client version 20.9.1.4571 (official build).
Connecting to localhost:9000 as user user0.
Connected to ClickHouse server version 20.9.1 revision 54439.

clicktest :) insert into table0(d) Values ('01-14-2020')

INSERT INTO table0 (d) VALUES

Received exception from server (version 20.9.1):
Code: 497. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: user0: Not enough privileges. To execute this query it's necessary to have the grant SELECT(d, a, b, x, y) ON default.table0.
```
And after granting SELECT on table0
```
clicktest :) insert into table0(d) Values ('01-14-2020')

INSERT INTO table0 (d) VALUES

Received exception from server (version 20.9.1):
Code: 497. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: user0: Not enough privileges. To execute this query it's necessary to have the grant INSERT(d) ON default.target0.

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.008 sec.
```
**Expected behavior**
Only INSERT is required.
author: MyroTk

comments.body:
@MyroTk I see nothing wrong in this behaviour.
@vitlibar Please clarify.

Inserting into the source table of a material view causes automatically inserting into the materialized view's target table.
Both operations are executing in the same context, that's why you should have the INSERT privilege on both the source table and the target table to make the inserting into the source table.

I think we should fix that, because the user executing an INSERT into the source table must be able to do that without even knowing about the existence of the target table. It looks more convenient if ClickHouse would check the INSERT privilege on the target table when the materialized view is created, not when someone's trying to insert into the source table.
Duplicate #27570

title: Using _part and _partition_id inside MATERIALIZED VIEW
body:
Hi

I want to optimize my query by filtering partition name in WHERE clause like this:
```sql
select
	*
from
	test1
where
	_partition_id = '20200914'
````

It works well for me, but when I try to insert it into `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW TO` statement I get error:
> Not found column _partition_id in block.

Further tests made me think `_part` and `partition_id` fields are not visible in MV neither in WHERE clause nor in SELECT.
Code example:
```sql
drop table if exists test1;
create table test1
(
	name String
	, loaded datetime materialized now()
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
partition by toYYYYMMDD(loaded)
order by name
;

drop table if exists test2;
create table test2
(
	name String
	, value UInt8
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
order by name
;

drop table if exists test_trigger;
create materialized view test_trigger to test2
(
	name String
	, value UInt8
	, partition_id String
)
as
(
	select
		name as name
		, 1 as value
		, _partition_id as partition_id
	from
		test1
)
;

insert into test1 values('aaa'); -- this will occur the error
```
ClickHouse 20.5.3.27

Is it an expected and correct behavior of ClickHouse or am I doing something wrong?
author: sokolov-alexey

comments.body:
>_partition_id = '20200914'

1. It's huge mistake overall. CH does not guarantee that partition pruning will work against _partition_id column in the future.

   use `toYYYYMMDD(loaded) = 20200914`
   or better `loaded  >= '2020-09-14 00:00:00' and loaded < '2020-09-15 00:00:00'`


2. _partition_id is a virtual column in the table `test1`. MV select works over **inserted buffer** (rows from insert command). 
MV never reads real `test1` table.

   instead of  `_partition_id as partition_id`
   you should use `toYYYYMMDD(loaded) as partition_id`

title: About performance between hash join and partial merge join
body:
Hi ,
Now we face some join case, and I had test the newest  version about the join algorithm between hash join and partial merge join:

```
SET join_algorithm = 'partial_merge'
SELECT number * 200000 as n, j FROM numbers(5) nums ANY LEFT JOIN (     SELECT number * 2 AS n, number AS j     FROM numbers(10000000) ) js2 USING n;

MemoryTracker: Peak memory usage (for query): 457.46 MiB.
5 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.918 sec. Processed 10.02 million rows, 80.18 MB (10.92 million rows/s., 87.39 MB/s.) 

SET join_algorithm = 'hash'
SELECT number * 200000 as n, j FROM numbers(5) nums ANY LEFT JOIN (     SELECT number * 2 AS n, number AS j     FROM numbers(10000000) ) js2 USING n;

MemoryTracker: Peak memory usage (for query): 845.12 MiB.
5 rows in set. Elapsed: 2.023 sec. Processed 10.02 million rows, 80.18 MB (4.95 million rows/s., 39.63 MB/s.)
```

Seems the partial merge join has two times better than hash join in respect of memory/time cost at least. And also do some test against business data,  give the same result.

After profiling the hash join, found all the cost from building memory table for right table. But how the partial merge join work? seems no detail doc about this.  Just plan to upgrade to the partial merge join version and want make sure the partial merge join is really good for join case. big thanks.
author: compasses

comments.body:
I checked 'partial_merge' vs 'hash' algo when it was implemented on data from TPC-H test. It was 3-4 times slower when all data is in memory. So in general it should be slower.

Any case, It's expected that in some cases (when data in both tables is already sorted by joining key) MergeJoin would be faster than HashJoin. But it needs more code out of join algo itself to make such improvement: we should pass sort info through query pipeline to take it into account. I think you've find a special case that works even without such optimizations.

We need to investigate you question and recheck perf test results.

@4ertus2 very appreciate for your quick answer, please check my comments 

> I checked 'partial_merge' vs 'hash' algo when it was implemented on data from TPC-H test. It was 3-4 times slower when all data is in memory. So in general it should be slower.

How big the TPC-H data-set? I mean build the memory hash table need cost many memory and time. Maybe the data-set not big enough?

> Any case, It's expected that in some cases (when data in both tables is already sorted by joining key) MergeJoin would be faster than HashJoin. But it needs more code out of join algo itself to make such improvement: we should pass sort info through query pipeline to take it into account. I think you've find a special case that works even without such optimizations.

I think that's easy. The join table, left or right do have some related each other, and the join key exist in both two tables, 
and the order key of the two tables both contains the join key.  So it should be what you said 'data in both tables is already sorted by joining key' ?

> How big the TPC-H data-set? I mean build the memory hash table need cost many memory and time. Maybe the data-set not big enough?

I do not remebmer data-set size exactly. But hash table size was about 10-16 Gb.

> So it should be what you said 'data in both tables is already sorted by joining key' ?

Let me describe how does 'partial_merge' join algo works. It's a variant of MergeJoin adapted to ClickHouse query pipeline. ClickHouse streams left table in blocks and join it over full-known right table. It's a way how HashJoin expects join algo (first it builds hash table, second it scans left one). For honest MergeJoin we have to sort both tables and merge sorted results. 'partial_merge' algo do not sort left table, but has build and scan phases as 'hash' one instead. At build phase 'partial_merge' sorts right table by join key in blocks (and in general it's more expensive than just to make hash table). And create min-max index for sorted blocks. At 'scan' phase it sorts parts of left table by join key and merge join them over right table. It's also uses index to skip unneded right table blocks from join.

So, 'partial_merge' join could be faster when we could avoid sorts in build and scan phase (when the data is already sorted by joining key). And it would be much more expensive to use 'partial_merge' instead of 'hash' join algo when your left table has some general distribution of join keys cause you have to join every left table part with entire right table and min-max index does not help you in this case.

To make benefits of MergeJoin we have to tell it not to sort columns.
If not we could have profit of merge join at build phase if sorting of blocks is faster then building a hash table. It could happen in joins with a few tight columns in key (when hash table memory alloacations are meaningful).
Also it's possible to have some benefits in scan phase if min-max index of right table + merge join works faster than hash table lookups. We could have such situation when left table data is near to sorted.
These are special cases. Make a uniform distribution of inputs and wide string column in joining key and hash join wins.

Big thanks, seems more clear now.

In consideration of resource cost, the  'partial_merge' algorithm will have more less memory footprint, and I think usually more memory cost always cost more time. And especially under some resource limit environment.

Start from partial merge algorithm, there are many ways to optimize your SQL or data localization, but the hash join we had nothing to do but need more memory.

Hello, i have one question, 
Can I use partial_merge to avoid the problem of insufficient memory?

> 

@mateng0915 Yes, you can.

title: Time series based select queries slower compare to aggregation query
body:
We have 2 node cluster and each node has single shard and single replica. Below are my create table statements. 

`"create table archive.d_traffic on cluster '{cluster}' (  a  UInt32,  b  UInt32,  c  UInt32,  d  String,  timestamp  datetime,  metric1  Float32,  outoctets  Float32,  c  String, INDEX idxa (a) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxb (b) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxc (c) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxTime (timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxh (c) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbTime (b,timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxaTime (a,timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxba (a,b) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbaTime (b,a,timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbacTime (b,a,c,timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbacdTime (b,a,c,d,timestamp) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbaTimeh (b,a,timestamp,c) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbacTimeh (b,a,c,timestamp,c) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4, INDEX idxbacdTimeh (b,a,c,d,timestamp,c) TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 4 ) ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY toYYYYMM( timestamp ) ORDER BY ( a ,  b , timestamp )"`

`create table archive.d_traffic_distribute on cluster '{cluster}' as archive.d_traffic ENGINE = Distributed(f_cluster, archive, d_traffic, rand());`

Below select query we are running in single and multi-node environment. 

Time series select query :-
`"select metric1 from archive.d_traffic_distribute where timestamp > 1599084720 and timestamp <= (1599084720+72000) and IPv4NumToString(router) = '100' and b in (1,2,3,4,5) order by timestamp";
` 
 *Above query max returns 120K rows*
Single node response time = 12.02 secs  
Multi node response time = 12.06 secs

Aggregation query :- 
`select c,sum(metric1) from archive.d_traffic_distribute group by protocol order by c` 

Single node response time = 8.08 secs  
Multi node response time = 2.019secs

For Aggregation type query we are getting better result in multi node cluster. But normal time series based query response time is almost same. Is this expected? Or we need to do any table creation / cluster configuration changes ?
author: sounaks01

comments.body:
1. Clickhouse is not a timeseries DB.

2. ALL your skip **indexes are WRONG. Remove them.**
  INDEX idxTime (timestamp) TYPE minmax
  INDEX idxbTime (b,timestamp) TYPE minmax
  skip indexes  <> BTree. 
  b,timestamp ===  minmax B, minmax timestamp
  idxTime is excessive because it's covered by idxbTime.

3. You have compared the speed of 2 different queries. Why do you expect that `order by timestamp` have to work faster than ` group by protocol order by c` ?
  **The second query is faster because CH does not read heavy columns (from disk) like timestamp,router**

4. your table structure is not suitable for a streaming processing (with index path) of the first query.

title: Restoring MergeTree table with s3 storage on another server
body:
### Clickhouse version

Docker image: yandex/clickhouse-server:20.5.3.27 (standalone)

### Question

There is a MergeTree table with s3 storage specified by a policy. Is there any way to restore this table on another clickhouse server in case the main clickhouse server is down. As I got it, there is a local metadata file which stores information about s3 objects. As MergeTree engine is used, merges are constantly processed, and the metadata file is constantly being re-written as well. That's how I understand how it works. Therefore to restore this table on another server we do need to have this metadata file, right? What if we have an old metadata file? Is it still possible to restore the table? Or the only way to restore is to download the partitions and attach them from detached dir?
author: macEar

comments.body:
Hello,
Such problems can be resolved using ReplicatedMergeTree, but there is no deduplication on S3 side, each part for each replica is stored to S3 separately. Functionally ReplicatedMergeTree works well with S3 storage, but not optimally.
To resolve the deduplication problem we need to have a shared metadata engine. We have plans to do that thing.
Also, there is no inner mechanism to restore metadata from the data in S3. 
As one of the solution I propose just copy metadata files from an old server to a new server with a configured storage policy and created a table with the same structure. It should work. Rewriting metadata files shouldn't be a problem, because any insert, merge, or mutation first written to a temporary directory and only then is renamed and attached to MergeTree (atomicity).

title: How to delete records/drop partition synchronously from a Materialized view when deleting or dropping operation hanppens on source table?
body:
As title mentioned, is there a method to delete records/drop partition synchronously from a Materialized view when deleting or dropping operation hanppens on source table?

Or Any suggestions?
author: BernieJiangDL

comments.body:
No. 
No transactions.
And the source table has no relation to the Materialized view. Materialized view watches INSERTS.

> No.
> No transactions.
> And the source table has no relation to the Materialized view. Materialized view watches INSERTS.

When some unexpected results occur(from bussiness side, it might be some wrong/dirty records from upstream) after inserting. Rerunning the task is easiest way and then dropping a relative partition before reinsert to guarantee data is not duplicate.

But at this point, how can we deal with the materialized view on this source table? If we do nothing, the data in materialized view will be double.

Any suggestions for this? many thanks~

There are many approaches. 
You can design partitions in MV the same way as a source table. Drop partitions in the source table and MV.
You can insert into MV the same data with negative sign to cancel rows in MV and drop partition in the source table.
You can truncate MV and re-calculate it (manually) after inserting into the source table.

title: can clickhouse-copier copy data to another cluster using different timezone?
body:
I don't know much about the migration principle of clickhouse-copier.
I have two clusters A B, A uses Asia/Shanghai time zone, and B uses Etc/UTC.
I used clickhouse-copier to migrate the data and found that the Datetime columns were actually eight hours apart.

But if I manually import it in the following way, the data is correct.
```
clickhouse-client -udefault -hB --query="select * from db.table1" --format=CSV> table1.csv
clickhouse-client -u default -hA --database=broker --query="INSERT INTO db.table1 FORMAT CSV" <table1.csv
```
I read the log and thought clickhouse-copier was also insert after select, but the result was problematic. So I want to know the difference between clickhouse-copier's  and "select to csv then insert"
author: Fanduzi

comments.body:
Datetime. The point in time is saved as a Unix timestamp, **regardless of the time zone or daylight saving time**. 
Additionally, the DateTime type can store time zone that is the same for the entire column, that affects how the values of the DateTime type values are **displayed in text format** and how the values specified **as strings are parsed** (‘2020-01-01 05:00:01’). The time zone is not stored in the rows of the table (or in resultset), but **is stored in the column metadata**.


clickhouse-copier copies Datetime value as is. Number of seconds 1599746203 stays as is 1599746203 when you copy data from server A to server B. When you query 1599746203 you see different TZ string representation at A and B.

When you use CSV you convert 1599746203 to a string and parse from a string accordingly the current TZ (for a client/server).

```

# TZ=UTC clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' --use_client_time_zone=1
2020-09-10 13:56:43

# TZ=Asia/Shanghai clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' --use_client_time_zone=1
2020-09-10 21:56:43
```

> Datetime. The point in time is saved as a Unix timestamp, **regardless of the time zone or daylight saving time**.
> Additionally, the DateTime type can store time zone that is the same for the entire column, that affects how the values of the DateTime type values are **displayed in text format** and how the values specified **as strings are parsed** (‘2020-01-01 05:00:01’). The time zone is not stored in the rows of the table (or in resultset), but **is stored in the column metadata**.
> 
> clickhouse-copier copies Datetime value as is. Number of seconds 1599746203 stays as is 1599746203 when you copy data from server A to server B. When you query 1599746203 you see different TZ string representation at A and B.
> 
> When you use CSV you convert 1599746203 to a string and parse from a string accordingly the current TZ (for a client/server).
> 
> ```
> 
> # TZ=UTC clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' --use_client_time_zone=1
> 2020-09-10 13:56:43
> 
> # TZ=Asia/Shanghai clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' --use_client_time_zone=1
> 2020-09-10 21:56:43
> ```

thank you.
Does this mean I cannot use clickhouse-copier to migrate data between two clusters with different time zone?

> 
> Does this mean I cannot use clickhouse-copier to migrate data between two clusters with different time zone?

You can use clickhouse-copier. You need to configure the client to see results in desired timezone.

example : 
**TZ=Asia/Shanghai** clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' **--use_client_time_zone=1**

> > Does this mean I cannot use clickhouse-copier to migrate data between two clusters with different time zone?
> 
> You can use clickhouse-copier. You need to configure the client to see results in desired timezone.
> 
> example :
> **TZ=Asia/Shanghai** clickhouse-client -q 'select toDateTime(1599746203)' **--use_client_time_zone=1**

Thank you very much, I get it

title: Protobuf Schema mutations
body:
Hello

In order to use Protobug schema, I have to put it in `var/lib/clickhouse/format_schemas`.
Should I restart CH if I change this schema, for example adding a field?
author: yonesko

comments.body: Restart is not needed, it rereads the schema every time.

Every time when what? 

I have Kafka engine that consumes protobuf topic and mat view on it.

To my experience I had to restart to reread the schema
Yes, for Kafka table, DETACH TABLE / ATTACH TABLE is required to reread format schema.

title: dictGet gives error External dictionary not found
body:
Select from `system.dictionaries` shows my external odbc-sourced dictionary with status `LOADED`.

I can SELECT from that dictionary successfully.

However, running `dictGet()` on that dictionary says it was not found.

> Code: 36, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: external dictionary 'my_d' not found (version 20.6.3.28 (official build))

```sql
SELECT dictGet('my_d', 'name', tuple(toUUID('f724ff3c-3302-4abd-b403-b50a4d00e66a')));

```sql
CREATE DICTIONARY IF NOT EXISTS my_d ON CLUSTER '{cluster}' (
    id UUID,
    name String
)
PRIMARY KEY id
SOURCE(ODBC(connection_string 'DSN=pg_conn' TABLE 't1'))
LAYOUT(complex_key_hashed())

title: Secondary index performance expectation
body:
Hello,

I'm testing out the secondary index feature, and I'd like to know what to expect.

I have this Replicated Materialized View (obfuscated irrelevant field names) - 
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW sample_1d.logs
(
    `a` UInt64 DEFAULT CAST(0, 'UInt64'),
    `b` UInt64 DEFAULT CAST(0, 'UInt64'),
    `c` UInt64,
    `d` LowCardinality(String),
    `e` UInt8 DEFAULT 1,
    `f` Date DEFAULT toDate(toStartOfDay(timestamp)),
    `timestamp` DateTime,
    `partition_code` String,
    `h` LowCardinality(String),
    `i` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `j` LowCardinality(String),
    `k` LowCardinality(String),
    `l` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `m` LowCardinality(String),
    `n` UInt32,
    `o` LowCardinality(String),
    `p` String,
    `q` String,
    `r` String,
    `user_agent` LowCardinality(String),
    `s` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `asn` UInt32 DEFAULT 0,
    `as_org` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `isp` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `region_name` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `city_name` LowCardinality(String) DEFAULT CAST('', 'LowCardinality(String)'),
    `t` String,
    `u` String,
    `v` String,
    `cnt` UInt64
)
ENGINE = ReplicatedSummingMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{layer}-{shard}/sample_1d.logs', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY partition_code
ORDER BY (a, b, c, d, e, f, timestamp, h, i, j, k, l, m, n, o, p, q, r, user_agent, s, asn, as_org, isp, region_name, city_name, t, u, v)
TTL timestamp + toIntervalDay(94)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192 AS
SELECT
    a,
    b,
    c,
    d,
    e,
    f,
    toStartOfDay(timestamp) AS timestamp,
    substring(partition_code, 1, 10) AS partition_code,
    h,
    i,
    j,
    k,
    l,
    m,
    n,
    o,
    p,
    q,
    r,
    user_agent,
    s,
    asn,
    as_org,
    isp,
    region_name,
    city_name,
    t,
    u,
    v,
    sum(cnt) AS cnt
FROM sample.logs
GROUP BY
    a,
    n,
    c,
    d,
    e,
    f,
    timestamp,
    partition_code,
    h,
    i,
    j,
    k,
    l,
    m,
    n,
    o,
    p,
    q,
    r,
    user_agent,
    s,
    asn,
    as_org,
    isp,
    region_name,
    city_name,
    t,
    u,
    v
```

I ran the following query before adding a secondary index - 
```sql
     select timestamp, city_name, count() 
       from sample_1d.logs 
     where timestamp >= '2020-08-01 00:00:00' and timestamp < '2020-08-25 00:00:00' 
         and user_agent = '' 
group by timestamp, city_name 
order by timestamp
```

And produced the following stats -
```bash
1611707 rows in set. Elapsed: 7.318 sec. Processed 223.95 million rows, 2.00 GB (30.60 million rows/s., 273.84 MB/s.)
```

Number of rows with `user_agent = ""` within the time range is 107393773

Total number of rows within the time range is 293180409

About **63%** of the data within the range is what I'm filtering out with the query.

I ran the following to add an index on `user_agent` - 
```sql
ALTER TABLE sample_1d.`.inner.logs` ADD INDEX idx_user_agent user_agent TYPE set(0) GRANULARITY 1
OPTIMIZE TABLE sample_1d.`.inner.logs` FINAL
```

After that, I ran the same query and that produced the following stats -
```
1611707 rows in set. Elapsed: 6.084 sec. Processed 202.48 million rows, 1.80 GB (33.28 million rows/s., 295.56 MB/s.)
```

I'm only seeing 10% improvement with this index.

What are the variables that cause such little improvement?

Is it possible the optimization to finish creating the index didn't work?

I tried `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx_user_agent` and it didn't do anything.

That command is even stuck in `system.mutations` for days, with error -
```Code: 49, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Part a83fd13795ab07f06fd6504529d5d912_2239_9526_32_14698 intersects previous part a83fd13795ab07f06fd6504529d5d912_2228_2243_3 (state Committed). It is a bug. (version 20.5.4.40 (official build))```

I tried `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx_user_agent ON PARTITION {PARTITION_CODE}` for all the partitions the above query is supposed to touch, and all of those commands are stuck like above.

Please advise.
author: iameugenejo

comments.body:
ClickHouse does not have conventional secondary b-tree indexes.  Indexes are skip indexes, and in most cases if the indexed expression is not correlated with the ClickHouse primary/ORDER BY index, data cannot be skipped and the index provides no meaningful benefit.   You can find additional detail on the web, and ClickHouse Inc. will soon be publishing a brief article that explains in more depth.

The stuck mutation is not specific to secondary indexes, and was presumably caused by a bug.  Several bugs in this area have been fixed since version 20.5.

title: How to set: joined_subquery_requires_alias=0 in config.xml
body:
We recently upgraded our Clickhouse server and started getting: 

```
DB::Exception: No alias for subquery or table function in JOIN (set joined_subquery_requires_alias=0 to disable restriction).
```

I can change this setting in the command line client, but I want to change it in the server's config.xml. I've tried putting it under the `<yandex>` tag, and under the default user profile but neither work. Is there some special tagging that needs to be used around this specific setting? Thanks,

Matt
author: mvcalder-xbk

comments.body:
Not config.xml
This parameter must be set in users profile in users.xml

for example
```

cat /etc/clickhouse-server/conf.d/any_join_distinct_right_table_keys.xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<yandex>
    <profiles>
        <default>
            <any_join_distinct_right_table_keys>1</any_join_distinct_right_table_keys>
	    <joined_subquery_requires_alias>0</joined_subquery_requires_alias>
        </default>
    </profiles>
</yandex>
```
@den-crane thanks.

title: How can I using Json-related-format to import multi-level nested Json data?
body:
Each line of my json data looks like:
```
{
    "id": 1, 
    "source": "china",
    "sentences":[
          { content:"I loved apples",
            words: [ {"content": "I", "stem": "i", weight: 5}, 
                     {"content": "loved", "stem": "love", weight: 10}, 
                     {"content": "apples", "stem": "apple", weight: 1}]}, 
         { content:"My parents have many apples",
            words: [ {"content": "My", "stem": "my", weight: 6}, 
                     {"content": "parentes", "stem": "parent", weight: 5}, 
                     ......
                     {"content": "apples", "stem": "apple", weight: 1}]}
    ]
}
```

"sentences" is an array, and "words" is an array too. 


How can I load this json data to table with JsonEachRow？
Because I want to each domain in my json schema like id, source, sentences.content, sentences.words.content, sentences.words.stem, sentences.words.weight is stored separatly. So it will use the benefits of column storage.
author: hexiaoting

comments.body: For complex JSON structures, it is good to import them as strings and use JSON functions (JSONExtract-).

@hczhcz 
> For complex JSON structures, it is good to import them as strings and use JSON functions (JSONExtract-).

You mean that take the entire json object as a string?
 But in the way, it is stored as a single column and we cannot take advantage of column storage in clickhouse?

@hexiaoting 
Simply materialize what you extract from json.
Import them as JSONAsString, parse them with JSON functions (can be in MV)

```sql
with
    '{
        "id": 1, 
        "source": "china",
        "sentences": [
              { "content": "I loved apples",
                "words": [ {"content": "I", "stem": "i", "weight": 5}, 
                         {"content": "loved", "stem": "love", "weight": 10}, 
                         {"content": "apples", "stem": "apple", "weight": 1}]}, 
             { "content": "My parents have many apples",
                "words": [ {"content": "My", "stem": "my", "weight": 6}, 
                         {"content": "parentes", "stem": "parent", "weight": 5},
                         {"content": "apples", "stem": "apple", "weight": 1}]}
        ]
    }' as root,
    JSONExtractArrayRaw(root, 'sentences') as sentences,
    arrayMap(s -> JSONExtractArrayRaw(s, 'words'), sentences) as words
select
    arrayMap(s -> JSONExtractString(s, 'content'), sentences) as sentences_content,
    arrayMap(s -> arrayMap(w -> JSONExtractString(w, 'content'), s), words) as words_content
```

```sql
create table data (
    root String,
    sentences Array(String) alias JSONExtractArrayRaw(root, 'sentences'),
    sentences_content Array(String) materialized arrayMap(s -> JSONExtractString(s, 'content'), sentences),
    ...
)
engine = ...
```

FYI.
@hczhcz Thanks a lot . That's what I want. ^^
Bookmarking this for later review.

@hexiaoting How did you make it work?

Can you post your DDL's here?

@ramazanpolat 
```
create table json1(
	root String,
	id String
		materialized JSONExtractString(root, '_id'),
	source String
		materialized JSONExtractString(root, 'source') ,
	sentences Array(String)
		alias JSONExtractArrayRaw(root, 'sentences'),
	sentences_content Array(String)
		materialized arrayMap(s -> JSONExtractString(s, 'content'), sentences),
	words Array(Array(String))
		materialized arrayMap(s -> JSONExtractArrayRaw(s, 'words'), sentences),
	words_content Array(Array(String))
		materialized arrayMap(s -> (arrayMap(k->JSONExtractString(k, 'content'), s)), words),
	words_stem Array(Array(String))
		materialized arrayMap(s -> (arrayMap(k->JSONExtractString(k, 'stem'), s)), words)
	) engine = MergeTree order by publish_time;

cat $file.json | clickhouse-client -q "insert into json1(root) format JSONAsString "
```

title: ALTER MODIFY ORDER BY does not work
body:
Hi guys,

My clickhouse version is 20.3.10.75. When altering the table order by expression, I got the exception message as follows:

```
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Existing column version is used in the expression that was added to the sorting key. You can add expressions that use only the newly added columns.
```

The table is defined as follows:
```
CREATE TABLE default.users_online
(
    `when` DateTime,
    `uid` UInt64,
    `duration` UInt64,
    `version` Int32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(when)
ORDER BY (uid, when)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192
```

The ALTER MODIFY ORDER BY command is ```ALTER TABLE users_online MODIFY ORDER BY (uid, when, version)```.

The expected behavior is table's order by expression should be modified.
Thanks.
author: fastio

comments.body:
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Existing column version is used in the expression that was added to the sorting key. **You can add expressions that use only the newly added columns.**


CREATE TABLE default.users_online
(
    when DateTime,
    uid UInt64,
    duration UInt64
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(when)
ORDER BY (uid, when)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

Ok.


ALTER TABLE default.users_online  **ADD COLUMN version Int32,**  MODIFY ORDER BY (uid, when, version)

Ok.
@den-crane Thank you for reply. I got it. If the ORDER BY expression modified with existing column,  the existing data of table should be re-sorted which will pay a huge cost.

Yes. 

And BTW, `MODIFY ORDER BY` does not change primary index, it changes only rows sorting (for new parts).


SHOW CREATE TABLE default.users_online

CREATE TABLE default.users_online
(
    when DateTime,
    uid UInt64,
    duration UInt64,
    version Int32
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(when)
**PRIMARY KEY (uid, when)**
**ORDER BY (uid, when, version)**
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

author: mbtolou

comments.body:
Do you mean you have Materialized View? 

Materialized View is an insert trigger and it reflects (sees) only inserts into source tables. 
It does not reflect any other change like drop table/ truncate table / alter update/ alter delete/ ...
Can i refresh Materialized View manually?

> Can i refresh Materialized View manually?

No, but you can re-create MV somehow:

truncate table /  insert into select ...
or
drop / create materialized view ... populate ...

title: concurrency control and lock variables
body:
Currently, there are serveral kinds of lock variables/methods in StorageMergeTree/StorageReplicatedMergeTree codes.

1) action lock: merge, move, send
2) IStorage: lockStructructure**, lockAlter**, lockExclusiely
3) MergeTreeData:  lockParts()

and other mutex/locks.  The new developers, including me, are totally confused with all these locks. Can anyone give a simple explainatioin?  We will all appriciate your work.  

Thanks!
author: etah000

comments.body:
1. Is an object that does not lock anything but prevents some actions to start or continue during the lifetime of the object (merge, move, send, respectfully).
2. Table-level RWLock to control DDL operations like DROP, RENAME, ALTER. Recently we have mostly eliminated the usages of this lock.
3. Just a mutex to access/modify the set of data parts in MergeTree.

comments.body: Can I ask why do you need Nullable there? You expect that some messages will not have json object?

Hi :)
I'm using Debezium as kafka source connector in data lake project.
Here is whole process of data flow.
PostgreSQL or MariaDB (Source DB) -> kafka source connector(Debezium) -> kafka cluster -> kafka sink connector(Confluent) -> PostgreSQL or etc...(Target DB)

There is a tombstone message when i delete a row.
When row is deleted, Two messages are created and send to kafka.
One is deleted row information(json object) and the other one is null(called tombstone).
Thanks to tombstone message, the row is automatically deleted in target DB.

For target DB, We will use PostgreSQL to gather data and want to make same as source DB. (only for data gathering from multiple source DB)

For time series DB(another target DB), I am considering ClickHouse. CH's compression rate is great and it is amazing for aggregation. It will store all of event in multiple source DB. but, we want to use a kafka cluster. I think it is waste of resource to make two kafka cluster and it can make more load to source DB.
so, I need a feature which can handle null message(tombstone message). If it ignore null message, there will be great also.

> Can I ask why do you need Nullable there? You expect that some messages will not have json object?

@filimonov 
Also in IBM Change Data Capture (which is another data capture software just like Debezium), delete rows are sent with NULL messages. Because there is no update or inserted data, message becames NULL.

This beaviour is common among data capture softwares.

Clients can infer deleted row from the KEY part of the message.
Hi, do you have any updates on support for this issue?
When i used format RawBLOB, It worked. Thanks

title: Shard macros per cluster
body:
Let's say that I have 6 servers s1-s6 and I have created a cluster with two shards and triple replication.
hypothetical metrika.xml looks like this:

```
<yandex>
	<clickhouse_remote_servers>
		<triple_replication>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s1</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s2</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s3</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s4</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s5</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s6</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
		</triple_replication>
	</clickhouse_remote_servers>
</yandex>
```

I have to specify macros as well, so I will create a macros.xml file on each server with contents:

```
<yandex>
	<macros>
		<layer>01</layer>
		<shard>01</shard>
		<replica>01</replica>
	</macros>
</yandex>
```

and changing key `<shard>` from 01 on servers s1-s3 and 02 on servers s4-s6, and `<replica>` from 01-06.

When I want to create a replicated table I will use:

```
CREATE TABLE table_name on cluster triple_replication
(
..
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{layer}-{shard}/table_name', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY ...
```

As you can see in the statement above "{shard}" placeholder will be replaced with `<shard>` from macros.xml file, so it will be 01 on s1-s3 or 02 on s4-s6

Let's say that I would like to create another cluster with 3 shards and double replication and use both clusters at the same time.
Now metrika.xml would look like:

```
<yandex>
	<clickhouse_remote_servers>
		<triple_replication>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s1</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s2</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s3</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s4</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s5</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s6</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
		</triple_replication>

		<double_replication>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s1</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s2</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s3</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s4</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
			<shard>
				<replica>
					<host>s5</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s6</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
		</double_replication>
	</clickhouse_remote_servers>
</yandex>
```

Now I have to two different sharding schemas that I have to support in macros.xml file. 
In order to do so, I will have to introduce new macro `<shard_double>` for new cluster, that will be 01 on s1,s2, 02 on s3,s4 and 03 on s5,s6.


```
<yandex>
	<macros>
		<layer>01</layer>
		<shard>01</shard>
		<replica>01</replica>

		<shard_double>01</shard>
	</macros>
</yandex>
```

From now on, when I am creating replicating tables for the new (double_replication) cluster, I will have to use modified syntax, something like this (there is `{shard_double}` instead of `{shard}`):

```
CREATE TABLE table_name on cluster double_replication
(
..
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{layer}-{shard_double}/table_name', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY ...
```

Is there a better way of setting macros?
For example, It would be better if I have an opportunity to set macros per cluster?
In that case I would be able to use the same syntax for creation of replicated tables, and clickhouse will take care of applying proper values which would minimize the chance for an error.
Something like this (`<shard_num>01</shard_num>`):
```
<yandex>
	<clickhouse_remote_servers>
		<triple_replication>
			<shard>
				<shard_num>01</shard_num>
				<replica>
					<host>s1</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s2</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s3</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
			<shard>
				<shard_num>02</shard_num>
				<replica>
					<host>s4</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s5</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s6</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
		</triple_replication>

		<double_replication>
			<shard>
				<shard_num>01</shard_num>
				<replica>
					<host>s1</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s2</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			<shard>
				<shard_num>02</shard_num>
				<replica>
					<host>s3</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s4</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
			<shard>
				<shard_num>03</shard_num>
				<replica>
					<host>s5</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
				<replica>
					<host>s6</host>
					<port>9000</port>
				</replica>
			</shard>
		</double_replication>
	</clickhouse_remote_servers>
</yandex>
```

And than use (`{shard_num}`) for all tables:

```
CREATE TABLE table_name on cluster any_cluster
(
..
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{layer}-{shard_num}/table_name', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY ...
```

At the moment I have to be very careful whether about which shard macros I will choose.
Maybe there is an approach that I am not aware of at the moment.
Please do advise.
author: ghuname

comments.body:
You can create own macros in any combination and use them as you want.  layer / shard / replica -- just a recommendation. 
You don't need layer because it's for huge clusters like 100+ nodes.

so for example create two shard macros **shard_double** and **shard_triple**

```
s1 shard_double=1 shard_triple=1  replica=s1
s2 shard_double=1 shard_triple=1  replica=s2
s3 shard_double=1 shard_triple=2  replica=s3
s4 shard_double=2 shard_triple=2  replica=s4
s5 shard_double=2 shard_triple=3  replica=s5
s6 shard_double=2 shard_triple=3  replica=s6

remote_servers -- is not related to Replication. 
Cluster description `remote_servers` is used by Distributed Engine to know which node to query.
Replicated engines use only ZK path `/clickhouse/tables/{shard_triple}/table_name', '{replica}' ` 

Helper `on Cluster` is just a simple helper for `create table` and it executes create on nodes from `remote_servers`.
It does not change tables' metadata at hosts. You can create tables without using `on Cluster` at each node by own automation or manually -- no difference.

Same issue!

Not sure why this has been closed as I don't think it's solved.

Macros are a great mechanism for scaling out CH with shards and replicas.
And having cluster-specific macros might be more helpful to simplify things with similar and even the same naming patterns.

For example:

Instead of flat macros:

```yaml
<clickhouse>
    <macros>
        <cluster>cluster_1s_3r</cluster>
        <shard>01</shard>
        <replica>01</replica>
    </macros>
</clickhouse>
```

We can introduce hierarchical, cluster-specific macros, on top of the flat ones, like:

```yaml
<clickhouse>
    <!-- flat macros -->
    <macros>
        <shard>01</shard>
        <replica>01</replica>
    </macros>

    <!-- cluster-specific macros -->
    <macros>
        <cluster_1s_3r>
            <shard>01</shard>
            <replica>01</replica>
        </cluster_1s_3r>
    </macros>
    <macros>
        <cluster_2s_2r>
            <shard>01</shard>
            <replica>01</replica>
        </cluster_2s_2r>
    </macros>
</clickhouse>
```

So in a 4-node CH setup:
1. The `cluster_1s_3r` can have node{1..3} with:
    - node1: cluster_1s_3r/shard and cluster_1s_3r/replica with 01, 01
    - node2: cluster_1s_3r/shard and cluster_1s_3r/replica with 01, 02
    - node3: cluster_1s_3r/shard and cluster_1s_3r/replica with 01, 03
2. Meanwhile, the macros can well support  `cluster_2s_2r` too, with:
    - node1: cluster_2s_2r/shard and cluster_2s_2r/replica with 01, 01
    - node2: cluster_2s_2r/shard and cluster_2s_2r/replica with 01, 02
    - node3: cluster_2s_2r/shard and cluster_2s_2r/replica with 02, 01
    - node4: cluster_2s_2r/shard and cluster_2s_2r/replica with 02, 01

In this case, we can still enjoy the same naming convention while creating tables, with things like:

```SQL
# in cluster cluster_1s_3r
:) create table if not exists my_table on cluster cluster_1s_3r (
...) engine=ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{cluster}/{shard}/my_table','{replica}')

# in cluster cluster_2s_2r
:) create table if not exists my_table on cluster cluster_2s_2r (
...) engine=ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{cluster}/{shard}/my_table','{replica}')
```

Doesn't it make more sense?

```SQL

title: Disable query complexity checks for distributed queries on root (initial) node
body:
Hello! I use `max_rows_to_read` query limit to decide whether to read data from table or discard the query. The table is distributed, so it distribute queries to multiple shards. The behaviour I observe is that `max_rows_to_read` is checked on all the shard nodes, and then checked once again on root (the caller) node while merging response. And this second check could also result into exception of `max_rows_to_read`. I find this counterproductive since all the "hard" work of reading data from disk was already done by shard nodes only to be discarded then by root node.
My question is whether it is possible to enforce query complexity checks on leaf nodes only? Is this a kind of feature that project could be interested in?
author: hagen1778

comments.body:
This feature will be nice to have.

The current behaviour (limit based on cumulative counter across all nodes) is correct, it's natural and it works as expected.
We should not change the current behaviour but we can introduce another setting.

Variants:
- another group of settings similar to max_rows_to_read, max_bytes_to_read but applied only on leaf nodes (more flexible);
- a setting that will alter the meaning of max_rows_to_read, max_bytes_to_read.

What if we add a special prefix to all the settings `leaf_` which will be renamed by the root executor before sending them to leafs and it will ignore itself? With this approach we will be able to send limits for both roots and leafs.

> What if we add a special prefix to all the settings leaf_

Let's made it suffix: max_rows_to_read_leaf :)

> which will be renamed by the root executor before sending them to leafs and it will ignore itself

Let's don't rename anything. Just send settings as usual, apply along with `max_rows_to_read` but don't apply for the progress from Remote source.

title: How does concurrency control work?
body: Hi. I'd like to know how **ClickHouse** ensures *concurrency control* at table level. For example, if there's many applications writing in the same table at the same time, won't data get corrupted?
author: zergon321

comments.body:
MergeTree tables are represented by a set of immutable data parts. Data parts are never modified, only created and deleted. INSERTs create new data parts. SELECTs take snapshot of required data parts and hold the snapshot during the query.
Snapshots are based on reference counting and snapshot acquire operation is very cheap.
Both SELECTs and INSERTs and even ALTERs can be executed concurrently.

Data parts are merged in background - a new larger data part is created as a result of merge, then source data parts are deleted.
When data needs to be modified (ALTER query), we perform copy-on-write - create another part and remove source part.
Version number and block number are tracked for each part.

When we write new data part, we create temporary data and then perform atomic commit (the data is appeared in a table atomically). The user cannot see partially written data part and no data corruption possible.

TLDR, it's MVCC.

PS. Other (rudimentary) table engines like Log, TinyLog, StripeLog are using simple read-write lock.
Memory table engine is using snapshot like MergeTree.
Thank you very much for the answer!

comments.body:
Skip indexes work by skipping blocks of data that are guaranteed not to contain the requested values.  They improve efficiency by reducing the amount of data that needs to be read and evaluated to accurately respond to the query.   Your skip index uses a granularity of 1, meaning that each block the index is applied to contains one granule.  By default those granules will contain 8192 values.

An ngram skip index uses a bloom filter to determine if the requested ngram is present in each granule.  You are using an ngram size of 3, meaning your filter value of `171.195` will be broken into five ngrams -- `171`, `71.1`, `1.1`, `1.19`, and `195`.  If **any** of those ngrams is contain within **any** of the 8192 IP values in the granule, ClickHouse cannot skip that granule and must read all of the data, so the skip index gains nothing.   The chances of at least one of those ngrams being present in a granule of 8192 values is very high.

 You might get better result if you use a larger ngram size, but chances are still high that you would not skip a meaningful number of granules.  Other approaches to improve your query performance, since as including the IP address as part of your primary key, will almost certainly be more effective.

title: how to kill optimize FINAL  in backgroud
body:
i optimize a big table (replicedReplacingMergeTree)   , it makes io  100%   ,so i want to kill this optimize FINAL  
how can i do ?

<Debug> default.users (ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue): Not executing log entry MERGE_PARTS for part 20200630_0_307423_23 because source parts size (67.06 GiB) is greater than the current maximum (7.58 GiB).

thanks advance
author: zhlovy

comments.body: select *  FROM system.processes  ;   the result is null   ,  so can`t kill it

**For normal MergeTree:**
The only way is to call `SYSTEM STOP MERGES table_name`. **All merges** will be aborted, after that, you should start them again with `SYSTEM START MERGES table_name`. After that normal merges will start again, without FINAL merges from OPTIMIZE. 

**For ReplicatedMergeTree:**
It's not possible, because merges were written in the zookeeper replication log. You can just tune the amount of resources for background merges with settings:
```
background_pool_size
number_of_free_entries_in_pool_to_lower_max_size_of_merge
max_replicated_merges_in_queue
```

title: Any way to get a correct X-ClickHouse-Summary without send_progress_in_http_headers?
body:
I have an application sending a big query to clickhouse using http interface, and I need to get the summary of the query at the end. (I cannot use JSON format for it)

The `X-ClickHouse-Summary` header from the request has all the fields set to 0, which is incorrect -
```
 X-ClickHouse-Summary: {"read_rows":"0","read_bytes":"0","written_rows":"0","written_bytes":"0","total_rows_to_read":"0"}
```

Only way I get the correct summary is to pass `send_progress_in_http_headers=1`

The problem is, http client modules I have tried throw an error for having too many headers in the response.

python requests -
```requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: ('Connection aborted.', HTTPException('got more than 100 headers',))```
nodejs requests -
```{ [Error: Parse Error] bytesParsed: 153, code: 'HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW'}```

Is there any way to get the correct summary output without the progress headers?
author: iameugenejo

comments.body:
I just found a workaround, adding a huge http_headers_progress_interval_ms value to suppress the progress header for a long time seems to work for my case. `http_headers_progress_interval_ms=3600000`.

I would still like to know if there's a better or a correct way to do this.

The way you have found is Ok: you want to get only one X-ClickHouse-Summary header at the end of query execution (if no data was sent at this moment), so you set progress interval to very large value. Looks appropriate.

I don't know any better way to do it.
If data is sent too early, you can also provide `wait_end_of_query=1` parameter in URL that will buffer all the data.

The most typical reason for such error is when you screw up the setting on the sharded system. For example - due to the wrong values of 'macros' shard2 uses the zookeeper path of shard1.

Check the macros settings (system.mactos) & zookeeper paths. 

Also you can check the following:

Get the  list of parts from zookeeper:
 ```sql
select name from system.zookeeper where path = '{zookeeper path to table}/replicas/{replica_name}/parts' order by name;
```

And compare them with list of parts from filesystem:
```bash
ls /var/lib/clickhouse/data/database_name/table_name/

title: Why we rewrite joined table by alias with prefix '--'
body:
Hi, recently I have tried to debug some features and there is a problem confusing me: Why joined table was rewritten by alias with prefix '--'. For example,

create tables
```
create table t1(c1 int, c2 int) engine=MergeTree partition by c1 order by c2;
create table t2(c1 int, c2 int) engine=MergeTree partition by c1 order by c2;

CREATE TABLE default.t1_all (`c1` Int32, `c2` Int32) ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, '', t1);
CREATE TABLE default.t2_all (`c1` Int32, `c2` Int32) ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, '', t2);
```

run sql
```
SELECT c2
FROM
(
    SELECT c2
    FROM
    (
        SELECT
            c1 AS c,
            c2
        FROM t1_all
    ) AS t0
    ANY LEFT JOIN
    (
        SELECT
            c1,
            c2 AS c
        FROM t2_all
    ) AS t3 ON t0.c = t3.c
    ANY LEFT JOIN
    (
        SELECT
            c1 AS c,
            c2
        FROM t1_all
    ) AS t4 ON t0.c = t4.c
)
```

the sql will be rewritten by adding prefix '--'
```
SELECT c2
FROM
(
    SELECT c2
    FROM
    (
        SELECT *
        FROM
        (
            SELECT
                c1 AS c,
                c2
            FROM t1_all
        ) AS t0
        ANY LEFT JOIN
        (
            SELECT
                c1,
                c2 AS c
            FROM t2_all
        ) AS t3 ON `--t0.c` = `--t3.c`
    )
    ANY LEFT JOIN
    (
        SELECT
            c1 AS c,
            c2
        FROM t1_all
    ) AS t4 ON `--t0.c` = t4.c
)

```
author: fancyqlx

comments.body:
It was the most simple way to integrate multiple JOINs logic in ClickHouse query pipeline: to automatically rewrite query with multiple JOINs into query with subselects each containing one JOIN. Unfortunatelly there're name collisions in this case that are solved via special aliases. Such aliases are expected to be unique throug the query.

Storage Distributed has its own query rewriter. There could be some inconsistency that leads to bugs there.
I've just run you query on master branch and it looks a bit different from your result:
```
SELECT c2
FROM 
(
    SELECT c2
    FROM 
    (
        SELECT 
            c AS `--t0.c`,
            c2,
            c1,
            t3.c AS `--t3.c`
        FROM 
        (
            SELECT 
                c1 AS c,
                c2
            FROM t1_all
        ) AS t0
        ANY LEFT JOIN 
        (
            SELECT 
                c1,
                c2 AS c
            FROM t2_all
        ) AS t3 ON `--t0.c` = `--t3.c`
    ) AS `--.s`
    ANY LEFT JOIN 
    (
        SELECT c1 AS c
        FROM t1_all
    ) AS t4 ON `--t0.c` = c
)
```

There were bugfixes around JOINs and Distributed. Probably you need an update.
There's also experimental `multiple_joins_rewriter_version=2` setting in new versions that tries to use less special aliases.

body:
Hello
In my scenario for testing have a 2 shard hosts
If a host-A in shard‌s turn off 
And the query data are INSERT into host-b in shards
What happens after host-A in shards if turned on?
are records evenly balance equal in shards?
author: arashkhavari

comments.body: If you insert into Distributed table then your inserted data will wait for node-A in a Distributed table folder. Data will be unavailable for queries until it inserted into MergeTree at node-A.

> If you insert into Distributed table then your inserted data will wait for node-A in a Distributed table folder. Data will be unavailable for queries until it inserted into MergeTree at node-A.

My concern about local databases in shard distributed clickhouse. the tables count in local database on each hosts not equal

>the tables count in local database on each hosts not equal

You mean replicas? 

>tables count

You mean rows count?

I guess what @arashkhavari meant is that suppose that we have 3 shards and the insertion is being distributed between them then for any reason one of the shards went down. In this case the load will be distributed over 2 shards? and when the 3rd shard is back online does it go back to 3 shards? and the data which was not inserted in shard 3 will it be re-balanced between the 3 shards?
@den-crane What do you think about it?

when insert into Distributed engine, CH creates .bin files in Distributed tables folder for each shard and process them async.

We have 3 shards. Shard 2 is down. We insert into Distributed table at node1 (shard1).

```
node1 (shard1)
     /var/lib/clickhouse/data/db/distributed_table/
           shard1
                 insert1.bin
                 insert2.bin
           shard2
                 insert1.bin
                 insert2.bin
                 insert3.bin
                 ....
                 insert55555.bin
           shard3
                 insert1.bin
                 insert2.bin
```

While shard2 is down the Inserted data is stored at node1 in .bin files (insert1.bin .... insert55555.bin) and waits for shard2 is up back to reinsert into real MergeTree table at shard2 and make it visible for selects.

If you have two or more replica in shards then insert from Distributed .bin files will be reinserted to another (live) replica. If all replicas are down reinsertion waits for them.

So once the shard is back online clickhouse will re-blance the data, during that the query will be distributed between the live shards, right? 
Ho much resources does this re-insert requires?
Does this unbalanced shards affects the query performance?

No any re-balance. Because nothing to re-balance. 
Data is not inserted until node is alive. 

>Ho much resources does this re-insert requires?

There is no additional work. 

>Does this unbalanced shards affects the query performance?

No unbalanced shards. Nowhere to affect.

Probably you still don't understand how Distributed engine work. Read documentation.

title: Import data with clickhouse-native-jdbc,disk space problem
body:
I tried to import data using addBatch() with clickhouse-native-jdbc.After I import several batches,the disk space became full(I remained about 100GB free disk space), later,the disk space was slowly freed automatically.So can you tell me what's the reason and how to solve this problem?
Thank you!
author: wallace-clickhouse

comments.body:
You can change MergeTree a parameter `old-parts-lifetime` in config.xml

```
<yandex>
    <merge_tree>
        <old_parts_lifetime>10</old_parts_lifetime>
        <temporary_directories_lifetime>10</temporary_directories_lifetime>
    </merge_tree>
</yandex>

```



---

## old \ _parts \ _lifetime {# old-parts-lifetime}

The time (in seconds) for storing inactive pieces to protect against data loss during spontaneous reboot of the server or OS.

Possible values:

- A positive integer.

The default value is 480.

After merging several pieces into a new piece, ClickHouse marks the original pieces as inactive and removes them after the `old_parts_lifetime` seconds.
Inactive chunks are deleted if they are not used in current requests, i.e. if the link reference counter is `refcount`, it is zero.

Inactive chunks are not deleted immediately, because `fsync` is not called when writing a new chunk, i.e. for a while, a new piece is only in the server’s RAM (OS cache). T.O. during a spontaneous reboot of the server, a new (contingent) piece may be lost or damaged. In this case, ClickHouse during the startup process when checking the integrity of the pieces will detect a problem, return inactive pieces to the list of active ones and later re-hold them. In this case, the broken piece is renamed (the prefix broken \ _ is added) and moved to the detached folder. If the integrity check does not detect problems in the contiguous chunk, then the original inactive chunks are renamed (the prefix ignored \ _ is added) and moved to the detached folder.

The default value for Linux dirty \ _expire \ _centisecs is 30 seconds (the maximum time that recorded data is stored only in RAM), but with heavy loads on the disk system, data can be written much later. The time was found experimentally - 480 seconds, during which a new piece is guaranteed to be recorded to disk.

title: Polymorphic parts
body: How to use polymorphic parts instead of buffer engines, If we have frequent updates (like 100 in a sec) ?
author: shubham721

comments.body: You can set settings `min_rows_for_wide_part` and `min_bytes_for_wide_part` for any `MergeTree`-family table (by `ALTER MODIFY SETTING` query or globally in config). In that case, if size of inserted part in rows or in bytes less than corresponding threshold, part will will be written in compact format, otherwise in wide (current) format. `10M` is considered to be a good value for `min_bytes_for_wide_part`. Note that you will be unable to downgrade to version lower than 20.3 if you use new parts format.

(

title: Buffer tables with KafkaEngine? When?
body:
I have a KafkaStreams topology where I connect the output topics (~15 of them) to KafkaEngine tables (then using usual MV > ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree > Distributed table). 
Some of my topics have a lot of messages but some other ones may have a few by minute, and that can fluctuate. 
Would it make sense to set a Buffer table layer in between those MV > *MergeTree tables with lower number of messages in order to group them?

What is the reliability of Buffer tables here? Being them in RAM, and since consuming from KafkaEngine would advance the offset, would I be facing a higher message loss if server breaks (or e.g. container is shut down by Docker daemon)?

I had a couple of TooManyParts errors in the past, although I cannot be certain that they are caused by these topics with smaller inserts.
author: xmariachi

comments.body:
You don't need Buffer tables after Kafka. Kafka flushes the data in blocks of `kafka_max_block_size`, or by timeout controlled by `stream_flush_interval_ms` setting.

Adjust those settings if you need to form bigger blocks.
