title: How to set maximum number of merge threads in the background via parameters?
body:
Is there any parameters in the config.xml to set maximum number of background merge threads besides set "parts_to_throw_insert" and batchsize of inserts?

The 'Too many parts ...' exception happens sometime when inserting batch of  parts into multiple partitions.
author: BernieJiangDL

comments.body:
Background merges are executed by thread from so called 'background thread pool'.
Check the `background_pool_size` setting. 

And usually, if you face 'Too many parts ...'  it's NOT caused by background pool. Most common reason is bad schema (too granular partitioning, too aggressive compression, etc) creating too many merges, or making them slow.

> Background merges are executed by thread from so called 'background thread pool'.
> Check the `background_pool_size` setting.
> 
> And usually, if you face 'Too many parts ...' it's NOT caused by background pool. Most common reason is bad schema (too granular partitioning, too aggressive compression, etc) creating too many merges, or making them slow.

Got it. But I found another parameter "max_replicated_merges_in_queue" which is described as "How many tasks of merging and mutating parts are allowed simultaneously in ReplicatedMergeTree queue".

Whats the significant difference between max_replicated_merges_in_queue and background_pool_size? Those seem the same literally.


BTW, the thought to have the number of threads up is came up with our high performance servers which might have made it more stable and faster than before.
@filimonov Hi !  Is `background_pool`  used by all MergeTree() engine on single node?
Yes, background pool is shared for all tables.
The default value of the size of background pool is mostly optimal, there is little sense tweaking it.

> Most common reason is bad schema (too granular partitioning, too aggressive compression, etc) creating too many merges, or making them slow.

+1 Absolutely true.

> Whats the significant difference between max_replicated_merges_in_queue and background_pool_size?

The first is the limit on scheduled merges and the second is on currently running merges.

Yes, this is the expected behavior since existing paths are not converted, so it is better to change this setting only after there are no more pending async distributed sends

>How can i drop info bout this old data from clickhouse ?

So the rules for setting use_compact_format_in_distributed_parts_names are:
- `system flush distributed [ on cluster] dist_table`
- stop the server
- `rmdir` old directories (`rmdir` over `rm -r` to avoid removing directories with pending files, or just ignore and `rm -r`)
- set `use_compact_format_in_distributed_parts_names=1`
- start the server

You need some extra steps for two reasons basically:
- use_compact_format_in_distributed_parts_names=1 does not convert existing files (unlikely will be fixed)
- distributed engine does not remove already existing empty directories, and this is pretty easy to fix, and is on my todo list, and this will help in your case, but if and only if, those directories are empty.

comments.body:
>when use distributed_group_by_no_merge ，which part of SQL execute on MergeTree node and which part execute distributed node ？

In case of `distributed_group_by_no_merge=1` query executed only on the shards (I guess this is "MergeTree node" in your terminology) and the initiator node (distributed node in your terminology I guess) just piping the data, so it does not do anything.

While in general (i.e. `distributed_group_by_no_merge=0`) it will do final aggregation, sorting, limiting  and so on.

title: Ideal schema for log files?
body:
Assuming no structure and just generic log format I've come up with this:

````
create table if not exists logging.logs (
  id        Uint64                             /* process id, etc */
  host      LowCardinality(String)  /* hostname */
  tags      String                           /* tags */
  content   String,
  timestamp DateTime Codec(DoubleDelta, LZ4)

  index tags_index (lower(tags), tags) tokenbf_v1(3, 256, 2, 0) granularity 8
  index content_index (lower(content), content) tokenbf_v1(3, 256, 2, 0) granularity 8
) ....
````

Is there any issues with this schema, should it be extended or will I end up with headaches down the road?
author: nwmcsween

comments.body:
It's completely depends on your queries.
You can make `partition by toYYYYMMDD(timestamp) order by (host, timestamp)` or  `partition by to toYYYYMM(timestamp) order by toDate(timestamp)` 
Or you can you can create additional table -- `tags (tags_key)` and create `logging.logs ... partition by toYYYYMMDD(timestamp) order by tags_key`

It looks like you are importing some column from Parquet into Date type in ClickHouse.

title: arrayJoin() uses too much memory
body:
I have a table with an array type column ,and want to explode it.
Before that,I do a subquery to make dataset smaller.

Table DDL like that:
```
CREATE TABLE t (
  `id` Int32 ,
  `array_column` Array(String) ,
  `dt` Date ,
) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY dt ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192
```


The SQL is bellow:
```
select *,arrayJoin(array_column) from (
    SELECT * FROM t
    WHERE condition
)
```

And then receive an error:
```
ClickHouse exception, code: 241, host: {hostname}, port: {port]; Code: 241, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Memory limit (for query) exceeded: would use 20.19 GiB (attempt to allocate chunk of 4297064448 bytes), maximum: 18.63 GiB: 
Code: 241, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Memory limit (for query) exceeded: would use 32.11 GiB (attempt to allocate chunk of 17179869184 bytes), maximum: 18.63 GiB (version 19.17.4.11 (official build)) (version 19.17.4.11 (official build))
```

I know that means the data is too large.However, when I add limit to subquery ,even though limit size is larger much then subquery result size,the SQL still can work well. New SQL is like that:
```
select *,arrayJoin(array_column) from (
    SELECT * FROM t 
    WHERE condition limit 10000000000000000
)
```

env desc:
- Clickhouse version:  19.17.4.11
- Memory limit: 18G
- array_column avg length: 250
- subquery result size: 200,000

I don't find out how to explain Clickhouse sql, but I guess sql query optimizer executes arrayJoin first,and then do subquery's where clause to filter result. Target table is too large without where clause,so memory limit exceeded . But if add limit ,Clickhouse will execute subquery first,and then execute arrayJoin.Subquery result is much smaller,so I can execute it to get a result.

Maybe this is a bug?
author: user919lx

comments.body:
Try `set max_threads=1`

Probably it just not enough memory for `select *` in many threads with max_blocks_size=65536
and the limit indirectly reduces the number of blocks then number of threads.

It's not clear how much memory uses each query. I.e. first one could need 18.5G and second one needs 17.5G. Could ypu create a sample with smaller data set that would successed for both queries and show max memory usage and spent time for them?

Mutations are executed asynchronously, out of current query context.

```sql
create table x Engine=MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() as SELECT * FROM numbers(100);

-- that temp table exists only in current session
create temporary table y as select * from numbers(10);

-- mutations are executed out of the session context (for replicated tables - even on different replicas).
-- so that mutation will fail:
alter table x update number=number+1000 where number in (y);
```

> After one error all mutations fails with the same error even if they don't use it and worked before.

That is expected. Mutation should executed in sequence (because later change may depend on previus change). You can kill bad mutations to unlock the mutations queue.

title: Revert alter query/mutations?
body:
By mistake I have executed following alter query
`alter table some_table delete where datetime > time` with incorrect time specified, so more data than expected were removed.

Any chances I can somehow get it back? I saw that there are mutation_* .txt files in data directory + partitions are still in place...
author: mrAndersen

comments.body: If less than 8 minutes passed you can detach `ALTER TABLE DETACH PARTITION` all partitions from your table and than found source parts for your mutation in `/detached` directory. For example: `all_1_10_1_132` -- mutated part, source part can have name `all_1_10_1_100` (the fifth number is less than in mutated part) or without fifth number `all_1_10_1` if it was the first mutation on your table. You can remove all mutated parts which have source one.  After that, you should attach all partitions with `ALTER TABLE ATTACH PARTITION`. But if 8 minutes already passed all source parts should be already deleted from file system :(

title: Duplicated primary key in materialized view
body:
I have a table
```sql
CREATE TABLE user_video_view (
	user_id				UInt64,
	video_id			UInt64,
	visitor_session_id	UUID,
	visitor_id			UInt64,
	visitor_ip			String,
	visitor_user_agent	String,
	created_at			DateTime
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
PARTITION BY (toYYYYMM(created_at), user_id, video_id)
ORDER BY (created_at, user_id, video_id, visitor_session_id)
```
and materialized view based on it
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW grouped_user_video_view
ENGINE = SummingMergeTree()
PARTITION BY week
ORDER BY (user_id, week)
POPULATE
AS SELECT
	intDiv(toRelativeWeekNum(created_at) - toRelativeWeekNum(toDateTime('2020-03-23 00:00:00')), 2) AS week,
	user_id,
	count() AS view_count
FROM user_video_view
GROUP BY user_id, week
```

For some combination of `user_id` and `week` I have duplicated rows in response:
```
┌─week─┬─user_id─┬─view_count─┐

title: single row SELECT query with ClickHouse
body:
We have a case that we have to use a `SELECT` query to return a single row record in a hundred million rows in ClickHouse. we need to do it so often that it may be risky for `RAM` usage.

We also know that 
If the query omits the `DISTINCT`, `GROUP BY` and `ORDER BY` clauses and the `IN` and `JOIN` subqueries, the query will be completely stream processed, using O(1) amount of `RAM`.
Otherwise, the query might consume a lot of `RAM` if the appropriate restrictions are not specified: `max_memory_usage`, `max_rows_to_group_by`, `max_rows_to_sort`, `max_rows_in_distinct`, `max_bytes_in_distinct`, `max_rows_in_set`, `max_bytes_in_set`, `max_rows_in_join`, `max_bytes_in_join`, `max_bytes_before_external_sort`, `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`.


So is there any clause or syntax that we can use to make this frequent single row `SELECT` query smooth?
author: hatrena

comments.body:
CH streaming blocks not rows, and in multiple threads. 
So it could be that your query will process 96*65536 rows to retrieve 1 row.

Try `set max_threads=1, max_block_size=1024`

title: AvroConfluent Schema registry changes not considered ?
body:
Thanks for the AvroConfluent support in Clickhouse. 

We ingest data from Kafka with Format AvroConfluent. 

It is working well, until there is a change in the Confluent schema registry, e.g. updating the schema registry with a new schema version of an existing topic. 

Clickhouse always uses the old schema (or probably schema version 1) for the kafka topic. 
It should use the latest schema version from the schema registry. 
Or maybe the schemas are cached within clickhouse but not updated. 

How can we force Clickhouse to reread the schema registry and use the latest schema version of the kafka topic ? 

Tested CH version: 20.3.3.6
author: tgdkere2

comments.body:
Yes, the schemas are cached.
We can introduce special SYSTEM query to flush this cache.
@oandrew

Thanks for the answer. 
In the meantime, is there any way I can flush the cache manually ?
Currently there is no way to flush it manually.

@tgdkere2 
You can't change the schema of messages on a topic because each  message already contains a schema id which is used by ClickHouse to find the schema.
Schema id is globally unique and should not cause any issues when schema is cached. 

In other words: ClickHouse doesn't even know which topic it consumes from, all that matters is the schema id that's already embedded in the messages.

Could you elaborate more on what exactly your problem is?

p.s.
you can check all schema ids of messages on the topic by running:
```
# show all unique schema ids 
kafkacat   -b kafka-broker:9092  -C -t topic -o beginning -s 'B I' | cut -d ' ' -f2  | uniq
```

My two cents... 
A schema (subject + version) pushed into schema registry is (should be) inmutable. Kafka clients (for instance Kafka Streams) keep a similar cache without requiring a refresh.
A flush shouldn't be necessary.

Hello @oandrew @maqroll , 
You are right, the problem was the long retention time configured in the Kafka topic. 
Therefore it was still trying to get the old schema for the old records. 
Thank you !

title: about implementation of data replication
body:
hi 
  I have some questions about the data replication when try to use ReplicatedMergeTree these days

  why use the ReplicatedMergeTree to implement data replication, but not apply shielding to upper layers, like the data shard. We just do some configuration  and It will replicate data depends on the configuration
 
 Could you share how you thought about it? thanks
author: peaksnail

comments.body:
CH has specific design -- all nodes are independent without the singe point of failure so nodes has zero knowledge about other nodes. 
ReplicatedMT knows nothing about a sharding and knows how to publish information about its parts using ZK. 
All shards ReplicatedMT are different tables.

It's also worth to note that replication is implement on per-table basis.
For example, you can have one table replicated three times, other table replicated ten times and other table not replicated at all.

title: Materialized View with targeting past data
body:
I am having an issue with a Materialized View which targets the past data. I know that MV works like a trigger for inserts to a table. 

I need a Materialized View only for yesterday. I have the following MV:

```
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW default.chart_yesterday
ENGINE = ReplicatedSummingMergeTree(
     '/clickhouse/tables/{shard}/default/chart_yesterday',
     '{replica}')
     PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(date)
     ORDER BY (date, hour, cityHash64(organization_id)
)
SAMPLE BY cityHash64(organization_id)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192
POPULATE AS
SELECT
     SUM(rejected) AS clr,
     (count() - clr) AS cla,
     toDate(request_time) AS date,
     toHour(request_time) as hour,
     organization_id
FROM mytable_sharded
WHERE date = yesterday()
GROUP BY date, hour, organization_id
ORDER BY hour;
```

After creating the VM, I have data only for yesterday, everything fine. but after a day, the VM has no data

Does it mean that since there is no trigger for yesterday's data, so VM doesn't get triggered, so no data?
author: hatrena

comments.body:
>WHERE date = yesterday()

You MV will get a new data only if `insert into mytable_sharded` will insert `date = yesterday()`

You can create MV without this condition `WHERE date = yesterday()`
With daily partitioning ` PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(date)`
And remove data older than yesterday by `drop partition` or by `table TTL`
then your MV will have data only for yesterday and today.
I used `PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(date)` with `table TTL`, and it worked perfectly. thanks

title: Optimize query on huge table
body:
Hello,

Are there any pros or cons to run query `optimize table test final;` on the huge table at every 5 or 10 minutes of intervals on a table with CollapsingMergeTree engine?

Reason to run `optimize table test final;` manually is - CollapsingMergeTree is not deleting the rows with -1 sign. So we have to run optimize query manually to get the correct stats from the table.

Any help would be appreciated.


Thanks,
Nishit
author: nshah14285

comments.body:
The main problem of optimize final (table or partition does not matter) that it re-writes/re-merges a partition fully even if partition have only 1 part which is excessive in 99.9999% occasions!!!! It re-merges old data which was finally merged already!!!

It needed because sometimes one needs to collapse rows (duplicates) inserted with single insert into partition with forever single part. It is a very very rare necessity.

So I recommend to run optimize final against partitions which have more than one part. You can use something like this
```
select concat('optimize table ',database, '.','\`', table, '\` partition ',partition , ' final;')
from system.parts
where active and (engine like '%ReplacingMergeTree' or  engine like '%CollapsingMergeTree')
group by database,table,partition
having   count()>1
```

body:
i use bitmap join select on distribute table ,i want set distributed_product_mode to local, but not effect。how can i solve this problem ?

create table :

```
CREATE TABLE t_r_308 on cluster test_2shards_2replicas
 ( did Int32,  
label_name String,  
label_value String, 
dataCycle Date default today(), 
did_bitmap AggregateFunction(groupBitmap, UInt64)  default arrayReduce('groupBitmapState', [toUInt64(did)])) 
ENGINE = ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{shard}/t_r_308','{replica}') 
Partition by toYYYYMMDD(dataCycle)
Order by did 
SETTINGS index_granularity=8192; 

CREATE TABLE t_r_309_all on cluster test_2shards_2replicas 
as t_r_309 
ENGINE  = Distributed( test_2shards_2replicas, 'default', t_r_309, did);

select bitmapAndCardinality(user1,user2) from 
(select 1 as join_id,groupBitmapMergeState(did_bitmap) as user1 from t_r_309_all ) as a
inner join (select 1 as join_id,groupBitmapMergeState(did_bitmap) as user2 from t_r_308_all) as b 
on a.join_id=b.join_id;

```
author: wushiming540

comments.body:
When you write a query in the form of two joined subqueries:

```
SELECT * FROM (SELECT ... FROM distributed) JOIN (SELECT ... FROM distributed)
```

data is transferred to initiator node and joined there. So, the JOIN is processed not in distributed fashion and the setting `distributed_product_mode` does not have any effect.

In contrast, when the left table is not a subquery, the JOIN is performed in distributed fashion:

```
SELECT * FROM distributed JOIN (SELECT ... FROM distributed)
```

And you can set `distributed_product_mode` to local if you know that the data is co-located.

```sql

set table1.col4 = table2.col4
from table2 
where table1.col1 = table2.col1 and table1.col2 = table2.col2 and table2.col3='2020-01-02';

I made a query like below, But, I got error and don`t know how to make 2 join condition.

```sql

CREATE TABLE test1
(
    `col1` Int8, 
    `col2` String,

    `col4` UInt16
)
ENGINE = Log

ENGINE = Join(ANY, LEFT, col1, col2)

Ok.

FROM test1
WHERE col3 = '2020-01-02'

-- update
:) ALTER TABLE test1 UPDATE col4 = joinGet('test_join', 'col4', col1, col2);

Syntax error: failed at position 73 (end of query):

ALTER TABLE test1 UPDATE col4 = joinGet('test_join', 'col4', col1, col2);

author: chu1070y

comments.body:
You've made something very strange.

1. ALTER UPDATE is special operation. Do not use it in general ETL logic.
2. Engine JOIN is a kind of optimisation of JOINs with joinGet extension. Do not use it for JOINs if general JOIN doesn't work. Do not use it in dictionary-like scenario if dictGet doesn't work.
3. It's not clear in docs but engine JOIN do not support complex keys yet.

You're trying to combine several special extensions in totally unexpected dangerous way. Nobody helps you if something goes wrong.
Create intermediate table and update via it.

```

(
    `col1` Int8, 
    `col2` String, 
    `col3` Date,

ALTER TABLE test1 UPDATE col4 = dictGet('default.test_join_dict', 'col4', tuple(col1, col2))
where dictHas('default.test_join_dict', tuple(col1, col2))

```

title: Multithread Insert into Distributed table
body:
Hi. I'm trying to insert big dataset(3-4 tables, each have few billion rows) into Distributed table(2 shard, 1 replica each, non replicated MergeTree tables), and I have sharding_key like `cityHash64(string_column)` and `string_column` is available on all tables.  Dataset are exported from Amazon Redshift and there are ~1000 gzip file for each table. Everything is ok, when I'm inserting with single thread. But when I'm inserting with multiple threads to speedup inserts, nobody use clickhouse, only my inserts (using tmux, command looks like `zcat test_table_[0,1,2,3...].gz | clickhouse-client --query="INSERT INTO test_table FORMAT TSV`), my disk get's full because of Distributed `*.bin` files didn't flushed to remote machines with multiple threads. I tried to set `distributed_directory_monitor_batch_inserts=1` for default profile, but clickhouse-server flushes 2-3 `*.bin`files at one time. I tried also following with `distributed_directory_monitor_batch_inserts=1` settings

1. `SYSTEM STOP DISTRIBUTED SENDS`
2. Insert few files. it generates ~30-40 `*.bin` files
3. `SYSTEM STOP DISTRIBUTED SENDS` 

ClickHouse still flushes maximum 2-3 `*.bin` files at 1 time instead of all.

Is there a way to enforce to flush all bin files or some settings that can help me?

Tested on 
```
ClickHouse client version 20.1.3.7 (official build).
Connecting to localhost:9000 as user default.
Connected to ClickHouse server version 20.1.3 revision 54431.
```

Thanks
author: artbeglaryan

comments.body:
@artbeglaryan Try the following in  `dbms/src/Core/Settings.h`: `min_insert_block_size_rows`, `min_insert_block_size_bytes`.
`StorageDistributedDirectoryMonitor::Batch::isEnoughSize()` reads those settings.

@artbeglaryan Yes, sending data to every shard is single-treaded when you use asynchronous INSERTS (that send data in background) and asynchronous mode is by default.

You can enable synchronous INSERTS with setting `insert_distributed_sync` set to 1.
With synchronous INSERTS, when you execute multiple queries concurrently, data will be also sent concurrenlty. Even more, it will eliminate unnecessarity writes and reads of data on filesystem.

The drawback of synchronous INSERTS is that they are unreliable for large clusters.

title: multiple update queries at the same time
body:
If I send more than one update query at the same time and the queries update same data, How does the ClickHouse handle data??

Does the ClickHouse handle query sequentially? If so, afterward update query is waiting for forward update query? 

If the queries update data at the same time, How does the ClickHouse keep data integrity?
author: chu1070y

comments.body:
Sequentially. Though several mutations can be combined into one. But still data will be updated as updates applied sequentially.

>How does the ClickHouse keep data integrity

Data will be consistent after all updates ended (eventually). But during mutations your selects will see partially updated data because mutations are not atomic.

Path | Previous location | Description
----- | ------ | -------

/src/contrib | moved from **/contrib** | external sources, may depend on other parts from **/contrib**
/src/dbms | moved from **/dbms/src** | separatable part for internal usage inside Yandex, may depend on **/src/base** and **/src/contrib**
/tests | moved from /dbms/tests | data used for automated testing in CI

│                    9 │
└──────────────────────┘

10 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.007 sec. 
```

What is expected behaviour for this query and `max_result_rows = 5`? In other words: which version contains bug the old or the new one?

Query `SELECT number FROM system.numbers LIMIT 10` works fine in both versions.
author: xzkostyan

comments.body: It is still actual -  20.5.2.7, current master (20.6.1).

It works as documented. Slightly more than `max_result_rows` can be returned if more rows are in the same block.

Don't mix up "query complexity settings" with the LIMIT clause.
If you want to limit the number of rows, you should use LIMIT clause.

When you use query complexity settings, the server will check these settings whenever appropriate and act accordingly without any additional efforts - it will stop query execution after first block when the limit is exceeded but it will not do additional work to cut this block precisely.
New versions work correctly (as documented), the old version (19.17) not.

author: ramazanpolat

comments.body:
partial_merge_join is in progress and not fully optimized yet. But it's expected that MergeJoin would be slower than HashJoin in general. The main case it should be faster is sorted inputs, where we could avoid sort phase in merge join. But it needs special support and not realized yet.

The main reason for partial_merge_join is "join on disk", not relpace for HashJoin in in-memory scenario. We need fully suport and optimize "join on disk" case first.

title: Number of columns in order by caluse
body:
Description: We have a table with 6 Billion rows 
                    create table contact_in
                    (
                     domain String,
                     topic String,
                     category String,
                     job_level String.
                     job_function String,
                     created_date Date,
                     ----
                     ----
) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY category
ORDER BY
  (topic, domain,job_level,job_function) SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

**The most used columns in the queries we have put in order by.**

How many columns can be used in the order by clause? 
Is it mandatory to use Date column in order by ? because we have only one date stored in the above "created_date" column.
Indexing will be done on all the columns in order by?
Query executing time is more with the above settings.
Should we change index granularity to something else?

and how to use the Skip index on this table?

Please help us to solve this.
author: Crazylearner30

comments.body:
>The most used columns in the queries we have put in order by.

It's not quite right.
All table -- all columns will be sorted in order of `ORDER BY`
You have to define `ORDER BY` to achieve maximum compression by puting similar values in columns as close as possible. The same time  `ORDER BY` -- creates an PRIMARY KEY index. This index can be used for filtering `where` conditions by index's **PREFIX PREFIX PREFIX!!!! PREFIX!!!!**.
If most of your queries contain `where topic` topic have to be on the first position in INDEX (order by).

Long indexes are useless and make performance worse because PRIMARY INDEX stored in memory -- bigger index -- less memory for queries. 

Also INDEX filtering works mostly by prefix -- no sense to put some column XXX into index on 7th position, it will be used only if leading 6 columns has equality conditions in `where`.

For example in your case index will be used for a column job_function only if `where  topic='some' and domain ='somexxx'  and job_level = ''somezzzz' and job_function >/=/< ....`

>Is it mandatory to use Date column in order by

No. If you don't use date filtering in where conditions you don't need to put Date in orderby/index.

					sum(data_table.`NewConnectionsNb`) as `NewConnectionsNb`,

					sum(data_table.`ServerDataPackets`) as `ServerDataPackets`,
					max(data_table.`ServerNetworkTimeMax`) as `ServerNetworkTimeMax`,
					min(data_table.`ServerNetworkTimeMin`) as `ServerNetworkTimeMin`,
					sum(data_table.`ServerNetworkTimeSum`) as `ServerNetworkTimeSum`,

					min(data_table.`TotalResponseTimeMin`) as `TotalResponseTimeMin`,
					sum(data_table.`TotalResponseTimeSum`) as `TotalResponseTimeSum`,
					max(data_table.`TotalTransactionTimeMax`) as `TotalTransactionTimeMax`,
					min(data_table.`TotalTransactionTimeMin`) as `TotalTransactionTimeMin`,
					sum(data_table.`TotalTransactionTimeSum`) as `TotalTransactionTimeSum`,
					sum(data_table.`TransactionsNb`) as `TransactionsNb`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasDreInput`) as `WaasDreInput`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasDreOutput`) as `WaasDreOutput`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasInputBytes`) as `WaasInputBytes`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasLzInput`) as `WaasLzInput`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasLzOutput`) as `WaasLzOutput`,
					sum(data_table.`WaasOutputBytes`) as `WaasOutputBytes`,
					data_table.`Agent` as `Agent`,
					data_table.`Application` as `Application`,
					data_table.`Source` as `Source`,
					data_table.`Protocol` as `Protocol`,
					data_table.`ClientOffice` as `ClientOffice`,
					data_table.`ServerOffice` as `ServerOffice`,
					data_table.`ClientInterface` as `ClientInterface`,
					data_table.`ServerInterface` as `ServerInterface`,
					data_table.`ClientIp` as `ClientIp`,
					data_table.`ServerIp` as `ServerIp`,
					data_table.`ClientCos` as `ClientCos`,
					data_table.`ServerCos` as `ServerCos`,
					data_table.`Port` as `Port`,
					data_table.`DomainName` as `DomainName`,
					data_table.`Flags` as `Flags`
			from
					/* @DATA_TABLE@ */
					avc.topconversationdetails as data_table
					/* @INNER_JOIN_PART@ */
					
			where
					/* @WHERE_PART@ */
					data_table.`Timestamp` >= toStartOfMinute(toDateTime('2020-01-01 15:54:00','Europe/Paris'), 'Europe/Paris')
					and data_table.`Timestamp` < toStartOfMinute(toDateTime('2020-01-08 15:54:00','Europe/Paris'), 'Europe/Paris')
					and ((toNullable(data_table.`Customer`)= (select a from (select `id` as a from sdm.customers where sdm.customers.`vmId` = 150005) as b)))
					and ((toNullable(data_table.`Service`)= (select a from (select `id` as a from sdm.services where sdm.services.`vmId` = 150006) as b)))
			group by 
					/* @GROUPBY_IN_PART@ */
					Timestamp,
					data_table.`Agent`,
					data_table.`Protocol`,
					`ServerIp`,
					data_table.`ServerCos`,
					data_table.`ClientOffice`,
					data_table.`ClientCos`,
					`Flags`,
					data_table.`ServerInterface`,
					data_table.`ClientInterface`,
					data_table.`Application`,
					data_table.`Source`,
					data_table.`ServerOffice`,
					`Port`,
					`DomainName`,
					`ClientIp`
		) as aggr_in
			/* @MIDDLE_JOIN_PART@ */
			
		group by
				/* @GROUPBY_OUT_PART@ */
				aggr_in.`Agent`,
				aggr_in.`Protocol`,
				c10,
				aggr_in.`ServerCos`,
				aggr_in.`ClientOffice`,
				aggr_in.`ClientCos`,
				c15,
				aggr_in.`ServerInterface`,
				aggr_in.`ClientInterface`,
				aggr_in.`Application`,
				aggr_in.`Source`,
				aggr_in.`ServerOffice`,
				c13,
				c14,
				c9
		order by
				/* @ORDERBY_PART@ */
				( empty(c10) OR c10 = '(UNDEFINED)' OR c10 IS NULL) ASC,
				c15 IS NULL ASC,
				c13 IS NULL ASC,
				c14 IS NULL ASC,
				( empty(c9) OR c9 = '(UNDEFINED)' OR c9 IS NULL) ASC,
				c16 desc
		) as aggr_out
	) as t
	/* @OUTER_JOIN_PART@ */
	
group by if(ranking_row<100, ranking_row, 101)
order by final_ranking asc
```

Where avc.topconversationdetails is a merge tree table, and the other tables are dictionnaries tables.
It is mostly a top N with others query, with 2 level of aggregation.

title: About deleting new values every day affects performance
body:
A multi-million data table needs to delete a part of the data and add a new part every day. Will this affect the performance of ck query?

 ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BA_MONTH
author: samz406

comments.body:
It's unclear how are you going to `delete a part`. 
`alter table ... drop partition`  does not affect performance.
no partition, first use ALTER TABLE table DELETE WHERE BA_MONTH='xxx', and insert data,Will this affect the performance  query?

`ALTER TABLE table DELETE` is very heavy operation in comparison with `drop partition` .
`ALTER TABLE table DELETE` causes a huge I/O and CPU usage. After it finishes it does not affect performance.

Consider to use `alter table ... drop partition` and table with monthly / daily partitioning. 
` drop partition` much more faster and more reliable operation.
ok. thank you

title: About MATERIALIZED VIEW on AggregatingMergeTree
body:
My Table in ClickHouse is like this:
-------------------------
## local table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dataDate201912_local (
  statdate Date,
  stattime DateTime,
  ip UInt32,
  domain String,
  type UInt8,
  flow UInt64,
  request UInt64,
)
ENGINE = ReplicatedSummingMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/dataDate201912/{shard}', '{replica}')
PARTITION BY statdate 
ORDER BY (statdate,stattime,ip,domain,type)
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;


## distribute table
CREATE TABLE dataDate201912 AS dataDate201912_local
ENGINE = Distributed(kstat_shard, currentDatabase(), dataDate201912_local, intHash32(stattime));

##local table: summary by date-domain
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS dataMonth201912_local
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree() 
ORDER BY (statdate,ip,idcid,domain,type)
POPULATE AS SELECT
  statdate,
  ip,
  domain,
  type,
  maxState(flow) as flow,
  sumState(request) as request
FROM kstat.dataDate201912_local
group by statdate,ip,idcid,domain,type;

## distribute table 
CREATE TABLE dataMonth201912 AS dataMonth201912_local
ENGINE = Distributed(kstat_shard, currentDatabase(), dataDate201912_local, rand());
-------------------------

I inserted data to distribute table dataDate201912, and I want to get daily summary data juest like this two ways, I expected the results of the following two SQLs are the same:
--------------
select maxMerge(flow) as peek_flow, sumMerge(request) as sum_request
from dataMonth201912
where statdate='2019-12-30'
and ip=12345
and type=0
and domain='aaa.example.net';

select max(flow) as peek_flow ,sum(request) as sum_request
from kstat.dataDate201912
where statdate='2019-12-30'
and ip=12345
and type=0
and domain='aaa.example.net';
--------------

Can you tell me, is there anything wrong in the MATERIALIZED VIEW ?

title: Exposing Clickhouse to the Internet- Direct User Read Only Access?
body:
I'm considering exposing ClickHouse directly to the internet (via a proxy) so I can provide my users direct access to ClickHouse for visualizations (and to save work on building an API layer). If I do this, I would dynamically generate a users.xml file for each tenant in my system, restricting them to only view records attached to their account ID.

Is this idea insane to be considering? The accounts would be limited to read only, and would be restricted further by quotas and table filters.
author: volfco

comments.body:
Running untrusted SQL code is generally not safe.

Two possible ideas:
* Give each user an isolated ClickHouse instance
* Reconstruct a restricted query from the user's input
Have a look at chproxy, you won't need to expose real ch users and you can set rate limits too.
@pachico It looks like chproxy can be used in conjunction with clickhouse user filtering. It doesn't look like chproxy can restrict or filter data?

No, not in chproxy but, depending on what you mean by restricting or filtering data, you can do it in CH.
So yes, it seems like a combination of the two might be what you need.
Cool. I'll poke around and see how it works. If I could expose Clickhouse semi-directly to the user then that drastically reduces complexity of my system.

This is exactly what we do.
We use chproxy for:
- roundrobin between all nodes (it performs healthcheck to point only to healthy ones, which was our first and original reason to adopt it)
- avoid exposing internal credentials 
- apply rate limit

title: MATERIALIZED VIEW from Kafka doesn't insert Nested data
body:
I have a materialized view loading data from a Kafka table into another table. All works except for the nested data isn't copied across - other fields are correctly populated.

e.g.

```
CREATE TABLE k1 (
  bet_id UInt64,
  parts Nested
	(
		category_name String
	)
) ENGINE = Kafka('localhost:9092', 'fct_bet', 'fctBetGroup', 'JSONEachRow');

CREATE TABLE t1 (
  dt Date,
  bet_id UInt64,
  parts Nested
	(
		category_name String
	)
) ENGINE = MergeTree(dt, bet_id, 8192);

 CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW v1 TO t1
 AS 
 SELECT	toDate(now()) as dt, bet_id, parts.category_name FROM k1;
```

If I insert ... select (i.e. "insert into t1 select toDate(now()) as dt, bet_id, parts.category_name FROM k1;") then it works correctly, so it's something related to the materialized view. I've also verified that it works correctly with a non-Kafka table as the source.

Sample JSON from Kafka -  {"parts":{"category_name":["Test1","Test2"]},"bet_id":1}

I added <input_format_import_nested_json>1</input_format_import_nested_json> to the default via users.xml (otherwise the nested structure didn't populate in the k1 table).

How many? 10 ? 100? Of course any number impact on performance.
We roll data daily, so there will be 300+ mv for the table.
Why do you need to create a MV per day instead of having a single one partitioned by day?
The original table is too big and uncontrollable increased, we have to query data daily and combine them in application layer.

> The original table is too big and uncontrollable increased, we have to query data daily and combine them in application layer.

You are mistaken. @nvartolomei is right. 
You need one MV partitioned by day. 
CH SQL partition pruning works almost exactly the same as a query to a separated table.

There is no difference
`select ... from T where date='2019-12-12'`
VS
`select ... from T_20191212 `

In case of daily partitioning and `where date='2019-12-12'`  it will be separated partition with `'2019-12-12'` and separated set of files. And CH will read only this set of files/rows.

Thanks for the information.

BTW, is there any way to change the partitioning key? or I have to create a new table, and copy all data into this new table?

Appreciate for your help.
@jsding you will have to create a new table and copy data.

title: Support Settings for Distributed table
body:
**Use case**
First create a replicated table
```sql
CREATE TABLE test_local on cluster cluster01 (
  id UInt32,
  dt String
) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{shard}/test_local', '{replica}') 
ORDER BY tuple()
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192
```
Then create MV on it
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW test_view_local on cluster cluster01
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree()
    partition by dt
    ORDER BY tuple()
    SETTINGS index_granularity = 1
AS SELECT
    dt,
    groupBitmapState(id) as uv
FROM test_local
GROUP BY dt;
```
Finnaly create a Distributed on MV
```sql
CREATE TABLE test_view on cluster cluster01 as test_view_local
ENGINE = Distributed(cluster01, default, test_view_local, rand());
```
Then I met such a situation: the query result is slightly different when different test_view_local  replica is used.
```sql
select groupBitmapMerge(uv) from test_view
```
The test_view_local replicas got different data(I guess it is due to different replica has a different pace to ingest data from the base test_local, also the test_local replicas' data is not fully synchronized), causing the above sql not stable(the second time result can be smaller when I run the query twice)

Then I want to set `load_balancing=first_or_random` and `prefer_localhost_replica=0` for this `test_view`, but not in server level config file

**Describe the solution you'd like**
can use SETTING for Distributed table
```sql
CREATE TABLE test_view on cluster cluster01 as test_view_local
ENGINE = Distributed(cluster01, default, test_view_local, rand())
SETTINGS load_balancing = 'first_or_random', prefer_localhost_replica=0;
```
author: kaijianding

comments.body:
test_view_local should replicated as well (ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree)

`MV test_view_local .... FROM test_local` sees only local inserts into test_local.
So each replica has own partial in test_view_local.
If wanted exactly this then you need to describe one more cluster `cluster02` and place each CH node as shards (without replicas) and create 

CREATE TABLE test_view on cluster cluster01 as test_view_local
ENGINE = Distributed(**cluster02**, default, test_view_local, rand())


HINT: CH node can be a member of any number of clusters.

though test_view_local is not replicated, the based table test_local is ReplicatedMergeTree.
the test_view_local only sees the local inserts into test_local, but can't see the inserts from another test_local replica?
MV never reads a source table. It just catches inserted rows from inserts. So it does not get anything from inserts at another node. You should create MV with ReplicatedAggregatingMergeTree engine.

title: What it depends on that ClickHouse will trigger DELETE/UPDATE syntaxs
body:
When I used the 

> ALTER TABLE [db.]table DELETE WHERE filter_expr

I found out that it took so many hours to delete all data.
I know the delete/update process is running in background,so I would like to know the mechanism that what it depends on that ClickHouse will trigger the operation?
author: byx313

comments.body:
CH starts to execute`Alter delete`  in background  right after you called it (if it is not blocked by other running delete or a running merge). It takes so long because it rewrites all data.

Try `truncate table` or `drop partition` if you need to remove all rows.

> CH starts to execute`Alter delete` in background right after you called it (if it is not blocked by other running delete or a running merge). It takes so long because it rewrites all data.
> 
> Try `truncate table` or `drop partition` if you need to remove all rows.

Do you mean that （1）CH get all data （2） check data whether meet the delete expression （3）delete the old data file & rewrite the left data to the disk?

Yes. CH evaluates which parts should be mutated (using where conditions) and do a special merge for those parts (CH writes each parts' columns to a new file excluding removed rows -> replaces old parts with new).
thx you so much!

What is the size will be moved ? 20 % of the first disk ?

It pushes data with move_factor between volumes, inside one volume it uses round-robin.

It will just move the largest part to next volume once the free space on first volume will go below

Use case is to avoid any network load on the node where data is being inserted in order to avoid a bottleneck because of majority bandwidth used in replication.

CH does not take care. All replicas fetch parts from all other available replicas. If only one replica has a part all replicas will fetch from that replica.

body:
Hi, how can I query something like this (like in MySQL) with 2 MergeTree tables
`SELECT
  TABLE_A.col1_from_a,
  (SELECT col1_from_b FROM TABLE_B WHERE col2_from_b = TABLE_A.col2_from_a LIMIT 1) AS some_alias
FROM TABLE_A
WHERE <some filter from TABLE_A>`

It queries a field from TABLE_B using a field from TABLE_A.
I tried using JOIN like this
`SELECT
    TABLE_A.col1_from_a,
    TABLE_B.col1_from_b
FROM TABLE_A
ANY LEFT JOIN TABLE_B ON TABLE_A.col2_from_a = TABLE_B.col2_from_b
WHERE <some filter from TABLE_A>`
but it showed processing all the rows from TABLE_B (tens of millions of rows).
`col2_from_a` is the sorting key of `TABLE_A`, `col2_from_b` is the sorting key of `TABLE_B`.
Any suggestion would be appreciated.
author: qza1800

comments.body:
>Hi, how can I query something like this

CH does not support correlated subqueries.

>I tried using JOIN like this
>but it showed processing all the rows from TABLE_B (tens of millions of rows).

It's actually the best way (HashJoin) to solve this on BigData.

>col2_from_a is the sorting key of TABLE_A, col2_from_b

HashJoin does not use sorting keys

Try
```
SELECT TABLE_A.col1_from_a, TABLE_B.col1_from_b 
   FROM TABLE_A 
   ANY LEFT JOIN (select col2_from_b TABLE_B where col2_from_b in 
      (select col2_from_a from TABLE_A where <some filter from TABLE_A>))
   ON TABLE_A.col2_from_a = TABLE_B.col2_from_b 
WHERE <some filter from TABLE_A>
```

Or you can use external dictionary with source=TABLE_B. 
Though such dictionary (tens of millions of rows) could use 5-100GB RAM.

body:
I have CSV file with comma as separator sign, but without quotes for column entries.

Issue I have is with double quote sign existing in string value for column,
when I try to escape it with another double quote ( "" ) for command line clickhouse-client
I got error and insert fails.

When I escape one double quote with backslash ( \" ) then it works but got backslash and quote in entry in column.

What is the proper way to escape double quote in CSV structure like I have ?

Clickhouse server version is 19.11.12

here is example for structures and data:
```
# testdata.csv
749a2c8c-3682-4745-aefe-c21b3164bade,name,""MY COMPANY"" COM
749a2c8c-3682-4745-aefe-c21b3164bade,hash,67FF87AF9E9E4BA9E4C03FAC4A23F21C

# table structure
CREATE TABLE temp.events (`event_id` String, `property_name` String, `property_value` String) ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY tuple() ORDER BY event_id SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192

#shell script to insert data
cat testdata.csv | clickhouse-client --host=localhost --query='INSERT INTO temp.events (event_id, property_name, property_value) FORMAT CSV'

Code: 117. DB::Exception: Expected end of line: (at row 1)

Row 1:
Column 0,   name: event_id,       type: String, parsed text: "749a2c8c-3682-4745-aefe-c21b3164bade"
Column 1,   name: property_name,  type: String, parsed text: "name"
Column 2,   name: property_value, type: String, parsed text: "<DOUBLE QUOTE><DOUBLE QUOTE>"
ERROR: There is no line feed. "M" found instead.
 It's like your file has more columns than expected.
And if your file have right number of columns, maybe it have unquoted string value with comma.
```
author: goranc

comments.body:
--format_csv_allow_double_quotes=0
```
cat testdata.csv | clickhouse-client --format_csv_allow_double_quotes=0 --host=localhost --query='INSERT INTO events (event_id, property_name, property_value) FORMAT CSV'
```

Ah, double quote escaping works only inside quoted string.
```
749a2c8c-3682-4745-aefe-c21b3164bade,name,"""Y COMPANY"" COM"
749a2c8c-3682-4745-aefe-c21b3164bade,hash,67FF87AF9E9E4BA9E4C03FAC4A23F21C
```

-----------------------
So yeah CH supports only double quote escaping by double quote.

This string `[,"MY COMPANY" COM]` needs escaping because it starts with "
This string `[,хаха "MY COMPANY" COM]` does not need escaping.
This string `[,\"MY COMPANY\" COM]` does not need escaping and \ -- is not escaping, but usual symbol and it works because the string starts with \ not with ".

title: Avoid `Too many partitions for single INSERT block` in Kafka Engine
body:
Hi! I'm using Kafka engine and getting this error: ```DB::Exception: Too many partitions for single INSERT block (more than 100). The limit is controlled by 'max_partitions_per_insert_block' setting. ...```
I understand why this error can occur in small inserts by hand (using clickhouse-client or http interface), but in case with Kafka engine documentation says: 
```
To improve performance, received messages are grouped into blocks the size of max_insert_block_size. If the block wasn't formed within stream_flush_interval_ms milliseconds, the data will be flushed to the table regardless of the completeness of the block.
```
So if I understand correctly Kafka engine should merge blocks before insert to increase performance and avoid this error. Also I can suspect the root of that error in my case is that in every kafka message is one `row` of data, so I suppose that blocks are merged but this does not reduce parts count. Is there a way to overcome this? Is it a bug? I'm hoping to avoid writing middleware pre-batching service, since Kafka engine does almost all needed things

I'm using version 19.15.5.18. Thanks in advance!
author: LizardWizzard

comments.body:
>I understand why this error can occur in small inserts by hand

No. It's not about this.
It's about partitioning key in your MV. One insert into kafka (into MV) tries to create more than 100 partitions.

For example 
```

create table A( D Date) Engine=MergeTree partition by D order by D;
insert into A select number from numbers(365);
Code: 252. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Too many partitions for single INSERT block (more than 100).
```

The error is because this insert tries to create 365 partitions

```
create table A( D Date) Engine=MergeTree partition by toYYYYMM(D) order by D;
insert into A select number from numbers(365);
OK.
```
No error. Because this insert creates only 12 partitions.
Thank you so much for explanation! Got it :) Changed partition expression and error is gone

comments.body:
It's possible to make T64 codec for fixed sized Arrays that use own min-max pairs for each array position. It's also possible to make the codec for general Arrays with one min-max for all the Array's positions. Both cases have some restrictions.

I think we should not add such a support fo Arrays now but we may implement generalized packed ```Integer``` and ```UInteger``` in future. Then it would be ```Array(UInteger)``` in colum declaration and something like ```toUInt64(a[1])``` in use.

title: Updates in replicated tables
body: When we update a table, the update's status gets updated in system.mutations table, you can easily check it with column is_done. comments.body: @blinkov I'd be interested

You can set `mutations_sync` setting to 1 for the query. When this setting enabled, the query will return success to the client only after mutation will be executed on every replica.

But if query will not return success (e.g. one replica is unavailable), mutation will be executed nevertheless. In that case, you have to check `system.mutations` on every replica manually.

title: Query speed  depends on JOIN order (number of records in each table & table join order)
body:
**Steps To Reproduce**

```
CREATE TABLE test1 (
    id UInt64,
    value UInt64
)
ENGINE=MergeTree()
ORDER BY id;

INSERT INTO test1 SELECT number, number * 2
FROM numbers(100000000)

CREATE TABLE test2 (
    id UInt64,
    value UInt64
)
ENGINE=MergeTree()
ORDER BY id

INSERT INTO test2 SELECT number, number * 2
FROM numbers(1000)
```

1. Fast Query (test1 join test2)
```

SELECT * FROM test1
INNER JOIN test2 ON test1.id = test2.id
```

Result

```
1000 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.245 sec. Processed 100.00 million rows, 1.60 GB (407.65 million rows/s., 6.52 GB/s.) )
```

clickhouse-server.log (Use all 24 threads)
```
executeQuery: Query pipeline:
Expression
 CreatingSets
  Lazy
  Union
   Expression × 24
    Expression
     MergeTreeThread
```
2. Slow Query (test2 join test1)

```
SELECT * FROM test2
INNER JOIN test1 ON test1.id = test2.id
```

Result

```
1000 rows in set. Elapsed: 9.202 sec. Processed 100.00 million rows, 1.60 GB (10.87 million rows/s., 173.88 MB/s.)
```

clickhouse-server.log (Use only 1 thread)

```
Query pipeline:
Expression
 CreatingSets
  Lazy
  Expression
   Expression
    MergeTreeThread
```
author: nhudinh2103

comments.body: It's expected. There's no join order optimizer. You should create joins with small right sides. There's Hash-Join under the hood so your right table would be entirely read and placed into hash-map, then stream from left table would be filtered by this hash-map. It's cheaper to have small map + big stream then big map + small stream.

title: If I add index, How does the Clickhouse make granules?
body:
When table is created, the table is sorted by primary key. so, primary key index can easily find data.

for example,
```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS table1 on cluster1
(
    CounterID UInt32,
    Date Date,
    Category String
) ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY (CounterID)
```

The data will be sorted by CounterID. so, when the CH access granules(.idx), It can easily find the data(.bin)

but, If I add index like `ALTER TABLE table1 ADD INDEX idx1 (Category) TYPE set(0) GRANULARITY 1;`, I do not know How to make index. Because the data already is sorted by `CounterID`.

Does the Clickhouse re-sort the data to make granule`s info? or uses the data already sorted by primary key?
author: chu1070y

comments.body:
related: #329

  In ClickHouse, the data is only stored in order of the `order by clause` and primary key info is generated based on the `primary key clause`(default same to `order by clause`).  
  When executing query, the `primary key index` always works on the granules level (filtering or retaining a granule).

  For the `skipping index`, it also works on the granules level(secondary filtering after the primary key has been filtered). It stores information that helps filter granule 
  without changing the order of the data store.  For example, the `minmax index` always records the minimum and maximum value for each granule.

  > but, If I add index like ALTER TABLE table1 ADD INDEX idx1 (Category) TYPE set(0) GRANULARITY 1;, I do not know How to make index. Because the data already is sorted by CounterID.

  Index information already exists for the newly written data. 
  For previously written data, you need to wait for the `merge task`(which is asynchronous) updates index information, 
  but you can also use the following statement to update(synchronously) the index information for all data.

  ```sql
  OPTIMIZE TABLE xxx FINAL;
  ```

  >Does the Clickhouse re-sort the data to make granule`s info? or uses the data already sorted by primary key?

  As far as I know, modifying the `order by clause` is not currently supported. I remember there was an issue about it. but I couldn't find it. @alexey-milovidov

Thanks for information. but, if you find the answer of below question,
> Does the Clickhouse re-sort the data to make granule`s info? or uses the data already sorted by primary key?

Please comment on this issue.

> Does the Clickhouse re-sort the data to make granule`s info? or uses the data already sorted by primary key?

ClickHouse only sorts data by order key (primary key). And the granules of secondary indices cover existing ranges of primary key.

> As far as I know, modifying the order by clause is not currently supported. I remember there was an issue about it.

There was support for extending ORDER BY key and adding a new column simultaneously. As far as I remember, it was implemented only for non-replicated MergeTree tables by feature request of one internal user and was removed.

title: How the index file works
body:
I want to know How index work except for primary key.

When the tables is created, data is sorted by primary key. and primary.idx file is created which has information for granules.

so, when I send a select query with using primary key, the clickhouse find granules in the primary.idx and use (column).mrk2 to find data in the (column).bin. Do I understand right?

Then......

When I add an index using an alter table query, skp_idx_(index_name).idx and skp_idx_(index_name).mrk2 files are created. what roles of these files??

And I have to use 'optimize final' for using index right away. 

However, These index files(.idx and .mrks) is created a little later. but I can use a new index by the way.

How these works??
author: chu1070y

comments.body:
Imagine you've created a table 
`create table T(A Int, B Int) order by A`
`insert into T values(1,1) `   --- first part no skip index
`alter table add index min_max(B);`
`insert into T values(1,2)`   --- second part with skip index file with B_min_max=(2,2)

And you run a query `select * from T where B>10000000`
Ch unable to use primary index to filter rows because there is no conditions on column A.
Then CH will scan 2 parts. The first part does not have skip index file so CH will read column B and checks the condition `B>10000000`. In the contrary in the second part CH will use B_min_max=(2,2) index file and will skip a reading of column B because obviously this part does not have rows with  `B>10000000`.
Later a merge process will merge these 2 parts to a new one with skip index B_min_max=(1,2).

title: Default Part size for mutations
body:
when we do mutation, the default maximum for part size is 150GB. Is it possible to change this size, if yes kindly throw some light on same. how do we do it, kindly share the procedural details.
How will affect the mutation if we increase or decrease the size of it?
author: aditi6622

comments.body: You are looking for `<merge_tree>` setting called `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool`
@filimonov Are you sure that this setting should be used to limit mutations?

Maximum part size `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool` doesn't related to mutations. Actually mutations can only decrease the size of the part, so they don't perform any size checks for result part size (only checks for available space on disk). 

Changing maximum parts size is not recommended, but you can do it with query:
```
ALTER TABLE table_name MODIFY SETTING max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool = 200 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
```
If you have any questions, just reopen.

But two uniqStates can be summed by +

So RunningDifference can be emulated like this
```
create table z(d Date, z String, u String)
Engine=MergeTree partition by tuple() order by tuple();

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mvz
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree order by (z,d) settings index_granularity = 8 
as select d, z,uniqState(u) as us from z group by z,d;

insert into z select today()+1, 'g1' , toString(number) from numbers(1000);
insert into z select today()+2, 'g1' , toString(number+100) from numbers(1000);
insert into z select today()+3, 'g1' , toString(number+200) from numbers(1000);
insert into z select today()+4, 'g1' , toString(number+200) from numbers(1000);
insert into z select today()+5, 'g1' , toString(number+300) from numbers(1000);

select m1, m2 from (
SELECT
        groupArray(d) AS gd,
        arrayMap(x -> toString(gd[x+1])||' - '||toString(gd[x+2]), range(toUInt64(length(gd)-1))) m1,
        groupArray(us) AS gus,
        arrayMap(x -> (arrayReduce('uniqMerge', [gus[x+1]+gus[x+2]]) - arrayReduce('uniqMerge', [gus[x+2]])) , range(toUInt64(length(gd)-1))) m2
          from (select d, us FROM mvz  order by d ) )
    Array Join m1, m2

┌─m1──────────────────────┬──m2─┐

│ 2019-10-26 - 2019-10-27 │   0 │
│ 2019-10-27 - 2019-10-28 │ 100 │
└─────────────────────────┴─────┘
```

> You can use 11 shards with MergeTree tables (without replication) but CH needs at least one small standalone Zookeeper for ON CLUSTER.

hi，I want to make it clear:
if I use 11 shards each with 1 replica, to use `on cluster` I have to deploy a standalone zookeeper and set `internal_replication = true`, right?   ` internal_replication = true` is necessary？or I only need a standalone zookeeper and set `internal_replication = false` also be fine?

Shards and replicas are not connected.  If you have sharded tables there is no replication between shards--the data are disjoint.  You don't need zookeeper in this case unless you plan to add replicas later. 

Note that if you don't use replication and a host drops out for some reason, any data on that host will become unavailable.  With replicas you would still have at least one copy of the data.  Also, if you plan to add replicas later you may want to start with ReplicatedMergeTree engine on replicated tables.  This avoids a migration at a future date and gets you used to managing zookeeper from the start.

Deduplication works for blocks.

title: Data written because of max_bytes_before_external_*
body:
Hello.

Is it possible to see how much data was written to disk during query because of max_bytes_before_external_* ?
author: Tri0L

comments.body:
Hi. This information you can find in `system.query_log` table (you need to enable query_log in config and set `log_queries=1`). Then if you know query id, run query like
```
SELECT 
    ProfileEvents.Names, 
    ProfileEvents.Values
FROM system.query_log
ARRAY JOIN ProfileEvents
WHERE query_id = '<query_id>' and ProfileEvents.Names = '<event_name>'
```

For external aggregation `<event_name>` is `ExternalAggregationCompressedBytes` or `ExternalAggregationUncompressedBytes`.
For external sorting there is no special event, but you can use `WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteBytes` to get the number of written bytes in total for query.

Thanks.
author: Crazylearner30

comments.body:
> Is it true that sharding key can't be anything other than a constant value or a column of table?

No, you can use arbitrary expressions as a sharding key. Your example is perfectly valid.

> When data distibutes with a shading key, can we predict which shard the data is insert?

Yes. Data will be placed by the remainder of division of the sharding key expression to the sum of shard weights.

> If each shard has the same weight, how should we set the sharding key for equal distribution of each shard?

Your example is totally right. Please check the values of `murmurHash3_64(domain)`, check the remainders of division on your ten records. Then check if the data is sent to remote servers successfully.

title: How to evaluate how many cores and ram volume in a cluster？
body:
HI，gus.

I am going to install a clickhouse  cluster in my company. 
and I am puzzled how many machines I need to buy.
We have 2TB logs data one day. 
how many cores and ram volume do I need in total ?

Can you guys do me a favor ?

Thanks..
author: Tasselmi

comments.body:
>2TB logs data one day

Raw or compressed? In average CH able to compress 5-10 times.
How many days are you going to store?

>how many cores and ram volume do I need in total ?

It's impossible to evaluate because the answer depends of your requirements to retention / latency / accuracy (CH has sampling and able to provide approximate results). 

You can extrapolate. Take a couple servers with 64GB with 2 CPU, load one week and run all queries. Or load 5-10% of logs for 2 months.
CH highly depends on IO performance. SSD is better than HDD. But HDD is fine too. In my experience CH performs much better with software raid10 (linux kernel -- mdraid) ( 12 - 24 HDD per server) than HW raid.

Thanks for your reply.

I want to store 90 days of logs  raw data( 2TB per day ) .
I am planing to buy 20 machines ( each with 32cores and 192GB RAM and 4TB ssd ) .
The cluster will be 10 shards and each 2 replicas.
We expect to run  query or function such as `left join` (at most join 2 times in one query on 2 keys ),  `sequenceMatch`,  `retention` with latency less than 5 minutes.

Can you give me some advice ?
Is my machine quantity enough ?

> > 2TB logs data one day
> 
> Raw or compressed? In average CH able to compress 5-10 times.
> How many days are you going to store?
> 
> > how many cores and ram volume do I need in total ?
> 
> It's impossible to evaluate because the answer depends of your requirements to retention / latency / accuracy (CH has sampling and able to provide approximate results).
> 
> You can extrapolate. Take a couple servers with 64GB with 2 CPU, load one week and run all queries. Or load 5-10% of logs for 2 months.
> CH highly depends on IO performance. SSD is better than HDD. But HDD is fine too. In my experience CH performs much better with software raid10 (linux kernel -- mdraid) ( 12 - 24 HDD per server) than HW raid.

Thanks you again.
Looking forward to your advice. I am new in installing CH cluster.

> I want to store 90 days of logs raw data( 2TB per day ) .
> I am planing to buy 20 machines ( each with 32cores and 192GB RAM and 4TB ssd ) .

90*2/10 = 18TB data per node (`4TB ssd`), you need to evaluate compression rate.

>We expect to run query or function such as left join (at most join 2 times in one query on 2 keys ), 
>sequenceMatch, retention with latency less than 5 minutes.

You should test `left join`. CH uses HashJoin only and puts a right table into memory. 
If the right table is about 100mil rows (wide: 100 bytes) it will eat 500GB RAM and will be much longer than 5min even for 1row table on the left.

>Can you give me some advice ?

Test on 5% -- 90days data, check compression rate, memory requirements.

Hard to say. It could be 5 server is enough by CPU / RAM , but not enough on SSD space.

**Env:**
`ClickHouse server version 19.13.1.11 (official build)` inside docker with default config.

**Problem:**
we are testing ClickHouse for our workload which includes many queries like this at the same time:
```
SELECT
       idxid,
       count(*) total,
       toInt8(avg(age)) age,
       countIf(liveness, equals(liveness, 2)) y1,

title: Replace Column Values

author: Sundarcj

comments.body:
That is happening when you do `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE colunmname=... WHERE ....`

There is also `ALTER TABLE tablename CLEAR COLUMN colunmname IN PARTITION ... `

Actually it combines the value but will still work ineffecient.

Instead you can create a simple key-value dictionary or table with engine=Join and just do `alter table update col1=dictGet..where 1` (or with joinGet in case of table with engine=Join).

which one will be efficient dictGet or Join.
i don't have knowledge about dict in CH. Is dictGet can be used in join Engine?

For dictionaries - use one of dictGet... functions. 

For engine=Join - use joinGet. 

Performance is almost the same. Engine=Join is bit more handy (no XML config, easy to fill / maintain). Dictionaries consume more memory.

title: Parts retrieval in ReplicatedMergeTree
body: It takes a long time. Looks like each part retrieved sequentially. Am I right? Is it any tweak, like configuration to make it faster, like downloading parts in parallel?
author: kreuzerkrieg

comments.body:
Parts fetching done in parallel with a maximum of "background_pool_size" connections.
Usually it saturates network 100% (at least for 10GBit) and cannot be made any faster.
It may have negative consequences though - sometimes you have to shape replication traffic manually.

Thanks!
If your network is overloaded and you need to save some bandwidth for queries.

title: Using runningDifference() and quantilesExactWeighted() correctly on time series data
body:
We need to calculate exact value quantiles on large non-uniformly sampled time series data. The schema is (String sensor_path, DateTime timestamp, Float64 value). 

It would be perfect if we could use something like „SELECT quantilesExactWeighted(...)(value, delta)...“,
where „delta“ is the result of „runningDifference(timestamp)“. 
Unfortunately, this does not work, because for each row, delta is the time difference between the previous and the current row instead of the time difference between the current and the next row, as needed for the weights parameter of quantilesExactWeighted(). 

Self-joining the time series to shift delta forward one row will probably not work when the time series does not fit into memory, right?

Is there maybe another, more efficient solution?

I’d be glad to try to submit a patch with a new variant of runningDifference() if there is no other solution. 

Many thanks for your excellent work on ClickHouse!
author: oflasch

comments.body:
You can use arrays to get a series per key, sort by timestamp then calculate pretty much anything on the series. Performance on array vectors is certainly not the same as column vectors however if you consider the fact you have to sort to get things in order you end up with performance that roughly matches the new optimize order by primary key functionality. GROUP BY can also spill to disk which can help the memory issue.

Example assuming positive values only - generate 1000 individual series and some metrics

```
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS timeseries;

CREATE TABLE timeseries
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toStartOfDay(ts)
ORDER BY (key, ts) AS
SELECT 
    concat('device-', toString(number % 1000)) AS key, 
    toDateTime('2019-01-01 00:00:00') + toIntervalSecond(rand(number) % 1000) AS ts, 
    any(rand(number + 100000)) AS value
FROM numbers(1000000)
GROUP BY key, ts;
```

Calculate the delta and convert back to column

```
select
    key,
    quantilesExactWeighted(0.5)(_value, _delta) AS q
from (
    with
        arrayMap(i -> (_s[i].1, _s[i].2, abs(_s[i+1].2 - _s[i].2)), arrayEnumerate(arraySort(x -> x.1, groupArray((ts, value))) AS _s)) AS _d
    select
        key,
        (arrayJoin(_d) AS series).1 AS _ts,
        series.2 AS _value,
        series.3 AS _delta
    from 
        timeseries
    group by key
) group by key
```

Calculate the delta and use -Array combiner on the array without conversion.

```
select
    key,
    quantilesExactWeightedArray(0.5)(_d.2, _d.3) AS q
from (
    select
        key,
        arrayMap(i -> (_s[i].1, _s[i].2, abs(_s[i+1].2 - _s[i].2)), arrayEnumerate(arraySort(x -> x.1, groupArray((ts, value))) AS _s)) AS _d
    from timeseries
    group by key
) group by key
```

Many thanks for the detailed solution, looks very good. I did not know about the effect of GROUP BY on memory usage. Neat optimization!

Your observation that the series must be sorted anyway brought another possible solution to mind that I wanted to document for others perhaps facing the same task:
We can simply sort the series by timestamp in descending order before calculating runningDifference(), then apply abs() to the resulting negative deltas, which should give the desired “forward_delta”:

```
SELECT 
    *, 
    abs(runningDifference(q)) AS forward_delta
FROM 
(
    SELECT 
        number AS n, 
        n * n AS q
    FROM numbers(15)
    ORDER BY n DESC
)
ORDER BY n ASC

┌──n─┬───q─┬─forward_delta─┐
│  0 │   0 │             1 │
│  1 │   1 │             3 │
│  2 │   4 │             5 │
│  3 │   9 │             7 │
│  4 │  16 │             9 │
│  5 │  25 │            11 │
│  6 │  36 │            13 │
│  7 │  49 │            15 │
│  8 │  64 │            17 │
│  9 │  81 │            19 │
│ 10 │ 100 │            21 │
│ 11 │ 121 │            23 │
│ 12 │ 144 │            25 │
│ 13 │ 169 │            27 │
│ 14 │ 196 │             0 │
└────┴─────┴───────────────┘
```

 ...... ...... ...... ``` Works on 19.9.4.34 and older.
author: mikeeremin

comments.body:
Dictionaries will load successfully regardless to this warning.

This warning present, because some config elements get substituted into `/etc/clickhouse-server/dnl_dictionary.xml`. You can check it in `/etc/clickhouse-server/preprocessed/...` directory.

Extraneous config elements are substituted from `conf.d` directory.
You can override configuration with files from `conf.d` or _config_name_.d directory, for example `config.d`, `users.d` or `dnl_dictionary.d`. Overrides from `conf.d` directory will be substituted into every configuration file while overrides from _config_name_.d directories will be substituted only to the corresponding configuration file.

```
clickhouse-test-node1 :) system reload dictionaries;

SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARIES

Ok.

0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.005 sec.

clickhouse-test-node1 :) select * from system.dictionaries\G

SELECT *
FROM system.dictionaries

Row 1:
──────
name:               programreleasefiles
status:             NOT_LOADED
origin:             /etc/clickhouse-server/dnl_dictionary.xml
type:
key:
attribute.names:    []
attribute.types:    []
bytes_allocated:    0
query_count:        0
hit_rate:           0
element_count:      0
load_factor:        0
source:
loading_start_time: 0000-00-00 00:00:00
loading_duration:   0
last_exception:


```

`SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARIES` reloads only those dictionaries which have been loaded before.
Clickhouse has not loaded `programreleasefiles` before so the command `SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARIES` doesn't reload it.

If you want `programreleasefiles` to be loaded use

```
SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARY programreleasefiles
```

or just start using this dictionary
```
SELECT dictGetUInt64('programreleasefiles', 'a', 1)
```

comments.body:
this is contradicts SQL.

you can use 
select formatReadableSize(size)
...
order by size

It is not a bug. `formatReadableSize` return strings, so they are ordered as strings.

Use the approach shown in @den-crane 's answer,

@abraithwaite 

Consider more simple example:

```
SELECT toString(number) AS x FROM numbers(100) ORDER BY x
```

It's obvious that this query sort data alphabetically (by String value). And it is the only way it should work.

`formatReadableSize` is similar. This function returns `String` data type, not some `String but sort numerically` magic.
Thanks!  I was aware that it was being converted to a string but didn't realize I could order by the original field.  Works great!

title: How to pretty print a generated RowBinary file?
body:
Hello all,

Given a valid ClickHouse RowBinary file, how I can prettyprint the row data within the file?

Thank you
author: Jack012a

comments.body:
Sure! It's very easy to do with `clickhouse-local`:

```
clickhouse-local --structure "x UInt8, y String, ..." --query "SELECT * FROM table" --input-format RowBinary --output-format TSV < file
```

You have to know correct data structure (`--structure` parameter).

You can use `clickhouse-local` tool for converting between various formats and for data processing without a server.
If you want **pretty**print, use `--output-format Pretty`.

It works for me.

Thank you!

title: How much RAM is required for ZooKeeper?
body:
Is there a guide for memory usage of ZooKeeper for ClickHouse?

My system uses the ReplicatedMergeTree, creates 3000 parts for one day and stores it about one year.

I set 8GB memory for ZooKeeper. I don't know whether is it enough or not.

I hope your help.
author: achimbab

comments.body:
ZK is in-memory database. 

So lets check ZK database size

echo mntr | nc localhost 2181|grep zk_approximate_data_size
zk_approximate_data_size	68723698

~68MB

The same size as snapshot size
du -sh /var/lib/zookeeper/version-2/snapshot.4350f30c19
77M	/var/lib/zookeeper/version-2/snapshot.4350f30c19

So in my case ZK needs 77MB+~200MB JVM needs.
I would say 500MB is enough.


Check a MergeTree setting **use_minimalistic_part_header_in_zookeeper**. If enabled, Replicated tables will store compact part metadata in a single part znode. This can dramatically reduce ZooKeeper snapshot size (especially if the tables have a lot of columns). Note that after enabling this setting you will not be able to downgrade to a version that doesn't support it.

@den-crane 
The use_minimalistic_checksums_in_zookeeper is enabled.
```
:) select * from system.merge_tree_settings

... 
use_minimalistic_checksums_in_zookeeper                    │ 1            │       0 │
...
```
My ZooKeeper's zk_approximate_data_size is ```1219607498.```

I will monitor how this value grows.

It's very helpful, thank you very much.

> DB::Exception: ALTER of key column column3 must be metadata-only (version 19.6.2.11 (official build))

column3 is included in primary key. You can modify it only if data is not modified during alter. But changing type to LowCardinality causes data modification and this action is not supported.

simple and fast linear disk read + simple & 'brute force' vector processing

to

author: nshah14285

```
SELECT
  itemName,
  SUM(itemAmount) AS totalAmount
FROM
(
  SELECT
    transactionID,
    arrayJoin(items) AS flattened
  FROM test
  WHERE transactionID IN ('abcxyz', 'abcxyzz')
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  itemName;

```
