title: Clickhouse and mysterious activity
body:
Hello,

I've inserted some data into clickhouse but recently stopped the stream (and greped for clickhouse client, the only one running was the one with which I'm checking the database).

However when I run top I see:

1687 clickho+  20   0 10.099g 748716  16548 S 240.2  2.3 365:20.17 clickhouse-serv

Clickhouse-server is EATING 1-4 of my cpus. Is this normal activity ? My queries are waaay slower during this process and I can't find its cause.

Edit:

I should mention that iostats is showing the db writes to disk and I can see it modifying the size of a table file (both increases and decreases by ~5%) the table is a MergeTree and this has been going on for about 40 minutes.
author: George3d6

comments.body: Almost certainly this is the merge process. MergeTree table consists of a number of parts that are sorted by the primary key. Each INSERT statement creates at least one new part. Merge process periodically selects several parts and merges them into one bigger part that is also sorted by primary key. Yes, this is normal activity.
You could do `SELECT * FROM system.merges` to show currently running background merges (also known as "compactions").

Isn't there any way to stop these merging when executing queries ? They appear to be quite greedy with both processor time and I/O. Can't I set a "limit" for how many resources merges can take ? Or even better, set the db up in such a way that merges stop when I run SELECT queries.

Ok, since there was no update, I'm going to phrase the question otherwise:

If I were to modify the code in so I could be able to set a flag using the client in order to stop all background operations whilst running a query, do you think that would break anything important ? Or just slow down the merges ?

You could adjust size of thread pool for background operations.
It could be set in `users.xml` in `background_pool_size` in `/profiles/default/`.
Default value is 16. Lowering the size of this pool allows you to limit maximum CPU and disk usage.
But don't set it too low.

Also you could adjust some fine settings for MergeTree.
They are located in `config.xml` in `<merge_tree>` section.
List of available options along with documentation and default values is located in `MergeTreeSettings.h` file. These settings are intended only for fine tuning.

Hy, I am a coworker of George3d6,
Thank you very much for the response, and this AMAZING piece of software!
I would like to add some more info:
We left click house "digest" those 1B row / 165 colum, about 170GB of data for one night, but activity is still on.

We are running some preliminary test, so hardware spec was "modest" a AMD FX6300 (6 cores) with 32GB ram, we have both SSD and HDD, but the problem of the slowdown is probably connected with some internal mutex.

(Psss ehi! on which hardware do you run clickhouse ? For networking what you suggest, I am planning to wire up in Infiniband 40gbit)

So I digged in the source code, and I fear that even setting very few thread is not the right options...

Simply because inside BackgroundProcessingPool::threadFunction() the Tasks = std::multimap<Poco::Timestamp, TaskHandle>; will fill up.

Certain task are almost instant but other really takes times (and once finished it restart after very few moment), so the benefit will be VERY small.

I will try to collect a list of the type of background job, the only question is

IS possible  / OK that I insert a condition to "sleep" those background thread ?
OR there are certain task that CANNOT be delayed

If certain task can not be delayed, not a big problem, I will only "avoid" the execution of the background Merge job for "a bit", of course if a thread is still running, I will let it finish.


Thank you

There are two types of background actions:
- merging of data parts;
- fetching of data part from replica.

When you use non-replicated MergeTree, there are only tasks of first type.
And when you use ReplicatedMergeTree, in fact there is single type of tasks, that look at replication queue and then doing either merge or fetch.

Background tasks could be delayed a bit. It doesn't matter if the task will be executed right now or few seconds later.

If you delay merges for long time, you will face a risk of having too much data parts in a table. It leads to increase of SELECT latency, and also, when number of data parts (within single partition) raised up to few hundreds, INSERTs start to be throttled.

If you delay fetching from replica, you will get replication lag.

> the problem of the slowdown is probably connected with some internal mutex

You could check this easily.

First check `SELECT * FROM system.merges`. Do you see high number of running merges?

Run `top`. You will see high CPU or high disk usage.
If you see high CPU usage, run `sudo perf top` (requires to install `linux-tools-common`).
Then you will see top functions that are run by CPU.

To check disk usage, run `iotop`, `iostat -dmx 1` and `dstat`.

1) Suppose that you want to store pairs of (`user`, `user_visit_time`) in your distributed db
2) You have many `local` (or replicated) tables on each server with such data
3) The data is updated periodically, you insert several thousands pairs each `n` minutes
4) In addition to your data stored in many `local` tables, you want to store some metadata (or statistics) for each portion of data inserted in `local` tables. For example, you want to store number of uniq users for each minute.
5) To do so, on each server you create `local_stat` tables that are MaterializedView tables: (approx.) `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW local_stat (createDate DateTime, uniq_users AggregateFunction(uniq)) AS SELECT now() AS createDate, uniqState(user) AS uniq_users FROM local GROUP BY toRelativeMinuteNum(user_visit_time)`
6) Now on each server you have `local` tables with main data and `local_stat` MaterializedView tables with auxiliary statistics
7) Each `INSERT` into `local` makes corresponding INSERT SELECT into `local_stat`
8) Now you want to wrap many local tables (`local` and `local_stat`) into convenient `Distributed` tables: `local_all` and `local_stat_all` (and create such wrapper on each node).
9) Now each INSERT into `local_all` is transformed in many local INSERTs into `local` tables. Each local INSERT activate INSERT SELECT for each "attached" MaterializedView table (i.e. for `local_stat`).
10) After these chain of INSERTs are finished, you could SELECT results via Distrubuted tables `local` and `local_stat`

title: CLI interactive mode: formatting
body:
Why does `PrettyCompact` creates a new "table" for the aggregated/`DISTINCT` data if it isn't properly ordered? I'm not sure how to phrase this correctly, but here's an example:

```
:) SELECT DISTINCT toDate(created_at) FROM test FORMAT PrettyCompact;

┌─toDate(created_at)┐
│        2016-09-05 │
│        2016-09-03 │
│        2016-09-04 │
└───────────────────┘
┌─toDate(created_at)┐
│        2016-09-01 │
│        2016-09-02 │
└───────────────────┘
```

```
:) SELECT DISTINCT toDate(created_at) FROM test ORDER BY created_at FORMAT PrettyCompact;

┌─toDate(created_at)┐
│        2016-09-01 │
│        2016-09-02 │
│        2016-09-03 │
│        2016-09-04 │
│        2016-09-05 │
└───────────────────┘
```

```
:) SELECT DISTINCT toDate(created_at) FROM test FORMAT PrettyCompactMonoBlock;

┌─toDate(created_at)┐
│        2016-09-05 │
│        2016-09-03 │
│        2016-09-04 │
│        2016-09-01 │
│        2016-09-02 │
└───────────────────┘
```

Wouldn't it be better to make `PrettyCompactMonoBlock` the default formatter for the CLI?
If not, what are the use-cases of `PrettyCompact` behaving like that (with multiple tables displayed) being useful?

And by the way - is GitHub issues appropriate to ask these kind of questions or should I ask it on StackOverflow/Google Groups instead?

Thanks in advance!
author: hatarist

comments.body:
In Pretty formats, to render a table, we need to know maximum widths of columns.
To calculate them, we must buffer data for that table.
But we don't want to buffer all data, for two reasons:
1. We don't want to consume too much memory.
   (Really not a reason because there is limit for 10 000 rows in Pretty formats)
2. We want to output data as soon as it is received.
   Data is received in blocks. As soon as each block is received, we render it.
   When query is "streaming" it will send result block by block.

Several workarounds possible.
We may not render each small block instantly, but wait for some timeout, and render it only if next block has not arrived within that timeout. I think, this is unnecessarily complex solution.

By the way, it is possible to set default format in configuration file of clickhouse-client.
Configuration file is searched in:

```
./clickhouse-client.xml
~/.clickhouse-client/config.xml
/etc/clickhouse-client/config.xml
```

Create it with following content:

```
<config>
    <format>PrettyCompactMonoBlock</format>
</config>
```

> And by the way - is GitHub issues appropriate to ask these kind of questions or should I ask it on StackOverflow/Google Groups instead?

GitHub is appropriate. Stackoverflow is too.
Maybe Google Groups are better (there is already more questions), but I am not sure.

```

in `check-large-objects.sh`

Alexey is right!

`总计` is a Chinese word that means `total`. In the script, it uses 'grep -v total' to filter out rows that contains `total`, but if your OS uses Chinese, the line contains the word `total` becomes a line that contains `总计`, so that script fails to filter out that line and prints out an error.

I encountered the same problem and I temporally replace `total` by `总计` to work it around. In the long term, maybe we can avoid using 'grep -v total' but to match only the line contains object files in the script.

While implementing `reconfig`, I've discussed it with @antonio2368, and the decision was against this text file.

In Zookeeper, the whole reconfig batch is decided on a single voting so we can write a file with an updated config -- it will be applied eventually.

On the other hand, in Keeper each command part is decided on separately due to limitations of Nuraft protocol so there is a consistency issue -- what if a reconfig add 1,2 fails on 2? What should be written to disk?

title: New function: throwError
body:
Is there any way to manually make CH throw a specific error?

Something like this:
```sql
SELECT throwError(999);

Received exception from server (version 22.2.2):
Code: 999. DB::Exception: KEEPER_EXCEPTION ...
```

PS:
*Although there is a similar function (`throwIf`), it only returns code=395 (FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO).*

**Use case**

We're looking something like this so we can simulate errors and take relevant actions agains some errors.
author: ramazanpolat

comments.body:
> We're looking something like this so we can simulate errors and take relevant actions agains some errors.

Is it needed for building / debugging some client library? 

Maybe for some subset of error you can just create a scenario in clickhouse leading to that error? 
Or use some mock WS which will return needed data?

I find this useful as well to test exceptions on an application built on top of ClickHouse; for example, verify the behaviour when you reach `TOO_MANY_PARTS`.

It can be done through mocking, or by forcing CH to trigger the exception by normal means, but something like this could be a simpler way to inject errors. Maybe there are better ways though.

@filimonov 
> Is it needed for building / debugging some client library?

We'll be using it for testing purposes. 
* To react against some specific errors (e.g. retry insert, only if it is failed because of error code X)
* To use different alert levels for some specific error codes.
* To see how our software reacts to different errors.

> Maybe for some subset of error you can just create a scenario in clickhouse leading to that error?

It is practically impossible to create a scenario for each and every error. Even for a subset of errors, it is not feasible to make it happen because it takes too much time and resource (e.g. Too Many Parts, Keeper Exception, Memory Limit Exceeded, ...)

Ok. It can be an extension for `throwIf` with an additional argument.
But it should be disabled by default and enabled only with a special configuration.

Because we don't want to have "fake errors" in normal environments.

title: startsWith function for arrays
body:
Support for arrays in `startsWith` (and, maybe, `endsWith`)

**Use case**

Would be quite useful for handling tree-like structured data where the node paths are specified as arrays of names or IDs.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The desired behavior would be like this:
```
startsWith([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2])  -- true (1)
startsWith(['qwe', 'rty', 'ui', 'op'], ['qwe', 'rty'])  -- true (1)
startsWith([1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 4])  -- false (0)
startsWith([1, 1, 2, 2], [1, 2])  -- false (0)
```

And similarly, for `endsWith`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Something like `arraySlice(first, 1, length(second)) = second`

But `startsWith` would be much more readable, harder to make a mistake in and, probably, can be better optimized (i.e. might not have to create new objects like `arraySlice` does)

title: Pass execution context to table functions for accessing external datasource
body:
Does it make sense to pass execution context to table functions for accessing external datasource?

Taking `url` and `jdbc` as example, since they're based on http protocol, it would be great if ClickHouse can put below headers in **request**. With that, extension like JDBC bridge can implement role-based access control and detect recursive query like mentioned in #33802. 

| Header | Mandatory | Description |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| User-Agent | N | server/lib + version |
| X-ClickHouse-Server-Display-Name | N | server display name |
| X-ClickHouse-Format | N | different default value for different table function |
| X-ClickHouse-Query-Id | Y | query id |
| X-ClickHouse-User | Y | user who issued the query on ClickHouse, it could be user name, id or even a hash for security reason |
| X-ClickHouse-Timezone | Y | server time zone |
| X-ClickHouse-Version | N |server version |
| X-ClickHouse-Revision | N | server revision |

Note: more headers can be added for tracing when needed.
author: zhicwu

comments.body: Yes, it makes sense. We already do with User-Agent IIRC. We should also pass OpenTelemetry headers.

title: Settings limit/offset dose not work as expected on View
body:

```sql

INSERT INTO counter SELECT number, now() FROM numbers(500);

CREATE VIEW vcounter AS
SELECT
    intDiv(id, 10) AS tens,
    max(createdAt) AS maxid
FROM counter
GROUP BY tens;

ORDER BY tens ASC
LIMIT 100

title: Debuginfo is not always used in CentOS
body:
If ClickHouse RPMs are built by the native rpm toolchain debuginfo is not suitable for backtraces and reflection, while third party tools (e.g. gdb or readelf -n) do not have any issues.

This is happening because ClickHouse uses Program Header (ELF table) to obtain Build ID to validate debuginfo against executable. This approach does not seem reliable, it is better to use Section Header.
author: ilejn

comments.body:
I failed to find any proper guideline, just a number of hints.

In readelf.c from elfutils 0.176 there is a comment

> If we have section headers, just look for SHT_NOTE sections.
> In a debuginfo file, the program headers are not reliable.  */

In man elf(5)

> Program headers are meaningful only for executable and shared object files

I've tweaked readelf to use Program Headers and behaviour is the same as demonstrated by ClickHouse

> ./src/readelf -n /tmp/clickhouse.debug
> 
> Note segment of 68 bytes at offset 0x2fc:
>   Owner          Data size  Type
>                          4  <unknown>: 20
> ./src/readelf: cannot get content of note: garbage data

While intact readelf works fine

> ./src/readelf -n /tmp/clickhouse.debug
> 
> Note section [ 2] '.note.ABI-tag' of 32 bytes at offset 0x2e0:
>   Owner          Data size  Type
>   GNU                   16  GNU_ABI_TAG
>     OS: Linux, ABI: 3.2.0
> 
> Note section [ 3] '.note.gnu.build-id' of 36 bytes at offset 0x300:
>   Owner          Data size  Type
>   GNU                   20  GNU_BUILD_ID
>     Build ID: b16a083ed23e14e92d6e8017099cc9103e73d8b5

I willingly handle it, while I appreciate additional information and suggestions.

Was the choice of Program Headers deliberate? 
Should we keep Program Headers as a fallback (readelf behaves in this way, if no Section Headers look into Program Headers)?
What should be tested to ensure nothing is broken (some exotic platforms may be)?
This is about Elf::getBuildID

Yes, separate debug info file does not necessary contain proper program headers.
We can start with section headers if we are using separate debug info.

But if we are using the binary with embedded debug info, it is better to use program headers, because they are already loaded in memory.

PS. We don't use or support native rpm toolchain, so I don't care about this issue.
Nevertheless, it will be better to fix.

title: Graceful server shutdown
body:
Currently, running queries are cancelled and server waits for clients to close connections for `shutdown_wait_unfinished`.

Proposal: Do not cancel running queries and let them run for some timeout before trying to shut down storages.

This should be useful for large clusters with long-running distributed queries and high release cadence.
author: nvartolomei

comments.body:
I would better not implement this feature.

It will introduce complications on server side while clients still should always support retries (with exponential backoff and limits) and be ready to return error for user. This is required for high availability.

But this feature is very easy to implement (just add a flag to disable query cancellation on shutdown).
If you want to implement it, please send a PR.

CREATE TABLE t
(

body:
That was working on 21.1 and older:
```
WITH JSONExtract('{"Orders":[{"id":1,"name":"a"},{"id":2,"name":"b"}]}', 'Orders', 'Nested(UInt64, String)') AS orders
SELECT
    orders.1,
    orders.2
```

```
Received exception from server (version 21.2.10):
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Data type Nested accepts only pairs with name and type: While processing (JSONExtract('{"Orders":[{"id":1,"name":"a"},{"id":2,"name":"b"}]}', 'Orders', 'Nested(UInt64, String)') AS orders).1, orders.2. 
```

Workaround (works on both old and new version)
```
WITH JSONExtract('{"Orders":[{"id":1,"name":"a"},{"id":2,"name":"b"}]}', 'Orders', 'Nested(id UInt64, name String)') AS orders
SELECT
    orders.1,
    orders.2

title: Direct conversion to IPv6 from string
body:
Currently there are the `toIPv4()` and `toIPv6()` functions to parse an IP address from a `String` type.
In order to be able to store both v4 and v6 addresses in a column, it needs to be IPv6, obviously.
Alternatively, they could be stored as `String` as well, but that would imply loosing CIDR matching.

Now, v4 addresses need to be "mapped" to v6 address in order to work correctly (e.g. `::ffff:192.168.1.1`).
With the current version of `toIPv6()` it is not possible to directly parse an IPv4 address.
Workarounds do exist (e.g. `if(toIPv6(src_ip) != defaultValueOfTypeName('IPv6'), toIPv6(src_ip), toIPv6(concat('::ffff:', src_ip)))`), but they are quite cumbersome to use.

It would be nice to either:

- Have `toIPv6()` also parse IPv4 strings, and automatically do the v6 mapping
- Have a new function (e.g. something like `parseIPv6()`) that implements this behavior, so `toIPv6()` stays backwards compatible.
author: ifoo

title: users_config and/or access_control_path together with entries from user_directories may produce duplicate access info storages
body:
Discovered during testing of #12736

When `config.xml` contains both (or one of) `users_config` and `access_control_path`, together with the corresponding entries in `user_directories`, and when the paths/values in those sections are the same, duplicate access storage are created in memory.

This leads to unexpected behavior, e.g., when a role is removed - it will be removed in one of `access_control_path`/`local_directory` duplicate and will be preserved in another, effectively making that role still available.

`SHOW ROLES`, for example, before the deletion, will show duplicate roles.

Potential solution would be avoiding creating duplicate storage when old and new corresponding config sections point to the same actual file/path.

**Describe the unexpected behaviour**
When using groupArray function with max_size parameter defined as constant in WITH clause got error message:

**How to reproduce**
ClickHouse server version 20.3.8.53
```
with 1 as max_size
select groupArray(max_size)(col) from (
select 1 as col
UNION ALL
select 2
)
```

It would be nice to have this function accept max_size parameter as defined in WITH clause.
author: pic-Nick

comments.body:
When a function in clickhouse has multiple ()() in it's definition, parameters being passed to the first brackets can't be dynamically set during execution and should be constant.

```

SELECT
    1 AS max_size,
    groupArray(max_size)(col)
FROM
(
    SELECT 1 AS col
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2
)

Query id: 4113a11a-bd97-4acb-8055-c29f1e1c7019


Received exception from server (version 20.13.1):
Code: 134. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Parameters to aggregate functions must be literals. Got parameter 'max_size'.
```

So it looks like a misleading error message.

There's no reason to not allow constant expressions in aggregate function parameters.

Changed to "feature request".

title: SYSTEM DROP REPLICA
body:
Sometime you need to remove the 'dead' replica. 
attach + DROP is a bit too 'costy' and complicated.
removing nodes in zookeeper is also a bad option as requires knowledge of ClickHouse internals.  

It would be better to have a possibility to remove 'dead' replica from healthy one (only in case if it's offline and stale, exception otherwise).
author: filimonov

comments.body:
Typical usecase: server was off for a long time / replace replica with new one.

Currently it will not allow you to CREATE (replica already exists), ATTACH has not to much sense and will requite enabling replica recovery, and will try to 'execute' obsolete queue.
Hi, is there any timeline for supporting this? This would be a great feature.

There is no timeline for this task. But it is easy to implement.

The only important thing is to check that replica is not active, and while removing - remove some nodes first in a multi transaction with check of `active` node - to avoid possible race condition.
Bump, is there any update on supporting this? This would be a super useful feature!
Hi, is it safe to `rmr /path/to/replica` on ZK for this case? Is there anything else to be deleted?

Almost safe. You only have to check that the replica is not active and do it within the same transaction.

Yes, only `/path/to/replica` has to be deleted.
Thank you!

title: clickhouse-client timings output file instead of stderr
body:
Due to the issues related to `query_log` table reported in #4518 I am measuring timings of queries using `clickhouse-client -t` argument, as suggested in documentation.
```
  -t [ --time ]                         print query execution time to stderr in
                                        non-interactive mode (for benchmarks)
```
Precisely speaking, I am redirecting STDERR to a file so I can extract timings in automated manner.
```sh
cat "clickhouse/groupby-clickhouse.sql" | clickhouse-client -t -mn --max_memory_usage=$CH_MEM --format=Pretty --output_format_pretty_max_rows 1 2> clickhouse/log/groupby_G2_1e9_1e2_0_0.out
```
This works quite well
```sh
cat clickhouse/log/groupby_G2_1e9_1e2_0_0.out 
#45.763
#2.864
#...
```
as long as there is no real error raised by clickhouse-client, then file looks like
```sh
cat clickhouse/log/groupby_G2_1e9_2e0_0_0.out
#36.362
#2.290
#...
#197.714
#Error on processing query: SELECT id3, sum(v1) AS v1, avg(v3) AS v3 FROM G2_1e9_2e0_0_0 GROUP BY id3;
#Code: 32, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Attempt to read after eof: while receiving packet from localhost:9000, 127.0.0.1, Stack trace:
```
In such cases my log files are useless as they cannot be automatically processed.

----

I would like to request an extra argument to `clickhouse-client`, lets say `tout` (or `tfile`), to provide a file name to write timings, rather than using STDERR, which to be fair, should not be used for storing query timings.
author: jangorecki

comments.body: any chance to have this feature incorporated? seems to be pretty straightforward. `query_log` doesn't seems to be reliable, as explained in linked issue.
Workaround, if you don’t want to wait for this feature/fix: generate query ids, then sleep for few seconds flush logs and get timings from query log table.

> any chance to have this feature incorporated?

It's quite easy to implement, the chance is high. But this feature request is not assigned to anyone in my team right now.
Also you can use `grep -P '^\d'` to preprocess your file.

I treat this feature request as having very low priority.
It targets a very specific use case and a workaround is easy.
@alexey-milovidov could you provide PR I'd that resolved this issue? Or a least link to documentation about the feature.

@jangorecki I'm closing it because no one is willing to implement it in 3.5 years.
I also don't need this feature. If you need this feature, you can implement it.

title: DB::Exception: Illegal type UUID of argument of function notEmpty.
body:
Version 18.14.54409

When executing JOIN's involving UUID column, you could expect that some of them are not filled in; so using the notEmpty() should be possible; However it seems that this is currently not supported.

Testcase:
```sql
CREATE DATABASE uuid_empty;
CREATE TABLE uuid_empty.users (user_id UUID) ENGINE = Memory;
CREATE TABLE uuid_empty.orders (order_id UUID, user_id UUID) ENGINE = Memory;
INSERT INTO uuid_empty.users VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001');
INSERT INTO uuid_empty.users VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002');
INSERT INTO uuid_empty.orders VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003', '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001');

SELECT 
    uniq(user_id) AS users, 
    uniqIf(order_id, notEmpty(order_id)) AS orders
FROM 
(
    SELECT * FROM uuid_empty.users
) ALL LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT * FROM uuid_empty.orders 
) USING (user_id);

DROP DATABASE uuid_empty;
```
Should result in (currently the result using String type)
```sql
┌─users─┬─orders─┐
│     2 │      1 │
└───────┴────────┘
```
But now returns
```
Received exception from server (version 18.14.54409):
Code: 43. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000, 127.0.0.1. DB::Exception: Illegal type UUID of argument of function notEmpty. 

```

Executing the following query without aggregating gives the (empty?) uuid `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`?

```sql
SELECT 
    user_id, 
    order_id
FROM 
(
    SELECT *
    FROM uuid_empty.users 
) 
ALL LEFT JOIN 
(
    SELECT *
    FROM uuid_empty.orders 
) USING (user_id)

┌──────────────────────────────user_id─┬─────────────────────────────order_id─┐
│ 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 │ 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003 │
│ 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002 │ 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 │
└──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘
```
author: sjoerdmulder

comments.body:
Simpler test-case:
```
select notEmpty(toUUID('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'));
```

comments.body:
Hi,

arm32 and arm64 architectures are not currently supported. It was possible to build ClickHouse on arm64, but there might be problems though.
For 32 bit architectures it's more difficult. The ability to build on 32 bit was recently committed, but visible problems are:

- Possible lack of memory during compilation. Some files may need more than 2GB RAM.
- Not all of the tests are passed for i386.
- There are parts of the code where size_t assumed to be 64 bit

Before trying to compile I did increase my swapfile and rebooted my Raspberry Pi:

```
$ grep CONF_SWAPSIZE /etc/dphys-swapfile
CONF_SWAPSIZE=2048
```

It allowed for 1 GB of RAM and 2 GB of Swap. It's slow but I was hoping it would alleviate any memory issues. So far I've made it to about 54% of the way through compilation until I hit ``dbms/src/Common/BitHelpers.h`` and then the system locks up. I'm not sure if there is a way to somehow lower the memory usage during compilation. I'm going to continue to look into this.

with swap your compile time will take days and you have chance to kill sd card.
and now you need ~3.4G ram
I have tried to compile on boards with 2g ram + swap and all attempts are unsuccessful

I've been able to attach mechanical SATA drives via USB to avoid hitting the SD card too much.

Do you know of any parameters make or cmake can be given to try and lower that memory footprint? 3.4 GB doesn't feel like a world away from >3 GB.

> There are parts of the code where size_t assumed to be 64 bit

If this does end up being an issue I can try and run an arm64 OS + Kernel on the Raspberry Pi. I'll most likely address that after I can get the code compiled and running in some form on arm32 first.

No, we need to split/refactor some c++ template code.
Maybe for now easier/faster to use debian arm on qemu or cross compile
We have support for Aarch64 and PPC64, but we aren't going to support 32 bit architectures.
